dependent_variable: log monthly all-cause mortality rate (lndrate)
main_predictor: Days with mean temperature >=90F (b10_10) interacted with post-1960 indicator
sample_definition: State-month observations 1930-2004, all 48 contiguous states + DC (43,464 obs after dropping missing mortality)

The pre-1960 effect of a hot day is 0.0257 log points and the post-1960 effect is essentially zero (0.0257-0.0254=0.0003), indicating a large, statistically significant decline in the temperature-mortality relationship, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Two-year first difference in combined normalized PIAT math-reading score (renormalized in the random sample to mean 0, SD 1)

reasoning: Using my reconstructed simulated-EITC instrument in a 2SLS specification analogous to Table 3 of the paper, the IV coefficient on the 2-year change in total family income (in $1000s of year-2000 dollars) is -0.014 (SE = 0.027, t = -0.53, p = 0.60), which is not statistically distinguishable from zero and actually wrong-signed. dependent_variable: Difference in mentions: (anti-immigration actions - pro-immigration actions) mentioned in a letter

Consistent with the paper, sending more in the trust game significantly reduces the probability of participating in the lab experiment.

dependent_variable: Normalized combined math-reading PIAT score (average of standardized math and reading-recognition, renormalized on the random sample)

operationalization_notes: The headline 6%-of-SD claim comes from a 2SLS using a TAXSIM-based simulated EITC instrument, which cannot be reconstructed from the provided main.dta alone. I therefore implemented the closest defensible levels-OLS counterpart on the combined math-reading achievement measure (the same dependent variable as the IV baseline in Table 3, column 1), which tests the directional content of the claim.

A $1,000 income increase is associated with ~0.009 SD higher combined achievement, supporting the directional claim that higher family income raises short-run combined math-reading scores. The magnitude is smaller than the paper's IV estimate (≈0.06), as expected given OLS attenuation and the absence of the EITC instrument.

dependent_variable: ProperName (whether the response used the applicant's proper name; 1=yes, 0=no) among responders

A Pearson chi-squared test of independence yields chi2(1)=14.42, p<.001, confirming Hispanic applicants were significantly less likely than white applicants to be greeted by name.

dependent_variable: Session-level frequency of normal quality (qualityc==2) among trades

A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test yields W=15, p=0.03125, indicating significantly less shading under rigid contracts, replicating the paper's finding.

dependent_variable: log total CO2 emissions (carbon_unadj)

This confirms the paper's claim of a positive relationship between working hours and CO2 emissions over 2007-2013.

dependent_variable: consider (considered attack against a nuclear program, dyad-year)

The negative sign indicates that less politically dominant (more marginalized) counties are more likely to secede — consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: recog1dum: dichotomous diplomatic recognition (State B recognizes State A)

dependent_variable: Log of absolute opinion change on the pro-immigration index between wave 2 and wave 3

operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Model 2b (Table 2): magnitude of opinion change as log of absolute change, predicted by group-level justification rationality with controls; this is the analysis directly tied to the claim that opinion change is greater when rational justification is used.

Higher justification rationality in the discussion group is associated with larger opinion change.

dependent_variable: Mean effort (work, 0/1) per matching group across all rounds
main_predictor: Reward scheme (discriminating 345COM vs symmetrical 444COM)
sample_definition: All subject-rounds in the complementarity treatments (345COM and 444COM); aggregated to 6 independent matching groups per treatment
model_specification: Two-sided Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney rank-sum test on matching-group means
operationalization_notes: Matching group (smg) is the independent unit of observation as in the paper; effort averaged across rounds and subjects within each matching group.
reasoning: Mann-Whitney U comparing matching-group mean effort under complementarity: 345COM (discriminating) mean ≈0.917 vs 444COM (symmetrical) mean ≈0.727; U=31, n1=n2=6, two-sided p=0.041. Symmetrical reward elicits significantly lower effort than the cost-equivalent discriminating scheme.

dependent_variable: Tailoring index per senator: (mention anti-immigration action) - (mention pro-immigration action), computed separately for each constituent letter
main_predictor: Letter audience: anti-immigration constituent vs. pro-immigration constituent (within-subject)

operationalization_notes: This directly operationalizes 'tailoring' as the within-senator shift in which type of action (anti- vs pro-immigration) is emphasized depending on which constituent is being addressed, matching the 'Anti - Pro' contrast in Table 2 of the paper.
reasoning: Within-senator paired t-test of the tailoring index (mentions of anti-immigration actions minus pro-immigration actions) comparing responses to the anti-immigration constituent letter vs. the pro-immigration constituent letter gives t(55)=3.45, p=0.001 (N=56 senators who responded to both letters). Senators emphasized anti-immigration actions more (and pro-immigration actions less) when writing to the anti-immigration constituent than to the pro-immigration constituent, confirming that senators tailor their explanations to their audiences.

dependent_variable: log(last U.S. wage) - log(last home wage), in PPP-adjusted dollars
main_predictor: Education category (no high school, some HS, HS grad, some college; college grad omitted)

model_specification: OLS: gain ~ education category dummies + country fixed effects

The coefficient on 'no high school' is +0.197 (SE 0.129, t=1.52, N=2854), indicating immigrants with no high school gain ~22% more than college graduates. The direction matches the paper's claim (paper reports 0.599, ~82%, using pooled NIS+MMP, N=3,539), though the MMP-only estimate is not statistically significant at conventional levels.

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses reflecting the learned cue meaning (combined homographic and nonhomographic; FAbaseC vs FAsuppC)

The available SPSS file corresponds to Experiment 2; I used the combined-cue-type means (FAbaseC, FAsuppC) consistent with the paper's stated collapsing across homograph/nonhomograph.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being (8-item CES-D mean, higher = better)
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction: Lives-with-children (vs. childless) × country-level % (strongly) disapproving of childlessness
sample_definition: Men aged 41+ in 24 European countries from ESS Round 3 with complete data (missing==0); N=10,473
model_specification: Two-level linear mixed model with random intercept for country, fixed effects for parental status (3 cat.), country-level % disapprove, their interactions, plus individual controls
controls: Age, age², marital status (4 cat.), own education (4 cat.), parents' education (4 cat. + missing), religious attendance, paid employment, born in country
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 3 Model 2a in the paper; country-level disapproval computed as the share of respondents within each country answering 3 or 4 on the childless_disapp item. Focused on men because the paper presents the norms interaction for men in Model 2a, and used the Lives-with-children × disapproval term as the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: In a multilevel model for men (random intercept by country) regressing CES-D well-being on parental status interacted with the country-level percentage of (strong) disapproval of childlessness plus individual controls, the Lives-with-children × %-disapprove interaction is positive (B≈0.001, z=2.135, p=.033). Since childless is the reference, a positive interaction means the parent advantage (i.e., childless disadvantage) grows in countries with more disapproval and shrinks where norms are tolerant—matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: DSM-5 total psychopathology score (DSM5_Total)
main_predictor: Mini-K life history strategy total (higher = slower)

reasoning: Pearson correlation between Mini-K (higher = slower life history strategy) and DSM-5 total psychopathology score was r = -.587, t(136) = -8.46, p < .001, indicating that faster life-history strategies (lower Mini-K) are associated with greater psychopathology symptoms, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (sum of correct answers on 20-item political knowledge test)
main_predictor: Stereotype activation condition (condition 1: not activated vs. condition 3: activated by gender difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender_alle==1) passing the Filter==1 criterion, in condition 1 or condition 3

operationalization_notes: Used the filtered analytic sample as in the paper. Gender variable 'gender_alle' was used because the variable 'gender' was only collected in conditions 2 and 3; the paper's reported cell sizes (73 and 70) match this choice. The t-test on the raw knowledge score directly maps to the claim's pairwise comparison.
reasoning: Among female participants, mean political knowledge score in the stereotype-not-activated condition (M=8.90, SD=4.60, N=73) was significantly higher than in the stereotype-activated-by-gender-difference-statement condition (M=7.03, SD=4.11, N=70), t(141)=2.57, p=0.011, d=0.43. This confirms the paper's reported directional effect.

dependent_variable: GDP growth at t+2 (gdpidx, last year=100)

controls: Starting-year (predecessor) log GDP, log population, log fixed investment, GDP index for both msec and mayor; net transfer (dep) at t+1; msec and mayor age, gender (male), college education
operationalization_notes: Operationalized following the paper's baseline model (Table 1, col 3). Connection = max of msec2currentsec and mayor2currentsec. reasoning: Replicating Table 1 Model 3, a two-way fixed effects (city FE + province-year FE) regression of GDP growth at t+2 on whether either city secretary or mayor is connected to the incumbent provincial secretary, with city economic and leader controls and city-clustered SEs, yields a positive and highly significant coefficient on Connected (b=0.576, SE=0.140, t=4.11, p<0.001). Connected city leaders deliver faster growth, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: log(fraction of foreign players in the first league), with cells defined by country × year × ability (top vs. lower)

controls: All lower-order terms of the triple interaction (top, dk, post, and all two-way interactions) act as fixed effects/controls
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns ability composition of foreigners in Denmark after the 1991 reform. The most direct statistical test is the triple-difference coefficient (top × Denmark × post-1991) in a regression of log(fraction foreign) across ability-country-year cells, with Sweden as the comparison since Online Appendix Table A2 places 63-77% of the synthetic-control weight on Sweden.
reasoning: In a triple-difference (DDD) OLS of log(fraction of foreign players) on top-ability × Denmark × post-1991, comparing Denmark to Sweden (the dominant synthetic-control donor for Denmark) over 1985-2008, the triple-interaction coefficient is 1.346 (HC1 SE 0.554, z = 2.43, p = 0.015). The positive and statistically significant DDD coefficient indicates that after the 1991 Danish preferential tax scheme for foreigners, the share of foreign players in Denmark shifted toward high-ability players relative to Sweden, supporting the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Willingness to pay to protect the environment (willingness_to_pay)
main_predictor: Intrinsic relative to extrinsic values (intrin_extrin, I/E index)

dependent_variable: Post-dispute log product-level imports (imports_post)

reasoning: Replicating Model 2 (early-settlement subsample), the Complainant indicator has a positive, statistically significant coefficient (b=0.469, cluster-robust SE=0.236, z=1.99, p=0.047, N=6,027), indicating that within privately-settled disputes complainant countries see significantly larger post-dispute import growth than other WTO members - same direction and significance as Kucik & Pelc report.

dependent_variable: Early-stage entrepreneurship rate that pays wages (entre_wage)
main_predictor: Median age of working-age population (medage_20_64)
sample_definition: All GEM country-year observations 2001-2010 (N=393)
model_specification: WLS with year fixed effects, weighted by nobs_cy, SE clustered by country

dependent_variable: Ratio of perceived to actual arm length

model_specification: Paired-samples t-test on RatioRight vs RatioLeft

reasoning: Paired t-test among right-handed participants comparing right vs. left arm perceived/actual ratio: t(14)=2.12, one-tailed p≈.026. Right arm ratio (M=0.97) was greater than left arm ratio (M=0.92), indicating right arm was perceived as relatively longer than left, replicating the paper.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (mean of 3 items: appreciated, valued, satisfied)

dependent_variable: Standardized exam score (midterm + final), s_tot
main_predictor: Share female among neighbor 5 peers (avg5_girl)

controls: Baseline test score, height, age, birth order, mother's and father's education, interest in Chinese/math/English, average baseline score of neighbor 5, desk mate special status, share special among neighbor 4
operationalization_notes: Follows equation (2) in paper (Table 5, Panel B, column 1) with neighbor-5 specification; matches paper's N=245 after excluding special students and missing covariates.
reasoning: OLS of standardized exam score on share-female-in-neighbor-5 with baseline controls and block fixed effects on the female subsample yields coefficient 0.211 (SE 0.105, t=2.01, p=0.046, n=245), matching the paper's reported 0.21 SD effect and supporting the claim that being surrounded by females raises females' test scores.

dependent_variable: Absolute change in mean attitude rating between T1 and T2 (|att_T2 - att_T1|)
main_predictor: Objective ambivalence × overall attitude certainty interaction (mean-centered)
sample_definition: Study 1 participants with complete T1 and T2 attitude data (N=174)

operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Study 1 procedure: objective ambivalence via Griffin formula ((P+N)/2 - |P-N|), certainty as mean of 7 certainty items, attitudes averaged across three items, extremity as deviation from scale midpoint.
reasoning: Replicated Study 1: the objective ambivalence × certainty interaction significantly predicts absolute attitude change over 1 month, B=0.037, t(169)=2.28, p=.024, controlling for extremity. Consistent with the claim that certainty is associated with greater stability as ambivalence decreases.

dependent_variable: Voter turnout (% of registered voters)
main_predictor: Portfolio Equity Stock (log)
sample_definition: Election-year observations in 23 OECD countries, 1970-2007, with non-missing turnout, lagged turnout, all controls and portfolio equity stock
model_specification: OLS with lagged dependent variable, country fixed effects, country-specific linear and quadratic time trends; standard errors clustered by country
controls: Log registered voters; %VAP age 30-69; years since last election; US-midterm indicator; compulsory voting; mixed system; PR system; disproportionality; ENPS; closeness/margin
operationalization_notes: Among the foreign-ownership measures, Portfolio Equity Stock is highlighted in the paper as the most flexible (and the strongest constraint). Specification mirrors Table 1 Model 4. Ownership Scale (the factor score) was not pre-computed in the dataset, so I used the most directly relevant ownership variable.
reasoning: Replicating Table 1 Model 4: OLS of turnout on log Portfolio Equity Stock with lagged turnout, electoral/political controls, country fixed effects and country-specific linear and quadratic time trends (clustered SEs by country) yields a coefficient of -2.24 (SE 0.66), t = -3.41 (p < .001, N=251). This negative, highly significant coefficient on the most flexible foreign-ownership measure supports the ownership-constraint hypothesis that foreign ownership reduces turnout.

dependent_variable: Number of BBB service complaints in 2008 (complaints_2008)

dependent_variable: log monthly mortality rate (lndrate)
main_predictor: number of days in each temperature bin (>90°F, 80-89°F, <40°F) interacted with post-1960 indicator

The key >90°F × post-1960 interaction is large and negative (-0.0192, t=-4.71), indicating the hot-day mortality effect declined sharply after 1960, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Log continuously compounded reservation interest rate (interval-censored)

dependent_variable: Absolute ideological distance of plurality party from the median voter (pldist1, manifesto-based)

reasoning: Pearson correlation between subject-level error rate in the LV format (proportion of dominated-lottery choices out of 10) and degree of risk aversion (average number of safe choices in the PV and RV formats) is r = -0.443 (t(77) = -4.33, p ≈ 4.4e-5) on the 79 risk-averse subjects. dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of group-level partial semantic networks built from animal-fluency responses (TMFG-filtered, binarized, induced subgraphs).

controls: None (nodes matched across groups by construction; equal number of edges via TMFG).
operationalization_notes: Closely follows the paper's partial bootstrap procedure (Kenett et al. 2013/2014); the 50% node-retention condition was chosen as the primary test since it is the conventional bootstrap fraction and is one of the conditions reported in the paper's Table 3.
reasoning: Across 1000 partial-network bootstraps (50% of nodes retained), the high-openness group's induced subgraph had a significantly smaller ASPL (M = 3.73) than the low-openness group's (M = 3.83), independent-samples t(1998) = -2.94, p = .003, Cohen's d = -0.13. The direction (high < low in ASPL = more interconnected) matches the published claim, though the magnitude of the effect is smaller than reported in the paper (likely due to differences in the similarity metric used to build the network prior to TMFG filtering).

model_specification: Negative binomial GLM with municipality fixed effects, month-year fixed effects, and population control; SEs clustered at municipality
controls: Population of males 15-39; municipality and time fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Replicates column 1 of Table 2; the short-term effect is identified by the after(1-6 months)*leader coefficient. Default alpha=1 used for NB dispersion (statsmodels), which slightly differs from Stata's MLE alpha but yields the same sign and significance.
reasoning: Negative binomial regression with municipality and time fixed effects on the leader-treatment subsample (Table 2, col. 1) yields a positive and statistically significant coefficient on after(1-6 months)*leader (b=0.250, SE=0.126, z=1.99, p=0.047), indicating that DTO-related homicides (males 15-39) rose in the first six months after a leader's capture/killing, consistent with the paper's claim of an exacerbating short-term effect.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of bootstrapped partial semantic networks
main_predictor: Openness-to-experience group (high vs. low, median split on mean of NEO-FFI Openness and BFAS Openness aspect)
sample_definition: All 516 retained participants; networks constructed on 167 animal-fluency responses given by ≥2 participants in BOTH groups (common-node restriction).
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test comparing ASPL across 1000 bootstrap realizations per group (50% of nodes retained, sampled without replacement). Networks built from binary participant×response matrix via cosine similarity, filtered with the Triangulated Maximally Filtered Graph (TMFG), then binarized and analyzed as unweighted undirected graphs.
controls: Equal nodes/edges between groups via common-node restriction and TMFG (same number of edges 3n-6); no additional covariates
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Kenett/SemNeT pipeline: cosine similarity + TMFG + binarization + bootstrapped node-drop comparison. Group construction used a simple median split on the composite of o_ffi and o_bfas as a proxy for the paper's CFA latent factor (intellect items excluded a priori in the BFAS aspect-level scoring). Implemented TMFG and graph metrics in Python (NetworkX).
reasoning: Bootstrapped partial networks (1000 realizations, 50% nodes retained) showed the high-openness group had significantly lower ASPL (M=3.07) than the low-openness group (M=3.34), t(1998)=-13.13, p<.001, d=-0.59. Lower ASPL indicates greater interconnectivity, replicating the published finding that the high-openness network is more interconnected.

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Index (0-8 ordinal)
main_predictor: Reliance on Taxes (tax_rev_new)
sample_definition: Country-year panel observations with non-missing data on the DV, lagged DV, and all controls
model_specification: Ordered probit with lagged dependent variable
controls: Size of government revenues, log population, income per capita, Polity democracy, external conflict, internal armed conflict, UK colony, lagged DV
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 2 column 6 (ordered probit with full controls and lagged DV), the paper's primary specification for the claim.
reasoning: Ordered probit of the CIRI Physical Integrity Index on Reliance on Taxes with the lagged DV and the paper's controls yields a positive, significant coefficient on tax reliance (b=0.0056, SE=0.0019, z=2.98, p=0.003, N=1739), matching the direction and significance reported in Table 2 column 6.

dependent_variable: School-level % students passing ≥5 GCSEs at grades A-C (pt_gcse_5_a_c)
main_predictor: GM status (gm_school) instrumented by winning the GM ballot (vote share > 50%)
sample_definition: Main RD sample of secondary schools that held a first GM vote; observations with non-missing outcome and baseline (N=8,665 school-year observations, 742 schools)
model_specification: Fuzzy regression discontinuity estimated by 2SLS; instrument WIN = I(vote>50) for endogenous GM_school; standard errors clustered at school level
controls: Linear running variable (vote share − 50) and baseline pre-vote pass rate (pt_gcse_5_a_c_base)
operationalization_notes: Follows eq. (1) in the paper using the linear-in-vote-share specification with baseline performance control, matching the headline 2SLS column of Table 2 for the secondary school sample.
reasoning: Fuzzy RD 2SLS: GM conversion (instrumented by winning the GM vote) raised the share of students passing 5+ GCSEs at A–C by 4.20 percentage points (SE 1.08, t = 3.89, p < 0.001, clustered by 742 schools), confirming the paper's claim of large achievement gains for converted GM schools.

dependent_variable: Participated in lab experiment (0/1)
main_predictor: Amount sent in trust game (Sent_Class, $0/$10/$20)
sample_definition: All students who played the trust game and provided an amount-sent decision (N=658)
model_specification: Probit with tutor-clustered robust SEs
controls: Female, Commerce, International, day-of-week dummies, flyer-after-experiment dummy, Chosen-for-Payment dummy, tutor fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 3 column 4 of Cleave et al. (2013): probit of lab participation on amount sent with demographic, scheduling, and tutor controls.
reasoning: Probit of lab participation on amount sent (controlling for female, commerce, international, day, flyer-order, paid-for-classroom, tutor fixed effects, with tutor-clustered SEs) yields a coefficient on Sent_Class of -0.024, z=-2.54, p=0.011 (N=658). Consistent with the paper's claim: students who sent less in the trust game were significantly more likely to participate in the lab experiment.

dependent_variable: took_act (illness episode treated with an ACT)
main_predictor: ACT subsidy = 92% (act40 indicator)
sample_definition: First illness episodes only; households assigned ACT subsidy only or control; RDT-subsidy households and surprise-RDT households excluded
model_specification: OLS linear probability model with dummies for the three ACT subsidy levels (92%, 88%, 80%), strata fixed effects, and SEs clustered at the household level
controls: Age of household head (imputed) and 28 strata fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Follows Table 2, Panel B, Column 1 of the paper; coefficient on the 92% subsidy dummy directly tests whether a very high subsidy increases ACT access relative to the no-subsidy control.
reasoning: Regressing an indicator for taking an ACT on dummies for each ACT subsidy level (controlling for household head age and strata FE, with household-clustered SEs), the 92% subsidy raises ACT access by 22.3 percentage points (SE=0.053; t=4.19, p<0.001), compared to a 19% control mean. The very-high subsidy more than doubles access, replicating the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Two-year change in normalized combined math-reading PIAT score (average of piamatsn and piarersn, then differenced)
main_predictor: Two-year change in real total family income in $1,000 of year-2000 dollars (sum of earnincrsimp + unearnincrsimp + nontaxincrsimp + totweadimp2, deflated by CPI)
sample_definition: NLSY child-mother sample with two consecutive PIAT test waves exactly 2 years apart and non-missing income and baseline covariates (9,777 child-pair observations across 3,138 families)
model_specification: OLS regression on two-year first differences (eliminates child fixed effects); cluster-robust SE at family (momid) level
controls: Child gender (male), race indicators (black, hispanic, other), mother's age at the test year, change in number of children in household, year-of-test fixed effects
operationalization_notes: The paper's headline claim is from a 2SLS estimator using simulated EITC schedule changes as an instrument for income changes. Constructing that simulated instrument from the raw NLSY file is outside the scope of what can be done with the data alone, so I committed to the most direct non-IV analog reported in the paper itself (Table 2 panel B, column 1): OLS in two-year first differences of the combined math-reading score on changes in real family income, with baseline child controls and year FE, clustered at the family level. This isolates the within-child time-varying association between income and achievement that the IV is meant to identify causally.
reasoning: Estimating the 'contemporaneous effects' model in two-year differences via OLS yields a coefficient on the change in family income (in $1,000s of year-2000 dollars) of 3.1e-5 (cluster-robust SE 4.9e-4), t = 0.06, p = 0.95, on the change in the combined math/reading PIAT z-score. The estimated short-run effect of a $1,000 income increase is therefore indistinguishable from zero in this OLS specification, consistent with the paper's own OLS-in-differences result (also small and insignificant) but not with the headline IV claim that $1,000 raises scores by ~6% of an SD. Faithfully replicating the paper's IV would require constructing the simulated EITC instrument from federal/state EITC schedules, which is not feasible from the provided files.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs)
main_predictor: Single/childless dummy (singchild1; 1=single childless, 0=other)
sample_definition: Currently employed business school alumni respondents with complete data on absorption, single/childless, gender, age, position (n=355)
model_specification: OLS linear regression
operationalization_notes: Followed Study 1 methods as described in the paper: OLS regression of absorption on the single/childless indicator with the three controls.
reasoning: OLS regression of work absorption on the single/childless dummy, controlling for gender, age, and job level, yields b=-0.296, t(350)=-2.24, p=.026. Single, childless workers report significantly lower absorption than workers with other family structures, replicating the paper's Study 1 finding.

dependent_variable: ProperName (1 = greeted by proper name in reply, 0 = not)
main_predictor: Sender race (Hispanic vs white name, from TreatmentGroup)
sample_definition: Emails sent by Hispanic- or white-named senders with non-missing ProperName (i.e., responses that could be coded for greeting); black-named senders excluded.
model_specification: Pearson chi-squared test of independence on a 2x2 contingency table (race x ProperName), no continuity correction
operationalization_notes: The claim is a simple bivariate comparison of greeting-by-name rates between Hispanic and white senders; a chi-squared test on the 2x2 table is the most direct test.
reasoning: Among emails that received a response with codable name-greeting data, 41.2% of Hispanic-named senders were greeted by name vs 61.1% of white-named senders (chi2(1)=14.42, p<.001, N=362), consistent with the paper's claim that Hispanic applicants were less likely to be greeted by name than white applicants.

dependent_variable: Indicator for normal (high) quality (qualityc==2)
main_predictor: Flexible-contract dummy (contracttypec==2)
sample_definition: Baseline condition (condition==1), contract realized (contractrealizedc==1), good state (cost<=25); N=805
model_specification: OLS: normal ~ price_increment + flex + price_increment:flex, with cluster-robust SEs by session_no
controls: Price increment (price-35) and its interaction with flexible
operationalization_notes: This mirrors the paper's Table 3 column 1, which is the most direct regression test of the shading-by-contract-type claim. I report the z-statistic on the flexible-contract dummy.
reasoning: Replicating Table 3 column 1, OLS of normal-quality indicator on price increment, flexible-contract dummy, and their interaction (baseline condition, realized contracts, good state) yields a flexible-contract coefficient of -0.335 with cluster-robust (by session) z = -5.60, p < 0.001. Sellers are about 33.5 percentage points less likely to provide normal quality (i.e., shade more) under flexible than rigid contracts, supporting the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: log of total state CO2 emissions (carbon_adj)
main_predictor: log of average weekly working hours (wrkhrs)
sample_definition: 50 US states, 2007-2013 (N=350 state-years)
model_specification: OLS with two-way fixed effects (state and year dummies), Model 1 (Scale FE) specification from Table 3
controls: log employed population %, log GDP per hour, log total population, log manufacturing % of GDP, log energy production, log working-age population, state FE, year FE
operationalization_notes: Used compiled.dta which lacked household size and state environmentalism, so estimated Model 1 (Scale FE) from Table 3 with available scale controls plus state and year fixed effects on log-log data.
reasoning: Two-way (state and year) fixed-effects OLS of log CO2 emissions on log working hours with scale controls (employed pop %, GDP per hour, total pop, manufacturing %, energy production, working-age pop) yields a positive coefficient of 0.465 on log working hours (t=1.95, df=287, p=0.052, N=350), consistent with the paper's positive relationship between state-level carbon emissions and average working hours.

dependent_variable: considered attack on the target's nuclear program (consider, 0/1)
main_predictor: prior violent militarized conflict (hostileMID, 0/1; ongoing MID involving use of force in t-1)
sample_definition: Politically relevant dyad-years 1941-2000 (polrel==1) where the target had a nuclear program
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on the 2x2 contingency table of hostileMID by consider
operationalization_notes: The claim is most directly tested in the paper's Table 2A bivariate cross-tabulation of violent conflict against considered attacks; I replicated that χ² test on the politically-relevant sample.
reasoning: Among politically-relevant dyad-years, considered attacks on nuclear programs are much more common after prior violent MIDs (28/569 ≈ 4.9%) than after peace (13/5117 ≈ 0.25%); χ²(1,N=5686)=155.79, p<.0001, supporting H1 that prior violent militarized conflict raises the proliferation-threat salience.

dependent_variable: splinter: indicator that the county became part of a new (splinter) district in electoral wave t
main_predictor: DEC share ratio (county's share of seats on District Executive Committee divided by its population share) - measure of political marginalization (lower = more marginalized)
sample_definition: County-wave panel of Ugandan counties across electoral waves; observations with non-missing covariates (N=466)
model_specification: Logistic regression with region and electoral wave fixed effects (analogue to Model 4 in Table 3, which uses xtmelogit random-effects logit)
controls: Ethnic minority indicator, development summary index (MARG), number of counties in district, breakup lag, supported LC5 loser, opposed chair election, Museveni vote share lag and its square, log county population, ethnic fractionalization, region indicators, wave indicators
operationalization_notes: The paper's H1 is most directly tested by the coefficient on DEC share ratio in the Table 3 Model 4 specification; political marginalization is operationalized as 1/DEC_rep effectively, so a negative coefficient on DEC_rep supports the claim. Used standard logit rather than mixed-effects logit for tractability; coefficient magnitudes are close to the paper's reported -0.79.
reasoning: In a logit model of county secession (splinter) on DEC share ratio (political marginalization), ethnic minority, development index, and the paper's full set of controls (Model 4-equivalent), the coefficient on DEC share ratio is -0.72 with z = -3.68, p < 0.001. Higher political representation reduces the probability of secession, equivalently, more politically marginalized counties are more likely to secede - consistent with the paper's H1.

dependent_variable: recog1dum (whether State B diplomatically recognizes State A)
main_predictor: nukeduma (State A has nuclear weapons capability)
sample_definition: Directed dyad-years 1945-2000 with non-missing values on recognition and covariates (paper's Table 2, dichotomous model sample)
model_specification: Probit regression of recognition on nuclear status A, nuclear status B, their interaction, monadic and dyadic rivalry, CINC A, CINC B and interaction, democracy A/B and interaction, contiguity, ln distance, alliance
controls: Nuclear Weapons B, Nuke A×B, Rivalry A, Rivalry B, Dyadic Rivalry, CINC A, CINC B, CINC A×B, Democracy A, Democracy B, Dem A×B, contiguity, ln(distance), alliance
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 2 dichotomous specification; the most directly claim-relevant statistic is the z on Nuclear Weapons A in the recognition probit.
reasoning: Probit replicating Table 2 (dichotomous DV: State B recognizes State A) shows the coefficient on Nuclear Weapons A is positive and highly significant (b=0.502, z=28.53, p<0.001), so nuclear-capable states are significantly more likely to be recognized by others, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Logarithm of absolute change in pro-immigration index between wave 2 and wave 3 (change_w3w2_log)
main_predictor: Group-level mean justification rationality (DQ_jlev)
sample_definition: EuroPolis DP participants in 13 small discussion groups with complete data on outcome, predictor and controls (N=174)
model_specification: Multilevel linear regression (REML) with individuals nested in discussion groups (statsmodels MixedLM)
controls: gender, age, education, Catholic, Protestant, working class, religiosity, left-right ideology + squared, knowledge change, four 'clarify thinking' items (other participants, experts, politicians, briefing material), social conformity pressure above/below, left-party and right-party vote intention
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 2 Model 2b of Gerber et al., which is the analysis the abstract claim directly references; uses SANDERS_Replication.dta variables already constructed for this purpose.
reasoning: Multilevel REML model of log absolute immigration-attitude change (wave 2→3) on group-level justification rationality with Sanders' controls yields coef = 0.130 (SE 0.066), z = 1.96, p ≈ 0.049 with N = 174 individuals in 13 groups, matching the paper's Model 2b result that higher justification rationality predicts greater opinion change.

dependent_variable: Mean effort (work indicator) per matching group across all rounds
main_predictor: Reward scheme: symmetrical (444COM) vs discriminating (345COM)
sample_definition: All subject-round observations from the two complementarity treatments (444COM and 345COM), aggregated to matching-group means (6 matching groups per treatment)
model_specification: Two-sided Mann-Whitney (Wilcoxon rank-sum) U test on matching-group mean effort
operationalization_notes: The paper treats matching groups as the unit of independent observation and tests effort/efficiency differences with rank-sum tests; I followed that approach using the binary effort variable averaged over rounds within each matching group.
reasoning: Mean effort (work) per matching group is lower in 444COM (symmetrical, mean ~0.73) than in 345COM (discriminating, mean ~0.92). A two-sided Mann-Whitney U test on the 6 vs 6 matching-group means gives U=5, p=0.041, confirming that the symmetrical reward scheme under complementarity elicits substantially lower efforts than the cost-equivalent discriminating scheme.

dependent_variable: Within-senator difference in (anti-immigration policy actions mentioned) minus (pro-immigration policy actions mentioned) in the senator's letter response
main_predictor: Letter condition: anti-immigration constituent letter vs. pro-immigration constituent letter (within-subject)
sample_definition: Senators who responded to both the anti- and pro-immigration constituent letters (N=56)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing the (anti - pro) action-mention composite under the anti-letter vs. the pro-letter
operationalization_notes: This is the most direct test of senatorial tailoring in Experiment 1, mirroring the 'Anti - Pro' column of the paper's tailoring table, using the four indicator variables companti_anti, comppro_anti, companti_pro, comppro_pro.
reasoning: Paired t-test on the within-senator difference (anti-immigration actions minus pro-immigration actions mentioned) across the two letter conditions yields t(55)=3.45, p=0.0011. Senators mentioned anti-immigration actions more often (and pro-immigration actions less often) when responding to the anti-immigration letter than to the pro-immigration letter, supporting the claim that senators tailor explanations to their audiences.

dependent_variable: log(last U.S. wage adjusted) - log(last home wage adjusted)
main_predictor: Education category dummy 'no high school' (edyrs < 9), reference = college graduate (edyrs >= 16)
sample_definition: All MMP/LAMP (MP) immigrants in the provided wage_gain_table with positive pre- and post-migration adjusted wages (10 origin countries incl. Mexico). The NIS portion of the pooled Table III sample was not available in the data directory, so the analysis is restricted to the MP sample.
model_specification: OLS: gain ~ C(educ, ref=college) + C(country); five education categories (no HS, some HS, HS grad, some college, college).
operationalization_notes: Follows the paper's Table III specification (Section IV.A) -- pooled regression of log wage gain on education dummies with country FE and college as omitted category -- but restricted to MP data because the NIS micro-data are not present in the supplied dataset (the NIS folders contain only .DS_Store files).
reasoning: OLS regression of the log wage gain at migration on education category dummies (college graduates as the omitted reference) with country fixed effects yields a coefficient of 0.197 (SE=0.129, t=1.52) on the 'no high school' dummy. The sign is positive, indicating that immigrants without any high school exposure experience larger wage gains at migration than college graduates -- the same direction as reported in the paper -- though the effect is not statistically significant in this MP-only subsample (the paper's pooled NIS+MP analysis yields a larger, significant coefficient).

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses reflecting the learned (negative) meaning of the cue (FAbaseC vs FAsuppC, collapsed across homographic and non-homographic cue types)
main_predictor: Cue status (baseline vs. suppressed), within-subjects
sample_definition: Experiment 2 nonruminators only (Group==1; n=27); ruminators excluded.
model_specification: Mixed-design ANOVA with cue status (baseline, suppressed) as within-subjects factor, counterbalancing set (CB) as between-subjects factor, and subject as a random factor; F reported for the cue-status main effect.
controls: Counterbalancing factor (CB) included as a between-subjects factor to reduce error variance
operationalization_notes: The claim about nonruminators benefiting in the 'transfer tasks' is directly indexed by Experiment 2's free-association SIF contrast (baseline vs. suppressed) within the nonruminator subgroup. Operationalization follows the paper's described mixed-design ANOVA collapsing across homograph/non-homograph (which did not interact).
reasoning: Within nonruminators, the contrast of baseline vs. suppressed cue conditions on the percentage of learned-meaning responses in the free-association task yielded F(1,24)=10.94, p=.003, indicating fewer learned-meaning (negative) free-associations to suppressed than to baseline cues — i.e., suppression practice transferred to a benefit (SIF) for nonruminators.

dependent_variable: CES-D psychological well-being scale (higher = better)
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction of parental status (childless ref.) with country-level percentage who (strongly) disapprove of childlessness
sample_definition: ESS Round 3 respondents aged 41+ in 24 European countries with no missing data on model variables (n=23,313, 24 countries)
model_specification: Two-level linear mixed model with random intercepts by country; ML estimation
controls: Female, age, age^2, marital status (4 cat.), own education (4 cat.), parental education (5 cat. incl. missing), religious attendance, paid employment, born in country
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Model 2a specification but pooled men and women (adding female as covariate) to obtain a single test directly tied to the claim. Joint Wald chi2 across both parental-status × disapproval interaction terms is the most direct overall test of whether the childlessness disadvantage varies with country-level tolerance.
reasoning: Joint Wald test of the two cross-level interactions (parental status × country-level % disapproving of childlessness) in a multilevel model is significant (chi2(2)=16.40, p<.001). The 'lives with children × disapproval' coefficient is positive (b=0.024, z=2.53, p=.011), meaning parents' well-being advantage over the childless is larger where disapproval is stronger — equivalently, the childless disadvantage is smaller in countries with more tolerant norms, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Total DSM-5 psychopathology score (DSM5_Total)
main_predictor: Mini-K total score (slower life history strategy = higher)
sample_definition: All 138 participants with complete data on Mini-K and DSM-5 totals
model_specification: Bivariate Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: Most direct test of the claim: zero-order correlation between the primary LH measure (Mini-K) and the total psychopathology score. Negative correlation indicates faster LH strategies associate with more psychopathology.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between Mini-K (slow LH strategy score) and total DSM-5 psychopathology score is r = -.587, t(136) = -8.46, p < .001. Higher slow-LH scores predict fewer psychopathology symptoms — equivalently, faster life strategies are associated with greater psychopathology, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (political knowledge test score, 0-20)
main_predictor: Stereotypaktivierung condition (0 = not activated vs. 2 = activated by gender difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender=1) with Filter=1 (valid cases) in conditions 0 and 2
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test (pooled variance)
operationalization_notes: Claim compares female participants in condition 1 (not activated) vs condition 3 (activated by gender difference statement); used PolWis_score as the knowledge outcome.
reasoning: Among female participants (Filter=1), those in the stereotype-not-activated condition scored higher on the political knowledge test (M=8.87, SD=4.64, n=70) than those in the stereotype-activated-by-gender-difference-statement condition (M=7.03, SD=4.11, n=70); independent t-test t(138)=2.49, p=0.014.

dependent_variable: f2gdpidx (GDP growth index at t+2, prior year=100)
main_predictor: msec2currentsec (city party secretary has informal tie to incumbent provincial party secretary, 0/1)
sample_definition: City-year panel 1999-2014 with non-missing growth, connection indicator, and controls; 333 cities, 3840 obs after singleton drop
model_specification: Two-way fixed-effects OLS (city FE + province-year FE), standard errors clustered by city (pyfixest feols)
controls: loggdp, logpop, govsize (city economic); msec_tenure, mayor_tenure, msec_birthyear, mayor_birthyear, msec_localtime, msec_prov_exp, msec_central_exp, mayor_prov_exp, mayor_central_exp (leader)
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Table 1 column 3 specification (city + province-year FE, economic + leader controls, clustered by city). Education-year leader controls were excluded because they were missing for ~1250 observations and would have shrunk the sample well below the paper's 3693.
reasoning: Replicating Table 1 column 3 (Jiang 2018), regressing GDP growth index at t+2 on a binary indicator for the city party secretary being connected to the incumbent provincial party secretary, with city and province-year fixed effects plus economic and leader controls and city-clustered SEs, gives a coefficient of 0.181 (SE=0.139), t=1.30, p=0.19, N=3840. The point estimate is positive (consistent with the claim's direction) but not statistically significant, so the result is inconclusive at conventional thresholds.

dependent_variable: Share of top-quality players among all foreign players in the national first league (stop / (stop+slow)); top-quality defined as having played for one's national team)
main_predictor: Treat (Denmark = 1) x Post (year >= 1991) interaction
sample_definition: Country-year observations for 14 European countries, 1980-2008, restricted to country-years with at least one foreign player in the first league (so the share is defined); using the synthetic-control graph dataset (basesynthetic_control.dta).
model_specification: OLS DiD: share_top ~ treat*post + country FE + year FE, with HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors.
controls: Country fixed effects and year fixed effects
operationalization_notes: The claim is specifically about ability composition (the mix shifting toward higher-ability players), so the natural outcome is the share of top-quality players among foreigners rather than levels. I use the same top-quality definition the paper uses for its Denmark synthetic-control figure (Figure 3) and apply a standard DiD with all other 13 countries as controls (rather than the synthetic combination) because the synthetic control method is purely graphical and does not yield an inferential test statistic.
reasoning: Difference-in-differences on the share of top-quality players among foreigners (treatment = Denmark, post = year >= 1991), with country and year fixed effects and HC1-robust SEs, yields a treat*post coefficient of 0.461 (SE 0.066), t = 7.02 (df = 346), p < 0.001. The composition of foreign players in the Danish first league shifted strongly toward higher-ability players after the 1991/1992 preferential tax scheme, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay (composite WTP scale)
main_predictor: intrin_extrin (intrinsic minus extrinsic values composite)
sample_definition: All Study 1 participants with non-missing values on both variables
model_specification: Pearson product-moment correlation
operationalization_notes: The claim directly concerns the bivariate association between relative intrinsic/extrinsic value endorsement and WTP in Study 1, mirroring the paper's Study 1 zero-order correlation analysis.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between the intrinsic-minus-extrinsic value score (intrin_extrin) and willingness_to_pay was r = .426, t(153) = 5.83, p < .001, n = 155, indicating that higher endorsement of intrinsic relative to extrinsic values is associated with higher WTP to protect the environment.

dependent_variable: ln_imports (logged product-level imports from partner)
main_predictor: Complainant_{j,d} (dummy indicating partner is the complainant in dispute d)
sample_definition: Product-level trade flows in disputes that ended in early settlement (earlysettle==1), with non-missing covariates; disputes 1995-2011
model_specification: OLS regression with dispute-clustered standard errors (second-stage analog of the Heckman outcome equation reported in Model 8)
controls: Defendant GDP (log), Partner GDP (log), lagged disputed imports, Democratic Pair, Total Imports (log)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether complainants gain disproportionately from early settlement; the most direct test is the Complainant coefficient in the outcome equation of Model 8. Implemented as the second-stage OLS on the early-settled subsample rather than the full Heckman two-step (which is not implemented natively in statsmodels).
reasoning: On the subsample of early-settled disputes, OLS regression of ln(imports) on a complainant indicator with controls (defendant/partner GDP, lagged disputed imports, democratic pair, total imports) and dispute-clustered SE yields a positive coefficient on complainant of 0.183 (z=2.25, p=0.024), consistent with the paper's finding that complainants gain more imports than the rest of the membership under early settlement (Model 8: 0.469*).

dependent_variable: entre_wage (new business formation rate, country-year)
main_predictor: r (median age measure)
sample_definition: All country-year observations in GEM_Country_Year.dta (2001-2010, 82 countries)
model_specification: WLS with year fixed effects; standard errors clustered at country level
controls: Year fixed effects only (Table 2, column 1 baseline)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Table 2 column 1 baseline specification.
