model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of complaints_2008 on an intercept and first_A, equivalent to a pooled two-sample t-test of mean complaints by name type.
operationalization_notes: The paper's focal descriptive claim and Table 2 compare average BBB complaints for Illinois plumbing firms by whether the firm has an A/number-starting name, so I used the corresponding firm-level dataset and direct difference in means.
reasoning: In an OLS difference-in-means regression, firms whose name begins with A/a number had higher complaint counts than other firms (means 1.339 vs. 0.248 complaints). The difference of 1.091 complaints was statistically significant, t(2291)=6.788, p=1.44e-11, supporting the claim that A/number-name firms receive more service complaints.

dependent_variable: Cooperative bargaining strategy (ordinal dv coded 0-3, with higher values indicating more cooperative behavior/concessions)
main_predictor: Issue-linkage structure
sample_definition: All 588 state-by-negotiation-phase observations in the original dataset; no observations excluded.
model_specification: Partial proportional-odds/generalized ordered logit model for dv, with the issue-linkage coefficient constrained equal across the three cumulative logits and standard errors clustered by negotiation phase.
controls: ln GDP, security/foreign and defense policy, Euro state, new member state, agreement importance, parliamentary scrutiny, majority voting, publicity, presidency, and lagged dependent variable.
operationalization_notes: I followed the paper's primary Model 1 specification because the claim corresponds directly to Hypothesis S1 and the paper argues that generalized ordered logit is appropriate for the four-category cooperative strategy outcome.
reasoning: In a generalized ordered logit model of cooperative bargaining strategy, the issue-linkage structure coefficient was positive (b = 1.2193) and highly statistically significant using cluster-robust standard errors by negotiation phase (z = 6.35, p = 2.22e-10). This supports the claim that negotiations with more differently valued linked issues are associated with more cooperative/concessionary bargaining behavior.

dependent_variable: Credit to Government and State-Owned Enterprises (% of GDP; credittogovtstateenterp)
main_predictor: Lagged state capacity, IQG index (icrg_qog; higher values indicate stronger states)
sample_definition: Country-year panel observations from the original Country Year Dataset in 1984-2011 with nonmissing directed credit, one-period lagged directed credit, lagged IQG, and lagged private credit; 129 countries contributed 2,630 level-equation country-years.
model_specification: Two-step dynamic system GMM: current directed credit regressed on lagged directed credit, lagged IQG, lagged private credit, a linear time trend, and a constant; endogenous dynamic regressors were instrumented using collapsed lagged levels in the differenced equation and lagged first differences in the levels equation.
controls: Lagged dependent variable, lagged Private Credit (% GDP), and a linear time trend.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies Credit to Government and SOEs as the directed-credit outcome, IQG as the state-capacity measure, and Private Credit as the control for profit potential from financial repression; I therefore followed the paper's dynamic panel specification most directly tied to the claim.
reasoning: In a two-step dynamic system-GMM model, the coefficient on lagged state capacity (IQG) was negative (beta = -10.896) with z = -12.450, p = 1.40e-35. Because higher IQG means stronger state capacity, this negative coefficient implies that weaker states direct more credit to the government and SOEs after controlling for private credit.

dependent_variable: MID initiation as originator (originit)
main_predictor: Predicted coup risk from a first-stage model of logged coup events (lcoupsum)
sample_definition: All Latin America country-years in the provided dataset with complete data for the variables used, 1961-1999 (22 countries; N = 798).
model_specification: First-stage OLS predicting logged coup events from coup-risk instruments and covariates; second-stage probit model of MID initiation on predicted coup risk and controls, with standard errors clustered by country.
controls: Previous force/MID involvement ending in prior year (lagforceend), ethnic fractionalization, relative power (CINC), number of borders, logged number of allies, regional conflict, lagged Polity, and lagged logged real GDP. First-stage excluded predictors included previous coup, recent war, and conflict ending (forceend), along with coup-equation covariates.
operationalization_notes: The paper's primary test models conflict initiation as a monadic country-year outcome and uses coup risk as the diversionary-threat measure. I followed that structure by generating a coup-risk regressor from the coup-events equation and testing its coefficient in the conflict-initiation probit.
reasoning: In a two-stage endogenous-regressor probit, the estimated effect of predicted coup risk on MID initiation was positive (coefficient = 2.796) and statistically significant using country-clustered standard errors (z = 2.793, p = 0.0052, N = 798). Thus, greater threats to political survival, operationalized as coup risk, are associated with a higher likelihood of conflict initiation.

dependent_variable: d12outgroup: amount sent to an out-group (Albanian) recipient in the dictator game, censored at 0 and 5 euros
main_predictor: Ordinal out-group exposure/proximity score coded 0 = Primarily Serb region, 1 = Border region, 2 = Primarily Albanian region
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb participants in the replication dataset; all had complete data on the dictator-game outcome, proximity measure, and selected controls
model_specification: Maximum-likelihood Tobit censored regression with lower censoring at 0 euros and upper censoring at 5 euros; the reported statistic is the Wald z test for the ordinal exposure coefficient using the model-based standard error
controls: female, age, education, employed, village, alphaviolence, alphadamaged, displaced
operationalization_notes: The paper operationalizes contact as region in order of decreasing proximity to Albanians and uses Tobit models for dictator giving. I used the out-group giving outcome for H1 and replaced the two regional indicators with a single ordered exposure score to obtain one direct trend test of the directional claim while retaining the paper's extended controls.
reasoning: A Tobit regression of out-group dictator giving on an ordinal proximity/exposure score estimated a positive exposure coefficient of 1.016 euros per step toward greater Albanian exposure. This effect was statistically significant, z = 3.181, p = 0.00147, supporting the claim that out-group bridging altruism increases with exposure to the out-group.

dependent_variable: Relative preference/enjoyment rating comparing the first animated clip with the target sword-fight clip (enjoyrelativ, 1-7 scale)
main_predictor: Commercial interruption condition (interrupted by a 30-second Bell South Yellow Pages commercial vs. uninterrupted)
sample_definition: Study 2 participants with condition coded 'good' or 'no' and non-missing enjoyrelativ; excluded trailing spreadsheet rows containing no participant data.
model_specification: Two-sample independent t test comparing mean enjoyrelativ between interrupted and uninterrupted conditions, using pooled variance.
operationalization_notes: The quoted claim appears in the Study 2 Results; the paper identifies the relative preference/enjoyment rating as the direct measure for whether the commercial disruption made the target program more enjoyable.
reasoning: In Study 2 experiencers, mean relative preference/enjoyment was higher in the commercial-interruption condition (M = 5.38, n = 53) than in the uninterrupted condition (M = 4.47, n = 49). An independent-samples t test gave t(100) = 2.45, p = 0.016, supporting the claim that commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable.

dependent_variable: Recoded likelihood that Don Swensen was resigning because he was under investigation for bribery, with higher values indicating greater likelihood/acceptance of the innuendo (5 - GSU211).
main_predictor: Contrast between causal correction condition and denial-only condition among innuendo-exposed respondents.
sample_definition: Respondents assigned to the innuendo, denial, or causal-correction conditions with nonmissing responses to GSU211; control-condition respondents were excluded because they were not asked this outcome.
model_specification: Inverse-probability-weighted OLS regression of recoded investigation-rumor likelihood on indicators for denial and causal correction, using the innuendo-only group as the reference category; the reported t-test is the linear contrast causal correction minus denial.
controls: None; only treatment indicators and an intercept were included, with inverse probability weights for block-randomized assignment probabilities.
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns acceptance of the specific causal innuendo about why the politician resigned, so I used the outcome directly asking whether he resigned because he was under investigation and compared the causal-correction treatment to the evidence-backed denial treatment, following the paper's Model 5/IPW approach.
reasoning: In an inverse-probability-weighted OLS model among respondents exposed to the innuendo, the causal-correction condition produced lower acceptance of the rumor than the denial-only condition (contrast = -0.335 on the 1-4 likelihood scale), t(761) = -5.065, p = 5.12e-7. This indicates that the alternate causal explanation was more effective than the denial with evidentiary support at limiting the misperception.

dependent_variable: Aggregated intimacy score computed as the mean of r1, reverse-coded r4, r6, and r7 on the 7-point scale
main_predictor: Attention condition (cnd = 1 attention/80% blue signal vs cnd = 2 no attention/0% blue signal)
sample_definition: Study 2a observations in Sheet3 with valid condition and intimacy-item data, excluding ID 20 as the apparent participant excluded for suspicion of deception under the paper's stated method; final N = 29.
model_specification: Independent-samples Student t-test comparing mean intimacy between attention and no-attention conditions, equivalent to a two-group OLS model with no covariates.
operationalization_notes: This directly follows Study 2a, which manipulated whether the partner monitored the participant and assessed the post-task four-item intimacy score; sex was not controlled because the paper reports no sex effects and omits sex from the analysis.
reasoning: In the Study 2a data, intimacy was higher in the attention condition (M = 4.58, SD = 0.82, n = 15) than in the no-attention condition (M = 2.82, SD = 0.79, n = 14), t(27) = 5.91, p = 2.69e-6. This supports the claim that receiving attention from the partner increased participants' intimacy with that partner.

dependent_variable: Binary indicator q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2: interested in learning more about how the district government spends money in the budget (willing to monitor the budget)
main_predictor: Assigned tax revenue treatment (taxgrp=1) versus windfall treatment (taxgrp=0)
sample_definition: All 1,863 campaign participants in the original dataset; no observations excluded because q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2 and taxgrp were nonmissing for all cases.
model_specification: Difference in means / Welch two-sample t-test for the binary monitoring outcome comparing tax and windfall groups, equivalent to an unadjusted linear probability model with Neyman heteroskedastic standard error.
operationalization_notes: The paper's main H1 monitoring result defines monitoring as interest in learning more about how the district government spends budget money, and estimates the average tax-versus-windfall treatment effect by difference in mean outcomes across assigned revenue groups.
reasoning: Using all assigned participants with nonmissing monitoring outcome (N=1863), the tax group was more willing to monitor the budget (0.811) than the windfall group (0.760), a difference of 0.051. A Welch/Neyman two-sample test gives t=2.70, df=1847.31, p=0.007, supporting the claim that tax treatment increased monitoring.

dependent_variable: turnout (1 = voted, 0 = did not vote)
main_predictor: z1elite_avgprox (social proximity to elites, z-score)
sample_definition: All eligible voters in the Alexandria dataset with complete data for the model variables (N = 2216).
model_specification: Maximum-likelihood logistic regression of turnout on social proximity to elites and covariates; the reported statistic is the Wald z test for the social-proximity coefficient.
controls: Household wealth, log household wealth, mid-status occupation, high-status occupation, home ownership, age, log age, church membership, U.S.-born indicator, and network centrality (z1ev).
operationalization_notes: I used the paper-guided turnout specification for the nineteenth-century Alexandria election, focusing on the model that adds elite social proximity while adjusting for resource, demographic, religious, and general network-centrality covariates.
reasoning: In a logistic regression among eligible Alexandria voters, the coefficient for social proximity to elites was positive (b = 0.5566, SE = 0.1253), yielding z = 4.44, p = 8.85e-06. Thus, higher social proximity to elites is associated with a higher probability of turnout, consistent with the study's claim.

dependent_variable: Utilitarian response, coded as decision = 1 for push and 0 for no push
main_predictor: Mood condition, positive versus negative
sample_definition: Participants from Experiment 1 assigned to the active decision frame only; all 200 active-frame observations were included
model_specification: One-sided two-sample z-test for equality of proportions comparing the proportion of push decisions in positive versus negative mood conditions
operationalization_notes: The paper defines utilitarian responding as deciding to push and the target claim specifically concerns the active-frame condition, so I restricted to active-frame participants and compared push rates by mood without covariates, consistent with the reported analysis omitting autobiographical-memory condition.
reasoning: Within the active-frame condition, 28/100 participants in the positive-mood group chose the utilitarian option (push) compared with 9/100 in the negative-mood group. A one-sided two-sample test of proportions for positive > negative gave z = 3.46, p = 0.00027, supporting the claim that utilitarian responding was more likely in positive moods.

dependent_variable: TVA-estimated visual processing speed (v)
main_predictor: alerting condition: 85 dB auditory cue versus no cue
sample_definition: Experiment 1 final sample; all 28 participants with paired v_NoCue and v_85dBCue estimates included
model_specification: paired-samples t-test on within-participant differences in visual processing speed (v_85dBCue - v_NoCue)
operationalization_notes: The claim is directly tested in Experiment 1, where visual processing speed was estimated separately for each participant under no-cue and 85 dB phasic auditory alerting conditions; the within-subject comparison isolates the alerting effect on the TVA speed parameter.
reasoning: Using Experiment 1 participants' TVA-estimated visual processing speed, the 85 dB alerting-cue condition had higher processing speed than the no-cue condition (mean difference = 25.79 letters/s). A paired-samples t-test gave t(27) = 4.71, p = 0.000067, supporting the claim that phasic auditory alerting increases visual processing speed.

dependent_variable: Log mean value of owner-occupied housing units on the census block (lnavval)
main_predictor: Interaction of court-ordered desegregation-plan border, central-city/larger side of border, and 1980 indicator (yesbig1980)
sample_definition: Populated census blocks with nonmissing housing value and positive owner-occupied-unit weights, tierno < 2, adjacent to 80 non-Southern city-suburban school-district borders observed in 1970 and 1980 after the paper's sample exclusions; N = 4,352 block-year observations.
model_specification: Weighted least squares difference-in-differences regression of log housing value on PLAN x CITY x 1980 and CITY x 1980, with side-of-border fixed effects and border-by-year fixed effects; analytic weights are owner-occupied housing units; standard errors clustered by school-district jurisdiction.
controls: Side-of-border fixed effects, border-by-census-year fixed effects, and a common city-side-by-1980 trend; no additional block covariates.
operationalization_notes: I used the paper's main border-based housing-value specification because it is the analysis most directly tied to the claim that desegregation reduced central-city housing prices relative to neighboring suburbs.
reasoning: In a weighted difference-in-differences border specification, the coefficient on desegregation-plan city side in 1980 was -0.0595 log points with a cluster-robust SE of 0.0278, giving t(117) = -2.14, p = 0.0345. This indicates that housing values on treated central-city sides declined by about 6% relative to neighboring suburbs and relative to control borders.

dependent_variable: fraud_ordered: three-category ordered assessment of whether the December 2011 Duma election was free and fair, somewhat free and fair, or not free and fair, with higher values indicating more perceived fraud
main_predictor: opp_do_know: indicator for opposition voters who correctly identified Golos, compared with opposition voters who did not know Golos as the reference category
sample_definition: Respondents with non-missing fraud_ordered outcome and non-missing covariates; non-substantive fraud responses were excluded by construction of fraud_ordered, yielding N = 1728
model_specification: Proportional-odds ordered logistic regression on the full analytic sample, using indicators for voter-orientation-by-Golos-knowledge groups and omitting opposition voters who did not know Golos as the reference; the reported z test is for the opp_do_know coefficient
controls: female, age, Moscow residence, private-sector employment, wealth, education, family economic change over last year, political news interest, state-TV political news use, VKontakte, Odnoklasniki, Facebook, LiveJournal, and survey round
operationalization_notes: The paper tests this claim with ordered-logit models of Duma fraud perceptions and saturated demographic/media controls; I followed that approach and used the group-specific Golos knowledge dummy to estimate the within-opposition contrast directly.
reasoning: In an ordered-logit model of Duma election fraud perceptions, opposition voters who correctly identified Golos were significantly more likely to give a more fraud-skeptical response than opposition voters who did not know Golos (coefficient = 0.613, z = 2.526, p = 0.0115; OR = 1.85). This supports the claim that among regime opponents, familiarity with Golos is associated with stronger perceptions that the election was fraudulent.

dependent_variable: Party support for ethnic minority rights (eth_supp)
main_predictor: Economic left-right party position (lrecon), evaluated in countries with a federal-center-origin minority (comm_dom_min = 1)
sample_definition: All 195 party observations in Party_dataset.dta from the 14 East European countries with nonmissing eth_supp, lrecon, comm_dom_min, and control variables.
model_specification: OLS regression of eth_supp on lrecon, comm_dom_min, and their interaction; reported test is the linear contrast lrecon + lrecon:comm_dom_min = 0, with standard errors clustered by country.
controls: Communist regime type (categorical comm), year first rated free by Freedom House (free), GDP per capita PPP constant 2005 international dollars, and electoral district magnitude (m_dist).
operationalization_notes: The supplied data file is the CHES party-level dataset rather than the individual survey dataset used for the paper's Table 1. I therefore operationalized the claim through the paper's party-level mechanism: if federal-center minorities are associated with the left, then in countries with such minorities, more right-wing economic placement should predict lower support for ethnic minority rights.
reasoning: In a party-level OLS model with country-clustered standard errors, the marginal slope of economic left-right position in countries where the salient minority originated from the federal center was negative: b = -0.578 for ethnic-minority support per one-unit rightward shift, t(13) = -2.27, p = 0.041. Thus, in these countries, parties more supportive of federal-center minorities were significantly more economically left-leaning, consistent with the study's claim.

dependent_variable: Number of actions identified while watching the video as instances in which the actor made a choice (numactions)
main_predictor: Cultural context/group (U.S. vs. Indian participants)
sample_definition: Study 3 participants in the construal-of-choice condition with non-missing numactions; 30 U.S. and 34 Indian participants were included.
model_specification: Independent-samples two-tailed t-test comparing mean numactions between U.S. and Indian participants in the choice condition, equivalent to a one-predictor OLS model with culture as the grouping variable.
operationalization_notes: The paper states that Study 3 specifically tested cultural differences in construing other individuals' behaviors as choices using the video task. I therefore analyzed the choice-construal condition directly rather than the control condition, using the participant-level count of identified choices as the outcome.
reasoning: In Study 3's construal-of-choice condition, U.S. participants identified more of the actor's actions as choices (M = 38.33, n = 30) than Indian participants (M = 22.68, n = 34), t(62) = 3.11, p = .0029. This supports the claim that people in U.S. American contexts are more likely than those in Indian contexts to construe other individuals' behaviors as choices.

dependent_variable: Willingness to self-censor (reverse-coded willingness to disclose) ratings for the four information-recipient items
main_predictor: Ordered information-recipient distance/publicity category (close relations, in-group superiors, in-group NGOs, out-group NGOs)
sample_definition: All 71 Study 1 Israeli-Jewish participants with complete WSC recipient ratings and political-orientation data
model_specification: For each participant, I estimated a within-person linear trend slope of WSC on recipient order coded 1 to 4; I then tested the adjusted mean slope with an OLS regression of slopes on centered political orientation, using the intercept t-test as the main test.
controls: Centered self-reported political orientation (1 = extreme right to 5 = extreme left)
operationalization_notes: The paper describes Study 1 as a within-subject comparison of four recipient types, controlling for political orientation. Because the claim is directional (greater recipient distance/publicity leads to higher WSC), the single primary test was specified as the linear within-subject trend across the same four ordered recipient categories.
reasoning: Using Study 1 participants, WSC increased reliably across the ordered recipient categories (close relations, superiors, Israeli NGO, international NGO). The adjusted mean within-person linear slope was positive (0.628 WSC scale points per recipient step), t(69) = 9.43, p = 4.96e-14, supporting the claim that greater perceived distance/publicity of recipients is associated with higher WSC.

dependent_variable: log(total output across periods 1-8 + 1)
main_predictor: T_Continuous wage profile dummy, with Baseline constant wage as the omitted reference category
sample_definition: Agents in the main experiment only; one subject-level observation per agent after summing output across all 8 work periods; Baseline, T_Sudden, T_Successive, and T_Continuous profiles included (N=211).
model_specification: OLS regression of subject-level log(total output + 1) on treatment-profile dummies and trial-task ability, using HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors; the reported t-test is for the T_Continuous coefficient versus Baseline.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's overall treatment-effect analysis for the claim that the continuously increasing wage profile raises performance relative to the constant-wage Baseline while all wage profiles pay the same total wage sum.
reasoning: In the main-experiment subject-level regression, the T_Continuous coefficient for log(total output + 1) was 0.1484 with HC1 robust SE 0.0696, t(206)=2.13, p=0.034. This indicates significantly higher overall performance under continuously increasing wages than under the constant-wage baseline, controlling for trial-task ability.

dependent_variable: Perceived size of eaten food portion (Q27.0: 'How big was the food portion?', 1 = very small, 9 = very big)
main_predictor: Observation condition (camera/observed vs. no-camera control)
sample_definition: All 82 Study 1 participants with non-missing condition and portion-size rating; camera condition n = 39, no-camera condition n = 43.
model_specification: Two-sample independent-groups t-test comparing mean perceived portion size between observed and control conditions, using pooled variance.
operationalization_notes: The paper's Study 1 methods identify perceived portion size after eating as the critical dependent measure and the camera manipulation as the observed-versus-control factor; the direct test of the claim is therefore a between-condition comparison on this item.
reasoning: An independent-samples t-test showed that participants in the camera/observed condition rated the eaten portion as larger than participants in the no-camera control condition, t(80) = 2.204, p = 0.030. The observed group mean was 4.85 versus 4.00 in the control group, supporting the claim that being observed magnified recalled portion size.

dependent_variable: Percentage of women in the legislature (npctwomenlegsal)
main_predictor: All = 0 dummy (avg_pv_0), equal to 1 when ballot = 0, pool = 0, and vote = 0, indicating the most party-centered/weak personal-vote-incentive systems
sample_definition: Election-year observations from the paper's analysis sample: countries marked as included in the paper, nonmissing election rank and complete variables for the model, excluding Georgia and Morocco to match the 57-country appendix; N = 232 observations across 57 countries.
model_specification: Gaussian panel GEE/Prais-Winsten-style model with country panels, election rank as time, AR(1) working correlation, and robust standard errors; z test of the all-zero party-centered-system coefficient.
controls: Log district magnitude, left-party vote, years since women's suffrage, legislative seats, log GDP per capita, female labor force participation percentage, and government spending as percentage of GDP.
operationalization_notes: The paper operationalizes the broad party-centered versus candidate-centered claim most directly with the all = 0 indicator for systems with party control of ballot formation, party-level vote pooling, and party voting; I used the full-sample specification corresponding to that hypothesis with the paper's standard controls.
reasoning: In a 232-observation, 57-country panel model, the coefficient for the all-zero personal-vote dummy was positive (b = 4.82 percentage points) and statistically significant, z = 2.25, p = 0.024. This supports the claim that the most party-centered systems are associated with higher women's legislative representation than more candidate-centered systems, conditional on the controls.

dependent_variable: First year in which a country extended overseas voting rights to expatriate citizens
main_predictor: Indicator that at least one of the country’s six nearest centroid-based neighbors implemented overseas voting in the prior two years (k6delta)
sample_definition: Country-year survival-risk observations with complete data for the baseline covariates, excluding countries that later revoked overseas voting rights; 5,988 country-years from 176 countries with 105 failures.
model_specification: Cox proportional hazards model for annual country-year data using start-stop intervals, Breslow handling of ties, and robust standard errors clustered by country.
controls: Election year, referendum year, British empire, French empire, Spanish empire, English legal heritage, log GDP per capita, log population, and log years since regime change.
operationalization_notes: I used the paper’s baseline specification corresponding to the main diffusion test: an event-history model of first overseas-voting enactment, with the spatial lag defined by recent enactments among the six nearest geographic neighbors.
reasoning: In a Cox proportional hazards model, the coefficient for a recent franchise extension among a country’s six nearest neighbors was positive and statistically significant (z = 2.99, p = 0.0028), corresponding to a hazard ratio of about 1.87. This supports the claim that countries were more likely to enfranchise expatriate citizens shortly after nearby countries did so.

dependent_variable: logincom_male (log real annual earnings)
main_predictor: post_fILdie_male (indicator for years after the father-in-law's death)
sample_definition: SLCC person-year observations for urban married men aged 22 to 45 with non-missing log earnings, father-in-law death indicator, age variables, high-school education, province, year, years married, and individual ID.
model_specification: OLS panel regression of log real annual earnings on the post-father-in-law-death indicator with individual fixed effects and province-by-year fixed effects; cluster-robust standard errors by individual. The reported t statistic tests the coefficient on post_fILdie_male.
controls: Cubic in age, years married, high-school education indicator, individual fixed effects, and province-year fixed effects; no health control because SLCC lacks retrospective health measures.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's main equation for the SLCC data, where the claim's 7 percent earnings decrease is operationalized as the within-man change in log annual earnings after the father-in-law dies.
reasoning: In my SLCC fixed-effects regression, the post-father-in-law-death coefficient was negative (about -0.063 log points), but the cluster-robust test was not statistically distinguishable from zero: t(2679) = -1.171, p = 0.242. Thus, this operationalization points in the same negative direction as the claim but is statistically inconclusive.

dependent_variable: Progressive vote on the first vote on the Blessed Virgin Mary (IFRSTBV0)
main_predictor: Protestant field structuration among incumbent RCC organizational fields (NSTRUCTU + NSTRUCTU × NINCUMBE)
sample_definition: Bishops with nonmissing Mary vote and nonmissing covariates in the paper's full Model 4 specification; N = 1,921 individual bishops clustered by country of service.
model_specification: Binary logistic regression with country-clustered robust standard errors; reported statistic is a Wald z test for the linear combination NSTRUCTU + NSTRUCTU×NINCUMBE.
controls: Percent Catholic, religious freedom indicator, other-established-religion indicator, percent Catholic × religious freedom, percent Catholic × other-established-religion, RCC incumbency, change in percent Catholic, field structuration, incumbency × structuration, stability × incumbency, stability × structuration, stability × religious freedom, stability × other-established-religion.
operationalization_notes: The paper states that legitimacy concerns were especially central in the Mary vote, and its methods operationalize NIT with field structuration, stability, and RCC incumbency. I therefore tested the NIT claim using the full published logistic specification for the Mary vote and focused on the direct NIT contrast of structuration within incumbent fields.
reasoning: I fit the paper's full binary logistic model for the first Mary vote with country-clustered robust standard errors. Among incumbent RCC fields, being in a Protestant-structurated field increased the log-odds of a progressive vote by 2.068 (OR = 7.91), z = 6.997, p = 2.61e-12, supporting the claim that NIT-derived characteristics of the social environment predict bishops' legitimacy-oriented voting.

dependent_variable: Negative of PopDIFF_MaxCov_T1: the population shortfall from the ArcGIS maximum-coverage benchmark for new primary school locations in 2002-09, coded so higher values mean closer-to-optimal/broader coverage
main_predictor: Congruence_20km_CRavg_T1 (local-government average institutional congruence with a precolonial state, 20 km buffer, 2002 boundaries)
sample_definition: Local-government-level LocAllocT1 observations with nonmissing maximum-coverage outcome, institutional congruence, region cluster, local-need controls, and geographic controls; 283 rural communities in the 2002-09 primary-school location-allocation sample
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression with standard errors clustered by 2002 region; main test is the coefficient t-test for institutional congruence
controls: CR_PopDensity_T1, PercVillages_Schools_CR02, N_New_Schools_CR_T1, Perc_CR_Mouride_T1, LnPop2011_CR02, Avg_lnD_waterway, Avg_Elevation, and Ferlo_Zone
operationalization_notes: The claim specifically concerns broader spatial distribution, so I used the paper's location-allocation maximum-coverage analysis rather than the village-level access logit. I selected the full primary-school 2002-09 coverage specification with both local-need and geographic controls, matching the methods described for Table 2 but computing the statistic directly from the provided LocAllocT1 data.
reasoning: In an OLS location-allocation model for 2002-09 primary-school placement, institutional congruence has a positive coefficient of 596.81 on the coverage-efficiency outcome, with cluster-robust SE = 106.37, t = 5.61 using 10 cluster degrees of freedom (p = 0.00022). This indicates that local governments in areas more congruent with precolonial states placed schools so as to cover substantially more population, consistent with broader spatial distribution of public goods.

dependent_variable: Incumbent party share of the two-party presidential vote (IncVote)
main_predictor: Mood-based policy misrepresentation: absolute cumulative difference between enacted net liberal laws and the number predicted from Stimson's Policy Mood (AbsCumLiberalPoliciesMood)
sample_definition: U.S. presidential election-year observations from 1952 through 2012, using Cycle == 16 rows with nonmissing vote, income growth, and mood-based policy misrepresentation variables (N = 16).
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression: IncVote = intercept + CumRPCDI + AbsCumLiberalPoliciesMood; the reported t-test is for the policy misrepresentation coefficient.
