This effect was statistically significant using a robust OLS t-test, t(58) = -2.22, p = 0.030, supporting the claim that single women reported lower desired salaries when their preferences were expected to be visible to classmates.

dependent_variable: WTP_dummy: indicator that the parent prefers a R$120 conditional cash transfer to a strictly larger unconditional transfer (willing to pay to keep conditionality)
main_predictor: Text-message treatment versus baseline treatment
sample_definition: Parents assigned to the baseline treatment (treatment==1) or text-message treatment (treatment==2) with nonmissing WTP_dummy; nonclassroom and don't-tell treatments excluded
model_specification: Two-sample z test for equality of proportions, coded as text-message proportion minus baseline proportion using the pooled null standard error
operationalization_notes: The claim directly concerns the proportion of parents willing to pay to keep conditionality in the text-message treatment compared with the baseline treatment, so I used the paper's binary willingness-to-pay outcome and compared those two randomized groups directly.
reasoning: In the original data, 49 of 60 baseline parents (81.7%) were willing to pay to keep the conditionality, compared with 10 of 51 parents (19.6%) in the text-message treatment. A two-sample test of proportions gives z = -6.53, p = 6.59e-11, indicating a large and statistically significant drop under text-message monitoring.

dependent_variable: Monthly homicides of males aged 15-39 (SINAIS), used as the paper's proxy for DTO-related violence
main_predictor: Indicator for 1-6 months after a drug cartel leader capture or killing in the municipality (lpub_after06)
sample_definition: Municipality-month observations from December 2006 through December 2010 in municipalities where a leader was captured/killed, excluding Ciudad Juárez as in the paper; N = 637 observations across 13 municipalities.
model_specification: Negative binomial regression with municipality fixed effects and month fixed effects; inference based on robust standard errors clustered by municipality.
controls: Population of males aged 15-39; indicators for 7-12 months and >12 months after leader capture; indicators for 1-6, 7-12, and >12 months after lieutenant capture; municipality and month fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: I used the paper's treated-municipality specification for leadership removals and its stated SINAIS proxy for DTO-related violence, focusing on the first six post-capture months because the claim concerns short-term exacerbating effects.
reasoning: In a negative binomial model for monthly homicides of males ages 15-39, the coefficient for the first 1-6 months after a leader capture/kill was positive (b = 0.272), corresponding to about a 31.2% increase in the expected count. The cluster-robust z statistic was 2.15 (p = 0.032), supporting a short-term exacerbating effect on the study's proxy for DTO-related violence.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of bootstrapped partial semantic networks
main_predictor: High versus low openness-to-experience group based on the no-intellect openness latent score median split
sample_definition: All 516 participants in the cleaned data, split into low (n=258) and high (n=258) openness groups; network nodes were animal responses generated by at least two participants in each group (167 eligible nodes), with 84 nodes sampled without replacement in each of 1000 bootstrap realizations per group.
model_specification: Two-sample t-test comparing ASPL values from 1000 high-openness versus 1000 low-openness 50%-node bootstrapped partial semantic networks; networks were constructed from binary animal-fluency response matrices using cosine similarity and a greedy triangulated maximally filtered graph, then binarized before computing ASPL.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies lower ASPL as the network measure corresponding to greater interconnectivity and uses a partial bootstrapped network comparison to statistically test group differences, so I used the 50% node bootstrap ASPL comparison as the single direct test of the claim.
reasoning: Using 1000 bootstrapped 50%-node partial semantic networks per openness group, the high-openness networks had lower average shortest path length than the low-openness networks (M_high = 2.503, M_low = 2.641), t(1998) = -18.253, p = 5.76e-69. Lower ASPL indicates greater interconnectivity, so this supports the claim that the high-openness group's semantic network was more interconnected.

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Rights Index
main_predictor: Reliance on Taxes: tax and social security contributions as a percentage of total government revenue
sample_definition: Country-year observations from 1981-2007 with complete data on the dependent variable, lagged dependent variable, fiscal variables, and baseline controls; observations with tax-reliance values above 100% were excluded as outside the valid percentage range, leaving N = 1718.
model_specification: Ordered probit regression with robust (HC0) standard errors; reported statistic is the Wald z test for the Reliance on Taxes coefficient.
controls: Size of Government Revenues, log population, income per capita, Polity IV democracy, external conflict, internal armed conflict, UK colony, and lagged CIRI Physical Integrity Rights Index.
operationalization_notes: I used the paper's main time-series cross-sectional specification for physical integrity rights with baseline controls and a lagged dependent variable, because this is the model most directly tied to the broad claim about reliance on taxes and human rights protection.
reasoning: In an ordered probit model of the CIRI Physical Integrity Rights Index, the coefficient on Reliance on Taxes was positive (b = 0.00616) with a robust Wald z = 2.805 (p = 0.0050). This supports the claim that greater reliance on taxation is associated with better protection of physical integrity rights in the original data.

dependent_variable: Percentage of pupils achieving five or more GCSE grades A-C (pt_gcse_5_a_c)
main_predictor: GM school status (gm_school), instrumented by winning the first GM ballot (gm_win)
sample_definition: Main GM school sample observations with non-missing GCSE pass rate and covariates, restricted to school-years 2 through 8 years after each school's base/vote year; 4,954 school-year observations from 726 schools.
model_specification: Pooled 2SLS regression discontinuity model with school-clustered robust standard errors; linear vote-share running-variable terms allowed to differ on either side of the 50% threshold (lose_vote and win_vote), and year-relative-to-base fixed effects.
controls: Base-year GCSE pass rate, school type indicators, GM ballot year-term indicators, relative-year indicators, and linear running-variable terms on each side of the cutoff.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's primary achievement analysis in Table 1, panel B, using the pooled post-vote achievement window and estimating the treatment effect of actual GM conversion via the GM ballot win discontinuity.
reasoning: In a pooled regression-discontinuity IV model for base years +2 through +8, the estimated effect of GM conversion on the GCSE pass-rate outcome was positive (about 4.48 percentage points) with a cluster-robust z statistic of 3.10 (p = 0.002). This supports the claim that schools converting to GM status experienced improved student achievement.

dependent_variable: Participated (lab): indicator for whether the student participated in the laboratory experiment
main_predictor: Sent_Class: amount sent as Player A in the classroom trust game ($0, $10, or $20)
sample_definition: Students in the trust-game classroom treatments with a non-missing amount-sent decision (N = 658).
model_specification: Probit regression of lab participation on amount sent and covariates, with standard errors clustered by tutor.
controls: Female, Commerce major, International student, day-of-week fixed effects, order indicator for flyer administered after trust game, and chosen-for-payment indicator.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Table 3 amount-sent specification for the claim that lower sending in the classroom trust game predicted subsequent laboratory participation.
reasoning: In a probit model predicting laboratory participation, the coefficient for amount sent in the classroom trust game was negative and statistically significant (z = -2.664, p = 0.0077, N = 658). Thus, students who sent more were less likely to participate, equivalently those who sent less were more likely to participate.

dependent_variable: Indicator that the first illness episode was treated with an ACT (took_act)
main_predictor: Assignment to the 92% ACT subsidy arm (act40: adult-dose ACT price 40 Ksh), compared with the no-ACT-subsidy control arm
sample_definition: First illness episode with malaria-like symptoms after baseline among households not assigned to RDT vouchers and not selected for surprise RDT testing; observations with nonmissing ACT-use outcome included.
model_specification: OLS linear probability model with separate ACT-subsidy indicators (92%, 88%, 80%) and randomization-stratum fixed effects; cluster-robust standard errors at the household level.
controls: Household head age (imputed) and missing-age indicator, randomization strata fixed effects, and indicators for the other ACT subsidy levels.
operationalization_notes: The paper operationalizes ACT access as the share of first illness episodes treated with an ACT and estimates effects excluding RDT-intervention households, so I used that design and focused on the 92% subsidy as the 'very high subsidy' treatment.
reasoning: In a linear probability model for first post-baseline illness episodes, assignment to the very high 92% ACT subsidy increased the probability of taking an ACT by 0.225 relative to the no-subsidy control group (cluster-robust t(574)=4.27, p=2.33e-05). This provides strong evidence that the high subsidy increased access to antimalarials.

dependent_variable: Two-year change in normalized combined PIAT math, reading recognition, and reading comprehension score
main_predictor: Two-year change in family income measured in $1,000 units, instrumented with simulated change in federal EITC based on lagged earned income
sample_definition: Children in the NLSY child-mother file excluding the poor-white/military oversamples (sampblau==1), with valid math and reading PIAT components in consecutive two-year test observations from survey years 1988-2000, observed family income variables, and no maternal marital-status change over the two-year interval
model_specification: Two-stage least squares on two-year differences with mother-clustered standard errors; endogenous income change instrumented by simulated federal EITC change computed from lagged earned income, predicted current earnings, lagged number of dependents, and the federal EITC schedule
controls: Child male, Black, Hispanic, current child age, change in number of siblings, indicator for positive lagged earned income, and a fifth-order polynomial in lagged earned income
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's baseline contemporaneous-effects design: differencing removes child fixed effects and EITC schedule changes instrument income changes. I constructed the combined score from the provided standardized PIAT components and recomputed the EITC-based instrument from variables available in the dataset.
reasoning: In a two-year-differenced IV model, the estimated effect of a $1,000 increase in family income was positive (0.0572 standard deviations in combined math-reading achievement), with clustered t(2560)=3.75, p=0.00018. This supports the claim that income increases raise short-run test scores.

dependent_variable: engwkabs (work absorption scale)
main_predictor: singchild1 (1 = single and childless; 0 = all other family structures)
sample_definition: Study 1 alumni survey respondents who were employed full-time, part-time, or self-employed and had complete data on absorption, gender, age, job level, and single-childless status; listwise N = 353.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of work absorption on single-childless indicator and covariates; main result is the t test for the single-childless coefficient.
operationalization_notes: The claim corresponds to Hypothesis 1 in Study 1, for which the paper specifies an OLS regression predicting work absorption from family structure while controlling for gender, age, and job level. I reproduced that model directly from the SPSS dataset rather than using the printed statistic.
reasoning: In an OLS regression matching Study 1's specification, the coefficient for being single and childless was negative (b = -0.311) and statistically significant, t(348) = -2.36, p = 0.0188. Thus, single childless respondents reported lower work absorption than respondents with other family structures, controlling for gender, age, and job level.

dependent_variable: ProperName: whether the response began with a proper-name greeting
main_predictor: Applicant ethnicity treatment: Hispanic name versus white name
sample_definition: Observations assigned to Hispanic or white applicant names with nonmissing ProperName coding, i.e. responses for which greeting tone was coded; black-name observations and uncoded/nonresponse observations were excluded.
model_specification: Two-sample test of proportions with pooled standard error comparing the proportion of proper-name greetings for Hispanic versus white applicant-name treatments.
operationalization_notes: The paper operationalizes tone/friendliness as whether a responding official greeted the applicant by proper name and reports race/ethnicity treatments collapsed across male and female names. I used this direct outcome and compared Hispanic to white applicants, matching the claim's contrast.
reasoning: Among coded responses from white or Hispanic applicants, 77 of 187 Hispanic-applicant responses (41.2%) began with a proper-name greeting, compared with 107 of 175 white-applicant responses (61.1%). A pooled two-sample proportion z test for Hispanic minus white was z = -3.80, p = 0.00015, indicating Hispanics were significantly less likely to be greeted by name.

dependent_variable: Shading indicator, coded 1 when the seller chose low quality (qualityc = 1) and 0 when the seller chose normal quality (qualityc = 2)
main_predictor: Contract type: rigid contract versus flexible contract
sample_definition: Baseline condition only (condition = 1); observations with realized good state/trade and observed quality (costc in 20 or 25, qualityc in 1 or 2) for rigid and flexible contracts, collapsed to paired session-level means; 805 underlying contract observations across 5 sessions.
model_specification: One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test comparing session-level mean shading rates for rigid versus flexible contracts, testing rigid < flexible; z is the normal-approximation signed-rank statistic, with exact one-sided p-value reported.
operationalization_notes: Rigid contracts do not trade in the bad state, so the good state provides the direct within-state comparison of seller shading across contract types used in the paper's aggregate analysis; session-level paired testing treats sessions as the independent experimental units.
reasoning: In the baseline treatment's good-state trades, shading occurred in 6.3% of rigid-contract observations versus 25.1% of flexible-contract observations. A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the five paired session-level shading rates gave z = -2.023, exact p = 0.031, indicating significantly less shading under rigid contracts.

dependent_variable: ln(unadjusted state energy-related carbon dioxide emissions, million metric tons CO2)
main_predictor: ln(average weekly working hours of all private employees multiplied by 52)
sample_definition: Balanced panel of all 50 U.S. states for years 2007 through 2013; no observations excluded beyond restricting to the study period.
model_specification: Bivariate Pearson correlation / equivalent simple OLS regression of logged CO2 emissions on logged annual working hours; the reported statistic is the t test for a nonzero positive association.
operationalization_notes: The claim describes the overall positive relationship over 2007-2013, so I used the full state-year sample and the paper's logged transformations of emissions and working hours, focusing on the direct bivariate association rather than choosing among the paper's several multivariable panel specifications.
reasoning: Using all 350 state-year observations from 2007-2013, the bivariate log-log association between state CO2 emissions and average annual working hours was positive and highly statistically significant, t(348)=8.122, p=8.05e-15. This supports the claim that states/years with longer average working hours tended to have higher carbon emissions over this period.

dependent_variable: Any targeting of a nuclear program in year t, coded 1 if consider==1 or attack==1
main_predictor: Prior violent militarized conflict (hostileMID)
sample_definition: Politically relevant directed dyad-years in the dataset (polrel==1) with nonmissing targeting outcome and hostileMID, 1941-2000.
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence for a 2x2 table of any targeting by prior violent conflict, without continuity correction.
operationalization_notes: The paper first evaluates the hypothesis with cross-tabulations of attacks/considered attacks against violent conflict before multivariate rare-events logit models. I operationalized the verbal claim broadly as whether a dyad-year had either a considered or actual attack against the proliferator's nuclear program, compared across prior violent-conflict status in the politically relevant sample.
reasoning: In politically relevant directed dyad-years, targeting was much more frequent after prior violent militarized conflict: 28 of 569 conflict observations (4.92%) versus 13 of 5117 non-conflict observations (0.25%). A Pearson 2x2 chi-square test gives χ²(1, N=5686)=155.79, p=9.42e-36, supporting the claim that prior violent conflict increases the salience of the proliferation threat.

dependent_variable: splinter indicator: county became part of a new district in the electoral wave
main_predictor: DEC share ratio (county share of District Executive Committee seats divided by county population share; lower values indicate political marginalization)
sample_definition: County-wave observations for the three interelection waves after the baseline wave (wave > 0), restricted to counties in multi-county districts (ncounties > 1) with complete data on model covariates; N = 428 county-waves.
model_specification: Population-averaged logistic regression estimated by GEE with an exchangeable within-county correlation structure and robust standard errors.
controls: Ethnic marginalization, development summary index, number of counties in the district, lagged breakup status, support for losing district chair candidate, whether chairperson election was opposed, prior Museveni vote share and its square, log county population, ethnic fractionalization, region indicators, and electoral-wave indicators.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's county-wave design and the main Table 4 specification for local political marginalization; GEE was used to account for repeated observations by county while producing a directly interpretable robust z test.
reasoning: In a binomial GEE model of whether a county became a splinter district, the DEC share ratio coefficient was negative (b = -0.760, robust SE = 0.268), z = -2.84, p = 0.0045. Because lower DEC share ratio indicates greater political marginalization/under-representation, this result supports the claim that politically marginalized counties were more likely to secede.

dependent_variable: recog1duml: lead dichotomous diplomatic recognition, coded 1 if State B recognizes State A and 0 otherwise
main_predictor: nukeduma: State A nuclear weapons status
sample_definition: Directed dyad observations with non-missing lead diplomatic recognition and model covariates, restricted to years 1945-2000
model_specification: Probit regression with Huber-White/cluster-robust standard errors clustered by directed dyad
controls: State B nuclear weapons status; State A × State B nuclear interaction; rivalry status of A and B; dyadic rivalry; CINC of A and B and their interaction; democracy score of A and B and their interaction; COW ordinal contiguity; log distance; alliance dummy
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether nuclear states receive diplomatic recognition, so I used the dichotomous State B-recognizes-State A outcome from the diplomatic-recognition analysis and tested the State A nuclear-status coefficient in a directed-dyad probit with the principal controls described for Table 2.
reasoning: In a dyad-cluster-robust probit model, State A nuclear weapons status positively predicts whether State B recognizes State A at the next diplomatic-exchange observation (coefficient = 0.1666, SE = 0.0421, z = 3.96, p = 7.49e-05; N = 213,454). This supports the claim that nuclear-capable states are more likely to be recognized by other nations.

dependent_variable: Log absolute change in pro-immigration attitude index between wave 2 and wave 3 (change_w3w2_log).
main_predictor: Group-level mean DQI level of justification across speech acts in the discussion group (DQ_jlev, recomputed as the mean jlev by small_gr).
sample_definition: EuroPolis participants in the 13 DQI-coded migration discussion groups with non-missing wave-2/wave-3 opinion-change outcome, group justification score, and all covariates; complete-case N = 174 individuals nested in 13 groups.
model_specification: Linear mixed-effects regression with a random intercept for discussion group, estimated by REML; Wald z test for the coefficient on group-level justification rationality.
controls: Female, age, education, working class, Catholic, Protestant, religiosity, left-right ideology and squared term, intended left-party vote, intended right-party vote, knowledge change, ratings that other participants/experts/politicians/briefing material clarified thinking, and social conformity pressure above and below the respondent's pre-deliberation position.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies Model 2b as the analysis directly tied to this claim: opinion-change magnitude on immigration is regressed on group-level justification rationality as a deliberative group resource, with the Sanders covariate set and individuals nested in discussion groups.
reasoning: In a complete-case multilevel regression of log absolute immigration-opinion change, the group-level mean level of justification had a positive coefficient (b = 0.1301, SE = 0.0662), yielding z = 1.965 and two-sided p = 0.0494. Thus, participants in groups with more rational justification showed greater opinion change, consistent with the original claim.

dependent_variable: Mean of the binary work-hard indicator within each matching group across all six decision periods
main_predictor: Reward scheme under complementarity: discriminating 345COM versus symmetric 444COM
sample_definition: Observations from complementarity treatments only (345COM and 444COM); all six periods in the dataset included, aggregated to 23 independent matching-group means (12 in 345COM, 11 in 444COM).
model_specification: Welch independent-samples t-test comparing matching-group mean effort between 345COM and 444COM, with the contrast discriminating minus symmetric.
operationalization_notes: The paper treats matching groups as independent observations for repeated-round treatment comparisons, so I aggregated individual work decisions to the matching-group level and compared the cost-equivalent reward schemes within the complementarity production technology.
reasoning: Using independent matching groups as the unit of analysis under the complementarity technology, mean effort was higher in the discriminating 345COM treatment (M = 0.917, 12 groups) than in the symmetric 444COM treatment (M = 0.722, 11 groups). A Welch two-sample t-test on group-level mean effort gave t(17.40) = 2.32, p = 0.033, supporting the claim that symmetric rewards elicit lower effort than the cost-equivalent discriminating scheme.

dependent_variable: Anti-minus-pro immigration action balance in each senator response: 1 if anti-immigration actions only were mentioned, 0 if both or neither were mentioned, and -1 if pro-immigration actions only were mentioned
main_predictor: Constituent letter position, comparing anti-immigration versus pro-immigration letters within the same senator
sample_definition: U.S. senators in the Experiment 1 dataset who responded to both the pro-immigration and anti-immigration constituent letters (56 senators; 112 response letters)
model_specification: Paired t-test of the within-senator difference in anti-minus-pro action balance between the anti-immigration-letter response and the pro-immigration-letter response
controls: Senator-level fixed characteristics controlled by the paired within-subject design; no additional covariates
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns senators tailoring explanations to different audiences, so I used the paper's Experiment 1 within-subject design and its compensating/reinforcing action measures. A higher balance for anti-immigration than pro-immigration constituent letters captures tailoring of mentioned policy actions toward the audience.
reasoning: Among the 56 senators who responded to both letters, the mean anti-minus-pro action balance was 0.429 for responses to anti-immigration constituents versus 0.196 for responses to pro-immigration constituents. The within-senator paired difference was 0.232, t(55)=3.45, p=0.0011, indicating that senators shifted the actions they mentioned toward the constituent audience's position.

dependent_variable: Log wage gain at migration, log(last U.S. adjusted hourly wage) minus log(last home-country adjusted hourly wage)
main_predictor: Indicator for no high school exposure (<9 years of schooling), compared with college degree or more (>=16 years; omitted category)
sample_definition: Public MP/LAMP wage_gain_table observations; excluded Puerto Rico; retained observations with adjusted home and U.S. hourly wages between $0.01 and $1,000 and premigration job year >=1983; N=2562.
model_specification: OLS regression of log wage gain on five education categories (college graduates omitted/reference) and country fixed effects; the reported t-test is for the no-high-school coefficient.
controls: Country fixed effects and indicators for some high school, high-school graduate, and some college education categories.
operationalization_notes: The paper tests this claim using wage gains at migration by education with country fixed effects. Because the restricted NIS microdata were not present in the provided public files, I used the readable MP/LAMP wage-gain data and mirrored the paper's education categories and wage-validity restrictions.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of log wage gain at migration on education categories with college graduates as the reference group and country fixed effects, the no-high-school coefficient was positive (0.388 log points, about 47% larger gain). The coefficient was statistically significant, t(2549)=3.323, p=0.00090, supporting the claim that immigrants with no high-school exposure gain more than college graduates.

dependent_variable: Percent of free-association responses categorized as reflecting the learned negative meaning of the cue
main_predictor: Cue status: baseline learned cue versus learned-and-suppressed cue
sample_definition: Experiment 2 participants classified as nonruminators with complete data in the provided final dataset (Group = 1; N = 27)
model_specification: Within-subject baseline vs suppressed comparison implemented as a repeated-measures ANOVA; equivalently, the participant-level baseline-minus-suppressed difference was tested against zero while including counterbalancing condition as a between-subject factor
controls: Counterbalancing condition (CB) included as a between-subject factor; no other covariates
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies baseline versus suppressed items as the indirect measure of suppression-induced forgetting, and the available dataset contains the Experiment 2 transfer task; therefore I tested whether nonruminators showed fewer learned-meaning associations after suppression than at baseline.
reasoning: Among nonruminators in Experiment 2, free-association responses reflected the learned negative meaning less often for suppressed cues (M = 29.63%) than for baseline cues (M = 45.68%). The baseline-vs-suppression comparison controlling for counterbalancing was significant, F(1, 24) = 10.94, p = .00296, supporting a beneficial effect of suppression practice on the transfer task.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being: mean of eight reverse-coded CES-D items, scaled 0-3 with higher values indicating better well-being
main_predictor: Interaction of parental status (any parent vs childless) with country-level standardized disapproval of voluntary childlessness (low values = more tolerant norms)
sample_definition: Respondents aged over 40 in the 24 non-Cyprus European countries in the provided final dataset, excluding cases missing well-being, parental status, country, country-level norm measure, individual norm/social-contact controls, or demographic controls
model_specification: Linear regression of psychological well-being on parenthood, country-level disapproval, and their interaction, with country fixed effects and standard errors clustered by country; the reported test is for the parenthood × country-level disapproval interaction
controls: Female gender, age, age squared, marital status, respondent education, parental education, religious attendance, paid employment, born in country, individual disapproval of childlessness, individual social contacts, and country fixed effects
operationalization_notes: The paper tests this claim as a cross-level moderation of the childlessness-well-being association by societal norms. I collapsed the two parent categories to a single parent indicator to match the verbal claim comparing childless people with people who have children, and tested whether that gap changes with country-level tolerance/disapproval.
reasoning: In an OLS model with country fixed effects and SEs clustered by country, the interaction between being a parent and country-level disapproval of childlessness was positive and statistically significant, t(23)=4.38, p=0.00022. This means the well-being advantage of parents over childless respondents is larger where childlessness is more disapproved of, equivalently the disadvantage of childless people is smaller in more tolerant countries.

dependent_variable: DSM5_Total: summed DSM-5 Self-Rated Level 1 Cross-Cutting Symptom Measure total psychopathology score
main_predictor: MiniK_Total: summed Mini-K life history strategy score, with lower scores indicating faster life history strategy
sample_definition: All 138 participants in the dataset with complete Age, MiniK_Total, and DSM5_Total values; no additional exclusions were needed.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares linear regression: DSM5_Total ~ MiniK_Total + Age; the reported statistic is the t test for the MiniK_Total regression coefficient.
operationalization_notes: The paper's main analysis tested associations between life-history measures and total psychopathology using partial correlations controlling for age. I operationalized the claim using the Mini-K because it is described as a behavioral life-history measure and tested its age-adjusted association with the total DSM-5 psychopathology severity score.
reasoning: In an OLS model predicting total DSM-5 symptom score from Mini-K life-history score while controlling for age, the Mini-K coefficient was significantly negative, t(135) = -6.95, p = 1.41e-10. Because higher Mini-K scores indicate a slower life strategy, this means faster life strategies were associated with greater psychopathology symptoms.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (sum correct on the 20-item political knowledge test)
main_predictor: Stereotypaktivierung: stereotype not activated (0) versus stereotype activated by gender difference statement (2)
sample_definition: Filtered Study 2 observations with Filter=1, restricted to female participants (gender_factor=1) assigned to stereotype-not-activated or gender-difference-statement conditions; N=143.
model_specification: OLS ANCOVA in the female subsample: PolWis_score ~ condition + field_of_study + PolInt_score; reported t test is the adjusted contrast for stereotype-not-activated versus gender-difference-statement condition.
controls: Political interest score (PolInt_score) and field of study (psychology vs politics).
operationalization_notes: The paper's methods used the cleaned/filter sample, political knowledge score as the dependent variable, political interest as covariate, and field of study as a design factor. I therefore tested the focal pairwise condition difference within female participants while adjusting for those variables.
reasoning: Among female participants in the control and gender-difference-statement conditions, an ANCOVA/OLS model showed higher political knowledge scores in the stereotype-not-activated condition than in the statement condition (condition contrast = 1.45 points), t(139) = 2.53, p = 0.0126. This supports the claim that female participants performed better without stereotype activation.

dependent_variable: Overall GDP growth index at t+2 (f2gdpidx)
main_predictor: Indicator that either the city party secretary or mayor was connected to the incumbent provincial party secretary (msec2currentsec == 1 or mayor2currentsec == 1)
sample_definition: City-year observations from 2000-2011 in the mainland prefecture/subprovincial city panel, excluding Tibet, with nonmissing outcome and covariates used in the model; 326 cities and 3,687 observations.
model_specification: OLS regression of GDP growth at t+2 on the connection indicator, city fixed effects, province-year fixed effects, and covariates; robust standard errors clustered by city.
controls: Net fiscal transfer variable (dep), predecessor-year economic controls for both secretary and mayor positions (GDP growth, log GDP, log population, log fixed asset investment), and city leader controls for both secretary and mayor (age, education, gender, and tenure-category indicators for <1, 1-3, and 3-5 years, with >5 years as reference).
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's baseline specification for the central claim: economic performance is measured as overall GDP growth two years later, and the treatment is whether either top city leader has the paper's promotion-based patronage tie to the incumbent provincial secretary.
reasoning: I estimated a city and province-year fixed-effects OLS model with city-clustered robust standard errors. The coefficient for connection to the incumbent provincial secretary was positive (0.353 percentage points in GDP growth at t+2) and statistically significant (z = 2.60, p = 0.0094), supporting faster economic growth in connected cities.

dependent_variable: Top-quality status among foreign players (top-quality foreign player count versus lower-quality foreign player count)
main_predictor: Post-1991 Danish foreigner tax scheme period (1991-2008 vs. 1985-1990)
sample_definition: Country-year aggregate observations for Denmark from 1985-2008 in basesynthetic_control.dta; included only foreign players, split into top-quality and lower-quality counts using the paper's top-quality definition.
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test on a 2x2 contingency table of foreign player quality category (top vs lower) by reform period (pre vs post).
operationalization_notes: The paper's Denmark case study uses 1985-1990 as the pre-reform period and 1991-2008 as the post-reform period, defining top-quality players as those selected for their home national team. To test the claimed change in ability composition directly, I tested whether the share of top-quality players among Denmark's foreign players increased after the tax cut.
reasoning: Among foreign players in Denmark, top-quality players were 4 of 24 foreign player-season observations in 1985-1990 versus 195 of 364 in 1991-2008. A chi-square test of the top-versus-lower foreign player composition by pre/post reform period was significant, chi-square(1, N=388)=12.27, p=0.00046, indicating a post-reform shift toward higher-ability foreigners.

dependent_variable: Willingness to Pay scale, computed as the mean of the income-for-environment item, tax-for-environment item, and reverse-scored not-my-money item
main_predictor: Intrinsic relative to extrinsic values (I/E) group: top quartile/high I/E versus bottom quartile/low I/E
sample_definition: Study 1 retained student respondents with I/E scores in the top quartile (E_I >= 0.61; n = 46) or bottom quartile (E_I <= 0.22; n = 35); middle-range I/E respondents were excluded from this contrast
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test comparing WTP means between high-I/E and low-I/E groups, using the pooled-variance Student t-test
operationalization_notes: The paper's Study 1 methods defined I/E from centered intrinsic and reverse-scored extrinsic Aspiration Index items and tested willingness to pay by contrasting the upper and lower I/E quartile groups; I followed that operationalization on the original SAV data.
reasoning: In Study 1, participants in the high intrinsic-relative-to-extrinsic values group had higher willingness to pay (M = 4.01, n = 46) than those in the low group (M = 3.30, n = 35), t(79) = 4.87, p = 5.56e-06. This supports the claim that stronger endorsement of intrinsic relative to extrinsic values is associated with greater willingness to pay to protect the environment.

dependent_variable: Natural log of annual disputed-product imports into the defendant market after the dispute (imports_post).
main_predictor: Indicator that the trade partner was a complainant in the dispute (complainant).
sample_definition: Post-dispute years 1 through 5 for WTO merchandise disputes that ended in early settlement, restricted to observations with complete data on the dependent variable, complainant indicator, controls, and dispute fixed effects; N = 6,027 country/dispute-partner-year observations across 45 corrected disputes.
model_specification: OLS linear regression with corrected dispute fixed effects; cluster-robust standard errors clustered by corrected dispute ID. The reported t-test is for the coefficient on complainant.
controls: Defendant GDP (logged), partner GDP (logged), democratic pair indicator, lagged disputed imports at t-1, and logged total bilateral imports.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Model 2 specification for testing discrimination under privacy: within early settlements, compare defendants' post-dispute disputed-product imports from complainants with imports from non-complainant WTO members while adjusting for market size, prior trade, total bilateral import penetration, regime pairing, and dispute-specific fixed effects.
reasoning: In the early-settlement subsample, the complainant indicator was positive and statistically significant (coefficient = 0.4301 log points, cluster-robust t(44) = 2.384, p = 0.0215). This supports the claim that in private settlements complainant countries obtain greater post-dispute import access than other WTO members.

dependent_variable: entre_wage: country-year entrepreneurship rate, defined as early-stage business ownership/management that pays wages
main_predictor: medage_20_64: country median age among ages 20-64
sample_definition: All non-missing GEM country-year observations in GEM_Country_Year.dta for 2001-2010 (393 country-years across 82 countries)
model_specification: Weighted least squares regression of entrepreneurship rate on median age and year fixed effects, using nobs_cy as analytic weights; standard errors clustered by countryid
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's country-year specification most directly tied to the claim that lower median age raises aggregate new business formation, using the paper's primary entrepreneurship measure and median-age demographic variable.
reasoning: In a weighted country-year regression with year fixed effects and country-clustered standard errors, median age among ages 20-64 negatively predicted the early-stage pays-wages entrepreneurship rate (coefficient = -0.00732 per year; t(81) = -5.71, p = 1.78e-7). Thus, lower median age is associated with higher new business formation, supporting the published claim.

dependent_variable: Perceived arm length divided by actual arm length (arm-length ratio)
main_predictor: Arm side within participant (right arm vs left arm)
sample_definition: The 15 participants coded as right-handed in Experiment 1 with nonmissing perceived and actual arm-length measurements for both arms.
model_specification: One-sided paired-samples t-test comparing RatioRight to RatioLeft within right-handed participants.
operationalization_notes: The Experiment 1 methods state that arm-length estimates were analyzed as ratios of perceived to actual arm length; restricting to right-handed participants and comparing right versus left arm ratios directly operationalizes the quoted claim.
reasoning: Among right-handed participants, the perceived/actual arm-length ratio was higher for the right arm (M = 0.970) than for the left arm (M = 0.920). A one-sided paired-samples t-test on right-minus-left ratios gave t(14) = 2.12, p = .026, supporting the directional claim that right-handed participants perceived their right arms as longer than their left arms.

dependent_variable: Mean of three felt-appreciation/valued/satisfaction items (dv_index3)
main_predictor: Acknowledgment condition: verbal acknowledgment only vs. financial acknowledgment with 5-cent benefit
sample_definition: Study 1a hotel conference center guests who completed the study and had non-missing dependent-variable and condition data; excluded participants marked as not finishing the study
model_specification: One-way between-subjects ANOVA equivalent to an independent-samples equal-variance t-test comparing dv_index3 by condition
operationalization_notes: The available dataset is Study 1a, an initial field test of the trivialization effect; the paper defines the key outcome as the average of three appreciation-related items and compares verbal versus 5-cent financial acknowledgments.
reasoning: Using the 49 completed Study 1a cases, a one-way ANOVA showed that the financial acknowledgment condition reported lower felt appreciation (M = 4.38) than the verbal acknowledgment condition (M = 5.57), F(1, 47) = 8.50, p = .00543. This supports the claim that a small financial acknowledgment can lead to less positive outcomes than a verbal acknowledgment.

dependent_variable: s_tot (mean standardized midterm and final exam score)
main_predictor: avg5_girl (share female among neighbor-5 peers: desk mate plus front/rear neighboring desks)
sample_definition: Female students only, excluding favored/special-seat students (special1==0) and observations missing the outcome, peer measures, classroom/block IDs, or model covariates.
model_specification: OLS regression of standardized exam score on share female in neighbor-5 peers and average baseline score of neighbor-5 peers, with randomization-block fixed effects; standard error for the main coefficient clustered by classroom.
controls: Baseline test score, height, age, birth order, mother's education, father's education, baseline interest in Chinese, English, and math, desk mate favored-status indicator, share favored among neighbor-4 peers, average baseline score of neighbor-5 peers, and block fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: The claim refers to female students surrounded by five females rather than five males, so I used the paper's neighbor-5 peer measure in the female sample and followed the paper's equation (2)/Table 5 panel B specification.
reasoning: In the female subsample, the estimated coefficient on the share of females among neighbor-5 peers was 0.211 standardized test-score units, so moving from five male to five female nearby peers corresponds to about a 0.21 SD increase. The cluster-robust test was t(11)=2.77, p=0.018, indicating a positive effect consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Absolute change in mean alcohol attitude from Time 1 to the one-year follow-up (Time 3); higher values indicate greater instability.
main_predictor: Interaction between mean-centered overall attitude certainty and mean-centered objective ambivalence at Time 1.
sample_definition: Study 2 participants with nonmissing Time 1 attitude, certainty, positive/negative reaction items, and one-year follow-up attitude items (N = 135).
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of absolute attitude change on attitude extremity, centered certainty, centered objective ambivalence, and their product interaction.
controls: Time 1 attitude extremity, computed as absolute deviation of the mean Time 1 attitude from the scale midpoint of 4.
operationalization_notes: I followed the Study 2 method: attitudes and certainty were averaged across their respective items; objective ambivalence was computed with the similarity-intensity formula, (positive + negative)/2 - |positive - negative|; stability was operationalized as absolute attitude change over time.
reasoning: In Study 2, the certainty × objective ambivalence interaction significantly predicted absolute attitude change over the one-year interval, t(130) = 3.42, p = 0.00084. Because the outcome was instability and the interaction coefficient was positive (B = 0.0745), the negative certainty-stability association was stronger at lower ambivalence and reversed at higher ambivalence, matching the published claim.

dependent_variable: Change in aggregate electoral turnout for lower-chamber elections
main_predictor: Change in log portfolio equity stock (foreign ownership)
sample_definition: Election-year observations in Turnout.dta with nonmissing turnout, lagged turnout, portfolio equity stock, electoral controls, and country-specific trend variables, across 23 OECD countries; first two usable elections per country were lost to lagging/instrumenting.
model_specification: First-differenced dynamic panel IV regression: delta turnout on delta lagged turnout, delta log portfolio equity stock, differenced controls, and differenced country-specific quadratic trends; delta lagged turnout instrumented with available turnout levels lagged two or more elections; standard errors clustered by country.
controls: Lagged turnout; registered voters (log); percent voting-age population aged 30-69; years since last election; US mid-term dummy; compulsory voting; mixed electoral system; PR system; disproportionality; effective number of parties; electoral margin; country-specific quadratic time trends.
operationalization_notes: The paper's turnout models use lower-chamber aggregate turnout, a dynamic panel specification with fixed country effects removed by differencing, country-specific trends, and several electoral controls. Portfolio equity stock was selected as the foreign-ownership measure because it is a direct ownership variable emphasized as highly mobile capital in the paper.
reasoning: In a dynamic first-differenced panel IV model, the coefficient on the change in log portfolio equity stock was negative; its cluster-robust test statistic was t(22) = -2.73, p = 0.012. Thus, higher foreign ownership is associated with lower electoral turnout in this operationalization.

dependent_variable: Number of Better Business Bureau complaints in the prior 3 years (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: Indicator that the firm uses at least one name beginning with A, a number, or a symbol (first_A)
sample_definition: All 2,293 independent Illinois plumbing firms in final_data.dta with nonmissing complaint and name-type data; multiple ReferenceUSA listings were represented at the constructed firm level as in the paper.
model_specification: Two-sample pooled-variance t-test, equivalently an OLS regression of complaints_2008 on first_A with an intercept and conventional standard error.
operationalization_notes: The verbal claim concerns the unconditional average number of service complaints for firms whose names begin with A or a number compared with other firms, so I used the paper's firm-level Illinois plumber sample and compared mean BBB complaints by name type.
reasoning: In the firm-level Illinois plumbing data, firms with a name beginning with A/a number/symbol averaged 1.339 Better Business Bureau complaints versus 0.248 for other firms. A two-sample pooled t-test of the difference in means gave t(2291)=6.788, p=1.44e-11, supporting the claim that A-name firms receive more complaints.

dependent_variable: Cooperative bargaining strategy ordinal score (dv; categories 0–3, higher = more cooperative/concession-offering)
main_predictor: Issue-linkage structure (issue_linkage_structure; extent to which opposing states value the negotiated issues differently)
sample_definition: All 588 state-bargaining observations in the provided DEU bargaining strategies dataset with complete data for the Model 1 variables.
model_specification: Partial proportional-odds/generalized ordered logistic regression for cumulative logits Pr(dv > j), j = 0,1,2; issue_linkage_structure constrained to have a common effect across cutpoints; standard errors clustered by bargaining phase.
controls: ln GDP, security/defense policy indicator (foreignpolicy), Euro state, new member state, agreement importance, parliamentary scrutiny, majority voting, publicity, presidency, and lagged dependent variable.
operationalization_notes: I followed the paper's main Table 1 Model 1 specification because Hypothesis S1 is tested by the issue-linkage structure predictor in the generalized ordered logit model of states' concession-offering bargaining strategies.
reasoning: In a generalized ordered logit model of cooperative bargaining strategy, the issue-linkage structure coefficient was positive (b = 1.2193) with a bargaining-phase clustered SE of 0.1922, giving z = 6.35, p = 2.22e-10. Thus, observations with more differently valued issues were significantly more likely to fall in higher, more concession-offering bargaining-strategy categories.

dependent_variable: Credit to Government and SOEs (percent GDP; credittogovtstateenterp)
main_predictor: Lagged state capacity, the IQG index (icrg_qog_L1)
sample_definition: Country-year observations from 1985-2011 in the Country Year Dataset with observed Credit to Government and SOEs and consecutive one-year lags of directed credit, IQG state capacity, and private credit; 129 countries, N = 2630.
model_specification: OLS dynamic panel regression with country fixed effects and a linear time trend; standard errors clustered by country. The reported t test is for the coefficient on lagged IQG state capacity.
controls: Lagged dependent variable, lagged Private Credit (percent GDP), linear time trend, and country fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: The paper tests this claim with a dynamic panel specification using Credit to Government and SOEs as the outcome and controls for Private Credit as the profit-potential proxy. I used the same core variables and lag structure but estimated a transparent country fixed-effects dynamic panel model rather than system GMM.
reasoning: In a dynamic country fixed-effects panel model, the coefficient on lagged state capacity (IQG) was positive rather than negative (b = 0.5625) and was not statistically distinguishable from zero, t(128) = 0.708, p = 0.480. Thus, this analysis does not support the claim that weaker states direct more credit to government and SOEs after controlling for private-credit profit potential.

dependent_variable: originit: binary indicator that the country initiated a militarized interstate dispute as originator in the country-year
main_predictor: coup_risk_hat: fitted log weighted coup-events measure, used as the estimated risk of coup events/threats to political survival
sample_definition: All available Latin American country-years in the dataset with nonmissing variables for the model, 22 countries during 1961-1999 (N = 798)
model_specification: Two-stage analysis: first-stage OLS predicted lcoupsum from the exogenous variables in the coup-risk and conflict equations; second-stage probit of MID initiation on fitted coup risk and controls, with standard errors clustered by country
controls: previous dispute (lagdisp), ethnic fractionalization, relative power (CINC), number of borders, log number of allies, regional conflict, lagged polity, and lagged log real GDP; first-stage predictors also included previous coup, recent war, and conflict ending with force
operationalization_notes: The paper's main test uses a country-year design and a simultaneous continuous/binary model linking coup events and dispute initiation. I used the paper's primary dispute-initiation outcome and controls, operationalizing threats to political survival as the predicted coup-event risk from the specified coup-risk equation.
reasoning: In a two-stage probit analysis of MID initiation, the fitted coup-risk measure had a positive coefficient of 2.763 with cluster-robust z = 2.58 (N = 798, p = 0.0098). This indicates that higher threats to political survival were associated with a higher probability of conflict initiation.

dependent_variable: d12outgroup: amount sent to an out-group (Albanian) recipient in the dictator game
main_predictor: albregion: Primarily Albanian region / highest exposure to Albanians, compared with Primarily Serb region baseline
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb adult participants with nonmissing dictator-game and covariate data in the replication dataset
model_specification: Tobit regression for a dependent variable censored at 0 and 5 euros; included regional indicators for Primarily Albanian and Border regions with Primarily Serb region as the omitted reference; standard errors clustered by experimental location
controls: borderregion, female, age, education, employed, village, alphaviolence, alphadamaged, displaced
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns out-group bridging norms increasing with exposure to the out-group, so I used out-group dictator giving as the behavioral altruism outcome and the paper's regional exposure coding and extended-control Tobit specification.
reasoning: In a Tobit model censoring dictator giving at 0 and 5 euros, the coefficient for living in the primarily Albanian region (highest exposure) relative to the primarily Serb region was positive and very large (b = 2.085). Using clustered sandwich standard errors by experimental location, this yielded z = 30.74, p = 1.55e-207, supporting higher out-group giving among Serbs with greater exposure to Albanians.

dependent_variable: Relative preference/enjoyment rating comparing the initial clip with the target animated sword-fight clip (7-point scale; higher values favor the target program).
main_predictor: Viewing condition: interrupted by a 30-second commercial vs. continuous/no interruption.
sample_definition: Study 2 observations in the Excel file with nonmissing experimental condition and enjoyment rating; excluded spreadsheet footer/p-value rows with missing condition, yielding N = 102.
model_specification: Two-sample independent-groups t-test comparing mean enjoyment ratings between interrupted and continuous conditions, using pooled variance.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies Study 2's relative preference/enjoyment rating as the direct test of the statement that the commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable, so I analyzed that outcome by the randomized disruption condition.
reasoning: An independent-samples t-test on the Study 2 relative enjoyment/preference rating showed higher enjoyment in the commercial-disruption condition (M = 5.38, n = 53) than in the continuous/no-commercial condition (M = 4.47, n = 49), t(100) = 2.45, p = .016. This supports the claim that commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable.

dependent_variable: acceptedbribes: belief that Don Swensen accepted bribes or engaged in other illegal practices, recoded so higher values indicate greater perceived likelihood on a 1-5 scale
main_predictor: Experimental treatment contrast: causal correction condition versus denial-of-innuendo condition
sample_definition: Respondents in the Don Swensen experiment with nonmissing acceptedbribes outcome and treatment assignment; all four experimental conditions included in the model (N=986).
model_specification: Inverse-probability-weighted OLS/WLS regression of acceptedbribes on indicators for innuendo, denial, and causal correction with control as the reference group; the reported statistic is the linear contrast causal correction minus denial.
controls: None; inverse probability weights account for the block-randomized treatment probabilities by prior belief that government officials are crooked.
operationalization_notes: The paper emphasizes the bribes/illegal-practices item as the key misperception outcome and reports models using inverse probability weights for the block-randomized design, so I used that outcome and compared the causal-correction arm directly to the denial arm.
reasoning: Using the recoded 1-5 belief scale, the inverse-probability-weighted mean belief that Swensen accepted bribes or engaged in illegal practices was lower in the causal-correction condition than in the denial condition by 0.481 points. The WLS treatment-contrast test was t(982) = -5.07, p = 4.65e-7, supporting the claim that the causal explanation was more effective than evidentiary denial at limiting this misperception.

dependent_variable: Aggregate intimacy score computed as the mean of the four intimacy questionnaire items, with the reversed caring item reverse-scored on the 1-7 scale
main_predictor: Attention condition (cnd = 1: partner monitored participant 80% of the time vs cnd = 2: partner never monitored participant)
sample_definition: All complete observations in Sheet3 of Ohtsubo_et_al2014Study2a_data.xls (15 attention and 15 no-attention participants); the dataset did not contain a usable flag identifying the manuscript's suspected-deception exclusion
model_specification: Two-sample Student independent-samples t-test comparing mean intimacy between the attention and no-attention conditions
operationalization_notes: The data file is for Study 2a, whose method directly manipulates receipt of partner attention while dissociating attention from task benefits; the paper identifies intimacy as the primary dependent variable for this claim.
reasoning: In an independent-samples t-test, participants in the attention condition reported higher intimacy (M = 4.58, n = 15) than participants in the no-attention condition (M = 2.78, n = 15), t(28) = 6.20, p = 1.07e-6. This supports the claim that receiving attention from the partner increased intimacy.

dependent_variable: Binary indicator q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2: interested in learning more in the future about how the district government spends money in the budget
main_predictor: taxgrp, assigned tax treatment (1) versus windfall treatment (0)
sample_definition: All 1,863 randomized participants with nonmissing monitoring outcome and treatment assignment; no exclusions were necessary for this outcome.
model_specification: Unadjusted Welch two-sample t-test comparing mean monitoring willingness between tax and windfall treatment groups (intent-to-treat by assigned treatment).
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies willingness to learn more about how the district government spends money in the budget as the main monitoring measure for H1 and estimates the tax-versus-windfall average treatment effect in the full sample, so I used that outcome and treatment contrast directly.
reasoning: In a Welch two-sample test, the tax group was more willing to monitor the budget (mean = 0.811, n = 931) than the windfall group (mean = 0.760, n = 932), a difference of 0.051. The test was statistically significant, t(1847.31) = 2.70, p = 0.007, supporting the claim that tax treatment increased monitoring.

dependent_variable: turnout
main_predictor: z1elite_avgprox (standardized social proximity to elites)
sample_definition: All eligible voters in the Newport, Kentucky dataset: males at least 21 years of age with complete data on turnout, social proximity, and covariates (N = 3416).
model_specification: Binary logistic regression predicting individual electoral turnout in Newport, corresponding to the paper's historical turnout model 3 for Newport.
controls: Household wealth, log household wealth, mid-status occupation, high-status occupation, home ownership, age, log age, Black race, U.S.-born status, and weighted eigenvector network centrality.
operationalization_notes: I used the Newport historical election because the paper's methods directly model turnout among eligible voters with social proximity to all local elites as the key predictor; the reported statistic is the Wald z-test for that predictor from the fitted logistic regression.
reasoning: Using a logistic regression of turnout in the Newport 1874 election, the coefficient for standardized social proximity to elites was positive (b = 0.717) and statistically significant, z = 5.281, p = 1.29e-7. This supports the claim that individuals who were more socially proximate to elites turned out at a higher rate.

dependent_variable: Binary utilitarian response coded 1 = push, 0 = no push
main_predictor: Mood condition, positive versus negative
sample_definition: Experiment 1 participants in the active-frame condition only (frame = active); all 200 such observations included
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test comparing mean binary utilitarian responding between positive- and negative-mood groups
operationalization_notes: The paper defines utilitarian responding as deciding to push and tests this claim within the active decision frame; recollection of autobiographical memories was not included because the methods/results state it had no effect and was omitted from the reported analyses.
reasoning: Restricting the Experiment 1 data to the active-frame condition, utilitarian responses occurred for 28/100 participants in the positive-mood group versus 9/100 in the negative-mood group. An independent-samples t-test on the binary push decision gave t(198)=3.55, p=0.00048, supporting the claim that utilitarian responding was more likely under positive mood in the active frame.

dependent_variable: TVA visual processing speed parameter v (nu)
main_predictor: auditory alerting condition: 85 dB cue versus no cue
sample_definition: All 28 Experiment 1 participants in the supplementary Exp1 parameter dataset; paired participant-level v estimates for no-cue and 85 dB cue conditions were included.
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing v_85dBCue to v_NoCue within participants.
operationalization_notes: Experiment 1 directly tested whether a high-intensity phasic auditory cue increases TVA-estimated visual processing speed relative to no cue, matching the claim and the paper's modeling approach using participant-level TVA parameter estimates.
reasoning: In Experiment 1, the mean TVA visual processing-speed estimate was higher with the 85 dB auditory cue (M = 92.69) than with no cue (M = 66.90). A paired-samples t-test on the 28 participant-level estimates gave t(27) = 4.71, p = 6.68e-05, supporting an increase in processing speed under phasic auditory alerting.

dependent_variable: ln(mean value of owner-occupied housing units on the census block)
main_predictor: interaction of court-ordered desegregation-plan border, central-city side of the border, and 1980 post period
sample_definition: Census blocks from 1970 and 1980 adjacent to city-suburban school-district borders (tierno < 2), excluding Georgia and the NYC-Floral Park border, requiring both sides of a border and both census years to be present, nonzero population, nonmissing housing value, and positive owner-occupied-unit weight.
model_specification: Weighted least squares difference-in-differences border model with cluster-robust standard errors by school district/jurisdiction; observations weighted by number of owner-occupied units on the block.
controls: Side-of-border fixed effects, border-by-year fixed effects, and the central-city-side × 1980 interaction to absorb the general city-suburban trend.
operationalization_notes: I followed the paper's preferred block-level border specification for the main housing-price result, using the log mean owner-occupied housing value as the outcome and the triple interaction identifying cities newly exposed to desegregation over the 1970s as the treatment contrast.
reasoning: In a weighted difference-in-differences border regression, the coefficient on the desegregation-plan × central-city-side × 1980 interaction was negative (about -0.0585 log points) and statistically different from zero, t(123) = -2.09, p = 0.039. This indicates that housing values on the city side declined relative to neighboring suburbs after desegregation orders, consistent with the study's claim.

dependent_variable: fraud_ordered: ordered evaluation of whether the December 2011 Duma election was free and fair, coded from free/fair to somewhat free/fair to not free/fair
main_predictor: opp_do_know: opposition voter who correctly identified Golos, compared to the omitted category of opposition voters who did not correctly identify Golos
sample_definition: Respondents with non-missing fraud_ordered and complete covariate data; all voter-orientation/Golos-knowledge groups included in the model, with opposition non-knowers as the reference category (N = 1728).
model_specification: Proportional-odds ordered logistic regression with five voter-orientation-by-Golos-knowledge indicator variables; the reported statistic is the Wald z test for opp_do_know relative to opposition voters who did not know Golos.
controls: female, age, Moscow residence, private-sector employment, financial status, education, retrospective economic evaluation, political-news interest, state-TV news use, VKontakte, Odnoklassniki, Facebook, LiveJournal, and survey round
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Figure 2 approach: model skepticism about Duma election fairness with an ordered-logit model and estimate the within-opposition-voter contrast for accurate knowledge of Golos while using the saturated demographic, political-engagement, media-use, and round controls.
reasoning: In a proportional-odds ordered logit model, opposition voters who correctly identified Golos had a positive coefficient for greater skepticism about the Duma election compared with opposition voters who did not know Golos (coefficient = 0.613, OR = 1.85). The Wald z test was z = 2.53, two-sided p = 0.0115, supporting the claim that knowledgeable regime opponents were more likely to view the election as fraudulent.

dependent_variable: Party support for ethnic minority rights (eth_supp)
main_predictor: Economic left-right party position (lrecon), evaluated where comm_dom_min = 1 (minority from a former communist federal center)
sample_definition: All party observations in Party_dataset.dta with non-missing eth_supp and covariates across the 14 East European party systems; N = 195.
model_specification: OLS regression of eth_supp on lrecon, comm_dom_min, their interaction, communist regime type, transition year, GDP per capita, and electoral district magnitude, with standard errors clustered by country. Main test is the linear combination lrecon + lrecon:comm_dom_min.
controls: Communist regime type (categorical comm), year first rated free by Freedom House (free), GDP per capita PPP constant 2005 dollars, and mean district magnitude (m_dist).
operationalization_notes: The available data are party-level rather than individual survey data, so I tested the claim via the paper's party-level operationalization: whether parties in countries with minorities from a federal center show greater minority-rights support on the economic left than on the right.
reasoning: In an OLS model of party support for ethnic-minority rights, the conditional slope of economic left-right position among countries with a politically significant minority from a former federal center was negative and statistically significant, t(13) = -2.27, p = 0.041. Because higher left-right scores indicate more right-wing positions, this means right-wing parties were less supportive of those minorities, consistent with such minorities being associated with the political left.

dependent_variable: Number of actions/button presses identified while watching the video as instances where the actor made a choice
main_predictor: Cultural context/national sample (U.S. American vs Indian)
sample_definition: Study 3 participants assigned to the construal-of-choice condition with non-missing numactions data; control/touch-object condition excluded
model_specification: Two-sample independent t-test comparing mean number of choice identifications between U.S. and Indian participants in the choice condition, using pooled variance
operationalization_notes: Study 3 directly tested the part of the claim concerning construal of other individuals' ongoing behaviors; restricting to the choice condition focuses the analysis on identifying another person's behaviors as choices rather than on the control task of identifying object touches.
reasoning: Among Study 3 participants in the construal-of-choice condition, U.S. participants identified more of the actor's behaviors as choices (M = 38.33, n = 30) than Indian participants (M = 22.68, n = 34). An independent-samples t-test gave t(62) = 3.11, p = .0029, supporting the claim that U.S. Americans were more likely than Indians to construe another individual's behaviors as choices.

dependent_variable: Reverse-coded willingness to disclose scores, interpreted as willingness to self-censor (WSC), for each recipient category
main_predictor: Within-subject information recipient category: close relations, in-group superiors, in-group NGOs, out-group NGOs
sample_definition: All 71 Study 1 Israeli-Jewish participants in the provided Study 1.sav dataset with complete WSC ratings
model_specification: One-way repeated-measures ANOVA testing the within-participant effect of recipient category on WSC
operationalization_notes: Study 1 measured each participant's WSC toward four potential recipients varying in social distance and public dissemination capability; the repeated-measures ANOVA directly tests whether WSC differs across these recipient categories in the original Study 1 design.
reasoning: In a one-way repeated-measures ANOVA on the four Study 1 WSC recipient ratings, recipient category significantly affected WSC, F(3, 210) = 47.85, p = 1.31e-23. The sample means increased from close relations (M = 2.99) and superiors (M = 3.01) to Israeli NGOs (M = 4.06) and outside NGOs (M = 4.73), supporting higher self-censorship for more distant/public recipients.

dependent_variable: log(total output + 1), where total output is the subject's number of correctly completed blocks summed over periods 1-8
main_predictor: T_Continuous wage profile indicator, compared with the constant-wage Baseline profile
sample_definition: Agents in the main experiment with complete observations across all 8 periods; period-level data aggregated to one observation per agent (Baseline, T_Sudden, T_Successive, and T_Continuous profiles), N=211

The cue-by-connectedness interaction was negative and statistically significant (z = -2.10, p = .0357), meaning that the opportunity-cost cue reduced purchase likelihood more strongly among respondents higher in connectedness.

dependent_variable: Referral is female (REF_female)
main_predictor: Conventional applicant is male versus female (OP_female coded 0 vs 1; contrast computed as male CA minus female CA)
sample_definition: Conventional applicants assigned to the either-gender referral treatment with nonmissing CA gender and observed referral gender; excludes gender-restricted treatments and observations without observed referral gender.
model_specification: Two-sample pooled z-test comparing the proportion of female referrals between male and female conventional applicants.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies the unrestricted/either-gender referral condition as the relevant setting for whether men versus women CAs choose to refer women, and Table 1 panel C uses referrals in this treatment arm. I therefore tested the raw difference in referral-female proportions by CA gender in that subsample.
reasoning: Among either-gender treatment referrals with observed referral gender, male CAs referred women in 30 of 133 cases (22.6%), whereas female CAs referred women in 37 of 87 cases (42.5%). A pooled two-sample test for the difference in proportions, computed as male CA rate minus female CA rate, gave z = -3.15, p = 0.00165, supporting the claim that CA men are less likely to refer women than CA women.

dependent_variable: Copying-adjusted standardized twelfth-grade ALI mathematics test score in program year 3
main_predictor: Treatment 3 assignment (aligned incentives for students, mathematics teachers, other teachers, and administrators), compared with control
sample_definition: Students in the 2008/9 tenth-grade entry cohort in the table_7_gr12_yr3 dataset, observed as twelfth graders in the 2010/11 program year, with nonmissing regression covariates; N=11,314 students in 87 schools.
model_specification: OLS regression of adjusted standardized ALI math score on T1, T2, and T3 indicators, using control schools as the reference group; standard errors clustered by school. The reported statistic is the t-test for the T3 coefficient.

operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Table 7 impact specification and focuses on the claim's T3 incentive package. I used the copying-adjusted outcome by replacing identified copiers' ALI scores with predictions from a control noncopier regression on ninth-grade ENLACE, twelfth-grade ENLACE, and missing-score indicators, then estimated the T3-vs-control treatment effect.
reasoning: In a school-clustered OLS regression for the 2008/9 entering tenth-grade cohort observed in twelfth grade in program year 3, the T3 coefficient was 56.96 standardized ALI-score points (about 0.57 SD) with cluster-robust SE 15.07, t(86)=3.78, p=0.00029. This provides clear evidence that the ALI incentive package involving students, teachers, and administrators increased mathematics test scores relative to control schools.

dependent_variable: Subject-level proportion of intertemporal choices in which the earlier payment was chosen (impatient choices)
main_predictor: Ethnicity-salience treatment indicator
sample_definition: Experiment 1 observations identified as Asian-American (raceA == 1), excluding non-Asian, white, other, unknown race, and observations with missing treatment or outcome; N = 71 subjects

operationalization_notes: The paper's Experiment 1 directly tests the Asian-American ethnic-identity claim; I used the subject-level percentage of impatient intertemporal choices reported in the dataset because the verbal claim refers to making more patient choices.
reasoning: Among Asian-American Experiment 1 subjects, the ethnicity-salience group chose the impatient option less often than controls (12.6% vs. 26.4%). A difference-in-means/OLS test of impatient-choice share on ethnicity salience gave t(69) = -3.43, p = 0.0010, supporting the claim that the prime made choices more patient.

dependent_variable: Subject-level mean cooperation rate (percentage of time cooperating) averaged across all 23 supergames
main_predictor: Termination rule in the short-duration treatments: deterministic horizon versus stochastic horizon

model_specification: Welch independent-samples t-test comparing subject-average cooperation rates between the two short-duration treatments
operationalization_notes: The paper defines cooperation rate as the fraction of time a subject spends cooperating and averages this across supergames to address non-independence; I used that subject-level outcome and directly compared the two treatment groups named in the claim.
reasoning: Among subjects in the two short-duration treatments, the mean subject-level cooperation rate was 63.28% under deterministic horizons versus 52.32% under stochastic horizons. A Welch two-sample t-test on subject averages gave t(79.19)=3.44, p=0.00094, supporting higher cooperation with deterministic horizons.

dependent_variable: pldist1: absolute ideological distance between the plurality vote-winning/largest party and the manifesto-estimated median voter on the 0-100 left-right scale
main_predictor: SMD election rules indicator (SMD vs PR)
sample_definition: All elections in powell_original.dta with non-missing pldist1 and non-missing SMD/PR classification; two elections with missing SMD classification were excluded, yielding 85 SMD and 244 PR elections.

operationalization_notes: Hypothesis 4a implies that SMD party competition should pull plurality winners toward the median; I operationalized this as lower plurality-winner-to-median distance under SMD than under PR, using the paper's manifesto-based distance measure available across the full time series.
reasoning: Using the manifesto election data, plurality-winner distance from the median voter was not smaller in SMD elections than in PR elections. The mean distance was slightly larger under SMD (11.40, n=85) than under PR (11.07, n=244), Welch t(181.04)=0.28 with one-sided p=0.61 for the hypothesized SMD < PR direction.

dependent_variable: nwar1 (indicator that a new civil war occurred)
main_predictor: T2nemths1 (months from civil war end to first postconflict national election)
