This indicates that later elections are associated with a lower likelihood of renewed war, so earlier elections are associated with a higher likelihood of renewed fighting, albeit at a weak conventional significance level.

dependent_variable: Femininity index: mean of the three feminine trait ratings (feminine, gentle, sensitive)
main_predictor: Target environmental behavior condition (green/reusable canvas bag vs. nongreen/plastic bag)
sample_definition: All 194 Study 2 participants with assigned target gender and behavior condition; no exclusions.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares factorial ANOVA with sum-to-zero coding: femininity index ~ behavior * target gender; Type III test for the main effect of behavior.
controls: Target gender and the behavior-by-target-gender interaction included as design factors; no demographic covariates.
operationalization_notes: This follows Study 2's primary test of the quoted claim: averaging the three feminine traits into a femininity index and testing whether it differs by green versus nongreen behavior while accounting for the target's gender in the 2x2 design.
reasoning: In a 2 (green vs. nongreen behavior) by 2 (male vs. female target) ANOVA predicting the femininity index, the main effect of green behavior was significant, F(1, 190) = 43.998, p = 3.33e-10. Targets shown engaging in green behavior had higher femininity ratings than targets shown engaging in nongreen behavior, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Subject-level decision error rate in the LV format, measured as the proportion of the 10 LV choices in which the dominated lottery was chosen; the equal-risk row 5 was counted as no error.
main_predictor: Degree of risk aversion, measured as the average number of safe choices across the PV and RV formats.
sample_definition: Original RiskData.dta excluding the two non-subject test stations identified by age 99; restricted to subjects with average PV/RV safe choices >= 5, yielding N = 79 risk-averse subjects.
model_specification: Pearson correlation test between subject-level LV error rate and average PV/RV safe choices.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Figure 4 approach: risk aversion is the average number of safe choices in the two elicitation tasks, and decision error is the rate of dominated-lottery choices in the LV task among risk-averse subjects.
reasoning: Among the 79 risk-averse subjects, the Pearson correlation between risk aversion and LV error rate was r = -0.4625, df = 77, p = 0.0000178. The negative and statistically significant association indicates that subjects with more safe choices in the PV/RV tasks made fewer stochastic-dominance errors, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Desired compensation, coded as midpoint of reported salary range in thousands of dollars
main_predictor: Public treatment indicator (answers expected to be discussed as 'your' answers with classmates) versus private/anonymized treatment
sample_definition: Single female MBA students in the primary experiment with non-missing desired compensation responses
model_specification: OLS regression of desired compensation on a public-treatment indicator, using HC1 robust standard errors; reported t test for the treatment coefficient
operationalization_notes: The paper's primary-experiment methods test this claim by comparing public versus private questionnaire versions within the single-women subgroup; salary ranges were coded to midpoints as described in the paper.
reasoning: Among single female students, the public-treatment group reported lower desired compensation than the private-treatment group (112.93 vs. 131.05 thousand dollars). In an OLS regression with robust standard errors, the public-treatment coefficient was -18.12 thousand dollars, t(58) = -2.22, p = 0.030, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: WTP_dummy: indicator that the parent prefers a R$120 conditional cash transfer to a strictly larger unconditional cash transfer
main_predictor: Text-message monitoring treatment versus baseline treatment
sample_definition: Parents randomly assigned to the baseline treatment (treatment==1) or text-message treatment (treatment==2) with non-missing WTP_dummy; nonclassroom and don't-tell treatment arms excluded
model_specification: Two-sample pooled z-test comparing the proportion with WTP_dummy=1 in the text-message treatment against the baseline treatment
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns a drop in the proportion of parents willing to pay to keep conditionality when free text-message monitoring is offered, so I directly compared the binary willingness-to-pay outcome across the baseline and text-message experimental cells.
reasoning: In the baseline group, 49 of 60 parents (81.7%) were willing to pay to keep the conditionality, compared with 10 of 51 parents (19.6%) in the text-message treatment. A two-sample pooled test of proportions gives z = -6.53, p = 6.59e-11, indicating a large and statistically significant drop under text-message monitoring.

dependent_variable: Monthly number of homicides of males aged 15-39 (SINAIS proxy for DTO-related violence)
main_predictor: Indicator for 1-6 months after a drug cartel leader capture or killing in the municipality (lpub_after06)
sample_definition: Municipality-months from December 2006 through December 2010 for municipalities where a leader was captured/killed, excluding Ciudad Juarez; 13 municipalities x 49 months = 637 observations.
model_specification: Negative binomial regression with municipality fixed effects and month fixed effects; cluster-robust standard errors by municipality.
controls: Population of males aged 15-39; indicators for 7-12 months and more than 12 months after leader capture; indicators for 1-6, 7-12, and more than 12 months after lieutenant capture; municipality and time fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies homicides of males aged 15-39 as the SINAIS-based proxy for DTO-related violence and uses negative binomial models over December 2006-December 2010. I used the paper's restricted treated-municipality difference-in-differences specification for leader captures and tested the short-term leader-capture coefficient most directly tied to the claim.
reasoning: In a negative binomial fixed-effects model, the coefficient for the first 1-6 months after a leader capture/kill was positive (log coefficient = 0.272) and statistically significant, z = 2.15, p = 0.032. This corresponds to higher short-term DTO-related homicide counts after leader neutralizations in the treated municipalities, supporting the study's claim.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of bootstrapped partial semantic networks
main_predictor: Openness to experience group (high vs. low)
sample_definition: All 516 cleaned participants were included, split into 258 low- and 258 high-openness participants by the no-intellect openness latent score; semantic-network nodes were cleaned animal fluency responses generated by at least two participants in both groups, and the t-test used 1000 randomly sampled 50%-node partial networks per group.
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test comparing high- versus low-openness groups on ASPL from 1000 bootstrapped 50%-node partial networks; networks were based on cosine similarity matrices, filtered with a greedy TMFG-style procedure, then binarized as unweighted undirected graphs.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies lower ASPL as the network measure most directly corresponding to greater interconnection and uses partial bootstrapped semantic networks to statistically compare openness groups; I therefore used ASPL from 50%-node bootstrapped partial networks as the single primary operationalization.
reasoning: In 1000 50%-node partial semantic-network bootstraps per openness group, the high-openness networks had lower average shortest path length than the low-openness networks (M_high = 2.503, M_low = 2.640), t(1998) = -18.47, p = 1.97e-70. Because lower ASPL indexes greater interconnection, this supports the claim that the high-openness group's network was more interconnected.

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Rights Index (0-8, higher = better protection)
main_predictor: Reliance on Taxes: tax and social security contributions as percent of total government revenue (tax_rev_new)
sample_definition: Country-year observations from the supplied dataset with non-missing CIRI Physical Integrity Index, Reliance on Taxes, Size of Government Revenues, lagged CIRI Physical Integrity Index, and all baseline controls; 1982-2007 complete cases (N = 1739).

controls: Size of Government Revenues, log population size, income per capita, Polity IV democracy, external conflict, internal armed conflict, UK colony indicator, and lagged CIRI Physical Integrity Rights Index.
operationalization_notes: I followed the paper's main time-series cross-sectional ordered probit specification for physical integrity rights, using the baseline controls and lagged dependent variable most directly tied to the tax-reliance claim.

This supports the claim that greater reliance on tax revenue is associated with better protection of physical integrity rights, conditional on the included controls and the lagged outcome.

dependent_variable: School GCSE pass rate: percent/fraction of grade 11 students passing five or more GCSE exams at grades A-C (pt_gcse_5_a_c)
main_predictor: Actual GM status (gm_school), instrumented by winning the first GM vote (gm_win)
sample_definition: Main GM sample schools with nonmissing pass-rate data in pooled post-vote years base+2 through base+8; 4,954 school-year observations from 726 schools.

operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's primary school-performance analysis for the claim: pass rates are the main achievement outcome, and the pooled base+2 to base+8 2SLS RD estimates the treatment effect of conversion rather than only the intention-to-treat effect of a vote win.

This supports the claim that schools converting to GM status experienced improved student achievement.

dependent_variable: Participated (lab), coded 1 if the student actually participated in the later laboratory experiment and 0 otherwise
main_predictor: Sent_Class: amount sent as Player A in the classroom trust game ($0, $10, or $20)

reasoning: In a probit model predicting actual lab participation, the coefficient on amount sent in the classroom trust game was negative (b = -0.0231) with a cluster-robust z = -2.664, p = 0.0077, among 658 students with nonmissing sending decisions. dependent_variable: Indicator that the illness episode was treated with an ACT (took_act)

dependent_variable: Normalized combined PIAT math, reading recognition, and reading comprehension score
main_predictor: Current family income in $1,000s of year-2000 dollars, constructed from earned, unearned, and nontaxable family income components

This supports the directional claim that higher income is associated with higher combined math/reading scores, though this operationalization is associational rather than the paper's full IV design.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs)
main_predictor: Single childless family structure indicator (singchild1: 1 = single/childless, 0 = all other family structures)

dependent_variable: ProperName: indicator that an email response began with a named greeting/proper-name salutation
main_predictor: Hispanic-name treatment indicator, compared with white-name treatment as the reference category

operationalization_notes: The paper's tone analysis uses proper-name greeting among responses and a logit model with race/ethnicity indicators and community/contact controls. Because the public dataset anonymizes continuous demographics into thirds, I used the corresponding tertile indicators as controls.
reasoning: In a logistic regression of whether the response began with a proper-name greeting, the Hispanic-name coefficient relative to the white-name reference group was negative (log-odds coefficient = -0.763) and statistically significant, z = -3.47, p = 0.00052, N = 549. dependent_variable: Indicator for seller shading (low quality; qualityc == 1)
main_predictor: Flexible contract indicator (contracttypec == 2) relative to rigid contracts

operationalization_notes: The paper analyzes the rigid-versus-flexible shading contrast in the baseline treatment's good state because both contract types can trade there; bad-state rigid contracts do not involve a seller quality decision. I used the paper-guided Table 3 specification but coded the outcome directly as shading rather than normal quality.
reasoning: In the baseline good-state observations, rigid contracts had shading in 25/398 cases (6.3%) and flexible contracts in 102/407 cases (25.1%). In an OLS linear probability model for shading with session-clustered standard errors, the flexible-contract coefficient was +0.335 at the competitive price, t(4)=5.60, p=0.00498, indicating substantially more shading under flexible than rigid contracts.

dependent_variable: Percent change in state-level carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel combustion (EPA MMTCO2), 2007 to 2013
main_predictor: Percent change in average weekly working hours per worker, 2007 to 2013

operationalization_notes: The paper's results section presents a scatterplot/correlation of state-level percent changes over 2007–2013, which directly operationalizes the claim of a positive relationship over this period.

This supports the study's claim of a positive state-level relationship over the 2007–2013 period.

dependent_variable: Considered attack against a nuclear program in the following year (dataset variable consider1)
main_predictor: Violent militarized conflict/use of force in the dyad (hostileMID)
sample_definition: Politically relevant directed dyad-years involving proliferating target states, 1941-2000, with complete data for the full considered-attack model; N = 5,360.

dependent_variable: Indicator that the county became a new splinter district in the electoral wave (splinter)
main_predictor: DEC share ratio: county share of District Executive Committee seats divided by county share of district population (lower values indicate greater political marginalization)
sample_definition: County-wave observations for electoral waves 1996-2000, 2001-2005, and 2006-2010; restricted to counties (ctype == 1) and complete cases on the variables in the model.

controls: Ethnic marginalization, development summary index, number of counties in district, lagged breakup status, support for losing LC5 chair candidate, opposed LC5 election indicator, lagged Museveni vote share and its square, log county population, ethnic fractionalization, region fixed effects, and electoral-wave fixed effects.

reasoning: In a GEE logistic regression of whether a county became a splinter district, the coefficient on DEC share ratio was negative and statistically significant (z = -3.16, p = 0.0016, N = 429). Because lower DEC representation relative to population indicates greater political marginalization, this supports the claim that politically marginalized counties were more likely to secede into new districts.

dependent_variable: Dichotomous diplomatic recognition: State B recognizes State A (recog1duml)
main_predictor: State A nuclear weapons status (nukeduma)
sample_definition: Directed dyad observations from 1945-2000 with non-missing diplomatic recognition, nuclear status, and covariates; N = 213,454.

reasoning: In a probit model for whether State B recognizes State A, the coefficient for State A nuclear-weapons status was positive (b = 0.1811) with a dyad-cluster-robust SE of 0.0418, giving z = 4.33 and p = 1.47e-5. This supports the claim that nuclear-capable states are more likely to be recognized by other nations.

dependent_variable: Log absolute change in pro-immigration attitude index between wave 2 and wave 3 (change_w3w2_log)
main_predictor: Group-level mean DQI level of justification/rational justification in speech acts (DQ_jlev)
sample_definition: EuroPolis participants in coded small-group discussions with complete data on wave-2 and wave-3 immigration opinion change, group justification, and all covariates; N = 174 individuals nested in 13 small groups.
model_specification: Linear mixed-effects regression estimated by REML with a random intercept for small discussion group; the reported test is the Wald z test for DQ_jlev.
controls: Gender/female, age, education, working class, Catholic, Protestant, religiosity, left-right ideology and squared term, intended left-party vote, intended right-party vote, change in knowledge, four perceived clarification variables (other participants, experts, politicians, briefing material), and social conformity pressure indicators for being above or below the group mean pre-deliberation opinion.
operationalization_notes: The paper's deliberative-influence section tests this claim by treating justification rationality as a group resource and predicting the magnitude of immigration opinion change from wave 2 to wave 3, so I used that specification and its complete-case sample.

This supports the claim that participants changed their opinions more when rational justification was used more in the group discussions.

dependent_variable: Matching-group mean effort rate: proportion of individual decisions to work hard across all six periods
main_predictor: Reward scheme within complementarity production technology: symmetrical reward scheme (444COM) versus discriminating reward scheme (345COM)
sample_definition: Independent matching groups in the complementarity treatments only; all available subject-period effort decisions across periods 1-6, aggregated to the matching-group level (11 groups in 444COM and 12 groups in 345COM).
model_specification: One-sided Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon rank-sum test comparing matching-group mean effort rates, with alternative 444COM < 345COM; reported z uses tie-corrected normal approximation with continuity correction.
operationalization_notes: The paper treats matching groups as the independent units for all-round analyses, so I aggregated repeated individual effort decisions to each matching group and compared the two cost-equivalent reward schemes under complementarity, which is the direct contrast in the claim.
reasoning: Among complementarity treatments, the symmetric-reward matching groups (444COM) had lower mean effort over all six periods (M = 0.722, n = 11 groups) than the cost-equivalent discriminating-reward groups (345COM; M = 0.917, n = 12 groups). A one-sided Mann-Whitney rank-sum test on independent matching-group averages gave U = 37 and z = -1.814, p = 0.035, supporting the claim that the symmetrical reward scheme elicits lower effort under complementarity.

dependent_variable: Within-senator difference in the anti-minus-pro immigration action balance of the response letter, coded from mentions of anti-immigration actions minus mentions of pro-immigration actions.
main_predictor: Constituent letter position: anti-immigration versus pro-immigration.
sample_definition: U.S. senators in the field experiment who sent usable responses to both the anti-immigration and pro-immigration constituent letters (56 senators); the sign-test statistic is based on the 14 non-tied within-senator paired differences.
model_specification: Paired within-subjects sign test comparing each senator's anti-minus-pro action balance in the anti-immigration response with the same balance in the pro-immigration response.
controls: None; within-senator paired design controls for time-invariant senator characteristics.
operationalization_notes: This operationalizes audience tailoring using the paper's primary Experiment 1 measure in Table 2: whether senators selectively mentioned compensating or reinforcing pro- and anti-immigration actions in letters to constituents with opposing immigration positions.
reasoning: Among the 56 senators who responded to both letters, the mean anti-minus-pro action balance was 0.429 in anti-immigration constituent letters versus 0.196 in pro-immigration constituent letters, a within-senator difference of 0.232 in the predicted direction. A two-sided paired sign test on the 14 non-tied senators gave z = 3.207, p = 0.00183, supporting the conclusion that senators tailored their explanations to audience position.

dependent_variable: Log wage gain at migration, log(lastUsWageAdjusted / lastHomeWageAdjusted)
main_predictor: Education category indicator for no high school (<9 years of schooling) versus omitted college degree category (>=16 years)
sample_definition: All observations in the public MMP/LAMP wage_gain_table.xlsx with nonmissing education, country, and adjusted pre- and postmigration wages; N=2854.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression with education-category dummies and country fixed effects; t-test of the no-high-school dummy coefficient relative to college graduates.
operationalization_notes: The paper's Table III operationalizes the claim by estimating log wage gains as a function of five education groups, controlling for country fixed effects, with college graduates omitted. I applied that specification to the readable public MMP/LAMP wage-gain table available in the dataset archive.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of log wage gain on education categories with country fixed effects, the no-high-school coefficient relative to college graduates was positive (0.197 log points, about 22% higher), but not statistically significant: t(2840)=1.52, p=0.128. Thus this available-data analysis points in the claimed direction but is inconclusive statistically.

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses categorized as indicating the learned negative meaning of the cue, combined across homograph and nonhomograph cues (FAbaseC and FAsuppC).
main_predictor: Cue status within subjects: baseline (learned but not practiced) versus suppression (learned and repeatedly suppressed).
sample_definition: Experiment 2 final-analysis participants in the nonruminator group only (Group = 1), n = 27; included all nonruminators present in Ashley_labels.sav with baseline and suppression free-association percentages.
model_specification: Within-subject baseline-versus-suppression comparison implemented as an ANOVA on participant difference scores with the three-level counterbalancing condition as a between-subject blocking factor; F test for the nonzero grand mean difference.
controls: Counterbalancing condition (CB) included as a blocking factor; no other covariates.
operationalization_notes: The claim refers to nonruminators showing benefits of suppression in transfer tasks. The available dataset contains Experiment 2 free-association transfer-task data, and the paper identifies the baseline-versus-suppression contrast among nonruminators as the direct test of suppression-induced forgetting, so I tested that contrast on the combined free-association outcome.
reasoning: Among nonruminators, cues from the suppression condition elicited fewer learned-negative-meaning free associations than baseline cues (M = 29.63% vs. 45.68%). A repeated-measures baseline-vs-suppression test controlling for counterbalancing condition was significant, F(1,24) = 10.94, p = .00296, supporting a suppression benefit in the transfer task.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being, measured as the mean of the recoded eight-item CES-D well-being scale (higher scores = better well-being)
main_predictor: Interaction between being childless (vs being a parent) and country-level standardized disapproval of childlessness (lower values indicate more tolerant norms)
sample_definition: Respondents in the prepared ESS 2006 data for the 24 included European countries, aged over 40, excluding cases with missing values on the outcome, parental status, country, gender, age, marital status, education, parental education, religious attendance, paid work, born-in-country, individual disapproval of childlessness, or individual social contacts; N = 24,420.
model_specification: Linear regression of psychological well-being on childlessness, country fixed effects, and the childless × country-level disapproval interaction, with standard errors clustered by country.
controls: Gender; age and age squared; marital status; respondent education; parental education; religious attendance; paid employment; born in country; individual-level disapproval of childlessness; individual social contacts; and country fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: The paper's claim concerns a cross-level moderation of the childlessness-well-being association by societal norms. I combined the two parental categories into one parent reference group to test the overall childless-versus-parent disadvantage and used the paper's country-level norm measure from the supplied recoded dataset; country fixed effects account for all country-level intercept differences while the interaction tests whether the childless-parent gap varies systematically with national tolerance.
reasoning: In a country-fixed-effects OLS model with standard errors clustered by country, the childless × national disapproval interaction was negative and statistically significant, t(23) = -4.38, p = 0.00022. Because higher values of the country norm variable mean more disapproval of childlessness, this indicates that childless adults' well-being disadvantage relative to parents is larger in less tolerant countries and therefore smaller in more tolerant countries.

dependent_variable: DSM5_Total (summed DSM-5 Self-Rated Level 1 Cross-Cutting Symptom Measure total psychopathology score)
main_predictor: MiniK_Total (summed Mini-K life history strategy score; higher scores indicate slower life strategy)
sample_definition: All 138 participants in the final dataset with complete Age, DSM5_Total, and MiniK_Total data; no additional exclusions.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares linear regression: DSM5_Total ~ MiniK_Total + Age; reported t test for the MiniK_Total regression coefficient, equivalent to the age-adjusted partial correlation.
operationalization_notes: The paper's main analysis for this claim used age-adjusted partial correlations between life-history measures and total psychopathology. I used Mini-K as the focal life-history measure because the methods describe it as better suited for behavioral traits of life-history strategy, and total DSM-5 symptom score directly operationalizes overall psychopathology severity.
reasoning: In a linear regression of total DSM-5 psychopathology symptoms on Mini-K life-history score controlling for age, the Mini-K coefficient was negative and highly significant, t(135) = -6.95, p = 1.41e-10. Because higher Mini-K scores indicate a slower life-history strategy, this negative association means faster life strategies were associated with greater psychopathology symptoms.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (sum of correct answers on the 20-item political knowledge test)
main_predictor: Stereotype activation condition: stereotype not activated vs. stereotype activated by gender difference statement
sample_definition: Study 2 observations with dataset Filter==1, restricted to female participants (gender_factor==1) assigned to condition 0 or condition 2 and with non-missing PolWis_score; total N=143.
model_specification: One-sided pooled-variance independent-samples t-test comparing female participants in condition 0 against female participants in condition 2, with alternative mean(condition 0) > mean(condition 2).
operationalization_notes: The quoted claim is a direct pairwise comparison of female participants' political knowledge scores between the first and third stereotype-activation conditions, so I used the same filtered Study 2 analytic sample and tested that directional simple contrast directly.
reasoning: Among filtered female participants, those in the stereotype-not-activated condition scored higher on the political knowledge test (n=73, M=8.90) than those in the gender-difference-statement condition (n=70, M=7.03). A one-sided pooled independent-samples t-test for the directional contrast gave t(141)=2.57, p=0.0056, supporting the claimed direction.

dependent_variable: GDP growth rate at t+2 (f2gdpidx; last year = 100)
main_predictor: Indicator that either the city party secretary or mayor was connected to the incumbent provincial party secretary (msec2currentsec == 1 or mayor2currentsec == 1)
sample_definition: City-year observations from 2000-2011 excluding Tibet, with nonmissing outcome, connection indicator, economic controls, age and tenure controls; N = 3,693 city-years in 326 cities.
model_specification: OLS fixed-effects regression of GDP growth at t+2 on connected-to-provincial-secretary indicator, city fixed effects, and province-by-year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by city with finite-sample correction.
controls: Fiscal expenditure minus revenue at t+1; predecessor-final-year city economic controls for both secretary and mayor predecessors: GDP growth, log GDP, log population, and log fixed-asset investment; leader controls for secretary and mayor: age, college education indicator (missing coded 0), female indicator, and tenure-category dummies for <1, 1-3, and 3-5 years in current position.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's baseline Model 3 specification for the central claim, using the overall GDP growth outcome at t+2 and defining connection as either top city leader having a patronage tie to the current provincial secretary.
reasoning: In a city and province-year fixed-effects regression, the coefficient for being connected to the incumbent provincial secretary was positive (0.3823 GDP-growth-index points) with a cluster-robust t statistic of 2.87 using 326 city clusters (p = 0.0044). This supports the claim that connected city leaders delivered faster subsequent economic growth than unconnected leaders.

dependent_variable: Indicator that a foreign player-year in the Danish first league was top-quality (counted as stop/(stop+slow), with top-quality based on national-team selection as in Figure 3)
main_predictor: Post-reform period after the Danish foreigner tax scheme (1991-2008 vs. 1985-1990)
sample_definition: Foreign player-year counts in Denmark's first league from the basesynthetic_control data, restricted to 1985-2008; pre-reform years 1985-1990 and post-reform years 1991-2008; observations are the 388 foreign player-year counts underlying stop and slow.
model_specification: Two-sample z test for equality of proportions comparing the top-quality share among Danish foreign players before versus after the reform.
operationalization_notes: The claim is specifically about the ability composition of foreigners in Denmark, so I used the paper's Figure 3 Denmark reform window and its top- versus lower-quality foreign-player counts, and tested whether the top-quality share among foreign players increased after the reform.
reasoning: Using Denmark foreign player-year counts from 1985-2008, the fraction of foreign players who were top-quality rose from 4/24 = 16.7% before the 1991 tax scheme to 195/364 = 53.6% afterward. A two-sample proportions test gives z = 3.50, two-sided p = 0.00046, supporting a shift in the ability composition of foreign players toward higher-ability players after the tax cut.

dependent_variable: Willingness to pay to protect the environment scale, computed as the mean of income_en, tax_en, and reverse-scored not_my_money_re items
main_predictor: Intrinsic relative to extrinsic values (I/E), computed from the Aspiration Index by person-centering value items, reversing centered extrinsic items, and averaging centered intrinsic plus reversed centered extrinsic items
sample_definition: All 155 retained Study 1 participants in the provided dataset with non-missing WTP, I/E, age, and sex variables
model_specification: Ordinary least squares linear regression of WTP on I/E, age, and male gender indicator; the reported statistic is the t-test for the I/E coefficient
operationalization_notes: The paper's Study 1 methods identify WTP as the target outcome and I/E values as the focal predictor, with age and gender included as demographic controls in the predictive model; I therefore used the analogous observed-variable OLS regression on the provided Study 1 data.
reasoning: In the Study 1 cleaned sample (N = 155), intrinsic relative to extrinsic values positively predicted willingness to pay in an OLS regression controlling for age and gender, b = 0.7095, t(151) = 5.195, p = 6.53e-7. Thus, participants with higher relative intrinsic value endorsement reported higher willingness to pay to protect the environment.

dependent_variable: Logged annual imports of disputed products into the defendant market after the dispute ended (ln_imports).
main_predictor: Complainant status for the defendant-trade-partner-dispute observation (complainant = 1 vs. all non-complainant WTO members).
sample_definition: Observations from disputes that ended in early settlement, restricted to the five years after the notified dispute end year and to cases with complete data on the dependent variable and covariates; N = 6,027 dispute-partner-year observations, clustered over 45 dispute_combined clusters.
model_specification: OLS linear regression with dispute fixed effects and cluster-robust standard errors by dispute_combined; main result is the t test for the complainant coefficient.
controls: Defendant GDP (log), partner GDP (log), democratic pair, lagged disputed imports at t-1 (logged), and total imports (logged), plus dispute fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: I used the paper's Model 2 operationalization because it directly tests the claim that private early settlements produce unequal post-dispute trade gains for complainants relative to non-complainants.
reasoning: In the early-settlement (private) subsample, the complainant indicator is positive and statistically significant: b = 0.4301, cluster-robust SE = 0.1804, t(44) = 2.384, p = 0.0215. This indicates that defendants' post-dispute imports of disputed products were higher from complainant countries than from the rest of the WTO membership, consistent with discriminatory gains under private settlement.

dependent_variable: entre_wage: country-year entrepreneurship rate for new businesses less than 42 months old that pay wages
main_predictor: medage_20_64: median age among ages 20-64
sample_definition: All GEM country-year observations in GEM_Country_Year.dta with nonmissing outcome, predictor, year, weight, and country identifier; 393 country-year cells from 82 countries, 2001-2010.
model_specification: Weighted least squares linear regression of entrepreneurship rate on median age and year indicators, using nobs_cy as analytic weights; standard errors clustered by country.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's country-year specification directly tied to the quoted claim, using the main entrepreneurship definition and median-age demographic measure from Table 2 column 3.
reasoning: In a weighted country-year regression with year fixed effects and country-clustered standard errors, median age was negatively associated with early-stage business ownership paying wages (coefficient = -0.00732, t(81) = -5.71, p = 1.78e-7). Thus, lower median age predicts higher new business formation, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Perceived arm length divided by actual arm length for each arm
main_predictor: Arm side (right vs. left) within right-handed participants
sample_definition: Experiment 1 participants coded as right-handed (Handedness = 2) with nonmissing perceived and actual left- and right-arm length data; n = 15.
model_specification: Paired-samples t test comparing RatioRight to RatioLeft, using a directional alternative that RatioRight > RatioLeft.
operationalization_notes: The paper's Experiment 1 operationalized arm-length perception as perceived/actual length ratios and tested the right-handed subgroup with a paired comparison of right versus left arm; this directly targets the directional claim.
reasoning: Among the 15 right-handed participants in Experiment 1, perceived/actual arm-length ratios were higher for the right arm (M = 0.970) than for the left arm (M = 0.920). A directional paired-samples t test on the right-minus-left ratio difference gave t(14) = 2.123, one-sided p = 0.026, supporting the claim that right-handed participants perceived their right arms as longer relative to actual length than their left arms.

dependent_variable: dv_index3: mean of three 1-7 items assessing felt appreciated, valued, and satisfied with the conference center's acknowledgment
main_predictor: condition: verbal acknowledgment only vs financial acknowledgment with $0.05
sample_definition: Study 1a hotel conference center participants who finished the study and had non-missing dependent-variable data; the two respondents flagged as not finishing/without DV responses were excluded
model_specification: One-way between-subjects ANOVA/OLS regression of dv_index3 on acknowledgment condition
operationalization_notes: The available dataset is Study 1a, which directly operationalizes the published claim by comparing a small monetary financial acknowledgment to an otherwise similar verbal acknowledgment after participants provided a customer review.
reasoning: In the Study 1a hotel field-study data, participants receiving the $0.05 financial acknowledgment reported lower felt appreciation/valuation/satisfaction (M = 4.38, n = 31) than those receiving the verbal acknowledgment (M = 5.57, n = 18). A one-way ANOVA showed this difference was statistically significant, F(1,47) = 8.499, p = 0.00543, supporting the trivialization-effect claim.

dependent_variable: s_tot: standardized combined midterm plus final exam score
main_predictor: avg5_girl: share female among the five nearest peers (desk mate plus neighbor-4 peers)
sample_definition: Female students only, excluding favored/special-seat students, with complete outcome, peer, baseline covariate, block, and classroom data (N=245).
model_specification: OLS regression of standardized exam score on neighbor-5 female share and neighbor-5 average baseline score, with randomization-block fixed effects; inference used classroom-clustered standard errors with 12 classroom clusters.
controls: Average baseline score of neighbor-5 peers; student's baseline test score, height, age, birth order, mother's education, father's education, baseline interest in Chinese, math, and English; desk-mate favored status; share favored among neighbor-4 peers; randomization-block fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: This is the most direct operationalization of the page-91 claim because the claim compares five female versus five male neighbors for female students; the neighbor-5 specification combines the desk mate and four adjacent peers as in the paper's main heterogeneous-effects analysis.
reasoning: Among non-favored female students, the coefficient for the share female among neighbor-5 peers was positive (0.211 SD); using the classroom-clustered SE of 0.076 gives t(11)=2.77, p=0.018. Thus the data support the claim that moving a girl from five male neighbors to five female neighbors increases her test scores.

dependent_variable: Absolute change in mean alcohol attitude from Time 1 to the one-year follow-up (Time 3); higher scores indicate greater instability.
main_predictor: Interaction between mean global attitude certainty and objective ambivalence computed from positive and negative reactions.
sample_definition: Study 2 alcohol-attitude participants with complete Time 1 attitude, certainty, positive/negative reaction, and one-year follow-up attitude data (N=135).
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of absolute attitude change on mean-centered certainty, mean-centered objective ambivalence, their interaction, and Time 1 attitude extremity.
controls: Time 1 attitude extremity, computed as the absolute distance of the mean Time 1 attitude from the scale midpoint.
operationalization_notes: I used Study 2 because it provides the paper's longitudinal one-year alcohol-attitude test. The model follows the paper's primary analysis: attitude instability is the absolute Time 1-to-follow-up attitude difference, certainty is the seven-item composite, objective ambivalence uses the similarity-intensity formula, and extremity is included as a covariate.
reasoning: In Study 2, the certainty × objective ambivalence interaction significantly predicted absolute attitude change, t(130)=3.42, p=0.00084. Because the dependent variable is instability, the positive interaction means the certainty-stability association was stronger in the stability direction when ambivalence was lower, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Aggregate electoral turnout (% of registered electorate, with U.S. measured using VAP)
main_predictor: Logged portfolio equity stock (assets plus liabilities as % of GDP), a foreign-ownership measure
sample_definition: Established OECD country lower-legislative elections from 1970-2007 with complete data for the turnout controls and portfolio equity stock; first usable election per country omitted for the lagged dependent variable (23 countries, N=227).
model_specification: OLS analogue of the paper's dynamic panel specification: turnout regressed on lagged turnout, logged portfolio equity stock, controls, country fixed effects, and country-specific quadratic time trends; standard errors clustered by country.
controls: Lagged turnout, logged registered voters, % voting-age population aged 30-69, years since last election, U.S. midterm election indicator, compulsory voting, mixed electoral system, PR system, disproportionality, effective number of parties, electoral margin, country fixed effects, and country-specific linear and quadratic trends.
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the direct ownership-constraint channel; portfolio equity stock is the paper's most mobile foreign-ownership indicator and corresponds to Table 2's direct turnout test. I used the paper's dependent variable, sample period, controls, fixed effects, and detrending strategy, estimating a transparent dynamic FE model with clustered inference on the original Turnout.dta data.
reasoning: In a dynamic country-panel model of turnout, the coefficient on logged portfolio equity stock was negative (b = -2.32) with a cluster-robust t(22) = -2.67, p = 0.014. This supports the claim that foreign ownership is associated with reduced electoral turnout.

dependent_variable: complaints_2008 (number of Better Business Bureau complaints)
main_predictor: first_A (indicator that the firm name begins with A, a number, or a symbol)
sample_definition: All 2,293 plumbing firms in final_data.dta with nonmissing complaints_2008 and first_A; 295 A/number/symbol-name firms and 1,998 other firms.
model_specification: Independent-samples pooled-variance t-test comparing mean complaints_2008 between first_A=1 and first_A=0 firms.
operationalization_notes: The verbal claim concerns the average number of service complaints for plumbing firms by whether the firm name begins with A or a number, so I used the paper's primary BBB complaints outcome and the paper's A-name indicator in the full plumbing-firm sample, without covariates.
reasoning: In the full Illinois plumbing-firm dataset, firms whose name began with A/a number/symbol averaged 1.339 Better Business Bureau complaints versus 0.248 for other firms. A pooled two-sample t-test gave t(2291)=6.79, p=1.44e-11, supporting the claim that A/number-name firms receive more complaints.

dependent_variable: dv: ordered cooperative/concession-offering bargaining strategy category from 0 to 3
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure
sample_definition: All 588 state-bargaining observations in the dataset across 23 EU bargaining interactions/phases; no observations excluded.
model_specification: Partial proportional-odds generalized ordered logit for Pr(dv > category), with the issue-linkage coefficient constrained equal across the three cutpoints and cluster-robust standard errors by bargaining interaction/phase (i_bargain).
controls: ln GDP, foreign/security-defense policy, Euro state, new member state, agreement importance, parliamentary scrutiny, qualified majority voting, publicity, Council presidency, and lagged dependent variable; agreement importance, parliamentary scrutiny, QMV, publicity, and lagged DV allowed to vary by cutpoint.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's primary Model 1 approach for Hypothesis S1: concession offering is the ordered outcome and issue-linkage structure measures how differently valued the negotiated issues are.
reasoning: In a generalized ordered logit model of concession-offering behavior, the coefficient for issue-linkage structure was positive (b = 1.2193) with a cluster-robust SE of 0.1960, giving z = 6.22 and p = 4.99e-10. Thus, observations from negotiations with more differently valued linked issues were significantly more likely to fall in higher, more concessionary strategy categories.

dependent_variable: Credit to Government and SOEs (% GDP; credittogovtstateenterp)
main_predictor: Lagged state capacity, measured by the Indicator Quality Government index (L1 icrg_qog)
sample_definition: Country-year observations from the Country Year Dataset with nonmissing directed credit, lagged directed credit, lagged IQG, lagged private credit, and consecutive prior-year data; 130 countries, years 1985-2011, N=2,682.
model_specification: One-step dynamic panel system GMM with a level equation and first-differenced equation; collapsed lagged-level instruments at lags 2 and deeper for the differenced equation and lagged-difference instruments for the level equation; country-clustered sandwich standard error; z test of the IQG coefficient.
controls: Lagged dependent variable, lagged private credit (% GDP), linear time trend, and a level-equation intercept.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Table 2 setup for the claim: directed credit is modeled dynamically as a function of state capacity while controlling for private credit as the proxy for profit potential from financial repression. I used the collapsed-instrument system-GMM specification as the single main operationalization.
reasoning: In a dynamic panel system-GMM analysis of 2,682 country-years, the coefficient on lagged state capacity (IQG) was negative (about -11.58), with z = -2.52 and two-sided p = 0.0117. Thus, conditional on lagged private credit and the dynamic controls, weaker states are associated with more credit directed to government and SOEs.

dependent_variable: MID initiation as originator in a country-year (originit)
main_predictor: Generated coup risk, operationalized as fitted values from a first-stage model of logged coup-event intensity (lcoupsum)
sample_definition: All 798 Latin American country-year observations in scamerica5.dta, 1960-1999, with nonmissing variables for the specified models
model_specification: Two-stage generated-regressor probit: first-stage OLS predicting logged coup-event intensity from the union of exogenous variables in the coup and conflict equations; second-stage probit of MID initiation on generated coup risk and conflict-equation controls, with standard errors clustered by country
controls: Previous dispute (lagdisp), ethnic fractionalization, relative power (CINC), number of borders, log number of allies, regional conflict, lagged Polity, lagged log real GDP; first-stage instruments also included recent coup, recent war, and conflict ending/forceend
operationalization_notes: The paper's primary test links threats to political survival to conflict initiation using a simultaneous-equations framework; I approximated that design directly with a two-stage generated coup-risk measure and the paper's MID-originator outcome and covariates.
reasoning: In a two-stage probit analysis of Latin American country-years, the generated coup-risk measure positively predicted MID initiation as originator (coefficient = 2.763, cluster-robust SE = 1.070), giving z = 2.583, p = 0.0098. This supports the claim that greater threats to political survival are associated with a higher likelihood of conflict involvement.

dependent_variable: d12outgroup: amount sent to an out-group/Albanian recipient in the dictator game (0 to 5 euros)
main_predictor: albregion: Primarily Albanian region (highest out-group exposure) versus omitted Primarily Serb region; borderregion included as the intermediate-exposure category
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb subjects in the replication dataset with complete dictator-game and covariate data
model_specification: Two-limit Tobit regression censored at 0 and 5 euros, with cluster-robust standard errors by experimental lab location; reported test is the z test for the albregion coefficient
controls: borderregion, female, age, education, employed, village, alphaviolence, alphadamaged, displaced
operationalization_notes: The paper operationalizes out-group bridging norms as dictator-game giving to Albanian recipients and treats region as the key proxy for proximity/contact with Albanians, so I used the paper's controlled Tobit specification for the out-group giving outcome and tested the highest-exposure versus lowest-exposure regional contrast.
reasoning: In a two-limit Tobit model for out-group dictator giving, the coefficient for living in the Primarily Albanian region rather than the Primarily Serb region was positive (b = 2.085) and very large relative to the clustered standard error (z = 31.88, p = 5.26e-223). This supports the claim that out-group bridging altruism is higher among Serbs with greater exposure/proximity to Albanians.

dependent_variable: Relative preference/enjoyment rating for the target clip versus the initial comparison clip (enjoyrelativ, 1-7 scale)
main_predictor: Viewing condition: interrupted by the commercial (condition = good) versus continuous/no interruption (condition = no)
sample_definition: All non-missing Study 2 participant observations in the Excel file with condition coded good or no and non-missing enjoyrelativ; excluded three non-data/trailing rows, yielding N = 102.
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test comparing mean enjoyrelativ between interrupted and continuous conditions, using pooled/equal variances.
operationalization_notes: The supplied dataset is Study 2, and the paper identifies the relative preference/enjoyment item as the direct test of whether the commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable; therefore I compared this outcome across the randomized interruption conditions without covariates.
reasoning: Using the Study 2 data, the interrupted-commercial condition had higher relative enjoyment ratings (M = 5.38, n = 53) than the continuous/no-commercial-interruption condition (M = 4.47, n = 49). An independent-samples equal-variance t-test gave t(100) = 2.45, two-sided p = 0.016, supporting the claim that the commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable.

dependent_variable: resigninvest: recoded likelihood that Don Swensen is resigning from office because he is under investigation for bribery, with higher values indicating greater belief in the rumor
main_predictor: causal correction condition versus denial-only condition
sample_definition: Respondents assigned to the three conditions that included the innuendo and with non-missing GSU211/resigninvest outcome data; the control condition was excluded because this outcome was not asked there (N=764).
model_specification: Inverse-probability-weighted OLS regression of resigninvest on indicators for denial and causal correction, with the innuendo-only condition as the reference group; the reported test is the linear contrast causal correction minus denial.
controls: None beyond inverse probability weights for block-randomized treatment assignment.
operationalization_notes: The paper's methods identify this four-point rumor-belief item as the direct measure of acceptance of the specific innuendo that Swensen resigned due to a bribery investigation; comparing the causal-correction arm to the denial-only arm directly tests whether the alternate causal explanation was more effective than evidence-backed denial alone.
reasoning: In an inverse-probability-weighted OLS model among respondents exposed to the innuendo, belief that Swensen resigned because he was under investigation was significantly lower in the causal-correction condition than in the denial-only condition. The causal-vs-denial contrast was -0.335 points on the 1-4 outcome scale, t(761) = -5.07, p = 5.1e-7, supporting the claim that the alternate causal explanation limited acceptance of the misperception more effectively.

dependent_variable: Intimacy score, computed as the mean of the four intimacy questionnaire items: r1, reverse-coded r4, r6, and r7
main_predictor: Partner attention condition (attention/80% signal change vs no-attention/0% signal change)
sample_definition: All 30 complete observations in Sheet3 of the Study 2a Excel data were included; condition 1 was identified as the attention condition from the manipulation-check frequency variable and condition 2 as no attention.
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test comparing mean intimacy between the attention and no-attention conditions, using the pooled-variance t statistic.
operationalization_notes: The available dataset is for Study 2a, whose method directly manipulates whether the partner paid attention and measures post-task intimacy; therefore the most direct test is the between-condition comparison of the intimacy score.

dependent_variable: Total number of givers per 23-minute session (g1g22009)

The cluster-robust test was t(15)=3.58, p=0.00275, supporting the conclusion that the verbal ask increased giving.

dependent_variable: Bagrut certification status (zakaibag)

controls: Arab school indicator, Jewish religious school indicator, lagged-score quartile indicators, father's education, mother's education, indicator for more than 4 siblings, and immigrant status; no pair effects for the single-sex specification.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's cross-sectional Equation (1) specification for the post-treatment 2001 cohort and the separate-girls analysis used for the claim about increased certification among girls.

This supports the claim that the award offer increased girls' Bagrut certification rates.

dependent_variable: Industry-year intrafirm import share, computed as related-party imports divided by related-party plus non-related-party imports
main_predictor: DownMeasure interacted with an indicator for above-median weighted-average buyer industry demand elasticity

model_specification: OLS regression of intrafirm import share on DownMeasure x below-median elasticity and DownMeasure x above-median elasticity, an above-median elasticity indicator, year fixed effects, and controls; cluster-robust standard errors by IO2002 industry
controls: Year fixed effects; above-median buyer elasticity indicator; buyer-industry log skill intensity, log equipment capital per worker, log plant capital per worker, log materials per worker, log(0.001 + R&D/Sales), and size dispersion
operationalization_notes: I used the paper's baseline cross-industry-year specification and one of its two stated downstreamness measures (DownMeasure). The corresponding low-elasticity interaction was not statistically distinguishable from zero in the same fitted model, so this supports the claimed positive downstreamness-intrafirm import share relationship for high-elasticity buyer industries.

dependent_variable: Whether the PAP ever submitted an application for the child/BMO in the observed panel
main_predictor: Child coded as a non-African American girl versus a non-African American boy
sample_definition: One observation per eligible unambiguous PAP-BMO pair from ChoicePanel2.dta; included pairs where the PAP type was inferably allowed by the BMO restrictions and the child was coded exactly as non-African American with known gender (nonaa_girl=1 or nonaa_boy=1); excluded 86 pairs inconsistently appearing in both gender categories.
model_specification: Pooled two-sample z test comparing the proportion of PAP-BMO pairs with any application between non-African American girls and non-African American boys, using the directional alternative that the girl application rate is higher.
operationalization_notes: The paper's preference analysis treats PAP applications as revealed preference evidence; I aggregated the daily choice panel to PAP-child pairs to avoid counting the same PAP-child opportunity repeatedly, then directly tested whether non-African American girls received applications more often than comparable non-African American boys.
reasoning: Among eligible PAP-child pairs involving non-African American children of known gender, applications occurred for 292 of 3544 girl pairs (8.24%) versus 304 of 5187 boy pairs (5.86%). A one-sided pooled two-proportion z test for a higher application rate for girls gave z = 4.33, p = 7.54e-06, supporting a positive preference for non-African American girls.

dependent_variable: a-insensitivity index a = 3*(1/3 - (mean composite matching probability - mean single matching probability))

reasoning: Using the paper's baseline regression on the reconstructed a-insensitivity index, the time-pressure condition in Part 1 increased a-insensitivity by 0.1895 relative to Part 1 control (cluster-robust SE = 0.0893), t(98) = 2.12, p = 0.036. This supports the claim that participants became more insensitive/perceived more ambiguity under time pressure.

dependent_variable: civil war duration in months (durationmonths)
main_predictor: indicator for irregular technology of rebellion (irregular vs conventional or SNC)
sample_definition: Technologies of Rebellion (TR) conflict-level dataset; completed civil wars with nonmissing duration and all model covariates, excluding cases with missing observed duration/covariates.

controls: post-Cold War dummy (poscoldwar91), rough terrain, log population, ethnic fractionalization, lagged democracy, oil exporter, GDP per capita, military personnel, external support for government, and external support for rebels
operationalization_notes: The paper tests the duration hypothesis using Weibull AFT models on the TR data; I operationalized the claim directly by combining conventional and SNC wars into the non-irregular reference category and estimating the adjusted AFT model on conflicts with observed duration.
reasoning: In a Weibull accelerated-failure-time model, irregular conflicts had a positive coefficient relative to conventional/SNC conflicts combined (z = 5.01, p = 5.42e-7). The estimated time ratio was exp(1.168) = 3.22, indicating substantially longer durations for irregular conflicts in this sample.

dependent_variable: Log monthly all-cause mortality rate (lndrate)
main_predictor: Interaction of post-1960 period with number of days having mean temperature above 90°F, summed over current and prior month exposure
sample_definition: State-month observations from 1931-2004 with nonmissing all-cause mortality and covariates in DATA_1900_2004.dta; 49 states/DC-equivalent state FIPS units as present in the file, weighted by contemporaneous state population
model_specification: Population-weighted linear regression of log monthly mortality on current and one-month-lag temperature-bin variables (<40°F, 80-89°F, >90°F) and their post-1960 interactions; the reported test is the cluster-robust t test for the sum of the current and lagged >90°F post-1960 interaction coefficients
controls: State-by-month fixed effects with state-by-month-specific quadratic year trends; year-by-month fixed effects; precipitation indicators for below-25th and above-75th percentile; month interactions with infant, age 1-44, age 45-64 population shares; month interactions with log real per-capita income. Standard errors clustered by state.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's baseline mortality specification and two-month cumulative exposure approach, but estimates the decline directly in one pooled model via post-1960 interactions rather than copying separate-period table entries.
reasoning: In a pooled 1931-2004 model, the post-1960 change in the cumulative effect of an additional >90°F day (current plus prior month exposure) was negative and statistically significant: coefficient = -0.01434 log points, t(48) = -3.08, p = 0.0034. The implied cumulative >90°F association declined from 0.01894 before 1960 to 0.00459 after 1960, supporting a decline in the temperature-mortality relationship.

dependent_variable: Binary DVD purchase choice (1 = chose to buy the DVD, 0 = chose not to buy)
main_predictor: Interaction between opportunity cost reminder condition and z-scored future-self connectedness
sample_definition: All 88 participants in the DVD_data dataset with complete choice, cue condition, and connectedness measures from Study 1A
model_specification: Logistic regression with purchase choice predicted by opportunity cost cue (0 = no reminder, 1 = reminder), z-scored connectedness, and their interaction; reported statistic is the Wald z test for the interaction coefficient
operationalization_notes: Study 1A directly manipulated opportunity-cost salience in the DVD spending scenario and measured future-self connectedness; the interaction in purchase likelihood is the most direct test of whether spending cues matter primarily for more connected participants.
reasoning: A logistic regression predicting DVD purchase found a significant negative opportunity-cost-cue × future-self-connectedness interaction (Wald z = -2.10, p = .036, N = 88). The negative interaction indicates that the opportunity cost reminder reduced purchase likelihood more strongly among participants higher in connectedness to their future selves.

dependent_variable: Indicator that the referred applicant was female (REF_female)
main_predictor: Conventional applicant gender, coded as male CA versus female CA (OP_female/OP_gender)
sample_definition: Conventional applicants randomized to the unrestricted/either-gender referral treatment, restricted to cases where a referral was made and referral gender was observed (N=220).

A two-sample test of proportions gave z = -3.15, p = 0.00165, indicating that male CAs were significantly less likely than female CAs to refer women.

dependent_variable: Copying-adjusted standardized ALI mathematics test score for 10th grade in program year 1

controls: School-level 2008 12th-grade ENLACE math and Spanish scores; region dummies; state dummies; school mean 9th-grade ENLACE math scores for current 10th- and 11th-grade students.
operationalization_notes: I used the paper's main Table 7 approach for the claim, focusing on the most direct aligned-incentives contrast, T3 versus control, in the first observed 10th-grade program-year sample. Following the paper's copying-adjustment description, suspected copiers' scores were replaced by values predicted from control noncopiers using baseline 9th-grade math ENLACE score and a missing-baseline indicator.
reasoning: In a cluster-robust regression for 10th-grade year-1 students, the aligned-incentives treatment (T3) coefficient was positive: 30.998 standardized score points relative to control, with t(86)=5.367 and p=6.68e-7. This supports the claim that the ALI aligned incentives increased mathematics test scores.

dependent_variable: Subject-level proportion of intertemporal choices in which the earlier payment was chosen (impatient choices)
main_predictor: Ethnicity-salience treatment indicator (treatE: 1 = ethnicity salient, 0 = control)

model_specification: Welch independent-samples t-test comparing mean impatient-choice proportions between ethnicity-salience and control groups, with the contrast defined as treated minus control.

A Welch two-sample t-test gives t(67.34) = -3.42, p = 0.0011, indicating significantly fewer impatient choices under ethnic-identity salience.

dependent_variable: Subject-level average cooperation rate: fraction/percentage of time spent cooperating, averaged across all 23 supergames

model_specification: Welch independent-samples t-test comparing mean subject-level cooperation rates between Short-Deterministic and Short-Stochastic treatments
operationalization_notes: The paper defines cooperation rate as the fraction of time a subject spends cooperating in a supergame and assesses treatment differences after averaging by subject across supergames; I used that subject-level outcome and directly compared the two short-duration horizon treatments named in the claim.

A Welch two-sample t-test of the deterministic-stochastic difference gave t(79.19)=3.44, two-sided p=0.00094, supporting higher cooperation with deterministic horizons.

dependent_variable: Absolute ideological distance between the plurality vote-winning party and the median voter (pldist1)
main_predictor: Election rule: SMD versus PR (smd)

operationalization_notes: Hypothesis 4a predicts convergence of the SMD plurality winner toward the median voter; the paper's manifesto data contain the directly corresponding distance variable, and Hypothesis 4b implies the plurality winner should be farther from the median under PR, making an SMD-versus-PR comparison a direct test.

dependent_variable: Renewed civil war onset (nwar1: indicator that a new civil war occurred)

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of partial semantic networks
main_predictor: Openness-to-experience group (high vs. low median split on latent openness score)
sample_definition: All 516 participants in the cleaned dataset; 258 lowest latent openness scores formed the low group and 258 highest formed the high group. model_specification: Independent-samples t-test comparing ASPL values from 1000 high-openness and 1000 low-openness bootstrapped partial semantic networks. Networks were constructed from participant-by-animal binary matrices using cosine similarity and a greedy triangulated maximally filtered graph; ASPL was computed on the resulting unweighted, undirected graph.
operationalization_notes: The paper operationalized interconnection as shorter ASPL and used bootstrapped partial semantic networks to test group differences. I followed that approach using the cleaned fluency responses, the latent openness median split, matched nodes appearing at least twice in both groups, and 50% node-retention bootstraps.
reasoning: Using bootstrapped partial semantic networks, the high-openness networks had shorter average shortest path length than the low-openness networks (M_high = 2.507, M_low = 2.675), t(1998) = -21.72, p = 4.76e-94. Because lower ASPL indicates greater interconnection among nodes, this supports the claim that the high-openness group’s network was more interconnected.

dependent_variable: Two-year change in combined math-reading PIAT score, constructed as the mean of normalized math, reading recognition, and reading comprehension scores and renormalized using the random sample
main_predictor: Two-year change in total family income (earned plus unearned taxable plus nontaxable income), measured in $1,000 CPI-adjusted units
sample_definition: Child-period observations in odd income years 1989-1999 with a valid same-child observation two years earlier (1987-1997), valid math and reading PIAT components in both periods, valid income and baseline controls, no change in mother's marital status across the two-year interval, family income not above $100,000 in either period, and excluding the top/bottom 1% of income changes
