controls: Child sex, child age, number of siblings, and race/ethnicity indicators (black and Hispanic) included in the differenced equation
operationalization_notes: The paper's baseline claim concerns short-run contemporaneous income effects on combined math-reading achievement using two-year differences to remove child fixed effects. I used the same differenced outcome structure and baseline child controls, but used observed family income changes directly rather than reconstructing the paper's full TAXSIM/EITC instrumental-variable measure from unavailable tax-output variables.
reasoning: In a two-year first-difference regression of the normalized combined math-reading score on the change in family income, the income-change coefficient was positive but not statistically distinguishable from zero (cluster-robust t = 0.635, df = 13269, p = 0.526; N = 13276 child-period differences). This analysis therefore does not provide statistically significant evidence that higher contemporaneous income raises combined test scores in the short run.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs; averaged absorption scale)
main_predictor: Single childless status (singchild1: 1 = single/childless, 0 = all other family structures)
sample_definition: Study 1 respondents who were currently employed full-time, part-time, or self-employed and had nonmissing data on work absorption, single/childless status, gender, age, and job level; listwise N = 353.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of work absorption on single/childless status and covariates; main test is the t test for the single/childless coefficient.
controls: Gender/sex, age in years, and job level.
operationalization_notes: The claim corresponds to Hypothesis 1 in Study 1, and the paper states that it tested this hypothesis with OLS using the employed alumni sample and these controls; I therefore reproduced that specification from the dataset rather than using the later diary mediation model.
reasoning: Using the Study 1 employed-alumni sample with listwise deletion, single/childless status negatively predicted work absorption in an OLS regression controlling for gender, age, and job level, b = -0.311 and t(348) = -2.36, p = .0188. Thus, single, childless workers reported significantly lower absorption than workers with other family structures.

dependent_variable: ProperName: whether the response began with a greeting addressing the applicant by proper name
main_predictor: Hispanic versus white emailer treatment assignment
sample_definition: Observations assigned to Hispanic (Santiago/Gabriela Martinez) or white (Brett/Emily Smith) names, restricted to emails that received a response and had nonmissing ProperName coding; black treatment observations and nonresponses were excluded.
model_specification: Two-sample test of equality of proportions (pooled standard error), comparing the named-greeting rate for Hispanic versus white applicants.
operationalization_notes: The paper defines friendliness/tone as a named salutation among responses and reports the Hispanic-white difference in these proportions; this directly tests the stated claim using the available response-level ProperName outcome.
reasoning: Among white and Hispanic treatment emails that received a response with nonmissing greeting coding, 77/187 Hispanic applicants (41.2%) versus 107/175 white applicants (61.1%) received a named greeting. A two-proportion z-test gives z = -3.80, p = 0.00015, indicating Hispanic applicants were significantly less likely than white applicants to be greeted by name.

dependent_variable: Session-level rate of shading, coded 1 when seller chose low quality and 0 when seller chose normal quality
main_predictor: Contract type: flexible versus rigid
sample_definition: Baseline condition only; realized trades in the good state of nature with a seller quality decision, yielding 805 contract-level quality observations aggregated to 5 session-level paired observations by contract type.
model_specification: One-sided paired t-test comparing, within session, the shading rate under flexible contracts to the shading rate under rigid contracts.
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the difference in shading between rigid and flexible contracts; in the experiment rigid contracts trade only in the good state, so I compared good-state realized trades in the baseline condition and used sessions as the independent unit of analysis.
reasoning: Using the five independent baseline sessions, the mean session-level shading rate was 6.4% in rigid contracts versus 25.0% in flexible contracts in the good state. A one-sided paired t-test on session-level shading-rate differences showed significantly more shading in flexible than rigid contracts, t(4)=8.47, p=0.00053.

dependent_variable: Natural log of total state-level CO2 emissions from fossil fuel combustion (carbon_unadj, million metric tons)
main_predictor: Natural log of average annualized working hours per worker, computed as average weekly working hours times 52
sample_definition: Balanced panel of all 50 U.S. states for years 2007-2013, excluding no observations with complete carbon_unadj and wrkhrs data (N=350).
model_specification: Pearson product-moment correlation test between logged CO2 emissions and logged working hours across state-year observations.
operationalization_notes: The claim states a positive relationship between state-level carbon emissions and average working hours over 2007-2013; I tested this directly with the bivariate association in the paper's full state-year sample, using the paper's log transformation convention and annualizing weekly hours.
reasoning: Using all 350 state-year observations from 2007-2013, logged carbon emissions and logged average annualized working hours were positively correlated, r = 0.3992, df = 348, p = 8.05e-15. This supports the claim that states/years with higher average working hours tended to have higher carbon emissions.

dependent_variable: considered attack against a proliferating state's nuclear program (consider = 1)
main_predictor: prior violent militarized conflict in the dyad (hostileMID = 1 for use of force or war)
sample_definition: Politically relevant directed dyad-years in the original dataset for 1941-2000 with nonmissing considered-attack and violent-conflict measures.
model_specification: Bivariate 2x2 Pearson chi-square test of independence between considered attack and prior violent conflict.
operationalization_notes: The paper's research design identifies directed dyad-years among politically relevant attackers and proliferating targets as the unit of analysis, and treats considered attack as the indicator that a proliferation threat became salient enough for serious military consideration. I used the authors' violent-conflict indicator as the focal prior-conflict measure and tested the unadjusted association directly.
reasoning: In politically relevant directed dyad-years from 1941-2000, considered attacks were much more frequent following violent militarized conflict: 28/563 conflict dyad-years (4.97%) versus 13/5039 non-conflict dyad-years (0.26%). The Pearson chi-square test was chi2(1, N=5602)=154.99, p=1.41e-35, supporting a positive relationship between prior violent conflict and salience/consideration of targeting nuclear programs.

dependent_variable: Indicator that the county became part of a new splinter district in the electoral wave
main_predictor: DEC share ratio: county share of seats on the District Executive Committee divided by county population share; lower values indicate greater political marginalization
sample_definition: County-wave observations for the three district-creation waves corresponding to 1996-2000, 2001-2005, and 2006-2010, restricted to complete cases on the dependent variable, DEC share ratio, marginalization controls, number of counties in district, lagged breakup, region indicators, and wave indicators
model_specification: Population-averaged logistic regression using generalized estimating equations with an exchangeable within-county correlation structure and robust standard errors clustered by county
controls: Ethnic marginalization, development summary index, number of counties in the district, lagged breakup indicator, region indicators, and electoral-wave indicators
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies DEC representation relative to population as its primary measure of political marginalization and models splinter status at the county-wave level; I used the same outcome and core covariate set, with GEE to account for repeated observations of counties over waves.
reasoning: In a county-wave logistic GEE model, the DEC share ratio coefficient was negative and statistically significant (z = -3.02, p = 0.0025; N = 472). Because lower DEC representation relative to population indicates greater political marginalization, this result implies that politically marginalized counties were more likely to become splinter districts.

dependent_variable: Dichotomous diplomatic recognition: State B recognizes State A (recog1duml)
main_predictor: State A nuclear weapons status (nukeduma)
sample_definition: Directed dyads with nonmissing diplomatic-recognition outcome and covariates for 1945-2000, using the observed COW diplomatic-recognition intervals rather than interpolated annual recognition values.
model_specification: Probit regression of dichotomous recognition on State A nuclear status, State B nuclear status, their interaction, controls, and four BKT-style temporal-dependence spline terms based on years since prior recognition within the directed dyad.
controls: State B nuclear status; Nuclear A × Nuclear B; rivalry status A; rivalry status B; dyadic rivalry; CINC A; CINC B; CINC A × CINC B; democracy A; democracy B; Democracy A × Democracy B; contiguity; logged distance; alliance; temporal-dependence splines.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Table 2 setup for the part of the claim about being recognized by other nations: State B recognizing State A is modeled in directed dyads, with Nuclear Weapons A as the focal predictor and the same substantive controls used in the paper's diplomatic-recognition analysis.
reasoning: In a probit model of whether State B recognizes State A, the coefficient for State A nuclear-weapons status was positive (b = 0.1442) with z = 6.09, p = 1.11e-9, among 213,454 directed dyad-period observations. This supports the claim that nuclear-capable states are more likely to be recognized by other nations, conditional on the included dyadic and monadic covariates.

dependent_variable: Log absolute opinion change on the pro-immigration index between wave 2 and wave 3 (change_w3w2_log)
main_predictor: Group-level deliberative quality: mean level of justification rationality in speech acts (DQ_jlev)
sample_definition: EuroPolis participants in the 13 discussion groups with coded DQI justification data and complete data on the opinion-change outcome and covariates; N = 174 individuals nested in 13 groups.
model_specification: Linear mixed-effects regression estimated by REML with a random intercept for discussion group; main test is the Wald z statistic for DQ_jlev.
controls: Knowledge change; reported clarification from other participants, experts, politicians, and briefing material; social conformity pressure above and below the respondent's wave-2 position; gender/female, age, education, Catholic, Protestant, working class, religiosity, left-right ideology and squared term, intended left-party vote, and intended right-party vote.
operationalization_notes: The paper's deliberative-influence section treats justification rationality as a group resource and tests whether it predicts the magnitude, rather than direction, of immigration opinion change from pre- to post-deliberation; I followed that specification using the supplied SANDERS replication data.
reasoning: In a REML random-intercept linear model for the log absolute change in immigration opinion from wave 2 to wave 3, the group-level mean justification-rationality coefficient was positive (b = 0.130) with z = 1.97, p = 0.049. Thus participants in groups with more rational justification showed greater opinion change, supporting the published claim.

dependent_variable: Matching-group mean effort: proportion of individual decisions coded work=1 across all six periods
main_predictor: Reward scheme under complementarity: symmetrical 444COM versus discriminating 345COM
sample_definition: All observations from complementarity treatments 345COM and 444COM were included; individual-period observations were aggregated to 23 independent matching groups (12 in 345COM, 11 in 444COM).
model_specification: One-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum/Mann-Whitney test comparing matching-group mean effort, testing 444COM < 345COM; z statistic computed from the rank-sum with tie-corrected variance and no continuity correction.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies matching groups as the independent units and compares mean effort across reward schemes within the complementarity production technology, so I used group-level mean effort over the repeated rounds to directly operationalize the claim about lower efforts.
reasoning: Using independent matching groups as the unit of analysis, mean effort was lower in the symmetrical complementarity treatment 444COM (M = 0.722, 11 groups) than in the cost-equivalent discriminating complementarity treatment 345COM (M = 0.917, 12 groups). A one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum normal-approximation test gave z = -1.846, p = 0.032, supporting the claim that symmetrical rewards elicit lower effort under complementarity.

dependent_variable: Anti-minus-pro immigration action balance in each senator response letter, coded 1 for mentioning anti-immigration action(s) but not pro-immigration action(s), 0 for mentioning neither or both, and -1 for mentioning pro-immigration action(s) but not anti-immigration action(s).
main_predictor: Constituent letter position: anti-immigration versus pro-immigration, compared within senator.
sample_definition: U.S. senators in the study who responded to both the pro-immigration and anti-immigration constituent letters; N=56 paired senators.
model_specification: Paired within-senator sign test on the change in anti-minus-pro action balance from the pro-immigration letter response to the anti-immigration letter response; reported as the asymptotic chi-square equivalent.
controls: None; the analysis uses the within-subject paired experimental design.
operationalization_notes: The paper's first experiment directly tests tailoring by comparing each senator's explanations to pro- and anti-immigration audiences. I used the combined anti-minus-pro action balance because it captures whether senators shifted emphasis toward actions congruent with the constituent audience.
reasoning: Among the 56 senators who replied to both letters, the within-senator anti-minus-pro action balance shifted in the expected direction for 13 senators and in the opposite direction for 1 senator. The sign-test chi-square equivalent was χ²(1)=10.29, p=0.0013, indicating that senators were significantly more likely to emphasize actions matching the constituent audience's immigration position.

dependent_variable: log wage gain at migration, log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted)
main_predictor: education category indicator for no high school (<9 years of schooling), compared with college degree (>=16 years, reference category)
sample_definition: All 2,854 observations in the provided Migration Project wage_gain_table.xlsx with positive adjusted pre-migration and U.S. wages, nonmissing years of schooling, and nonmissing country.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of log wage gain on education-category indicators (no high school, some high school, high school graduate, some college; college degree omitted) and country fixed effects; reported statistic is the t test for the no-high-school coefficient.
controls: Country fixed effects and indicators for the other education categories.
operationalization_notes: The paper states that this claim is based on comparing log wage gains by education category, controlling for country fixed effects, with college graduates as the omitted group. I applied that specification to the provided public wage-gain file and used the paper's education cutoffs (<9, 9-11, 12, 13-15, >=16 years).
reasoning: In an OLS regression of log wage gain on education categories with college degree as the reference and country fixed effects, the coefficient for no high school was positive (0.197 log points) but not statistically significant, t(2840)=1.52, p=0.128. Thus this analysis does not provide clear evidence that immigrants with no high-school exposure gained more than college graduates in this sample.

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses categorized as connoting the learned negative meaning of the cue, combined across homographic and nonhomographic cues
main_predictor: Cue status: baseline learned-but-not-practiced cues versus learned-and-suppressed cues
sample_definition: Experiment 2 nonruminator participants in the provided final dataset with nonmissing baseline and suppression free-association percentages (Group = 1; N = 27)
model_specification: Repeated-measures contrast of baseline vs suppressed cue status, implemented as an OLS model on participant-level difference scores (FAbaseC - FAsuppC) with intercept tested against zero and counterbalancing condition included as a between-subjects factor
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns nonruminators' beneficial suppression effects on a transfer task; the provided dataset contains Experiment 2 free-association transfer-task outcomes, and the paper identifies the baseline-minus-suppressed learned-meaning percentage as the indirect forgetting measure.
reasoning: Among nonruminators in Experiment 2, learned-meaning free-association responses were lower for suppressed cues (M = 29.63%) than for baseline cues (M = 45.68%). A within-person baseline-vs-suppressed test controlling for counterbalancing condition was significant, F(1, 24) = 10.94, p = .00296, supporting a beneficial suppression effect in the transfer task.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being: mean of eight recoded CES-D items, scaled 0-3 with higher values indicating better well-being
main_predictor: Interaction of parental status (living with children vs childless reference) with standardized country-level percentage disapproving/strongly disapproving of voluntary childlessness
sample_definition: Women aged over 40 in the 24 European countries in the Huijts ESS dataset, including childless, living-with-children, and empty-nest respondents, with listwise complete data on the model variables (N = 13,713).
model_specification: Linear mixed-effects regression with respondents nested in countries; random intercepts and random slopes by country for living-with-children and empty-nest parental-status indicators; fixed effects for living with children, empty nest, country-level disapproval, and their interactions. The reported statistic is the Wald z test for the living-with-children × country disapproval interaction.
controls: Age, age squared, marital status, respondent education, parental education, religious attendance, paid employment, born in country, individual attitude toward childlessness, and individual social contact frequency; empty-nest status and its interaction with country disapproval were included but not used as the main result.
operationalization_notes: The paper estimated sex-specific multilevel models and found cross-national variation especially among women, so I used the women-only model. Tolerant norms were operationalized as low country-level disapproval of voluntary childlessness; a positive interaction with disapproval directly tests that the childless disadvantage is larger where norms are less tolerant and smaller where norms are more tolerant.
reasoning: In the women-only multilevel model, the interaction between living with children and country-level disapproval of childlessness was positive and statistically significant (b = 0.0760 per SD of disapproval, z = 4.69, p = 2.78e-6). Thus, as societal disapproval increases, the well-being advantage of women living with children over childless women increases; equivalently, the childless disadvantage is smaller in more tolerant countries.

dependent_variable: DSM5_Total: summed DSM-5 Self-Rated Level 1 Cross-Cutting Symptom Measure total psychopathology severity
main_predictor: MiniK_Total life-history strategy score, with lower scores indicating faster life strategy and higher scores indicating slower life strategy
sample_definition: All 138 participants in the final dataset with complete DSM5_Total, MiniK_Total, and Age data; no additional exclusions
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of DSM5_Total on MiniK_Total and Age; main result is the t test for the MiniK_Total coefficient
operationalization_notes: The paper's main analyses tested life history strategy and psychopathology using partial correlations controlling for age because age correlated with outcomes. I operationalized the same association as the equivalent age-adjusted OLS coefficient test using the Mini-K, described in the methods as the stronger behavioral measure of life history strategy.
reasoning: In an age-adjusted linear regression, Mini-K life-history score significantly predicted DSM-5 total psychopathology symptoms, t(135) = -6.95, p = 1.41e-10. Because higher Mini-K scores indicate slower life strategy, the negative coefficient means faster life strategy was associated with greater psychopathology symptoms.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score, the 0-20 political knowledge test score (sum of correct answers)
main_predictor: Stereotypaktivierung condition: stereotype not activated vs. stereotype activated by gender difference statement
sample_definition: Study 2 observations selected by the dataset filter (gender_alle < 3, honesty = 1, citizen = 1; N=377 in full analytic sample), restricted to female participants (gender_factor = 1) in conditions 0 and 2; n = 143.
model_specification: Pooled independent-samples t-test comparing female participants in the first and third stereotype-activation conditions on political knowledge score.
operationalization_notes: The claim is a simple pairwise statement about female participants' political-knowledge performance in condition 1 versus condition 3, so I tested that contrast directly using the filtered Study 2 analytic sample and the paper's political knowledge score.
reasoning: Among eligible female participants, mean political knowledge was higher in the stereotype-not-activated condition (M = 8.90, n = 73) than in the gender-difference-statement condition (M = 7.03, n = 70). A pooled independent-samples t-test gave t(141) = 2.57, two-sided p = 0.011, supporting the claimed directional difference.

dependent_variable: GDP growth rate at t+2 (f2gdpidx)
main_predictor: Indicator equal to 1 if either the city party secretary or mayor was connected to the incumbent provincial party secretary
sample_definition: City-year observations for mainland prefecture/subprovincial cities from 2000-2011, excluding Tibet; observations included when required model variables were available, yielding 3,693 observations in 326 cities.
model_specification: OLS fixed-effects regression with city fixed effects and province-by-year fixed effects; robust standard errors clustered by city.
controls: Net fiscal transfer at t+1; predecessor-term starting GDP growth, log GDP, log population, and log fixed asset investment for both secretary and mayor; city secretary and mayor age, college education, gender, and tenure-category indicators.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's baseline specification for the main economic-growth claim, using overall GDP growth two years after the connection status measurement as the outcome and the combined secretary/mayor connection indicator as the focal predictor.
reasoning: In a city and province-year fixed-effects regression, the coefficient for being connected to the incumbent provincial secretary was positive (0.3823 percentage points) with a cluster-robust t statistic of 2.87 (df = 325, p = 0.0044). This supports the claim that connected city leaders delivered faster subsequent GDP growth.

dependent_variable: Top-quality status among foreign players (top-quality foreign player-year vs lower-quality foreign player-year, where top quality follows the paper's national-team-selection definition used in Figure 3).
main_predictor: Post-reform period for Denmark's preferential foreigner tax scheme (1991-2008 vs 1985-1990).
sample_definition: Foreign player-year counts in Denmark's first league from 1985-2008 in basesynthetic_control.dta; pre-reform years 1985-1990 and post-reform years 1991-2008; observations classified using stop and slow counts.
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 table: period (pre vs post Danish tax scheme) by foreign-player ability category (top vs lower quality).
operationalization_notes: The paper's Denmark case study uses 1985-1990 as the pre-reform period and 1991-2008 as post-reform, and separates foreign players into top- and lower-quality categories in Figure 3; I therefore tested whether the composition of Danish foreign players shifted toward top-quality players across the reform threshold.
reasoning: Among foreign player-year observations in Denmark, the top-quality share rose from 4/24 = 16.7% in 1985-1990 to 195/364 = 53.6% in 1991-2008. A 2x2 chi-square test of top-versus-lower quality by pre/post reform period was significant, chi-square(1, N=388) = 12.27, p = 0.00046, supporting a shift in the ability composition of foreigners toward higher-ability players after the Danish tax scheme.

dependent_variable: Willingness-to-pay scale, computed as the mean of the three environmental-payment items including the reverse-scored not-my-money item
main_predictor: Intrinsic-relative-to-extrinsic values group: top quartile of I/E scores versus bottom quartile of I/E scores
sample_definition: Study 1 university-student participants with I/E scores in the upper quartile (I/E >= approximately .61; n = 46) or lower quartile (I/E <= approximately .22; n = 35); middle 74 participants were excluded for this contrast
model_specification: Independent-samples pooled-variance t-test comparing mean willingness-to-pay scores between upper- and lower-quartile I/E groups
operationalization_notes: The paper's Study 1 results section operationalized the willingness-to-pay hypothesis by contrasting relative intrinsic and relative extrinsic groups defined from the upper and lower quartiles of the I/E score, so I used the same contrast and recomputed the test from the original SAV data.
reasoning: Using the Study 1 data, participants in the top quartile of intrinsic-relative-to-extrinsic values had higher willingness-to-pay scores (M = 4.01) than those in the bottom quartile (M = 3.30), t(79) = 4.87, p = 5.56e-6. This supports the claim that greater endorsement of intrinsic relative to extrinsic values is associated with greater willingness to pay to protect the environment.

dependent_variable: Logged disputed-product imports into the defendant/respondent market after the dispute
main_predictor: Indicator that the trade partner was a complainant in the dispute
sample_definition: Observations from disputes that ended in early settlement/private mutually agreed solution, using the non-missing estimation sample for the baseline early-settlement model (N = 6,027).
model_specification: OLS linear regression with dispute fixed effects and standard errors clustered by combined dispute identifier.
controls: Logged respondent GDP, logged partner GDP, democratic-pair indicator, logged disputed imports in the pre-dispute baseline year, and logged total bilateral imports.
operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Model 2 operationalization for Hypothesis 1: within early settlements, compare post-dispute trade flows of complainants with those of non-complainant WTO members while controlling for market size, baseline disputed trade, total bilateral trade, and dispute fixed effects.
reasoning: In a fixed-effects regression for early-settlement disputes, the complainant indicator was positive (coefficient = 0.4301) and statistically significant using dispute-clustered standard errors (z = 2.384, p = 0.0171). This indicates that complainants had higher post-dispute disputed-product imports into respondent markets than other WTO members under private early settlements.

dependent_variable: entre_wage: country-year entrepreneurship rate for businesses up to 42 months old that pay wages
main_predictor: medage_20_64: median age of the population aged 20-64
sample_definition: All nonmissing GEM country-year observations in GEM_Country_Year.dta, survey years 2001-2010; N=393 country-year observations from 82 countries
model_specification: Weighted least squares linear regression with analytic weights equal to nobs_cy and cluster-robust standard errors by countryid; test is the t test for the median-age coefficient
controls: Survey year fixed effects (year dummy variables)
operationalization_notes: This directly follows the paper's country-year specification for corollary 3/Table 2, using the primary entrepreneurship measure and median working-age age as the demographic predictor.
reasoning: In a weighted country-year regression of the early-stage wage-paying entrepreneurship rate on median working-age population age and year indicators, the coefficient on median age was negative (b = -0.00732) with a cluster-robust t(81) = -5.71, p = 1.78e-7. Thus, countries/years with lower median ages had higher new business formation rates, consistent with the published claim.

dependent_variable: perceived arm length divided by actual arm length ratio for each arm
main_predictor: arm side (right vs left) within right-handed participants
sample_definition: Experiment 1 participants coded as right-handed in the dataset; all 15 right-handed participants with right and left arm-length ratios included
model_specification: paired-samples t-test comparing RatioRight minus RatioLeft, with directional alternative RatioRight > RatioLeft
operationalization_notes: The Experiment 1 methods define perceived arm-length accuracy as perceived length divided by actual length and the target claim concerns the right-versus-left arm comparison specifically among right-handed participants, so I tested that within-subject difference directly.
reasoning: Among right-handed participants, the perceived/actual arm-length ratio was higher for the right arm (M = 0.970) than for the left arm (M = 0.920). A directional paired-samples t-test on the within-participant ratio difference was t(14) = 2.123, one-tailed p = 0.026, supporting the claim that right-handed participants perceived their right arms as longer than their left arms.

dependent_variable: dv_index3: mean of three 1-7 items measuring how appreciated, valued, and satisfied participants felt after the note
main_predictor: Acknowledgment condition: verbal acknowledgment without monetary benefit vs. financial acknowledgment with $.05
sample_definition: Study 1a hotel field-study participants with exclude = 0 and non-missing condition and dv_index3; two participants who left before dependent-variable questions were excluded, leaving N = 49.
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test comparing dv_index3 between the $.05 financial acknowledgment group and the verbal acknowledgment group, with the statistic signed as financial minus verbal; equivalent to a one-way ANOVA with two groups.
operationalization_notes: The available dataset is Study 1a, which directly tests the target trivialization claim in a real hotel customer-feedback context. The paper’s methods identify the three-item felt-appreciation index as the dependent variable and acknowledgment type as the randomized treatment.
reasoning: Among completed Study 1a participants, the $.05 financial acknowledgment group reported lower felt appreciation (M = 4.38) than the verbal acknowledgment group (M = 5.57). The independent-samples test was significant, t(47) = -2.92, p = .0054, supporting the claim that a small financial acknowledgment can produce less positive outcomes than a verbal acknowledgment.

dependent_variable: s_tot: standardized combined midterm and final exam score
main_predictor: avg5_girl: proportion female among the five neighboring peers (desk mate plus neighbor-4 peers)
sample_definition: Female students (girl = 1), excluding favored/nonrandom seat assignments (special1 = 0), and retaining complete cases for outcome, peer measures, block fixed effect, classroom cluster, and covariates
model_specification: OLS regression of standardized exam score on share female in neighbor 5 and average baseline score of neighbor 5, with randomization-block fixed effects; standard error for the main coefficient clustered by classroom with small-sample correction
controls: Baseline test score, height, age, birth order, mother's education, father's education, baseline interest in Chinese, math, and English, desk mate favored-status indicator, share favored among neighbor-4 peers, average baseline score of neighbor-5 peers, and randomization-block fixed effects
operationalization_notes: The paper states that the all-female versus all-male microenvironment claim is evaluated using the female-sample regression with the combined neighbor-5 peer measure; moving from five male to five female neighbors corresponds to increasing avg5_girl from 0 to 1.
reasoning: Among female, non-favored students with complete covariates (N = 245), the coefficient on the share female among neighbor-5 peers was 0.211 standardized exam-score units. Using classroom-clustered standard errors with 12 classroom clusters, this gave t(11) = 2.45, p = 0.032, supporting the claim that female students score higher when surrounded by females rather than males.

dependent_variable: Absolute attitude change toward alcohol from Time 1 to the one-year follow-up, computed as |mean T1 attitude - mean T3 attitude|; higher values indicate less stability/greater instability.
main_predictor: Interaction between Time 1 overall attitude certainty (mean of cert1-cert7) and Time 1 objective ambivalence computed as (positive + negative)/2 - |positive - negative|.
sample_definition: Study 2 participants with non-missing Time 1 and one-year follow-up (T3) attitude items; N=135.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression predicting absolute attitude change from mean-centered certainty, mean-centered objective ambivalence, their product interaction, and attitude extremity.
controls: Time 1 attitude extremity, computed as |mean Time 1 attitude - 4|.
operationalization_notes: I used the Study 2 alcohol dataset because the paper describes it as a longitudinal replication with a one-year delay, and followed the paper's specified construction of attitude change, certainty, objective ambivalence, and extremity covariate. The interaction term is the primary test of the claim that the certainty-stability relationship varies as ambivalence decreases.
reasoning: In Study 2 respondents with one-year follow-up data, the certainty × objective ambivalence interaction significantly predicted absolute attitude change, t(130)=3.42, p=0.00084. Because the outcome is instability and the interaction coefficient was positive (B=0.0745), the slope of certainty became more negative as ambivalence decreased, consistent with greater certainty being associated with greater stability for less ambivalent attitudes.

dependent_variable: Aggregate electoral turnout (% of registered voters, with U.S. measured as VAP turnout)
main_predictor: Portfolio Equity Stock (log), a foreign-ownership globalization measure
sample_definition: Complete-case lower legislative chamber election observations for OECD countries in 1970-2007 with nonmissing turnout, lagged turnout, portfolio equity stock, controls, and country-specific trend variables; 232 elections in 23 countries.
model_specification: Dynamic fixed-effects OLS regression of turnout on lagged turnout and log portfolio equity stock, with country fixed effects and country-specific quadratic time trends; standard errors clustered by country and t test evaluated with 23-1 cluster degrees of freedom.
controls: Registered voters (log), percent VAP age 30-69, years since last election, U.S. mid-term election dummy, compulsory voting, mixed electoral system, PR system, vote-seat disproportionality, effective number of parties by seats, and margin/closeness of victory.
operationalization_notes: The paper's main turnout analysis uses dynamic panel models with these controls and country-specific trends; I used the paper's noted fixed-effects OLS with lagged dependent variable and clustered standard errors as a directly comparable single test of the direct ownership-constraint hypothesis, focusing on portfolio equity stock because it is the most mobile ownership measure highlighted by the authors.
reasoning: In a dynamic country fixed-effects turnout model, the coefficient on log portfolio equity stock was negative (b = -2.235) with a cluster-robust t(22) = -2.644, p = 0.0148. This supports the directional claim that greater foreign ownership is associated with lower electoral turnout.

dependent_variable: Number of Better Business Bureau complaints in the preceding 3 years (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: Indicator that at least one firm name begins with A, a number, or a symbol (first_A)
sample_definition: All 2,293 Illinois plumbing firms in final_data.dta with nonmissing complaints_2008 and first_A; 295 first_A firms and 1,998 non-first_A firms.
model_specification: Independent two-sample t-test with pooled variance, equivalent to OLS regression of complaints_2008 on first_A with conventional standard errors; directional alternative first_A > non-first_A.
operationalization_notes: The claim is about average service complaints by name type, so I used the paper's primary Illinois plumbing-firm dataset and its BBB complaint count, comparing raw group means by the A/number-name indicator used in the paper's summary statistics.
reasoning: In the Illinois plumbing-firm data, firms with names beginning with A/a number had a higher mean number of BBB complaints (1.339; n=295) than other firms (0.248; n=1998). A two-sample t-test of this mean difference gave t(2291)=6.788, one-sided p=7.21e-12, supporting the claim that A/number-named firms receive more complaints on average.

dependent_variable: dv: ordered cooperative bargaining behavior / concession offering strategy, coded 0-3 with higher values indicating more cooperative concessions
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure
sample_definition: All 588 state-bargaining phase observations in the EU Council bargaining dataset with complete data, clustered across 23 bargaining phases.

operationalization_notes: This follows the paper's Model 1 specification, using the ordered concession-offering dependent variable and the issue-linkage structure measure that directly captures how differently opposing states value the issues under negotiation.
reasoning: In a generalized ordered logit model, the issue-linkage structure coefficient was positive (b = 1.2193) with a cluster-robust SE of 0.1960, yielding z = 6.22, p = 4.99e-10. Thus, bargaining phases with more differently valued linked issues were significantly more likely to show more cooperative, concession-offering bargaining behavior.

dependent_variable: Credit to government and state-owned enterprises (% GDP)
main_predictor: Lagged state capacity, measured by the Indicator Quality Government (IQG) index
sample_definition: Country-year panel observations from 1986-2011 with nonmissing directed credit to government/SOEs, IQG, private credit, and the lags needed for the dynamic GMM instruments; 126 countries and 2,474 country-years.
model_specification: Two-step dynamic system GMM with equations in first differences and levels; directed credit regressed on its one-year lag, one-year-lagged IQG, one-year-lagged private credit, and a linear time trend. Endogenous regressors were instrumented using internal lag instruments in collapsed form; the reported statistic is the asymptotic robust z test for the IQG coefficient.
controls: Lagged directed credit to government/SOEs, lagged private credit (% GDP), and a linear time trend.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies directed credit to government/SOEs as the outcome, IQG as state capacity, and private credit as the control for the profit potential of financial repression; I followed that setup in a dynamic panel GMM specification.
reasoning: In a dynamic system-GMM panel model, the coefficient on lagged state capacity (IQG, where higher means stronger state) was negative and highly significant (b = -10.71, robust SE = 0.872, z = -12.28, p = 1.13e-34). Thus, conditional on lagged directed credit, lagged private credit, and a time trend, weaker states are associated with more credit directed to the government and SOEs.

dependent_variable: MID initiation as originator (originit)
main_predictor: Lagged logged weighted coup events, ln(coupsum + 1) in the prior year (llcoupsum)
sample_definition: Latin American country-years in the provided dataset for 1960-1999 with nonmissing values on the dependent variable, lagged coup-events predictor, controls, and country code; first country-years lacking the lagged coup-events measure were excluded.
model_specification: Probit regression with standard errors clustered by country; the reported statistic is the z test for the lagged coup-events coefficient.
controls: Previous dispute (lagdisp), ethnic fractionalization (ethfrac), relative power/CINC (cinc), number of borders (nborder), logged number of allies (lnumber), regional conflict (regconf), lagged polity score (polity2l), and lagged logged real GDP (llrgdpch).
operationalization_notes: The paper's methods identify dispute initiation by originators as a primary conflict outcome and coup activity as the measure of threats to political survival. I used the paper's standard monadic probit specification with lagged observed coup events and the same control set to obtain a single directly interpretable test of the directional claim.
reasoning: In a probit model of MID initiation by originators, the coefficient for lagged logged coup events was negative (b = -0.0787) and not statistically distinguishable from zero using country-clustered standard errors, z = -0.567, p = 0.571. This does not provide evidence that greater threats to political survival increased conflict involvement in this operationalization.

dependent_variable: Amount sent to out-group recipient in the dictator game (d12outgroup; 0-5 euros)
main_predictor: Ordered exposure/proximity to Albanians by region, coded 0 = primarily Serb region, 1 = border region, 2 = primarily Albanian region

model_specification: Two-limit Tobit regression with censoring at 0 and 5 euros; the reported z statistic is the Wald test for the ordered exposure coefficient
controls: female, age, education, employed, village, alpha violence, alpha damage, displaced
operationalization_notes: The paper treats the three regions as decreasing/increasing proximity to Albanians and uses Tobit models for dictator giving; I used the out-group giving outcome and an ordered regional exposure score to test the directional claim directly while retaining the paper's extended controls.
reasoning: In a Tobit model for out-group dictator giving, the ordered exposure/proximity coefficient was positive (b = 1.016 euros per exposure category) and statistically different from zero, z = 3.18, p = 0.0015. This supports the claim that out-group bridging altruism increases with exposure to the out-group.

dependent_variable: enjoyrelativ: relative preference/enjoyment rating comparing the target animated sword-fight clip to the initial comparison clip, with higher values indicating greater preference for the target clip
main_predictor: condition: commercial-interruption condition ('good', interrupted by Bell South Yellow Pages commercial) versus no-interruption condition ('no')
sample_definition: Study 2 experiencer data from study 2 data.xlsx; included rows with condition equal to 'good' or 'no' and nonmissing enjoyrelativ, excluding blank/nonparticipant rows (N = 102).
model_specification: Two-sample independent t-test comparing mean enjoyrelativ between interrupted-commercial and no-interruption groups, using pooled variance/equal variances.
operationalization_notes: The paper's Study 2 methods identify the relative preference/enjoyment rating as the primary measure for whether the commercial disruption made the target program more enjoyable; the randomized condition directly contrasts an interrupted commercial viewing experience with a continuous one.
reasoning: Using the 102 participants with a valid interruption condition, the interrupted-commercial condition had higher relative enjoyment of the target clip than the no-interruption condition (M = 5.38 vs. 4.47). A pooled independent-samples t-test gave t(100) = 2.447, p = 0.016, supporting the claim that commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable.

dependent_variable: resigninvest: belief that Swensen was resigning because he was under investigation for bribery, recoded 1 = not likely at all to 4 = very likely
main_predictor: causal correction condition versus denial-of-innuendo condition
sample_definition: Respondents assigned to innuendo, denial, or causal-correction conditions who answered the resignation-investigation rumor item; control group excluded because this item was not asked there (N = 764).
model_specification: Weighted least-squares regression of resigninvest on denial and causal-correction indicators with innuendo-only as the reference category; main test is the linear contrast causal correction minus denial.
controls: None; inverse probability weights used to account for block-randomized assignment probabilities.
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies the investigation-rumor item as the direct measure of acceptance of the specific innuendo and estimates it only among respondents exposed to the rumor, so I tested whether the causal correction reduced this outcome more than denial-only using the paper's IPW OLS approach.
reasoning: In an inverse-probability-weighted OLS model among respondents exposed to the innuendo, the causal-correction condition produced lower acceptance of the resignation-investigation rumor than the denial-only condition by 0.335 scale points, t(761) = -5.07, p = 5.12e-7. This supports the claim that the alternate causal explanation was more effective than evidentiary denial at limiting the misperception.

dependent_variable: Intimacy score recomputed as the mean of the four intimacy questionnaire items, with the reversed concern item reverse-coded
main_predictor: Attention condition (partner signal blue 80% of trials vs 0% of trials)
sample_definition: All observations in Sheet3 with complete condition and intimacy-item data (15 attention, 15 no-attention)
model_specification: Independent-samples Student t-test comparing mean intimacy between attention and no-attention conditions
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies Study 2a as the laboratory test comparing attention versus no attention and reports no sex effects, so I used the unadjusted condition comparison for the intimacy outcome. Although the paper mentions excluding one participant who suspected deception, the data file did not provide a usable exclusion flag, so the analysis used all complete records available in the sheet.
reasoning: Using the Study 2a data, participants in the attention condition had higher recomputed intimacy scores (M = 4.58) than participants in the no-attention condition (M = 2.78), t(28) = 6.20, p = 1.07e-6. This supports the claim that receiving partner attention increased intimacy.

dependent_variable: q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2: indicator for being interested in learning more in the future about how the district government spends money in the budget
main_predictor: taxgrp: assignment to tax treatment versus windfall treatment
sample_definition: All 1,863 randomized participants with non-missing q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2 and taxgrp values; tax and windfall groups pooled across information-treatment conditions
model_specification: Two-sample difference-in-means test comparing tax versus windfall assignment, using the unequal-variance/Neyman standard error for the treatment effect
operationalization_notes: The paper identifies willingness to learn more about budget spending as the main monitoring measure for H1, and estimates the tax-versus-windfall average treatment effect by assignment in the full sample.
reasoning: In the full randomized sample, 81.10% of participants assigned to the tax treatment were interested in learning more about how the district government spends budget money, compared with 75.97% in the windfall group. The 5.13 percentage-point difference was positive and statistically significant in a Welch/Neyman difference-in-means test, t(1847.31)=2.70, p=0.007, supporting the claim that the tax treatment increased monitoring.

dependent_variable: turnout
main_predictor: z1elite_avgprox (standardized social proximity to elites)
sample_definition: All observations in Alexandria_Data.tsv, corresponding to eligible voters in the 1859 Alexandria, Virginia statewide elections (white males at least age 21), N = 2216.

controls: Household wealth, log household wealth, mid-status occupation, high-status occupation, home ownership, age, log age, church membership, U.S.-born indicator, and network centrality (z1ev).
operationalization_notes: The paper's turnout hypothesis is tested most directly by the Table 1-style model for the historical Alexandria election, using the eligible-voter sample, binary turnout outcome, and standardized elite-proximity predictor with the resource and demographic controls described in the methods.
reasoning: In a logistic regression of turnout among eligible Alexandria voters, the coefficient for standardized social proximity to elites was positive (b = 0.557) and statistically significant, z = 4.44, p = 8.85e-06. This supports the claim that individuals more socially proximate to elites turned out at a higher rate.

dependent_variable: Utilitarian response coded as decision to push (1=push, 0=no push)
main_predictor: Mood condition (positive vs negative)
sample_definition: Experiment 1 participants assigned to the active-frame condition only; all nonmissing observations in that frame were included (100 positive mood, 100 negative mood).
model_specification: Independent-samples Student t-test comparing mean binary utilitarian response rates between positive- and negative-mood groups, with the contrast oriented positive minus negative.
operationalization_notes: The paper's Experiment 1 methods used a 2 x 2 between-participants design with binary yes/no moral judgments and specifically tested this claim within the active frame; therefore I analyzed the active-frame subset and compared the push-response indicator across the two mood conditions without covariates.
reasoning: Among participants in the active-frame condition, 28/100 in the positive-mood group gave a utilitarian response versus 9/100 in the negative-mood group. An independent-samples t-test on the binary push decision gave t(198)=3.55, two-sided p=0.00048, supporting greater utilitarian responding in positive than negative moods.

dependent_variable: TVA visual processing speed estimate v (Hz)
main_predictor: auditory alerting condition: 85 dB cue versus no cue
sample_definition: All 28 participants in Experiment 1 with available participant-level TVA parameter estimates; paired no-cue and 85 dB cue processing-speed values included.
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing v_85dBCue to v_NoCue within participants.
operationalization_notes: The claim specifically concerns phasic auditory alerting increasing visual processing speed; Experiment 1 directly manipulated presence versus absence of an 85 dB auditory cue and the supplied dataset contains the TVA processing-speed estimates described in the methods.
reasoning: In Experiment 1, the mean TVA visual processing speed was higher in the 85 dB auditory cue condition (M = 92.69 Hz) than in the no-cue condition (M = 66.90 Hz). A paired-samples t-test on the 28 participant-level processing-speed estimates gave t(27) = 4.71, p = 0.000067, supporting an increase in visual processing speed with phasic auditory alerting.

dependent_variable: ln(average owner-reported housing value on the census block)
main_predictor: PLAN × central-city/bigger-side-of-border × 1980 indicator (yesbig1980)
sample_definition: Census blocks adjacent to nonsouthern city-suburban school district borders observed in 1970 and 1980, after the paper's exclusions for Georgia, border 44, one-sided/year-incomplete borders, zero-population blocks, and requiring nonmissing housing value with positive owner-occupied unit weight; N = 4,352 block-year observations clustered in 118 school-district jurisdictions.
model_specification: Weighted least squares difference-in-differences regression of log housing value on the desegregation-plan city-side post-1980 interaction and a general city-side post-1980 interaction, with side-of-border fixed effects and border-by-year fixed effects; cluster-robust inference by school district jurisdiction.
controls: Side-of-border fixed effects; border-by-year fixed effects; general central-city/bigger-side × 1980 interaction; observations weighted by number of owner-occupied units on the block.
operationalization_notes: The paper's main housing-price claim is most directly tested by its border-sample DID design for log owner-occupied housing values, comparing changes from 1970 to 1980 on city versus suburban sides of borders in areas with versus without a desegregation court order.
reasoning: In a weighted block-level difference-in-differences model, the treatment interaction coefficient for desegregation-plan city-side blocks in 1980 was negative (b = -0.0584, cluster-robust SE = 0.0278), giving t(117) = -2.10, p = 0.0378. This indicates that owner-occupied housing values declined by about 5.8 percent on treated central-city sides of borders relative to neighboring suburbs and comparison borders.

dependent_variable: fraud_ordered: three-category assessment of whether the 2011 Duma elections were free/fair versus fraudulent, ordered so higher values indicate greater skepticism/fraud perception
main_predictor: opp_do_know dummy: opposition voter who correctly identified Golos, compared with the omitted category of opposition voter who did not know Golos
sample_definition: Complete cases from the survey with nonmissing fraud_ordered, demographic controls, media/political engagement controls, and group-by-Golos-knowledge dummies; all voter-orientation groups included in the model, with the reported contrast within opposition voters (N = 1728).
model_specification: Ordered logistic regression with group-by-Golos-knowledge indicators; opposition voters not knowing Golos were the reference category, so the main coefficient tests the within-opposition difference associated with knowing Golos.
controls: sex, age, Moscow residence, private-sector employment, financial status, education, interest in political news, state TV use, VKontakte use, Odnoklassniki use, survey round, Facebook use, LiveJournal use, and evaluation of family economic situation last year; plus indicators for non-voters not knowing Golos, non-voters knowing Golos, regime voters not knowing Golos, and regime voters knowing Golos.

I implemented the opposition-voter contrast by omitting opposition voters who did not know Golos and estimating the coefficient for opposition voters who did know Golos.
reasoning: In an ordered-logit model of Duma election fraud perceptions, the coefficient for opposition voters who correctly identified Golos, relative to otherwise comparable opposition voters who did not, was positive (log-odds = 0.613; OR = 1.85) and statistically significant, z = 2.53, p = 0.0115. This supports the claim that regime opponents familiar with Golos were more likely to view the Duma elections as fraudulent.

dependent_variable: eth_supp (party support for ethnic minority rights)
main_predictor: Economic left-right position (lrecon), tested as the lrecon + lrecon:comm_dom_min slope when comm_dom_min = 1
sample_definition: Party-level observations in the 14-country CHES party dataset with non-missing eth_supp, lrecon, comm_dom_min, communist-regime type, transition year, GDP per capita, district magnitude, and country cluster identifiers; N = 195 across 14 countries.
model_specification: OLS regression: eth_supp ~ lrecon * comm_dom_min + C(comm) + free + GDP per capita PPP + district magnitude, with country-cluster-robust standard errors; the main test is the linear combination for the lrecon slope in federal-center-minority countries.

operationalization_notes: The paper's methods report individual-level OLS for this exact claim, but the supplied data file is the party-level dataset. I therefore used the closely related party-level operationalization described in the methods: whether, in countries with minorities originating from a federal center, left-wing parties are more supportive of minority rights than right-wing parties.
reasoning: In an OLS model of party support for ethnic minorities, the estimated slope of economic left-right among countries with federal-center-origin minorities was negative (b = -0.578, cluster-robust SE = 0.254), t(13) = -2.27, p = 0.041. Because higher left-right scores indicate more right-wing economics, this indicates that more left-wing parties were more supportive of these minorities, consistent with the study's claim that such minorities are aligned with the left.

dependent_variable: Number of actions in the video identified as choices
main_predictor: Cultural context/group (U.S. American vs Indian)
sample_definition: Study 3 participants assigned to the construal-of-choice condition with nonmissing numactions data; U.S. n = 30 and Indian n = 34.
model_specification: Welch independent-samples t-test comparing the number of identified choice actions between U.S. and Indian participants in the choice condition.
operationalization_notes: Study 3 directly operationalizes the claim about construing other individuals' behaviors as choices by having participants press a button whenever an actor in a video made a choice; the simple culture comparison within this choice condition is the most direct test of the stated claim.
reasoning: In Study 3's construal-of-choice condition, U.S. participants identified more of the actor's video behaviors as choices than Indian participants (M_US = 38.33, n = 30; M_IN = 22.68, n = 34). A Welch two-sample t-test gave t(53.22) = 3.05, p = .0036, supporting the claimed cultural difference.

dependent_variable: Reverse-coded willingness to disclose ratings, so higher scores indicate greater willingness to self-censor (WSC), measured for each of four potential information recipients.
main_predictor: Ordered recipient condition representing increasing perceived distance/publicity: closely related figures, in-group superiors, in-group NGOs, out-group NGOs.
sample_definition: All 71 Study 1 Israeli-Jewish participants in the provided Study 1.sav dataset; no exclusions because all had complete WSC and political-orientation data.
model_specification: For each participant I computed the within-person linear slope of WSC across the four ordered recipient conditions, then fit an OLS regression of that slope on centered political orientation; the reported t test is the intercept test of whether the adjusted average linear trend is greater than zero (reported with two-sided p value).
controls: Centered self-reported political orientation on the original 1=extreme right to 5=extreme left scale.
operationalization_notes: The paper's Study 1 methods identify recipient type as a within-subject manipulation and political orientation as a covariate. I used a pre-specified linear trend because the target claim is directional: WSC should rise as recipients become more distant and disclosure more public.
reasoning: I tested the ordered within-person trend in WSC across recipients from close/private to distant/public while controlling for political orientation. The adjusted mean linear slope was positive (0.628 WSC scale units per recipient-order step), t(69)=9.43, p=4.96e-14, with observed means increasing from close relations (2.99) and superiors (3.01) to Israeli NGOs (4.06) and outside NGOs (4.73).

dependent_variable: log(total output across periods 1-8 + 1)
main_predictor: T_Continuous treatment indicator versus Baseline constant wage, with T_Sudden and T_Successive indicators also included
sample_definition: Agents in the main experiment only (mainexp == 1), aggregated to one observation per subject across all eight working periods; N=211 subjects, excluding the five harsh/salient wage-increase cases already absent from the analysis dataset.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of subject-level log(total output + 1) on treatment indicators for T_Sudden, T_Successive, and T_Continuous plus trial-task ability; HC1 robust standard errors; main test is the T_Continuous coefficient.
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns overall performance under the continuous small-increase wage profile relative to a constant wage, so I followed the paper's overall treatment-effect specification using total output per subject in the main experiment and the constant-wage Baseline as the omitted category.
reasoning: In the main experiment subject-level OLS regression, the coefficient for T_Continuous relative to the constant-wage Baseline was 0.1484 on log(total output + 1), with a robust SE of 0.0696, t(206)=2.13, p=0.034. This indicates significantly higher total performance under continuously increasing wages than under constant wages.

dependent_variable: Rating of how big the eaten food portion was (Q27.0; 1 = very small, 9 = very big)
main_predictor: Observation condition: camera/observed versus no-camera control
sample_definition: All 82 Study 1 participants in the dataset with nonmissing condition and portion-size rating; no exclusions
model_specification: Two-sample independent t-test comparing mean portion-size ratings between observed and control groups, using pooled variance/equal-variance degrees of freedom
operationalization_notes: The Study 1 methods identify perceived size of the eaten corn-chip portion as the critical dependent measure and the camera versus no-camera manipulation as the one-factor between-subjects design, so this direct group comparison tests the target claim.
reasoning: In an independent-samples t-test, participants in the camera/observed condition rated the eaten portion as larger (M = 4.846, n = 39) than participants in the no-camera control condition (M = 4.000, n = 43), t(80) = 2.204, p = 0.030. This supports the claim that being observed while eating increased recalled/perceived portion size.

dependent_variable: Percentage of women in the legislature (npctwomenlegsal)
main_predictor: All = 0 dummy (avg_pv_0), indicating ballot, pool, and vote rules all equal zero / most party-centered systems
sample_definition: Election-year observations for the 57 countries listed in the paper appendix from 1980-2005, restricted to complete cases for the dependent variable, All = 0 predictor, and included controls (N = 232).
model_specification: Prais-Winsten linear panel regression with a common AR(1) correction and panel-corrected standard error; reported statistic is the z test for the All = 0 coefficient.
controls: Log district magnitude, left vote, years since women's suffrage, legislative seats, log GDP per capita, percent female labor-force participation, and government spending as percent of GDP.
operationalization_notes: The broad claim concerns party-centered versus candidate-centered electoral rules, so I used the paper's composite All = 0 indicator from its all-countries Model 4 specification as the main predictor and the paper's primary outcome and controls.
reasoning: In a Prais-Winsten panel regression, the coefficient on the party-centered electoral-system dummy (All = 0) was positive (b = 4.78 percentage points) and statistically distinguishable from zero using a panel-corrected SE (z = 2.43, p = 0.015, N = 232). This supports the claim that systems with weak personal-vote incentives have higher women's legislative representation than more candidate-centered systems.

dependent_variable: First implementation/extension of overseas voting rights to expatriate citizens (event indicator in a country-year survival model)
main_predictor: k6delta: whether the six-nearest-neighbor spatial lag of overseas voting changed during the previous two years, indicating a recent nearby franchise extension

model_specification: Cox proportional hazards regression with start-stop yearly intervals (_t0 to _t), Breslow ties, and standard errors clustered by country.
controls: Election year, referendum year, British Empire history, French Empire history, Spanish Empire history, English legal origin, ln(per-capita GDP), ln(population), and ln(years since regime change).
operationalization_notes: I used the baseline specification corresponding to the paper's main Table 1 column III, because the claim concerns the hazard of first extending expatriate voting rights after neighboring countries' recent adoption decisions.
reasoning: In a Cox proportional hazards model, the coefficient for recent nearby franchise extension was positive (log hazard ratio = 0.6240; hazard ratio = 1.87) with z = 2.99 and p = 0.0028. This indicates that countries were significantly more likely to extend overseas voting rights within two years after one of their six nearest neighbors did so, consistent with the original diffusion claim.

dependent_variable: Log real annual earnings for men (logincom_male)
main_predictor: Indicator for observations after the father-in-law's death (post_fILdie_male)
sample_definition: SLCC person-year observations for men aged 22-45 with nonmissing log annual earnings, father-in-law death indicator, province, individual ID, and years-married measure; observations with div_male == 1 were excluded.
model_specification: OLS linear regression with individual fixed effects and province-by-year fixed effects; inference used standard errors clustered by individual. The reported t-test is for the post_fILdie_male coefficient, using cluster degrees of freedom G-1.
controls: Cubic in age, years married, province-year fixed effects, and individual fixed effects; time-invariant education is absorbed by the individual fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: I used the paper's main equation (1) for log earnings and the SLCC sample corresponding to the paper's main earnings analysis, because the claim concerns the change in a man's earnings after the loss of his father-in-law.
reasoning: In a fixed-effects regression on the SLCC pseudo-panel, the post-father-in-law-death coefficient was negative (about -0.070 log points), but the cluster-robust test was not conventionally significant: t(2963) = -1.398, p = 0.162. Thus, although the estimated direction is consistent with lower earnings after the father-in-law's death, this reanalysis does not provide statistically conclusive evidence for the claim under this specification.

dependent_variable: Progressive vote on the first Blessed Virgin Mary schema (IFRSTBV0)
main_predictor: Interaction between RCC incumbency and organizational-field structuration by strong Protestant presence (NINCUMBE × NSTRUCTU; XINCUMS0)
sample_definition: Bishops with non-missing first-BVM vote, country-level NIT variables, religious-competition variables, interaction terms, and country cluster identifier; complete-case N = 1,921.

reasoning: In a clustered logistic regression predicting a progressive vote on the first Blessed Virgin Mary schema, the interaction between RCC incumbency and a structurated Protestant field was positive and statistically significant (log-odds = 1.523, z = 4.158, p = 0.000032). This supports the claim that NIT-derived features of bishops' organizational fields predicted voting in a direction consistent with prioritizing legitimacy concerns.

dependent_variable: PopDIFF_MaxCov_T1: difference between population/students that would be covered by coverage-maximizing primary-school locations and those actually covered by schools built in 2002-09; lower values indicate placement closer to the coverage-maximizing spatial allocation.
main_predictor: Congruence_20km_CRavg_T1: local-government average institutional congruence with 20 km buffers around precolonial power centers, scaled 0-1.
sample_definition: Local governments in the 2002-09 primary-school location-allocation dataset with non-missing outcome, congruence, region, and model covariates; N = 283, clustered by 11 2002 regions.
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression with cluster-robust standard errors by 2002 region; reported statistic is the t test for the institutional congruence coefficient.
controls: Logged local-government population, local-government population density, baseline share of villages with schools, number of new schools built by the local government in 2002-09, percent of village names with Mouride markers, average logged distance to navigable waterway, average elevation, and Ferlo ecological-zone indicator.
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns broad spatial distribution, so I used the paper's location-allocation coverage analysis rather than the village-level access logit. A negative coefficient on the coverage shortfall means areas with stronger precolonial institutional congruence built closer to the locations that maximize spatial coverage.

operationalization_notes: The paper operationalizes Hypothesis 2 using the restricted risk-averse sample and correlating LV error rate with the average number of safe choices in the PV and RV formats, so I reproduced that direct subject-level correlation from the raw choice variables.
reasoning: Among the 79 subjects classified as risk averse by averaging at least 5 safe choices across the PV and RV tasks, the Pearson correlation between LV decision-error rate and average safe choices was r = -0.4625, df = 77, p = 1.78e-05. The negative and statistically significant relationship supports the claim that decision error decreases as risk aversion increases.

dependent_variable: Desired compensation, coded in thousands of dollars using midpoints of selected salary ranges
main_predictor: Public treatment indicator: questionnaire said 'your' answers, rather than anonymized answers, would be discussed with the career class
sample_definition: Primary experiment respondents who were female, single, and had nonmissing desired compensation
model_specification: OLS regression of desired compensation on the public-treatment indicator; reported test is the coefficient test for public treatment using HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
operationalization_notes: The claim directly concerns the primary experiment's single female students and their reported desired salaries under classmate observability, so I used the single-women subsample and the desired-compensation outcome with the randomized public/private treatment as the sole predictor.
reasoning: Among single female students, mean desired compensation was 131.05 thousand dollars in the private condition and 112.93 thousand dollars in the public condition. An OLS regression with HC1 robust standard errors estimated a public-treatment effect of -18.12 thousand dollars, t(58) = -2.22, p = 0.030, supporting lower reported desired salaries when classmates could see responses.

dependent_variable: pay_for_conditionality: indicator that the parent was willing to pay a positive amount to keep the cash transfer conditional on attendance
main_predictor: text-message monitoring treatment versus baseline treatment
sample_definition: Parents assigned to the baseline treatment (treatment==1) or text-message treatment (treatment==2) with nonmissing pay_for_conditionality; all text-message-assigned parents were included, including those without a cell phone.
model_specification: Two-sample pooled z-test for equality of proportions, coded as text-message proportion minus baseline proportion.
operationalization_notes: The claim is explicitly about the proportion of parents willing to pay to keep conditionality dropping relative to baseline, so I directly compared the binary willingness-to-pay indicator between the baseline and text-message experimental cells.
reasoning: Among baseline parents, 49 of 60 (81.7%) were willing to pay to keep the conditionality, compared with 10 of 51 (19.6%) in the text-message treatment. A two-sample pooled test of proportions gave z = -6.53, p = 6.59e-11, indicating a large and statistically significant drop with text-message monitoring.

dependent_variable: Monthly count of homicides presumed to be related to drug trafficking (government DTO-related deaths; deaths_total)
main_predictor: Indicator for 1-6 months after a leader capture/killing in the municipality (lpub_after06)
