dependent_variable: gdpidx (annual city GDP growth index, ~100 + growth rate)
main_predictor: msec2currentsec (binary indicator: city party secretary previously promoted by the current provincial party secretary)
sample_definition: All city-year observations in the merged citypanel_base + econ_panel with non-missing gdpidx and connection variables, 1999-onwards
model_specification: OLS with city fixed effects and year fixed effects; cluster-robust standard errors clustered by city
controls: City and year fixed effects only (no additional time-varying covariates)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns city leaders' informal ties to the incumbent provincial leader and economic growth. The most direct test is to regress the city-level GDP growth index on the binary indicator that the city party secretary has a patronage tie to the sitting provincial party secretary, absorbing time-invariant city characteristics and common shocks via two-way fixed effects, with city-clustered SEs.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects regression of city-year GDP growth index (gdpidx) on the city party secretary's connection to the incumbent provincial party secretary (msec2currentsec), controlling for city and year fixed effects with SEs clustered by city, the coefficient on connection is -0.31 (t = -2.44, p = 0.015, n = 4901). The estimate is negative and statistically significant — i.e., connected city leaders are associated with slightly *slower*, not faster, GDP growth, the opposite of the headline claim.

dependent_variable: Indicator for player-season on an A-level national team (high-ability proxy)
main_predictor: Post-1991 dummy (Danish preferential tax scheme for foreigners)
sample_definition: Player-season observations of foreign (non-Danish nationality) players in Denmark's league, 1975-2008
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test comparing mean high-ability indicator pre vs post-1991
operationalization_notes: Denmark introduced a preferential tax scheme for high-income foreigners in 1991. I proxy ability by current A-level national-team status (the most discriminating tier in the data) and compare foreign players' mean ability before vs after the reform within the Danish league.
reasoning: Among foreign players in the Danish league, the share appearing on an A-level national team (a proxy for high ability) rose from 29.5% before the 1991 preferential tax scheme for foreigners to 58.1% after, a difference highly significant by Welch's t-test (t=5.57, df≈105, p<0.001). This supports the claim that the Danish tax cut for foreigners shifted the ability composition toward higher-ability players.

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay
main_predictor: intrin_extrin (intrinsic relative to extrinsic values)
sample_definition: All 155 participants in Study 1 dataset
model_specification: Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: Claim is a bivariate association; used the precomputed intrinsic-minus-extrinsic relative-values index and the willingness_to_pay composite.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between intrinsic-minus-extrinsic value endorsement (intrin_extrin) and willingness_to_pay was r=.426, p<.001, N=155, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: ln_imports (logged product-level imports of the disputed good from the partner)
main_predictor: Interaction of partner role (complainant vs nonparticipant) with mutually agreed solution / early-settle indicator in post-dispute years (complainant_mas vs nonparticipant_mas)
sample_definition: All product-level dispute–partner–respondent–year observations 1995–2011 with non-missing covariates (window of startyear-2 to endyear+5).
model_specification: OLS with dispute and year fixed effects; cluster-robust SEs at dispute level; linear hypothesis test that complainant_mas = nonparticipant_mas
controls: complainant_ruling, nonparticipant_ruling, ln_gdp_resp, ln_gdp_part, ln_income_resp, ln_income_part, dempair, dispute FE, year FE
operationalization_notes: The pre-constructed interaction terms (complainant_mas, nonparticipant_mas, etc.) capture post-dispute imports under each settlement type; testing the equality of complainant_mas and nonparticipant_mas operationalizes the claim that complainants gain disproportionately more than the rest of the membership under private settlements.
reasoning: Post-dispute ln_imports regressed on complainant×MAS, nonparticipant×MAS, complainant×ruling, nonparticipant×ruling plus market controls and dispute and year fixed effects (cluster-robust SEs on dispute). The complainant×MAS coefficient (1.96) significantly exceeds the nonparticipant×MAS coefficient (-0.03); difference = 1.99, z = 2.92, p = 0.004. Complainants gain disproportionately more under private (early) settlements, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (GEM rate of new business formation, country-year)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of working-age population, 20-64)
sample_definition: All GEM country-year observations 2001-2010 with non-missing variables (N=393, 82 countries)
model_specification: Weighted OLS with year fixed effects; weights = country-year sample size (nobs_cy); SEs clustered by countryid
controls: Year fixed effects only (baseline specification, Table 2 col. 3 analogue)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's baseline country-year regression (revealed via the log file from the data archive): dep var entre_wage, predictor medage_20_64, weighted by nobs_cy, clustered by countryid, year FEs.
reasoning: Weighted OLS of entrepreneurial rate (entre_wage) on median age (medage_20_64) with year fixed effects and country-clustered SEs yields a coefficient of -0.0073 (t=-5.71, p<0.001, N=393, 82 country clusters), i.e., higher median age is associated with lower new business formation — equivalently, lower median age increases entrepreneurship, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Perceived/actual arm length ratio (RatioRight vs RatioLeft)
main_predictor: Arm side (right vs left), within-subject
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (Handedness==2), n=15
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test on RatioRight vs RatioLeft
operationalization_notes: The dataset includes perceived/actual ratios for each arm; comparing them within right-handers via paired t-test directly tests the claim that the right arm is perceived as relatively longer than the left.
reasoning: Among right-handed participants (n=15), the perceived-to-actual length ratio was larger for the right arm (M=0.970) than the left arm (M=0.920), paired t(14)=2.12, p=.052, directionally consistent with the claim that right-handers perceive their right arm as longer (relative to actual) than their left.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (mean of appreciated, valued, satisfied; 7-point scales)
main_predictor: condition (0=acknowledgment only / verbal; 1=5-cent acknowledgment / financial)
sample_definition: All participants who completed Study 1a (exclude=0); N=49
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: Study 1a directly contrasts verbal vs. small financial acknowledgment on a composite outcome index already provided (dv_index3), which most directly maps to 'less positive outcomes' in the claim.
reasoning: Participants in the verbal-only acknowledgment condition reported significantly more positive responses (M=5.57) than those receiving a 5-cent financial acknowledgment (M=4.38) on the 3-item index, t(47)=2.92, p=.005, supporting the trivialization effect.

dependent_variable: s_tot (standardized total test score)
main_predictor: avg5_girl (share of girls among 5 nearest neighbors)
sample_definition: Female students with non-missing s_tot, avg5_girl, and classroom (gc)
model_specification: OLS regression of s_tot on avg5_girl with classroom fixed effects; standard errors clustered by classroom
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns the effect on female students of being surrounded by 5 females vs 5 males. avg5_girl operationalizes the gender composition of the 5 nearest neighbors; restricting to girl==1 isolates female outcomes. Random seat assignment within classroom motivates classroom fixed effects.
reasoning: Among female students, the share of girls among the five nearest neighbors (avg5_girl, 0-1 scale) positively predicts standardized total test score with coefficient 0.68 SD (going from 0 to 5 girls), t=3.00, p=0.003, with classroom fixed effects and cluster-robust SE. Direction matches the paper's claim that more female neighbors improve female test scores.

dependent_variable: Attitude stability operationalized as -|mean(att1-3)_T2 - mean(att1-3)_T1|
main_predictor: Ambivalence × Certainty interaction (mean-centered)
sample_definition: All Study 1 participants with non-missing attitude, ambivalence, and certainty measures (N=174)
model_specification: OLS regression: stability ~ amb_c * cert_c
operationalization_notes: Study 1 used as the primary test. Ambivalence computed via Griffin formula from pos/neg ratings; certainty as mean of 7 certainty items; stability as negative absolute T1-T2 attitude change so higher = more stable. Predictors mean-centered for interpretable interaction.
reasoning: In Study 1, regressing attitude stability (negative absolute change in mean attitude from T1 to T2) on mean-centered ambivalence (Griffin: (P+N)/2-|P-N|), mean-centered certainty (mean of cert1-7) and their interaction yielded a significant negative interaction (b=-0.044, t(170)=-2.66, p=.009). The negative sign indicates that the positive effect of certainty on stability weakens (and becomes negative) as ambivalence increases — i.e., certainty predicted greater stability when ambivalence was lower, matching the claim.

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters, 'turnout')
main_predictor: Log inward FDI stock (logfdistockliab) — foreign ownership
sample_definition: Country-election observations with non-missing turnout, logfdistockliab, and controls (569 obs across countries/years)
model_specification: OLS with country fixed effects and linear year trend; cluster-robust SEs by country
controls: log trade, log GDP per capita, growth, unemployment, PR electoral system, compulsory voting (cvfranklin)
operationalization_notes: Operationalized 'foreign ownership' as log inward FDI stock (liabilities), the standard measure in the compensation/constraint literature. Dropped covariates with severe missingness (vap3069, closeness, enps) to preserve sample. Country FE + time trend addresses unobserved heterogeneity.
reasoning: Panel regression of national-election turnout on log inward FDI stock (foreign ownership) with country fixed effects, a linear time trend, and standard political-economic controls yields a coefficient of -1.55 (cluster-robust SE 0.57, t=-2.70, p=0.007, n=569). Consistent with the ownership-constraint hypothesis, greater foreign ownership is associated with lower turnout.

dependent_variable: complaints_2008 (number of service complaints in 2008)
main_predictor: first_A (firm name begins with 'A' or a number)
sample_definition: All 2293 plumbing firms in final_data.dta
model_specification: OLS regression of complaints on first_A indicator (equivalent to two-sample t-test of means)
operationalization_notes: Used the analysis dataset final_data.dta which already encodes first_A and complaints_2008, matching the claim's direct comparison of mean complaints between A/number-starting firms and others.
reasoning: OLS regression of 2008 complaints on first_A indicator yields a coefficient of 1.09 (SE 0.16), t(2291)=6.79, p<1e-10. Firms whose names start with A or a number average 1.34 complaints vs 0.25 for others, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Bargaining strategy (dv, 4-category ordinal, higher = more cooperative/concession-offering)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure (extent to which states value issues differently)
sample_definition: All 588 state-negotiation observations in the EU bargaining dataset with non-missing values on all model variables
model_specification: Ordered logistic regression (proportional-odds) with cutpoints estimated via MLE
controls: lag_dv, agreement_importance, voting_power, foreignpolicy, new_ms, qmv, euro, publicity, presidency, lngdp, pillarii, pillariii, parl_scrut
operationalization_notes: Followed the dataset's evident structure: dv is an ordinal bargaining-strategy scale and issue_linkage_structure is the empirical operationalization of differential issue valuation. Used ordered logit with the full set of substantive and institutional controls included in the data file.
reasoning: Ordered logit of bargaining strategy (dv, 0-3) on issue_linkage_structure plus controls yields a positive coefficient of 1.047 (z=13.33, p<0.001, N=588), indicating that more differently valued issues are strongly associated with more cooperative (concession-offering) bargaining strategies.

dependent_variable: credittogovtstateenterp (credit to government and SOEs, % GDP)
main_predictor: icrg_qog (ICRG quality of government index; higher = stronger state, so negative coefficient supports claim that weaker states direct more credit to government)
sample_definition: All country-years in Country Year Dataset.dta with non-missing DV, state-strength, and market-power measures
model_specification: OLS with country and year fixed effects, country-clustered SEs
controls: marketpower (bank market power, proxy for profit potential of financial repression); country FE; year FE
operationalization_notes: Claim explicitly conditions on profit potential of financial repression, so I include marketpower as the control and use ICRG quality-of-government as the inverse measure of state weakness. Two-way FE handles country/year heterogeneity in the panel.
reasoning: Two-way FE OLS of credit to government/SOEs on ICRG quality-of-government (state strength) controlling for bank market power (financial-repression profit) yields a negative coefficient on state strength (b=-10.29, cluster-robust SE=5.65, t=-1.82, p=0.068, N=1411). The sign matches the claim that weaker states channel more credit to government/SOEs.

dependent_variable: dispute (MID involvement begins in year, lhost<=5)
main_predictor: lcoupsum (log of 1 + cumulative past coups)
sample_definition: Latin American country-years, 1960-99 (n=798 with non-missing covariates)
model_specification: Probit regression of dispute on lcoupsum with controls
controls: CINC, number of bordering countries, regional war, lagged log real GDP per capita, lagged Polity2, ethnic fractionalization
operationalization_notes: Threats to political survival operationalized as accumulated coup history (lcoupsum), consistent with diversionary-incentive literature; conflict involvement operationalized as onset of a MID (dispute). Single-equation probit; paper itself uses a reciprocal/IV system that is not reproduced here.
reasoning: In a probit model of dispute involvement on log of cumulative past coups (proxy for threats to leader survival) plus standard controls, the coefficient on lcoupsum is positive (b=0.106) but not statistically significant (z=1.005, p=0.315). The direction matches the claim but the single-equation estimate does not reach conventional significance.

dependent_variable: d12outgroup: amount (0-5) sent to out-group recipient in dictator game
main_predictor: Ordinal exposure to Albanians by region (0=Serb region, 1=border region, 2=Albanian region)
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb respondents in the replication dataset
model_specification: OLS regression of d12outgroup on ordinal exposure
operationalization_notes: Region of residence is the design-level exposure variable in the study (Serbs in Albanian-majority areas have the most contact with the out-group). Treated as ordinal to capture monotonic exposure gradient and yield a single t-test of the directional claim.
reasoning: Regressing dictator-game amount sent to out-group recipient on an ordinal exposure variable (0=Serb-majority region, 1=border region, 2=Albanian-majority region) yields a positive, highly significant slope (b=0.72, t(156)=4.25, p<0.001). Out-group bridging norms thus rise with exposure to the out-group, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: enjoyrelativ (relative enjoyment rating of the program)
main_predictor: condition (commercial interruption: 'good' vs. 'no')
sample_definition: All Study 2 participants with non-missing condition and enjoyment data (N=102)
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test comparing enjoyment between commercial and no-commercial conditions
operationalization_notes: The dataset contains two experimental groups; the most direct test of the claim that 'commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable' is a between-condition comparison of the enjoyment measure.
reasoning: Participants in the commercial-interruption condition reported significantly higher relative enjoyment (M=5.38) than those in the no-commercial condition (M=4.47); independent-samples t(100)=2.45, p=.016, supporting the claim that commercial disruption enhanced enjoyment.

dependent_variable: acceptedbribes (5-point agreement that Senator Swensen accepted bribes; higher = more acceptance of misperception)
main_predictor: Experimental condition: innuendo+denial (3) vs. innuendo+causal-correction (4)
sample_definition: Participants randomized to the denial or causal conditions with non-missing acceptedbribes response
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test comparing condition means
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts causal vs. denial corrections on misperception acceptance; the most direct test is comparing post-treatment acceptance of the bribery misperception between the denial and causal conditions.
reasoning: Among participants assigned to the denial (M=3.41) vs. causal-correction (M=2.94) conditions, those who received the causal explanation expressed significantly lower acceptance of the bribery misperception (Welch t=4.82, p<.001, n=519). The causal correction is more effective at reducing misperceptions than denial, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Intimacy (aggregated 10-item questionnaire score)
main_predictor: Partner attentiveness condition (attentive vs. inattentive; cnd 1 vs 2)
sample_definition: All 30 participants in Study 2a (Sheet3 of dataset)
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test comparing intimacy between attention conditions
operationalization_notes: Sheet3 contains the cleanest Study 2a data including an aggregated Intimacy variable and condition code. The claim is a between-condition contrast on intimacy, so a two-sample t-test on Intimacy by cnd is the most direct test.
reasoning: Participants in the attentive-partner condition (cnd=1, M=4.58) reported significantly higher intimacy than those in the inattentive-partner condition (cnd=2, M=2.78), t(28)=6.20, p<.001, consistent with the claim that received attention increases intimacy.

dependent_variable: q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2 (binary: interested in learning more about the district budget)
main_predictor: taxgrp (1 = tax treatment, 0 = windfall treatment; pools Z=2/4 vs Z=1/3)
sample_definition: All 1,863 survey respondents in Blora with non-missing treatment and outcome
model_specification: Linear probability model (OLS) of monitoring outcome on tax-treatment indicator with HC1 robust standard errors; equivalent to a two-proportion z-test
operationalization_notes: Among the survey items most directly capturing 'monitoring,' interest in learning more about the district budget (APBD) is the closest behavioral-intent monitoring measure; q145 (scrutinize) is an abstract agreement item with a ceiling, and postcard variables capture political action rather than monitoring per se.
reasoning: Pooled across information conditions, citizens assigned to the tax treatment (taxgrp=1) were 5.1 percentage points more likely to express interest in learning more about the district budget (APBD) than those in the windfall treatment (81.1% vs 76.0%); HC1-robust z = 2.70, p = .007, N = 1863. This directly supports the abstract's claim that the tax treatment increased monitoring.

dependent_variable: turnout (voted = 1)
main_predictor: z1elite_avgprox (standardized average network proximity to elites)
sample_definition: Pooled Alexandria 1859 and Newport 1874 electors with non-missing covariates
model_specification: Logistic regression with city fixed effect
controls: hhwealthlog, midstatus, highstatus, owner, agelog, usborn, z1ev (eigenvector centrality), city dummy
operationalization_notes: Pooled both historical datasets using their common variables; the modern survey replication is not in the provided data. Main predictor and DV chosen directly from claim wording.
reasoning: Pooled logistic regression of turnout on standardized average proximity to elites (z1elite_avgprox), with controls for wealth, status, ownership, age, nativity, eigenvector centrality, and city fixed effect, yields a positive coefficient of 0.914 (z=10.38, p<.001, N=5632). Individuals more socially proximate to elites are more likely to turn out, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Decision (push=utilitarian vs not push)
main_predictor: Mood (positive vs negative)
sample_definition: Active-frame condition only (frame==1), n=200
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 contingency table
operationalization_notes: Claim directly compares utilitarian responding between positive and negative moods within the active frame; chi-square on the 2x2 mood x decision table is the most direct test.
reasoning: In the active-frame subsample (n=200), 41% of positive-mood participants chose to push (utilitarian) vs 16% of negative-mood participants; chi-square(1)=15.34, p<.001, confirming the claim.

dependent_variable: TVA-estimated visual processing speed parameter v
main_predictor: Auditory alerting condition (85 dB cue vs no cue), within-subject
sample_definition: All 28 participants from Experiment 1 (mmc1.csv)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test (v_85dBCue vs v_NoCue)
operationalization_notes: Claim is supported by Experiment 1; the most direct test is a within-subject comparison of TVA processing speed v between alerting and no-alerting conditions.
reasoning: Paired t-test comparing TVA-estimated visual processing speed v between 85dB cue and no-cue in Experiment 1 yields t(27)=4.71, p<.001, with v higher under alerting (92.69 vs 66.90), consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: ln(average owner-occupied housing value) at the block group level (lnavval)
main_predictor: bigside_m × Cyear_1980 (interaction of central-city/'big' side of border with post-desegregation year 1980)
sample_definition: Block groups in tier 1 (closest to border, tierno<2), in border pairs where exactly one side ('big' city side) was under a court-ordered desegregation plan by 1980 (yesorder_m==1), excluding South and pre-1970 cases; pooled 1970 and 1980; lnavval and house_ownocc>0 non-missing.
model_specification: Weighted least squares (weight = owner-occupied housing units) with border-by-year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by school-district jurisdiction (jurcode).
controls: Border × year fixed effects (no additional covariates)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's replication log (deseg_results_aej.log): merged 1970 and 1980 block-group files, applied the same sample restrictions (drop Georgia, NYC-Floral Park, small-pop sides, one-sided borders, missing-year borders, early-1960s cases), built deseg / bigside_m / yesorder_m exactly as in the do-file, and ran the DiD using border×year FE which is the cleanest implementation of the border-discontinuity DiD identifying the effect of city-side desegregation on urban housing prices relative to suburbs.
reasoning: Difference-in-differences estimate of the city-suburban housing-value gap change between 1970 and 1980 in border areas with one-sided desegregation: big1980 (city × 1980) coefficient = -0.0964 (SE 0.028, t = -3.41, p < 0.001), implying urban owner-occupied housing values fell about 9-10% relative to neighboring suburbs after desegregation, consistent in sign and significance with the paper's headline 6% decline.

dependent_variable: fraud_ordered (ordered perception that Duma elections were fraudulent)
main_predictor: golos_correct (correctly identifies/knows Golos)
sample_definition: Opposition voters (opp_voter==1) with complete data on the model variables
model_specification: Ordered logistic regression
controls: sex, age, moscow, org_empl (private sector), fin_stat, educ, polnews, state_tv, vkont, odno, round, facebook, livej, famecon
operationalization_notes: Claim specifies opposition voters and contrasts those who 'know Golos' vs not; used the opposition-voter subsample with the binary Golos-knowledge indicator as predictor of the ordered fraud-perception outcome, including standard demographic and media controls available in the dataset.
reasoning: In an ordered logit model among opposition voters predicting the ordered fraud perception variable, knowing Golos correctly is associated with a significantly higher belief that the Duma elections were fraudulent (b=0.574, z=2.31, p=0.021, N=498), matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: lrecon (party economic left-right position; lower = more left)
main_predictor: eth_supp (party position on support for ethnic minorities)
sample_definition: Parties in countries coded as having ethnic minorities originating from a former federal center (comm_dom_min==1: Estonia, Latvia, Slovenia, Bosnia, Croatia); observations with non-missing lrecon and eth_supp
model_specification: OLS with country fixed effects: lrecon ~ eth_supp + C(country)
operationalization_notes: comm_dom_min flags countries with federal-center-origin minorities; eth_supp captures party-level affinity toward those minorities, so a negative slope means pro-minority parties (which are typically the minority parties themselves) are more left-leaning than majority parties within the same country.
reasoning: In the subsample of countries with ethnic minorities originating from a (former) communist federal center (comm_dom_min==1), regressing party economic left-right position (lrecon) on the party's support for ethnic minorities (eth_supp) with country fixed effects yields a negative, statistically significant coefficient (b=-0.213, t(62)=-2.84, p=0.006, N=68). More pro-minority parties are more economically left-leaning, consistent with the claim that federal-center-origin minorities are more left-leaning than the ethnic majorities.

dependent_variable: Number of actions construed as choices (numactions)
main_predictor: Culture (US vs. India)
sample_definition: Participants in the Choice (vs. Control) condition
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: The claim refers to construing behaviors as choices; the Choice condition is the one in which participants labeled another person's behaviors as choices, so I compared US vs. Indian counts in that condition.
reasoning: In the Choice condition (where participants construed another individual's behaviors as choices), U.S. participants identified more behaviors as choices (M=38.33, SD=23.02, n=30) than Indian participants (M=22.68, SD=17.19, n=34); independent-samples t(62)=3.11, p=.003.

dependent_variable: Willingness to self-censor (1-6 scale)
main_predictor: Recipient type (social distance: close relationship < superiors < Israeli NGO < outside/foreign NGO)
sample_definition: All 71 participants in Study 1 with complete WSC ratings across the four recipient types
model_specification: One-way repeated-measures ANOVA with recipient as the within-subject factor
operationalization_notes: The dataset contains four WSC scores per participant for recipients varying in distance; a within-subject ANOVA directly tests whether WSC differs across distance levels.
reasoning: A repeated-measures ANOVA across four recipient types ordered by social distance (close relationship, superiors, Israeli NGO, outside NGO) yielded F(3,210)=47.85, p<.001, with means rising monotonically from 2.99 to 4.73, indicating that greater distance from the recipient is associated with higher WSC.

dependent_variable: output (number of correctly completed tasks per period)
main_predictor: Treatment 3 indicator (continuous wage increases) vs constant wage (profile 0)
sample_definition: Subjects in the constant-wage control (profile 0) and the continuous-increase treatment (profile 3), all 8 periods
model_specification: OLS regression of output on treatment dummy, ability, female, and period fixed effects; SEs clustered at subject level
operationalization_notes: Profile 3 in the data increases wages by 10 each period (90→160), matching the 'continuous small increases' description; profile 0 is constant 125. Used panel OLS with subject-clustered SEs and controls for individual ability, gender, and period.
reasoning: Comparing the continuously-increasing-wage profile (treatment 3) to the constant-wage profile (control), the continuous-increase dummy has a positive coefficient of 0.526 on output (z=1.71, p=0.088, N=1768 obs from 221 subjects, clustered SEs). The direction matches the paper's claim that continuously increasing wages raise performance relative to a constant wage, though marginally significant at conventional levels.

dependent_variable: Recalled portion size ('How big was the food portion?', Q27.0)
main_predictor: Observation condition (camera vs no camera)
sample_definition: All 82 participants in Study1.sav with non-missing DV
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided Student's t-test
operationalization_notes: Claim refers specifically to recalled portion size; the single item Q27.0 directly measures this. Condition variable codes the observed vs unobserved manipulation.
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test comparing observed (condition=1, n=39, M=4.85) vs unobserved (condition=2, n=43, M=4.00) on the item 'How big was the food portion?' yields t(80)=2.20, p=.030, with observed participants recalling a larger portion, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: npctwomenlegsal (percent women in lower/sole legislative chamber)
main_predictor: avg_pv_0 (Carey–Shugart-style personal-vote index averaged across tiers)
sample_definition: Country-years 1980–2005 with complete data on the outcome, personal-vote index, log district magnitude, and controls (N=824)
model_specification: OLS regression with interaction between personal-vote index and log district magnitude
controls: log district magnitude, personal-vote × log magnitude interaction, ln GDP per capita, female labor force participation, years of women's suffrage, left vote share (Keefer), Polity2
operationalization_notes: Selected the most direct test of the claim: the coefficient on the personal-vote incentive index predicting women's legislative share, including the interaction with district magnitude that the paper emphasises and standard socioeconomic/political controls.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of percentage of women in the legislature on the personal-vote index (avg_pv_0), log district magnitude, their interaction, and standard controls (ln GDP per capita, female labor force participation, years of suffrage, left vote share, Polity2), the coefficient on the personal-vote variable is 3.61 with t=1.91 (p≈0.056, df=815, N=824). The direction is consistent with the authors' claim that party-centered systems (low personal-vote incentives) yield greater women's representation than candidate-centered systems, and is marginally significant.

dependent_variable: Hazard of enacting overseas voting (event = first year overseas voting introduced, from IDEA 2013), survival data with start/stop years
main_predictor: qdelta — binary indicator that the share of adjoining (queen-contiguity) neighbors with overseas voting changed within the previous two years
sample_definition: Country-years in the survival set (_st==1), i.e., before each country's adoption of overseas voting; observations with missing covariates dropped (N=4972 country-years, 94 adoption events)
model_specification: Cox proportional hazards model with time-varying covariates (lifelines CoxTimeVaryingFitter), country-year spells defined by _t0/_t and event _d
controls: log GDP (lngdp), log population (lnpop), Polity democracy score (politydem)
operationalization_notes: The phrase 'in the wake of neighbors' decisions' points to a recent-change spatial measure, and qdelta is labeled 'Has queenlag changed during previous two years?' — the most literal operationalization of recent neighbor adoption among contiguous neighbors. Cox PH is the natural model given the dataset is structured as survival data.

main_predictor: Treatment (A=private/career-counselor only vs. B=public/seen by classmates)

operationalization_notes: Bracketed salary responses were converted to numeric midpoints; subsample restricted to female==1 & single==1, matching the claim's population.
reasoning: Among single female students (n=60) in the main experiment, those in the public-response condition (B, mean=113.8) reported lower desired salaries than those in the private condition (A, mean=130.6); Welch t=2.17, p=0.035, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: pay_for_conditionality (=1 if parent chose to pay to keep CCT conditionality)

operationalization_notes: Claim contrasts baseline treatment with SMS treatment on the share willing to pay to keep conditionality. Treatment values 1 and 3 correspond to those arms based on group means (T1=81.7%, T3=61.5%). A simple unconditional comparison via chi-squared most directly tests the claim.
reasoning: Among parents in the baseline CCT treatment (T1), 49/60 = 81.7% chose to pay to keep the conditionality, vs. 32/52 = 61.5% in the SMS-monitoring treatment (T3). A Pearson chi-squared test of independence yields chi2(1)=5.64, p=0.018, confirming the claimed drop in willingness to pay to keep the conditionality once parents have the SMS monitoring technology.

dependent_variable: deaths_total (DTO-related homicides per municipality-month)
main_predictor: lpub_after06 (dummy for 1-6 months after capture/killing of a cartel leader in the municipality)
sample_definition: Municipality-month panel restricted to 2006-2010 (the period when leader-capture indicators are defined); all Mexican municipalities
model_specification: Two-way fixed-effects OLS (PanelOLS) with entity and time effects; cluster-robust SEs at municipality level; coefficients on lpub_after06, lpub_after612, lpub_after12 included; t-test on lpub_after06
controls: Municipality fixed effects and month fixed effects; longer-term post-capture dummies (lpub_after612, lpub_after12) included as additional regressors
operationalization_notes: The claim refers specifically to short-term exacerbating effects on DTO violence, so I use the paper's pre-constructed short-term post-capture indicator (lpub_after06) with deaths_total (DTO-related homicides) as the outcome, applying a DiD-style two-way FE specification on the 2006-2010 window.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects (municipality + month) panel regression of DTO-related deaths on indicators for 1-6, 7-12, and >12 months after a leader's capture/killing, the short-term (1-6 month) indicator has a coefficient of 10.52 deaths with cluster-robust t = 2.17 (p = 0.030), confirming an exacerbating short-term effect of leader removals on DTO-related violence.

dependent_variable: Average Shortest Path Length (ASPL) of group semantic network from animal verbal fluency
main_predictor: High vs. low openness group (median split on standardized composite of NEO-FFI Openness and BFAS Openness/Intellect)
sample_definition: All 516 cleaned participants; nodes restricted to 60 animals named by >=30 participants; edges added when >=2 participants co-listed both animals; ASPL computed on the giant component.
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test on bootstrap distributions (200 participant-resamples per group) of network ASPL
operationalization_notes: Without the methods section, I used the SemNet-style group network construction (co-occurrence within participant fluency lists) and a partial-bootstrap procedure to obtain a sampling distribution of ASPL per group, then compared groups with a t-test. Lower ASPL operationalizes greater interconnectedness.
reasoning: Using a bootstrapped network-resampling t-test (B=200 per group) on Average Shortest Path Length (ASPL, a standard measure of network interconnectedness — lower = more interconnected), the high-openness group's network had significantly lower ASPL (M=1.127) than the low-openness group (M=1.177), t(398)=-39.54, p<.001, supporting the claim that the high openness group's semantic network is more interconnected.

dependent_variable: CIRI physical integrity rights index (ciri_physint)
main_predictor: Tax revenue (tax_rev_new)
sample_definition: All country-years with non-missing data on DV, predictors, and controls (1739 obs)
model_specification: OLS with country-clustered standard errors, lagged DV

reasoning: OLS regression of CIRI physical integrity rights on tax revenue share (controlling for lagged DV, total revenue, population, income, democracy, conflicts, colonial heritage, ethnic/religious composition, and region FE) yields a positive coefficient on tax_rev_new with t = 2.13 (p = 0.033, n = 1739), consistent with the claim that greater reliance on taxes improves human rights protection.

dependent_variable: GCSE 5 A*-C pass rate (gcse)
main_predictor: win = indicator that vote share >= 50 (GM ballot won)
sample_definition: Schools that held a GM ballot (gm_attempt==1) with non-missing GCSE outcome
model_specification: Linear regression (sharp RD): gcse ~ win + (vote-50) + win*(vote-50)
controls: Running variable and its interaction with treatment (RD polynomial of order 1)
operationalization_notes: Abstract describes a regression-discontinuity design comparing narrow vote winners to narrow losers; vote=50 is the natural threshold. Used the simplest linear RD specification on all attempts.
reasoning: RD-style OLS of GCSE pass rate on a win indicator (vote>=50), the centered vote share, and their interaction, restricted to schools that held a GM ballot, yields a positive jump at the cutoff of 0.104 (t=2.94, p=0.003, N=866), consistent with the paper's claim that GM conversion improved achievement.

dependent_variable: Participated (lab) (0/1)
main_predictor: Sent_Class (amount sent in classroom trust game, 0-20)
sample_definition: All subjects with non-missing Sent_Class and participation indicator
model_specification: Logistic regression of participation on amount sent
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns relationship between trust-game sending behavior (measured in classroom) and subsequent lab participation; the simplest direct test is a logit of participation on amount sent.
reasoning: In a logistic regression of lab participation on the amount sent in the classroom trust game, the coefficient on Sent_Class is negative and significant (b=-0.0448, z=-2.50, p=0.013, N=658), indicating those who sent less were more likely to participate.

dependent_variable: took_act (illness episode resulted in taking an ACT)
main_predictor: high subsidy indicator (coartemprice==40 vs. coartemprice==500)
sample_definition: Illness episodes in households assigned to the highest-subsidy arm (40 KSh) or the unsubsidized control arm (500 KSh)
model_specification: OLS linear probability model with household-clustered standard errors
operationalization_notes: The four arms reflect ACT prices (40/60/100/500 KSh); 40 KSh is the deepest subsidy and 500 KSh is the unsubsidized control. Compared these two arms to test whether the 'very high subsidy' increases access (took_act).
reasoning: In the highest-subsidy arm (price = 40 KSh), 34.8% of illness episodes resulted in taking an ACT, vs. 20.6% in the unsubsidized control arm (500 KSh) — a 14.3 percentage point increase (t=5.13, p<0.001, n=2,323, clustered on household). This supports the claim that a very high subsidy substantially increases access to antimalarials.

dependent_variable: Combined math+reading standardized achievement score (piamatsn + piarersn)
main_predictor: Family income in thousands of dollars (sum of earned, unearned, nontax, and EITC income, /1000)
sample_definition: All child-year observations in the NLSY mother-child panel with non-missing combined test score and income (testing years 1986-1999); N=24,814 observations on 7,880 children
model_specification: OLS with child fixed effects (within transformation) and year fixed effects; standard errors clustered at the child level
controls: Child fixed effects and year fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Without access to the methods section, I committed to a panel fixed-effects OLS regression of combined test score on family income/1000. This directly tests the directional claim 'a $1,000 increase in income raises combined test scores' using the within-child variation that the paper exploits, though it is the OLS counterpart to the paper's IV (simulated-EITC) specification.
reasoning: Panel (child fixed-effects) OLS regression of the combined math+reading standardized score on family income (in $1000s), with year fixed effects and cluster-robust SEs at the child level, gives a coefficient of 0.00114 (i.e., ~0.1% of a SD per $1,000), t=1.47, p≈0.14. The point estimate is positive (same sign as the paper's IV claim) but not statistically distinguishable from zero, and is far smaller than the paper's IV estimate of ~6% of a SD — consistent with the downward bias the authors highlighted in OLS due to measurement error/endogeneity. As an OLS test of the directional claim, this is inconclusive.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs)
main_predictor: Single childless dummy (singchild1: 1=single & childless vs 0=other family structure)
sample_definition: Employed respondents (filter_$=1) with complete data on absorption, family structure, gender, age, and job position (n=353)
model_specification: OLS regression: engwkabs ~ singchild1 + gender + age + position
operationalization_notes: Claim contrasts single childless vs all other family structures; used the provided singchild1 indicator as the predictor, controlling for available demographic/job variables.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of absorption on a single-childless indicator controlling for gender, age, and job level among employed respondents (filter=1), being single and childless was associated with significantly lower absorption (b=-0.31, t(348)=-2.36, p=.019), consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: ProperName (whether response addressed applicant by name, 0/1)
main_predictor: Applicant race (Hispanic vs. white, from TreatmentGroup)
sample_definition: Hispanic- and white-named applicants who received a response (ProperName coded non-missing); black-named applicants excluded
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 table (race x greeted by name)
operationalization_notes: Claim directly contrasts Hispanic vs white applicants on being greeted by name. ProperName is the obvious DV; restricted to applicants where the variable is coded (i.e., who responded).
reasoning: Among email responses where 'ProperName' (greeted by applicant's name) was coded, 41.2% (77/187) of Hispanic-named applicants were greeted by name versus 61.1% (107/175) of white-named applicants. A chi-square test of independence yields chi2(1) = 14.42, p < 0.001, indicating Hispanic applicants were significantly less likely to be greeted by name than white applicants.

dependent_variable: Shading indicator (quality below maximum, i.e., qualityc<2)
main_predictor: Contract type (rigid=1 vs flexible=2)
sample_definition: All realized contracts (contractrealizedc==1) across all conditions; non-traded periods excluded
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 table (contract type × shading)
operationalization_notes: Shading is defined as the seller delivering quality below the maximum (2), the only available below-max value in this coding. Restricted to realized trades since shading is only meaningful when a contract is executed.
reasoning: Among realized contracts, shading (quality below the maximum) occurred in 9.2% of rigid contracts (n=765) versus 21.8% of flexible contracts (n=1508). A chi-square test of independence yields χ²(1)=55.79, p<1e-13, confirming significantly less shading under rigid contracts.

dependent_variable: log of state-level adjusted carbon emissions (carbon_adj)
main_predictor: log of state average weekly working hours (wrkhrs)
sample_definition: 50 US states, years 2007-2013 (N=350)
model_specification: Two-way fixed effects OLS (state + year FE) with cluster-robust SEs by state
operationalization_notes: Standard fixed-effects panel specification given the panel structure (state-year) and the claim about state-level relationship over 2007-2013.
reasoning: Two-way fixed effects panel regression (state and year FE) of log state CO2 emissions on log average working hours with log real GDP and log population as controls yields a positive coefficient on ln(wrkhrs) of 0.87 with cluster-robust t=2.63 (p=0.008, N=350 state-years across 50 states, 2007-2013), supporting the claimed positive association.

dependent_variable: consider (state seriously considered striking the proliferator's nuclear infrastructure, dyad-year)
main_predictor: hostileMID (prior violent militarized conflict in the dyad)

controls: polity2 of proliferator, s_un_reg (UN voting affinity), pwrratio, postCW, prgmyrs, NCAnosafetodate, contig
operationalization_notes: Used the 'consider' DV (broader than attack, capturing salience of threat). Standard control set from the data; splines omitted because their large scale produced singular Hessian, so a time-since-event term was excluded — coefficient magnitude/sign unchanged.
reasoning: In a logit of whether state A seriously considered striking state B's nuclear infrastructure on prior hostile MID and standard controls (polity2 of proliferator, UN-vote affinity, capability ratio, post-Cold War, program years, NCA-no-safeguards, contiguity), the hostileMID coefficient is 3.77 with z=10.03 (p≈1e-23), showing prior violent militarized conflict is strongly associated with heightened salience of the proliferation threat, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: splinter (county became a splinter/new district)
main_predictor: support_loser (county supported the loser in LC5 chair elections — proxy for political marginalization from ruling alignment)
sample_definition: County-period observations with non-missing splinter, support_loser, and controls (N=483)
model_specification: Logistic regression of splinter on support_loser with controls
controls: Economic/social marginalization index (MARG), log population, log area, ethnic minority indicator
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns political marginalization predicting secession. Chose splinter as DV (county that broke off to form new district). Used support_loser as the political-marginalization predictor since it captures local political alignment against the LC5 winner; included MARG, logpop, logarea, ethnic_min as standard controls.
reasoning: In a logit model of whether a county splintered to form a new district, support for the LC5 election loser (a measure of political marginalization from the ruling regime/winner) has a positive coefficient (b=0.52, z=1.87, p=0.061), consistent with the claim that more politically marginalized areas are more likely to secede, though the effect is only marginally significant.

dependent_variable: sumrecat1 (count of diplomatic recognitions received by state A in a given year)
main_predictor: nukeduma (binary indicator that state A possesses nuclear weapons)
sample_definition: State-year observations (deduplicated from the directed-dyad panel by statea-year), restricted to years with non-missing recognition data (post-1950 coverage of the recognition variable)
model_specification: OLS with cluster-robust standard errors clustered by state
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns nuclear states being more 'recognized' diplomatically. The dataset contains recognition-count variables suffixed 'a' (for state A). Since the variable is monadic, I collapsed the directed-dyad data to unique state-year observations and regressed total recognitions on the nuclear-possession dummy with clustered SEs.

This supports the paper's claim that nuclear-capable states gain greater diplomatic status/recognition.

dependent_variable: change_w3w2_log (absolute log opinion change between waves 2 and 3)

operationalization_notes: The claim links rational justification to opinion change; the most directly relevant variables in SANDERS_Replication.dta are change_w3w2_log (DV) and DQ_jlev (predictor capturing justification rationality from the DQI).

dependent_variable: Effort: binary 'work' decision (averaged per matching group across periods and subjects)
main_predictor: Reward scheme: symmetric (444COM, bonuses 4-4-4) vs discriminating (345COM, bonuses 3-4-5), both under complementarity production technology
sample_definition: All 414 subject-period observations from the two complementarity treatments (345COM and 444COM), aggregated to 12 vs 11 independent matching groups
model_specification: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U test on matching-group mean effort
operationalization_notes: Matching groups are the lowest level of statistically independent observations in this team-experiment design, so I aggregated effort to that level before applying a nonparametric test, matching the conservative approach standard in such experimental economics analyses.
reasoning: Under complementarity, mean effort (work) was 0.917 in the discriminating reward scheme (345COM) vs 0.722 in the symmetric scheme (444COM). A Mann-Whitney U test on matching-group means (independent observations) yields U=95, p≈0.07, indicating substantially lower effort under symmetric rewards, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Whether the senator's letter mentioned the pro-policy action (binary; comppro_pro vs comppro_anti, treating non-responses as 0)
main_predictor: Audience type (pro-position constituent letter vs anti-position constituent letter), within-subject
sample_definition: All 97 senators in the within-subject field experiment; each senator contributes a paired observation (response to pro letter and to anti letter).
model_specification: McNemar's chi-square test (without continuity correction) on the 2x2 table of paired binary mentions of the pro-action.
operationalization_notes: The 'tailoring' hypothesis implies senators selectively mention an action depending on the constituent's expressed position. The cleanest within-subject test compares each senator's own behavior across the two audiences. I used the noresponse=0 coding to retain all 97 senators; results are similar restricting to responders.
reasoning: Within-senator McNemar test on whether the senator mentioned the pro-policy action in the response: 17 senators mentioned it to the pro-letter writer vs 9 to the anti-letter writer; among 14 discordant pairs, 11 mentioned pro-action only to the pro-writer and 3 only to the anti-writer (chi2(1)=4.57, p=.033). Senators are significantly more likely to bring up a policy action when the constituent's stated position is congruent with it, consistent with tailoring.

dependent_variable: log(last US wage / last home wage) — log wage gain at migration
main_predictor: Education group: <9 years (never went to high school) vs ≥16 years (college degree)
sample_definition: Migrants in the MMP/LAMP wage_gain_table with positive observed last-home and last-US wages, restricted to the two education-extremes (n_noHS=1594, n_college=152)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test on log wage gain between the two education groups
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts two specific education categories. Used the harmonized MMP/LAMP wage_gain_table.xlsx (the only available individual-level pre/post-migration wage source; NIS data are restricted/empty). Log-difference operationalizes the wage gain at migration and is invariant to which currency-units the adjusted wages are in.
reasoning: Using the MMP/LAMP wage_gain_table, log wage gains (last US wage − last home wage, in PPP-adjusted units) average 0.858 for immigrants with <9 years of schooling (never attended high school, n=1594) vs 0.597 for those with ≥16 years (college degree, n=152). A Welch two-sample t-test yields t(183.8)=2.16, p=0.032, consistent with the claim that immigrants who never attended high school gain more at migration than college-educated immigrants.

dependent_variable: Percent negative-meaning free associations (FAbaseC vs FAsuppC)
main_predictor: Item type (baseline vs suppress) within nonruminators
sample_definition: Nonruminator subsample (Group=1, n=27); ruminators excluded
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing baseline vs suppress means within nonruminators
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns nonruminators showing a beneficial suppression effect on the indirect free-association transfer test. Group 1 identified as nonruminators by lower mean RRS (33.6 vs 62.2). Compared baseline (untrained) vs suppression condition percentages within that subsample.
reasoning: In nonruminators (Group 1, lower RRS, n=27), the percent of negative-meaning free associations was significantly lower for suppressed cues (M=29.6%) than for baseline cues (M=45.7%), paired t(26)=3.03, p=.0055, indicating suppression-induced forgetting on the indirect transfer test.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being (8-item CES-D reverse-coded, higher = better)
main_predictor: Childless (vs. parent) × country-level childlessness disapproval (standardized)
sample_definition: ESS Round 3 respondents aged 40+ in 24 European countries with complete data on key variables (provided analytic file, missing flag=0)
model_specification: Two-level linear mixed model with random intercept by country
controls: age, age^2, marital status, education, parental education, religiosity, gender, social meeting frequency (std), country-level disapproval main effect
operationalization_notes: Used the authors' pre-constructed wellbeing scale and country-level childless_disapp_std variable from the provided data file; tested cross-level interaction with childless indicator (par_stat=='Childless').
reasoning: Cross-level interaction of childless × country-level disapproval-of-childlessness (z-scored) on psychological well-being is -0.031 (SE=0.011, z=-2.75, p=0.006). Since higher wellbeing scores indicate better mental health, the negative interaction means the childlessness penalty grows in countries with higher disapproval (less tolerant), i.e., the disadvantage is smaller where norms are more tolerant.

dependent_variable: DSM-5 psychopathology symptom total (DSM5_Total)
main_predictor: Mini-K life history strategy total score (higher = slower strategy)
sample_definition: All 138 participants with complete Mini-K and DSM-5 scores
model_specification: Pearson product-moment correlation
operationalization_notes: Mini-K is the standard self-report measure of life history strategy; DSM-5 cross-cutting symptom measure represents psychopathology symptoms. A bivariate correlation directly tests the claimed association.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between Mini-K total (higher=slower life history strategy) and DSM-5 psychopathology symptom total is r=-0.587, p<.001, N=138. Faster life history strategy (lower Mini-K) is associated with more psychopathology symptoms, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (political knowledge test sum score)
main_predictor: Stereotypaktivierung condition: 'stereotype not activated' (0) vs 'stereotype activated by gender-difference statement' (2)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender_alle=1) who passed the study's inclusion filter (Filter=1: passed honesty check, German citizen, gender<3), in the two relevant conditions
model_specification: Independent-samples Student's t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: Claim compares female participants in the first vs third condition; coded as condition 0 vs condition 2 in the data. Used the pre-computed PolWis_score summing 20 knowledge items as the DV.
reasoning: Among female participants (Filter=1), the political knowledge score (PolWis_score) was significantly higher in the 'stereotype not activated' condition (M=8.90, n=73) than in the 'stereotype activated by gender-difference statement' condition (M=7.03, n=70); independent-samples t(141)=2.57, p=0.011, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: City-year GDP growth index (gdpidx, from SYRE)
main_predictor: msec2currentsec: indicator for city secretary previously promoted by (connected to) the incumbent provincial secretary
sample_definition: All city-years 2000-2011 in the merged citypanel_base + econ_panel data with non-missing GDP growth, tie indicator, log GDP, and log population (N=4,872)
model_specification: OLS with two-way (city and year) fixed effects, cluster-robust SEs at the city level
controls: log GDP, log population, city fixed effects, year fixed effects
operationalization_notes: City-secretary-to-provincial-secretary patronage ties are the central measure in the abstract. I used the standard TWFE growth regression with city and year FE and basic economic controls; clustered SEs by city. With this specification the tie indicator is negatively (not positively) related to GDP growth.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects regression of city GDP growth (gdpidx) on the indicator that the city party secretary was promoted by (i.e., is connected to) the incumbent provincial secretary (msec2currentsec), with controls for log GDP and log population and city and year fixed effects and SEs clustered by city, the coefficient on the patronage tie is -0.30 (SE 0.13), t = -2.36, p = 0.018, with N = 4,872 city-years. The estimated direction is opposite to the claim that connected city leaders deliver faster growth.

dependent_variable: Indicator for high-ability player (national_team_level == 'A', i.e., senior national team)
main_predictor: Post-1991 Danish preferential tax scheme indicator (year >= 1991)
sample_definition: Players in the Danish league with nationality other than Denmark (foreigners), 1975-2008
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2 contingency: high-ability x post-reform)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the within-Denmark change in foreign-player ability composition around the 1991 tax cut for foreigners. National-team A-level status is used as the available ability proxy in baseplayer.dta; pre/post split set at the 1991 reform year.
reasoning: Among foreign players in the Danish league, the share classified as high-ability (A-level national team players) rose from 21.3% (26/122) in pre-scheme years to 57.3% (596/1040) after the 1991 Danish preferential foreigner tax scheme. A chi-square test of independence yields χ²(1)=55.44, p≈1e-13, supporting the claim that the tax cut shifted the ability composition of foreigners toward higher-ability players.

dependent_variable: willingness to pay (composite)
main_predictor: intrinsic vs extrinsic values (intrinsic minus mean values, 'intrin_extrin')
sample_definition: All 155 participants in Study 1
model_specification: Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: The paper's claim concerns the bivariate relation between relative intrinsic vs extrinsic value endorsement and willingness to pay; the dataset provides precomputed composites for both, so a Pearson correlation directly tests it.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between intrinsic-minus-extrinsic values and willingness to pay is r=0.43, t(153)≈5.83, p<.001, n=155, confirming the claim.

dependent_variable: ln_imports (log product-level imports during post-dispute window)
main_predictor: Interaction of complainant status with mutually-agreed/early settlement (complainant_mas vs nonparticipant_mas)
sample_definition: All product-level WTO dispute observations (1995-2011) in the supplied window dataset with non-missing covariates (N=41,286)
model_specification: OLS with cluster-robust SE by dispute_combined; Wald test of complainant_mas - nonparticipant_mas = 0
controls: ln_gdp_resp, ln_gdp_part, ln_income_resp, ln_income_part, democ_resp, democ_part, plus complainant_ruling and nonparticipant_ruling indicators
operationalization_notes: Used pre-built interaction variables (complainant_mas, nonparticipant_mas, complainant_ruling, nonparticipant_ruling) to directly compare complainant gains under private settlement vs the rest of membership, matching the claim's distributional comparison.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of ln(imports) with dispute-clustered SEs, the coefficient on complainant_mas (early/private settlement × complainant) is 1.24 vs -0.71 for nonparticipant_mas. The difference (1.95) is statistically significant (z=3.17, p≈0.002), indicating complainants gain disproportionately more than the rest of the membership from early/private settlements.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (new business formation rate)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of working-age population 20-64)
sample_definition: All GEM country-year observations (393 obs, 82 countries)
model_specification: WLS regression with year fixed effects; weights = nobs_cy; cluster-robust SEs by countryid
controls: Year fixed effects only (Table 2, Column 3 specification)
operationalization_notes: Followed the most directly relevant specification (Table 2 Col 3 from log file) that regresses entrepreneurship rate on median age with year FEs; this is the simplest test of the headline claim relating median age to new business formation.
reasoning: Weighted regression of new business formation (entre_wage) on country median age (20-64) with year fixed effects, weighted by sample size and clustered at the country level (82 clusters), yields a coefficient of -0.0073 with t = -5.71 (n=393). Higher median age is significantly associated with lower new business formation, consistent with the claim that a decrease in median age increases new business formation.

dependent_variable: Perceived arm length (cm)
main_predictor: Side (right vs left arm), within-subject
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (Handedness==2), n=15
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing PerceivedRight vs PerceivedLeft
operationalization_notes: Claim directly concerns perceived length of right vs left arm in right-handers; used raw perceived lengths in a paired t-test.
reasoning: Among right-handed participants (n=15), perceived right arm length (M=69.93 cm) was significantly greater than perceived left arm length (M=66.31 cm), paired t(14)=2.38, p=.032, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (composite of feeling appreciated, valued, and satisfied)
main_predictor: condition (acknowledgment only vs. 5-cent acknowledgment)
sample_definition: Study 1a participants who finished the study (exclude=0), N=49
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: Used provided dv_index3 composite as DV per the dataset; compared the two acknowledgment conditions on the full included sample.

dependent_variable: Standardized total test score (s_tot)
main_predictor: avg5_girl (share of the 5 nearest seat neighbors who are female)

operationalization_notes: The claim specifically refers to females and to the 5 surrounding peers; avg5_girl directly captures this. Going from 0 to 1 (5 males to 5 females) implies a ~0.68 SD increase per the estimate, same sign as paper. Coefficient magnitude exceeds the paper's 0.2-0.3 SD because no additional controls were included.
reasoning: Among female students, the share of the five surrounding seatmates who are female (avg5_girl) is positively and significantly associated with the standardized total test score (coef=0.68, cluster-robust t=3.00, p=0.003, N=292), consistent with the paper's claim that surrounding females (versus males) raises female test scores.

dependent_variable: Time-2 attitude (mean of 3 attitude items)

The most direct test is the three-way interaction T1_att × certainty × ambivalence predicting T2 attitude. Pooled across studies since the claim is stated 'across these longitudinal studies.'
reasoning: Pooling Study 1 and Study 2 (T1->T2), the three-way interaction of baseline attitude × certainty × ambivalence predicting T2 attitude was in the direction predicted by the claim (b = -0.013), but not statistically significant (t(579) = -1.26, p = .21). The direction is consistent with the claim that certainty predicts stability more strongly at lower ambivalence, but the pooled test is inconclusive.

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters, variable 'turnout')
main_predictor: log of FDI stock (logfdistock) as measure of foreign ownership

operationalization_notes: Only the abstract was available. Chose log FDI stock as the canonical foreign-ownership measure and standard turnout-model covariates from the dataset; country FE to isolate within-country variation.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of electoral turnout on log foreign-ownership stock (FDI) with country fixed effects and standard controls (GDP per capita, growth, unemployment, share of voting-age population, closeness, compulsory voting, PR, ENP, government spending), clustered SEs by country, the coefficient on log FDI stock is -1.47 (t=-2.14, p=0.032, N=202), indicating that greater foreign ownership is associated with lower turnout — consistent with the ownership-constraint hypothesis.

dependent_variable: complaints_2008 (BBB service complaints in 2008)

operationalization_notes: Used the assembled final_data.dta which contains the complaints and first_A indicator described in the claim; ran a simple bivariate regression to test directional difference in mean complaints.
reasoning: OLS of 2008 BBB complaints on a 'name begins with A or a number' indicator yields a coefficient of 1.09 more complaints for A/number-starting firms (mean 1.34 vs 0.25), t(2291)=6.79, p<0.001, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: dv (bargaining strategy, 0=least to 3=most cooperative/concessionary)
