operationalization_notes: Issue linkage structure captures how differently valued the issues being bargained are. Ordered logit is appropriate for the 4-category ordinal cooperation DV; controls include the standard set of power/socialization/structural variables in the dataset.
reasoning: In an ordered logit predicting cooperative bargaining strategy (dv 0-3), issue_linkage_structure has a positive, highly significant coefficient (b=1.047, z=13.33, p<0.001), indicating that greater issue-value differentiation/linkage potential predicts more concessionary strategies, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: credittogovtstateenterp (credit by domestic money banks to government and SOEs, % of GDP)
main_predictor: lagged icrg_qog (ICRG Quality of Government, inverse proxy for state weakness)
sample_definition: Country-year panel from the paper's Country Year Dataset, complete cases on DV, predictor, controls and one-year lags; 1980s-2010 window implied by data availability (N=827).
model_specification: OLS with country (wbcodeMEN) and year fixed effects, lagged dependent variable, country-clustered SEs.
controls: Lagged marketpower (Lerner index), lagged netinterestmargin, lagged overheadcosts (profit-potential proxies), lagged DV, country FE, year FE.
operationalization_notes: Claim: 'after controlling for profit potential, weaker states direct more credit to government/SOEs.' Operationalized state weakness as low ICRG quality of government; profit potential as bank-market-power and margin/overhead variables. Used a lagged-DV two-way FE specification consistent with the paper's dynamic panel framing (full Arellano-Bond IV not feasible here without linearmodels).
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects panel regression of credit to government/SOEs (% GDP) on lagged ICRG quality-of-government (inverse measure of state weakness), controlling for the profit-potential proxies (lagged market power/Lerner index, net interest margin, overhead costs) and the lagged DV, the coefficient on lagged ICRG_QOG is +2.47 (cluster-robust SE = 3.28; t = 0.75, p = 0.45, N = 827). The sign is opposite to the paper's prediction (weaker state should raise directed credit, i.e. negative coefficient on quality-of-government), but the estimate is far from statistical significance, so the claim does not replicate in this OLS specification.

dependent_variable: forceinit (state initiated a militarized dispute involving use of force in the year)
main_predictor: rcoupbin (coup occurred in the previous 10 years, =1)
sample_definition: All Latin American country-years 1960-1999 in scamerica5.dta with non-missing covariates
model_specification: Binary logistic regression (MLE)
controls: log lagged real GDP per capita, lagged polity2, ethnic fractionalization, number of bordering countries, CINC, log(MID count+1), regional war indicator, regional conflict (5-yr pma)
operationalization_notes: Threats to political survival operationalized via recent coup history (rcoupbin), a standard proxy used in the diversionary-conflict literature; force-based MID initiation is the most direct measure of 'conflict involvement' as initiator.
reasoning: In a logistic regression of force initiation on a binary indicator that a coup occurred in the previous 10 years (proxy for threats to political survival), controlling for GDP, polity, ethnic fractionalization, number of borders, CINC, log-MIDs, regional war, and regional conflict, the coup-threat coefficient is positive (b=0.825, z=2.50, p=0.012, n=798), supporting the diversionary claim.

dependent_variable: d12outgroup (amount allocated to out-group in dictator game, 0-5)
main_predictor: Ordinal exposure to Albanians by region (Primarily Serb=0, Border=1, Primarily Albanian=2)
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb respondents in the replication dataset
model_specification: OLS regression: d12outgroup = a + b*exposure
operationalization_notes: The 'regions' variable captures varying contact with the Albanian out-group, so it is the most direct proxy for exposure. Out-group bridging is operationalized as the dictator-game amount given to the out-group (d12outgroup).
reasoning: OLS regression of out-group dictator-game allocation (d12outgroup) on an ordinal exposure measure (Serb region=0, Border=1, Albanian region=2) yields a positive, highly significant coefficient (b=0.725, t(156)=4.25, p<0.001), consistent with the claim that out-group bridging norms rise with exposure to the out-group.

dependent_variable: enjoyrelativ (relative enjoyment of the program)
main_predictor: condition (commercial interruption vs. no commercial)
sample_definition: All Study 2 participants with non-missing condition and enjoyment ratings (good ad n=53; no ad n=49)
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test
operationalization_notes: The claim is the main effect of commercial interruption on enjoyment in Study 2; the dataset contains two conditions (good commercial vs. no commercial). A two-sample t-test on the enjoyment measure directly tests whether interruption increased enjoyment.
reasoning: Participants in the commercial-interruption (good ad) condition reported higher relative enjoyment (M=5.38, SD=1.69, n=53) than those in the no-commercial condition (M=4.47, SD=2.05, n=49); independent-samples t(100)=2.45, p=.016, confirming that commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable.

dependent_variable: acceptedbribes (5-point agreement that the senator accepted bribes)
main_predictor: Experimental condition: causal explanation vs. denial
sample_definition: Subjects assigned to either the causal or denial condition with non-missing acceptedbribes (innuendo and control conditions excluded)
model_specification: Two-sample independent t-test (equal variances) comparing means of acceptedbribes across causal vs denial groups
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts the causal correction with the evidence-backed denial on the central misperception outcome (belief that the politician took bribes). A simple two-sample t-test between these two arms most directly tests the claim.
reasoning: Mean agreement that Senator Swensen accepted bribes was significantly lower in the causal-explanation condition (M=2.94, n=276) than in the denial condition (M=3.41, n=243); t(517)=-4.77, p<.001, indicating the causal correction was more effective at limiting misperceptions than the denial.

dependent_variable: Intimacy (aggregated intimacy questionnaire score)
main_predictor: Attention condition (attentive vs. inattentive partner)
sample_definition: All 30 participants in Study 2a (Sheet3)
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test comparing intimacy between attention conditions
operationalization_notes: Study 2a data with a clear two-level condition variable (cnd) and an aggregated Intimacy score; the most direct test of whether attention raises intimacy is a between-condition comparison of intimacy scores.
reasoning: Participants in the attention condition (cnd=1, M=4.58) reported significantly higher intimacy with the partner than those in the no-attention condition (cnd=2, M=2.78), t(28)=6.20, p<.001, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Monitoring index — mean of three binary survey items: q145_scrutinize_REC2 (one should scrutinize government), q146_learnmore_govt_REC2 (interest in learning more about government), q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2 (interest in learning more about district budget/APBD)
main_predictor: taxgrp (1 = tax treatment, 0 = windfall treatment)
sample_definition: All 1,857 respondents with non-missing values on the three monitoring items (full experimental sample collapsing across the info/no-info subtreatment)
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test comparing mean monitoring index between tax and windfall conditions
operationalization_notes: The abstract identifies 'monitoring' as one of the outcomes affected by tax treatment. The three q145–q147 items most directly capture survey-based monitoring inclinations (scrutiny of and interest in learning about government spending). I averaged the binary recodes into a simple index and contrasted tax vs windfall assignment (taxgrp), pooling over the orthogonal information treatment.
reasoning: Citizens in the tax treatment scored higher on the monitoring index (mean 0.837 vs 0.812 for windfall), a directional difference consistent with the claim. Welch's t = 1.80, p ≈ 0.072 (two-sided; one-sided p ≈ 0.036), suggesting the tax treatment increased monitoring as the paper claims, though the effect is modest in size.

dependent_variable: turnout (voted = 1)
main_predictor: z1elite_avgprox (social proximity to elites)
sample_definition: All individuals in the Alexandria 1859 and Newport 1874 datasets with non-missing values on the regression variables (pooled, N=5632).
model_specification: Logistic regression (MLE) with a city fixed effect
controls: hhwealthlog, midstatus, highstatus, owner, agelog, usborn, z1ev (eigenvector centrality), city dummy
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns turnout as a function of elite proximity. I pooled the two historical datasets provided (common variables) and ran a logistic regression with the standard SES/demographic controls available, plus network centrality (z1ev) and city FE, to isolate elite-proximity effects.
reasoning: In a pooled logistic regression of turnout on social proximity to elites (z1elite_avgprox) with controls (household wealth log, mid/high status, home ownership, log age, US-born, eigenvector centrality z1ev, and a city fixed effect) across the Alexandria 1859 and Newport 1874 datasets, the coefficient on proximity to elites is positive and highly significant (b=0.91, z=10.38, p<0.001, N=5632), consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Utilitarian decision (decision: 1=yes/utilitarian, 0=no)
main_predictor: Mood (0=negative, 1=positive)
sample_definition: Participants in the active-frame condition only (frame==1), N=200
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 mood × decision table
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns the active-frame subgroup and a difference in proportion of utilitarian responses between mood groups; a chi-square test directly maps to this contrast.
reasoning: In the active frame (frame=1), utilitarian responses occurred in 41% of positive-mood vs 16% of negative-mood participants; χ²(1, N=200)=15.34, p<.001, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: TVA processing speed parameter v
main_predictor: Cue condition (85dB auditory cue vs no cue), within-subject
sample_definition: All 28 participants in Experiment 1 (mmc1.csv)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test (v_85dBCue vs v_NoCue)
operationalization_notes: Claim specifically pertains to Experiment 1's effect of phasic auditory alertness on visual processing speed (v); a paired t-test directly compares the two within-subject conditions.
reasoning: Paired t-test on Experiment 1 TVA-estimated visual processing speed parameter v shows v is significantly higher with the 85dB auditory cue (M=92.69) than with no cue (M=66.90), t(27)=4.71, p<.001, supporting the claim that phasic auditory alertness increases visual processing speed.

dependent_variable: ln(average owner-occupied housing value) at the block level
main_predictor: big1980 = bigside_m (=1 for the central-city/larger jurisdiction in the border pair) interacted with Cyear_1980 (=1 in 1980)
sample_definition: Block-level observations in 1970 and 1980 on either side of jurisdiction (school district) boundaries; tierno<2 (closest blocks to border); restricted to border areas where exactly one side ever received a court-ordered desegregation plan (yesorder_m==1); dropped low-pop jurisdictions (<10k), Georgia, NYC-Floral Park, single-side or single-year borders, blocks with zero residents, and missing/zero owner-occupied housing.
model_specification: WLS with weights = number of owner-occupied housing units, jurisdiction-by-border ('extra') and border-by-year fixed effects absorbed via dummies, cluster-robust SEs by jurisdiction
controls: Jurisdiction-by-border FEs and border-by-year FEs; Cyear_1980 main effect
operationalization_notes: Replicates the central DD specification from the author's analysis log: 'areg lnavval big1980 Cyear_1980 A* if tierno<2 & yesorder_m==1 [aw=house_ownocc], absorb(extra) cluster(jurcode)', which is the specification most directly tied to the claim about a 6% relative city-suburban price decline.
reasoning: In a difference-in-differences regression of log block-level average owner-occupied housing values on big1980 (city-side x post-1980), with jurisdiction-by-border and border-by-year fixed effects, weighted by housing units and clustered by jurisdiction (43 clusters), the coefficient on big1980 is -0.0637 (SE=0.0232), t=-2.74, p=0.006. Housing values in central cities fell by about 6% relative to neighboring suburbs after desegregation, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: fraud_ordered (ordinal perception of Duma election fraud)
main_predictor: golos_correct (correctly identifies Golos as an election monitoring NGO)
sample_definition: Respondents coded as opposition voters (opp_voter==1) with non-missing outcome and covariates (N=498)
model_specification: Ordered logistic regression
controls: sex, age, moscow, org_empl (private sector), fin_stat, educ, polnews, state_tv, vkont, odno, round, facebook, livej, famecon
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns regime opponents who know Golos vs not; restricted to opposition voters and used the Golos knowledge indicator as the main predictor with the standard demographic/media controls available in the dataset.

dependent_variable: lrecon (economic left-right position; lower = more left)
main_predictor: eth_supp (party's support for ethnic minorities)
sample_definition: Parties in countries coded as having a dominant ethnic minority from a former federal center (comm_dom_min==1): Estonia, Latvia, Slovenia, Bosnia, Croatia; observations with non-missing lrecon and eth_supp (N=68).
model_specification: OLS regression of lrecon on eth_supp
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts minority vs majority parties in federal-center successor states. The dataset contains a continuous eth_supp score capturing each party's pro-minority stance, which serves as the most direct proxy for minority-affiliation; restricting to comm_dom_min==1 isolates the federal-center context.
reasoning: In countries with an ethnic minority originating from a former federal center (comm_dom_min=1), parties more supportive of ethnic minorities (higher eth_supp) are significantly more left-leaning on the economic left-right (lrecon) scale: b=-0.224, t(66)=-3.18, p=.002. This supports the paper's claim that minority-affiliated parties are more left-leaning than majority-affiliated ones in these settings.

dependent_variable: Number of observed actions construed as choices (numactions)
main_predictor: Cultural context (US vs. India)
sample_definition: Participants in the Choice condition only (n=30 US, n=34 IN); Control condition excluded as it counts actions, not choices
model_specification: Welch's independent-samples t-test
operationalization_notes: The dataset records, per participant, the number of actions construed as choices. Restricting to the Choice condition isolates the construal-as-choice DV most directly tied to the claim; comparing US vs. IN means tests the directional cultural difference.
reasoning: In the Choice condition, U.S. participants construed substantially more actions as choices (M=38.3) than Indian participants (M=22.7); Welch's t(53.22)=3.05, p=.004, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Willingness to self-censor (WSC), 1-6 scale
main_predictor: Recipient type (4 within-subject conditions: close relationship, superiors, Israeli NGO, outside NGO)
sample_definition: All 71 participants in Study 1
model_specification: One-way repeated-measures ANOVA

Means increase monotonically from close (2.99) to outside NGO (4.73), consistent with the claim that greater distance/dissemination capacity raises WSC.

dependent_variable: output (per-period performance)
main_predictor: continuous wage increase profile (tr3=1) vs constant wage profile (tr0=0)

model_specification: OLS regression of output on treatment dummy with cluster-robust standard errors at the subject level
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts the 'continuous small increases' profile with the constant-wage profile. Pooling all periods captures the overall performance difference; subject-clustered SEs account for repeated measures.
reasoning: Comparing average output across all 8 periods between the continuous-wage-increase profile (tr3) and the constant wage profile, the continuous treatment shows a positive but statistically insignificant coefficient of 0.31 (z=0.97, p=0.33, cluster-robust SE by subject; N=1800 obs from 225 subjects). The direction matches the paper's claim but is not significant at conventional levels in this simple specification.

dependent_variable: Q27.0 — recalled portion size ('How big was the food portion?')
main_predictor: condition (1 = camera/observed vs 2 = no camera/unobserved)
sample_definition: All 82 participants with valid condition and portion-size responses
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: Claim is about recalled portion size after eating; Q27.0 directly asks 'How big was the food portion?' and the condition variable encodes the observed/unobserved manipulation via the camera presence.
reasoning: Observed (camera, M=4.85) participants recalled a larger food portion than unobserved (no camera, M=4.00) participants, t(80)=2.20, p=.030, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: npctwomenlegsal (percent women in lower house)
main_predictor: avg_pv_0 (Carey-Shugart personal-vote index; higher = more party-centered) and its interaction with log district magnitude
sample_definition: Country-year observations 1980-2005 with non-missing values on all model covariates (N=761, 63 country clusters)
model_specification: OLS with cluster-robust SEs at the country level; joint F-test on avg_pv_0 and avg_pv_0×logm_dist
controls: log district magnitude, ln GDP per capita, female labor force %, years since suffrage, left party vote share (Keefer), polity2, non-European dummy
operationalization_notes: Used the personal-vote summary index (avg_pv_0) interacted with log district magnitude as the most direct test of the personal-vote-incentive theory; chose OLS with country-clustered SEs as the standard approach for cross-national panel data and a joint test of the two PV-related coefficients to capture the overall PV effect.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of percent women in the legislature on the Carey-Shugart personal-vote index (avg_pv_0), log district magnitude, their interaction, and controls (GDP, female labor share, years of suffrage, left vote, polity2, non-European dummy) with country-clustered SEs, the joint F-test on avg_pv_0 and avg_pv_0×logM is F(2,62)=0.43, p=0.65. The avg_pv_0 main-effect coefficient is positive (b=6.26, z=0.81), nominally consistent with the claim that party-centered systems increase women's representation, but not statistically distinguishable from zero.

dependent_variable: Hazard of enacting overseas voting (newextvote/_d event in survival data)
main_predictor: qdelta — indicator that the queen-contiguity neighbors' average overseas-voting status changed in the previous two years
sample_definition: Country-years still at risk (_st==1, prior to enactment), 1960-2010, with non-missing covariates; 4972 country-years, 94 enactment events
model_specification: Cox proportional hazards model with time-varying covariates (start-stop format)
controls: lngdp (log GDP), lnpop (log population), politydem (Polity democracy score)
operationalization_notes: Abstract emphasizes 'neighbors' recent enactment' nearly doubling adoption chances, mapping directly to the qdelta variable (recent change in queen-neighbors' overseas-voting status). Used a parsimonious Cox model with standard development/democracy controls.
reasoning: Cox proportional hazards model with time-varying covariates yields a coefficient of 0.624 on qdelta (HR=1.87, z=2.34, p=0.02), indicating that recent adoption of overseas voting by adjoining neighbors nearly doubles the hazard of enfranchisement — consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: loghrindinc_real (log real hourly individual income)
main_predictor: post_FILdie (indicator for years after the father-in-law's death)
sample_definition: Married men in CHNS panel with non-missing income, post_FILdie, age, age^2, education, id, and year (N=10,191).
model_specification: OLS with two-way fixed effects (individual + year) implemented via iterative within-demeaning; cluster-robust SEs at the individual level.
controls: age, age^2, years of education; individual and year fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Abstract identifies the effect via post-marriage death of the father-in-law on a married man's earnings using Chinese panel data; CHNS (chns.dta) provides such a panel with post_FILdie and log hourly income, so I restricted to married men and ran a two-way FE earnings regression with standard human-capital controls.
reasoning: In a two-way (individual and year) fixed-effects regression of log real hourly individual income on the post-father-in-law-death indicator with age, age^2, and years of education as controls, the coefficient on post_FILdie was +0.026 (cluster-robust SE 0.051; t=0.51, p=0.61) on 10,191 married-male observations. The estimate is small, statistically indistinguishable from zero, and of the opposite sign from the paper's claimed -7% effect, so the data do not reproduce the claimed reduction in earnings.

dependent_variable: Vote on religious liberty schema, progressive (1) vs conservative (0) (IRELIGPC)
main_predictor: National percentage Catholic in 1965 (NPERCATH, rescaled 0-1)
sample_definition: All bishops with non-missing religious liberty vote and country % Catholic
model_specification: Binary logistic regression (Logit)
operationalization_notes: The religious liberty vote is one of the two 'contentious issues' highlighted in the abstract; % Catholic at the country level is the canonical organizational-field/NIT measure of legitimacy pressure (Catholic minorities face legitimacy concerns prompting progressive votes). A simple logit isolates the directional NIT prediction.
reasoning: Logistic regression of progressive vote on religious liberty on national % Catholic yields z = -3.71 (p < .001, N = 1885). Bishops from countries where Catholics are a smaller share of the population (i.e., facing greater legitimacy concerns vis-a-vis other actors in their organizational field) were significantly more likely to vote progressively, consistent with the NIT-derived prediction that legitimacy concerns shape leaders' actions.

dependent_variable: PopDIFF_MaxCov_T1 (gap between max-coverage ideal allocation and actual locations of new primary schools, 2002-09)
main_predictor: Congruence_20km_CRavg_T1 (avg congruence with precolonial state centralization, 20km buffer)
sample_definition: Local governments (communautés rurales) existing in 2002 with non-missing outcome (N=278)
model_specification: OLS regression with region fixed effects
controls: log population, population density, average elevation, avg log distance to waterway, Ferlo zone dummy, ELF, party gap, national-coalition alignment, % Mouride villages, region fixed effects
operationalization_notes: The LocAllocT1 dataset operationalizes 'distributing goods broadly across space' as the PopDIFF measure from a location-allocation maximum-coverage model: smaller PopDIFF indicates allocation closer to the spatially optimal (i.e., more broadly distributed). A negative coefficient on precolonial congruence thus supports the claim.
reasoning: OLS regression of the difference between maximum-coverage ideal-point allocation and actual school allocation (PopDIFF_MaxCov_T1) on local-government average precolonial-state congruence yields a significantly negative coefficient (b=-545.4, t=-2.79, p=0.006, N=278), meaning local governments with more precolonial-state heritage distribute schools closer to the spatially optimal (broadly distributed) allocation — consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Incumbent presidential party vote share (IncVote)
main_predictor: AbsCumLiberalPoliciesMood — absolute deviation of cumulative liberal laws over the term from what would be predicted by the public's policy mood
sample_definition: All U.S. presidential elections in the dataset with non-missing values on the variables of interest (1952–2012; n = 16)
model_specification: OLS regression of IncVote on AbsCumLiberalPoliciesMood with controls
controls: Cumulative real per-capita disposable income growth (CumRPCDI) and presidential-party tenure (Tenure)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns producing more or fewer liberal laws than predicted from mood; this is exactly the absolute deviation captured by AbsCumLiberalPoliciesMood. I controlled for the economy and tenure given the abstract's emphasis on these alternative drivers; restricting to a bivariate model yields a similar negative but slightly less significant effect (t≈-1.85).
reasoning: Regressing incumbent presidential vote share on the absolute deviation between cumulative liberal laws and the deviation predicted by public mood, controlling for cumulative real per-capita disposable income growth and presidential-party tenure, yields a negative and marginally significant coefficient on policy misrepresentation (b = -0.174, t(12) = -2.12, p = .056, n = 16 elections). The negative sign supports the paper's claim that misrepresenting the public's policy mood costs the incumbent party votes.

dependent_variable: Mean Empathic Concern score (x_ecall, 7-item IRI EC subscale)
main_predictor: Power condition (1=high power vs 2=low power)
sample_definition: All 36 participants in Experiment 3 (social manipulation: power)
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test
operationalization_notes: Dataset corresponds to Experiment 3 (power manipulation as the social manipulation). Low power = detailed processing context per claim. Used precomputed mean of recoded EC items.
reasoning: Low-power participants (detailed processing; M=3.89) reported significantly higher empathic concern than high-power participants (abstract processing; M=3.47), t(34)=-2.40, p=.022, supporting the claim that detailed processing enhances empathic concern.

dependent_variable: cowwar (dyadic militarized dispute escalates to interstate war)
main_predictor: terrXmixed (territorial dispute × mixed democracy-autocracy dyad interaction)

main_predictor: gm_win (indicator that the GM ballot passed, i.e. vote share >50%)
sample_definition: All school-year observations in main_data.dta from schools that held a GM ballot, with non-missing GCSE outcomes (1992-2003)
model_specification: OLS regression discontinuity: pt_gcse_5_a_c ~ gm_win + win_vote + lose_vote + year FE + base-year FE, with SEs clustered by school id
controls: Linear vote-margin slopes on each side of threshold (win_vote, lose_vote); year fixed effects; base (ballot-year) fixed effects
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns achievement gains at GM converters, identified via RD on the parental ballot share with the 50% threshold. I used a simple linear RD on the full sample of ballot schools, including running-variable controls on each side of the cutoff and fixed effects for year and ballot cohort.
reasoning: In a regression discontinuity specification regressing the share of pupils achieving 5+ GCSEs A-C on a GM-win dummy with linear vote-margin controls on each side of the 50% threshold and year and base-year fixed effects (SE clustered by school), the coefficient on gm_win is +6.03 percentage points (z=1.99, p=0.047, N=8665). Schools that narrowly passed the GM ballot subsequently performed significantly better than those that narrowly failed, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Participated (lab) (0/1)
main_predictor: Sent_Class (amount sent in classroom trust game, 0-20)
sample_definition: Subjects with non-missing trust-game send amount in the classroom session (those assigned to the trust-game treatment)
model_specification: Logistic regression of lab participation on amount sent
operationalization_notes: Claim refers to trust-game senders' subsequent lab participation; simplest direct test is a logit of lab participation on the classroom Sent amount among trust-game classroom subjects.
reasoning: Logistic regression of lab participation on amount sent in the classroom trust game yields a negative coefficient (b=-0.0448, z=-2.50, p=0.013, N=658), indicating that participants who sent less were significantly more likely to participate in the lab experiment.

dependent_variable: used_act (household obtained/used an ACT during the follow-up period)
main_predictor: Indicator for very-high-subsidy arm (Coartem retail price = 40 Ksh) vs. unsubsidized control (500 Ksh)
sample_definition: Households in the AllMain dataset assigned to either the 40 Ksh price arm or the 500 Ksh control arm
model_specification: OLS linear probability model of used_act on the high-subsidy indicator with HC1-robust standard errors
operationalization_notes: The four ACT price arms (40/60/100/500 Ksh) represent decreasing subsidies; 40 Ksh is the 'very high' subsidy and 500 Ksh is approximately the unsubsidized market price, serving as the natural comparison for testing whether a very high subsidy increases access.
reasoning: Comparing the highest-subsidy arm (Coartem price = 40 Ksh) to the no-subsidy control (500 Ksh), the share of households obtaining an ACT rises from 4.4% to 43.9% — a 39.5 pp increase (HC1-robust z = 16.41, p < 0.001, N = 902). The very high subsidy thus substantially increases access to antimalarials, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: First difference of combined standardized PIAT math + reading scores (piamatsn + piarersn) across consecutive test waves within child
main_predictor: First difference of real total family income (earnincrsimp + unearnincrsimp + nontaxincrsimp), expressed per $1,000
sample_definition: Child-year observations from the NLSY children panel (main.dta) with non-missing PIAT math AND reading scores; differences taken between successive PIAT waves within child, yielding 16,934 child-wave-pair observations.
model_specification: First-difference linear regression with year fixed effects; standard errors clustered at the child level.
controls: Year (calendar) fixed effects only; child fixed effects absorbed by differencing.
operationalization_notes: Without the methods section, I committed to a within-child first-difference OLS specification that directly maps to the paper's short-run causal claim (change in income -> change in test scores). I did not attempt to construct the EITC simulated-instrument, so this is the reduced-form OLS counterpart of the paper's IV analysis.
reasoning: First-difference OLS of the change in combined PIAT math+reading standardized scores on the change in real total family income (per $1,000), with year fixed effects and child-clustered SEs, yields a coefficient of 0.0004 SD per $1,000 (SE=0.00082, t=0.49, p=0.63, N=16,934). The point estimate is positive (same sign as the paper's IV claim) but is not statistically distinguishable from zero and far smaller than the paper's IV estimate of ~0.06 SD, consistent with attenuation in OLS relative to the EITC-instrumented effect.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs)
main_predictor: Single childless indicator (singchild1: 1 = single & childless, 0 = other family structures)
sample_definition: Study 1 business-school alumni filtered by employ in {1,2,3}; cases with complete data on the variables in the model (N=353)
model_specification: OLS linear regression with t-test on the singchild1 coefficient
operationalization_notes: Abstract names Study 1 (alumni survey) for this claim; used the single-childless dummy as predictor of absorption with standard demographic controls available in the dataset.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of work absorption on a single-childless indicator controlling for gender, age, and job level (Study 1 sample, N=353), single childless workers scored significantly lower on absorption than others (b=-0.31, t(348)=-2.36, p=.019), matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: ProperName (greeted by proper name, 0/1)
main_predictor: Sender race (Hispanic vs. white, pooled across male/female aliases)
sample_definition: Email audits with Hispanic or white sender aliases and non-missing ProperName (i.e., responses received)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2)
operationalization_notes: Claim compares Hispanic to white senders; pooled male+female within each race. ProperName is defined only for responses, so the test conditions on response receipt.
reasoning: Among emails that received a response (non-missing ProperName), 41.2% of Hispanic-sender emails were greeted by name vs 61.1% of white-sender emails. A chi-square test of independence yields χ²(1)=14.42, p<.001, N=362, supporting the claim that Hispanic applicants were less likely to be greeted by name than white applicants.

dependent_variable: qualityc (ex post quality; lower values indicate more shading; shading defined as quality<2)
main_predictor: contracttypec (1=flexible, 2=rigid)
sample_definition: All transactions in the dataset (all conditions and periods)
model_specification: Mann-Whitney U test (two-sided) on qualityc by contract type, with normal-approximation z
operationalization_notes: Quality takes values -1, 1, 2; -1 and 1 represent shading. A nonparametric rank test on qualityc directly captures the shading comparison the paper makes between flexible and rigid contracts.
reasoning: Mann-Whitney comparison of ex post quality between flexible (n=952, mean quality=1.34) and rigid (n=1508, mean quality=1.78) contracts yields z=-3.98, p<0.001. Quality is significantly lower (more shading) under flexible contracts, consistent with the paper's claim that rigid contracts produce much less shading.

dependent_variable: ln(state CO2 emissions, carbon_adj)
main_predictor: ln(average working hours, wrkhrs)
sample_definition: All 50 US states, years 2007–2013 (N=350 state-years)
model_specification: OLS with state and year fixed effects, cluster-robust SEs by state
controls: ln(real GDP per capita), ln(population), ln(manufacturing share), ln(employment-to-population ratio), year FE, state FE
operationalization_notes: STIRPAT-style log-log panel with two-way fixed effects is the most direct test of the paper's claim that working hours are positively related to state CO2 emissions, 2007–2013.
reasoning: In a two-way (state and year) fixed-effects log-log model with state-clustered SEs, the coefficient on ln(working hours) is positive (β=0.53) with t≈1.65 (p≈0.098), indicating a positive association between average working hours and CO2 emissions, consistent with the paper's claim of a positive relationship, although the magnitude is only borderline significant under this stringent specification.

dependent_variable: consider (state struck or seriously considered striking another's nuclear infrastructure, dyad-year)
main_predictor: hostileMID (prior violent militarized interstate dispute in the dyad)
sample_definition: All directed dyad-years 1941-2000 with non-missing covariates (N=58,001)
model_specification: Logistic regression with peace-years cubic splines
controls: polity2, s_un_reg, pwrratio, postCW, prgmyrs, NCAnosafetodate, contig, noconsideryrs + 3 splines
operationalization_notes: Chose 'consider' as the broader DV most directly capturing salience of the proliferation threat; hostileMID operationalizes 'prior violent militarized conflict.' Controls reflect variables present in the dataset typical of dyadic conflict models.
reasoning: In a logit of 'consider' (state struck or seriously considered striking another's nuclear program) on hostileMID with standard controls (polity2, UN voting affinity, capability ratio, post-Cold War, program years, NCA no-safeguards, contiguity, and peace-years splines), prior hostile MID has a large positive, highly significant coefficient (b=3.80, z=7.58, p<.001), supporting the claim that prior violent militarized conflict increases the likelihood of strike consideration.

dependent_variable: splinter (county broke away from its district to form a new district)
main_predictor: support_loser (county majority supported the losing LC5 chair candidate — proxy for political marginalization within the existing local administrative unit)
sample_definition: All county-period observations in DistrictFormation.dta with non-missing values on the predictors (N=483)
model_specification: Binary logistic regression
controls: MARG (economic/social marginalization index), ethnic_min, log population, log area
operationalization_notes: The claim is about *political* marginalization driving secession. Among available political measures, support_loser most directly captures whether a county is politically marginalized within its current district (its preferred LC5 candidate lost). Standard demographic and socioeconomic controls included.
reasoning: In a logit of splinter (whether a county broke away to form a new district) on a county-level indicator of political marginalization—whether the county supported the losing LC5 chair candidate—the coefficient is positive (b=0.52, z=1.87, p=0.061), consistent with the paper's claim that politically marginalized areas are more likely to secede. Direction matches the claim; significance is borderline.

dependent_variable: sumrecother1 (sum of diplomatic representatives at state A from other states)
main_predictor: n_cap7a (7-stage nuclear capability index for state A)
sample_definition: State-year observations (collapsed from directed-dyad-year), non-missing on predictors and outcome
model_specification: OLS with cluster-robust SE (clustered on state)
controls: CINC capabilities (cap_1), log GDP per capita (lngdp96pa), democracy (idemauta)
operationalization_notes: Claim is about state-level diplomatic recognition, so I collapsed the directed-dyad-year data to state-year using state A's attributes. Used the continuous 7-stage nuclear capability scale as the main predictor with standard controls for power, wealth, and regime type.
reasoning: In an OLS regression at the state-year level, the nuclear-capability index (n_cap7a, 0-7) is a strong positive predictor of diplomatic recognition received from other states (sumrecother1), b=6.91, cluster-robust z=15.80, p<0.001, N=1218, controlling for material capabilities, log GDP per capita, and democracy. This supports the paper's claim that nuclear-capable states attract greater diplomatic recognition.

dependent_variable: change_w3w2_log: log of absolute opinion change between wave 2 (pre-deliberation) and wave 3 (post-deliberation)
main_predictor: DQ_jlev: participant-level mean Discourse Quality Index level-of-justification score
sample_definition: 191 EuroPolis participants with non-missing opinion-change and DQ justification scores
model_specification: OLS regression: change_w3w2_log ~ DQ_jlev
operationalization_notes: Used the provided SANDERS_Replication.dta, which contains the paper's constructed opinion-change variable (log of |w3-w2|) and the participant-level mean justification (jlev) score. Bivariate model isolates the test of the claim that more rational justification corresponds to more opinion change.
reasoning: OLS regression of the log of absolute opinion change between wave 2 and wave 3 on the participant-level mean justification level (DQ_jlev) yields a positive, statistically significant coefficient (b=0.158, t(189)=2.60, p=.010). Higher levels of rational justification in deliberation are associated with greater opinion change, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Mean effort (work, binary) per matching group
main_predictor: Reward scheme (345COM discriminating vs 444COM symmetric)
sample_definition: Only complementarity treatments (345COM and 444COM); unit of analysis = independent matching group (mg)
model_specification: One-sided Mann-Whitney U test on matching-group mean effort
operationalization_notes: Matching groups are the standard independent unit; effort is binary per period, aggregated to group mean. Directional alternative reflects the directional claim.
reasoning: Aggregating effort (work) by independent matching group under the complementarity production technology, mean effort in the discriminating reward scheme 345COM (0.917) was substantially higher than in the symmetric 444COM (0.722). A one-sided Mann-Whitney U test gives U=95, p=0.035 (n1=12, n2=11), supporting the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Senator's letter content score = (pro-content indicator) − (anti-content indicator), computed separately for the response to the pro audience and to the anti audience
main_predictor: Audience type (pro- vs anti-cloture constituent letter), within-subject
sample_definition: All senators who responded to both the pro and anti constituent letters (n = 56)
model_specification: Paired/within-subject two-sided t-test comparing the senator's content score to the pro vs anti audience
operationalization_notes: The claim is about within-senator tailoring of explanations across audiences. Using the coded content of each senator's two letters, I formed a pro−anti content score for each audience and compared paired scores across audiences. A positive difference (pro-audience score > anti-audience score) is direct evidence of tailoring.
reasoning: Among the 56 senators who responded to both the pro- and anti-cloture constituent letters, the pro-minus-anti content score was significantly higher when the audience was pro (mean = -0.20) than when the audience was anti (mean = -0.43); paired t(55) = 3.45, p = .001. This indicates senators tailor explanation content to audience.

dependent_variable: log wage gain at migration (post-migration US wage minus pre-migration home-country wage)
main_predictor: education category (no high school vs. college degree)
sample_definition: intended: NIS immigrants with valid pre- and post-migration wages; not available in the provided data
model_specification: intended: OLS of log wage gain on education indicators, or two-sample t-test of mean gain (no-HS vs. college)
controls: intended: age, sex, year of migration; none computed (data unavailable)
operationalization_notes: The provided Dataverse archive (`code and data.zip`) ships only US CPS wage-regression objects and Caselli/Barro-Lee country aggregates; the immigrant-level NIS file required to compute wage gains by education is not included. Therefore no test statistic could be produced.
reasoning: The claim concerns immigrant wage gains at migration to the United States compared across education groups (no-high-school vs. college). Testing it requires individual-level pre- and post-migration wage data from the New Immigrant Survey (NIS). The provided dataverse archive contains only the US CPS wage-regression inputs (data_table_YYYY.mat, logwage.txt) and country-level development-accounting variables (handbookdata.dta, BL2013). No NIS immigrant micro-file with pre/post-migration wages and education is present — the mmp/cps/imperfect_substitution program archives contain only code, not the underlying immigrant survey microdata (likely restricted-access). I therefore cannot compute the relevant test statistic on the supplied data.

dependent_variable: Free-association consistency (FAbaseC vs FAsuppC)
main_predictor: Item condition: baseline vs. suppress (within-subjects)
sample_definition: Nonruminators: participants with RRS <= sample median (43); n=27 of 54
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing baseline vs. suppress consistency
operationalization_notes: Claim refers to Experiment 2 indirect transfer (free-association) showing suppression benefit for nonruminators. Operationalized 'nonruminator' as RRS median split (low half) and tested baseline>suppress within that subgroup.
reasoning: Among nonruminators (RRS at or below the sample median of 43), free-association consistency was higher for baseline cues (M=46.3) than for suppressed cues (M=30.2), paired t(26)=3.03, p=.005, indicating suppression-induced forgetting on the indirect free-association transfer task.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being (CES-D 8-item composite, variable 'wellbeing' in author dataset)
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction: individual childlessness (par_stat == 'Childless' vs parents) × country-level childlessness-disapproval (childless_disapp_std)
sample_definition: ESS Round 3 respondents aged 40+ in 24 European countries; listwise deletion on outcome, predictors and controls (n=25,082)
model_specification: Linear two-level mixed-effects model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML) with random intercept and random childless slope by country
controls: age, age^2, marital status, education, parental education, religiosity, gender, born in country, paid work
operationalization_notes: Used the author-prepared analysis file which contains the constructed wellbeing scale, parental-status categorisation, and country-level childlessness-disapproval norm; tested the key cross-level interaction central to the claim.
reasoning: In a multilevel model with random intercepts and random childless slopes across 24 countries, the cross-level interaction childless × country-level childlessness-disapproval (standardised) was negative (b = -0.036, z = -1.15, p = .25), pointing in the direction predicted by the claim (childless people fare relatively worse where disapproval is higher / tolerance is lower) but not statistically significant.

dependent_variable: DSM5_Total (self-reported DSM-5 cross-cutting symptom measure of psychopathology)
main_predictor: MiniK_Total (Mini-K life history strategy score; higher = slower life strategy)
sample_definition: All 138 participants with non-missing Mini-K and DSM-5 totals
model_specification: Bivariate Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: The claim directly links life history strategy speed (Mini-K) to psychopathology symptoms (DSM-5 total). A bivariate Pearson correlation is the most direct test; a negative coefficient indicates faster life strategy associates with greater psychopathology.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between Mini-K total (higher = slower life strategy) and DSM-5 psychopathology total is r = -0.587, t(136) = -8.46, p < .001, N = 138. The negative correlation means faster life strategy (lower Mini-K) is associated with more psychopathology symptoms, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (political knowledge score)
main_predictor: Stereotypaktivierung condition (0 = not activated vs 2 = activated by gender-difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender_alle=1) from Study 2 in conditions 0 and 2
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test
operationalization_notes: Claim is a within-female comparison across two specific experimental conditions; direct two-group t-test on the political knowledge sum score is the most direct test.
reasoning: Female participants in the stereotype-not-activated condition scored higher on the political knowledge test (M=8.38, SD=4.80, n=79) than female participants in the stereotype-activated-by-gender-difference-statement condition (M=7.17, SD=4.20, n=81); Welch t(154.18)=1.69, p=.093. The direction matches the claim though it does not reach conventional significance.

dependent_variable: gdpidx (annual city GDP growth index)
main_predictor: msec2currentsec (city party secretary connected to current provincial party secretary via past promotion, 0/1)
sample_definition: City-year panel 2000-2011 from citypanel_base.dta merged with econ_panel.dta, observations with non-missing gdpidx, tie indicator, loggdp and logpop (N=4,872).
model_specification: OLS with city and year fixed effects, standard errors clustered at the city level.
controls: log GDP (loggdp), log population (logpop), city fixed effects, year fixed effects
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns city-leader patronage ties to incumbent provincial leaders. The city party secretary is the senior city leader, and 'msec2currentsec' is the codebook's promotion-based patronage tie to the current provincial secretary. A standard two-way FE growth regression with basic economic controls is the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects (city + year) OLS regression of city GDP growth (gdpidx) on the city secretary's connection to the current provincial secretary (msec2currentsec), controlling for log GDP and log population, the tie indicator has a coefficient of -0.299 (cluster-robust SE 0.127, t = -2.36, p = 0.018, N = 4,872). Thus the connected leaders are estimated to deliver slightly SLOWER, not faster, GDP growth in this specification, which is opposite to the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Indicator for foreign player having played at A national-team level (high-ability proxy)
main_predictor: Post-1991 indicator (Denmark's preferential tax scheme for foreigners)
sample_definition: Player-year observations of foreign (non-Danish nationality) players appearing in the Danish league, 1975-2008
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 table (post x high-ability)
operationalization_notes: National_team_level=='A' used as high-ability indicator; cutoff at 1991 corresponds to the Danish foreigner tax cut highlighted in the paper's case study.
reasoning: Among foreign players in the Danish league, the share who had played at the A-national-team level (proxy for high ability) rose from 21.3% (26/122) before the 1991 Danish preferential tax scheme to 57.3% (596/1040) afterwards. A chi-square test of independence yields χ²(1)=55.44, p≈1e-13, strongly supporting the claim that the tax cut for foreigners shifted the ability composition toward higher-ability players.

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay
main_predictor: intrin_extrin (intrinsic relative to extrinsic values)
sample_definition: All 155 participants with complete data on both variables
model_specification: Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: The dataset already contains a composite variable 'intrin_extrin' capturing intrinsic relative to extrinsic value endorsement and 'willingness_to_pay'; the claim is most directly tested by their bivariate correlation.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between intrinsic-relative-to-extrinsic values (intrin_extrin) and willingness to pay to protect the environment is r=0.426, p<.001, n=155, indicating a positive relationship consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: ln_imports (log product-level imports from partner into respondent in post-dispute years)
main_predictor: complainant indicator (1 = complainant country, 0 = nonparticipant 'rest of membership')
sample_definition: Observations from disputes settled early (earlysettle==1), post-dispute years only (counter>0), restricted to complainant and nonparticipant trading partners; missing covariates dropped.
model_specification: OLS regression of ln_imports on complainant dummy with standard errors clustered by dispute
controls: ln GDP of respondent and partner, ln per-capita income of respondent and partner
operationalization_notes: The claim is about discriminatory post-settlement trade gains accruing to complainants relative to the rest of the WTO membership under private (early) settlements. I therefore subset to early-settled disputes in the post-period and tested the complainant-vs-nonparticipant gap in product-level log imports, controlling for standard gravity-type covariates and clustering SEs at the dispute level.
reasoning: In early-settled WTO disputes, post-dispute log product-level imports are significantly higher for complainant countries than for nonparticipant (rest-of-membership) countries (coef = 2.05, cluster-robust z = 4.27, p < 0.001, N = 5,856 product-year observations across disputes). This directly supports the paper's claim that private/early settlements yield discriminatory trade outcomes favoring complainants.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (new business formation rate, country-year)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of working-age population 20-64)
sample_definition: All GEM country-year observations (2001-2010), 82 countries, weighted by number of survey respondents (nobs_cy)
model_specification: WLS regression with year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by country
controls: Year fixed effects only (Table 2 column 3 specification)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Table 2 column 3 reduced-form specification linking median age to entrepreneurship, since the claim directly concerns the median-age effect on new business formation.
reasoning: Weighted OLS of new-business formation rate (entre_wage) on country median age (medage_20_64) with year fixed effects and standard errors clustered by country yields a coefficient of -0.0073 (t = -5.71, N = 393, 82 country clusters). Higher median age is strongly associated with lower entrepreneurship, consistent with the claim that decreases in median age increase new business formation.

dependent_variable: Ratio of perceived to actual arm length (RatioRight, RatioLeft)
main_predictor: Arm side (right vs left), within-subject
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (Handedness == 1), N = 15
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing RatioRight and RatioLeft
controls: None (ratio inherently controls for actual arm length)
operationalization_notes: Used perceived/actual ratio because actual arm lengths differ between right and left arms; this isolates perceptual distortion. Right-handers selected because the claim is specifically about them.
reasoning: Paired t-test of perceived/actual arm length ratio (right vs left) among right-handers yielded t(14) = -0.82, p = .43. Mean ratio right = 0.978, left = 0.993; the numerical direction is opposite the claim but not statistically distinguishable from zero.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (mean of feeling appreciated, valued, satisfied)
main_predictor: condition (0=verbal acknowledgment, 1=financial acknowledgment)
sample_definition: Study 1a participants with exclude=0 (n=49)
model_specification: Independent samples two-sided t-test
operationalization_notes: Only Study 1a data are provided; the composite DV index (dv_index3) directly captures positive customer outcomes referenced in the claim, and condition is the verbal-vs-financial contrast.
reasoning: Comparing the verbal-acknowledgment (cond=0, M=5.57) vs. financial-acknowledgment (cond=1, M=4.38) conditions on the 3-item DV index (feel appreciated/valued/satisfied) among non-excluded participants, an independent-samples t-test yields t(47)=2.92, p=.005, with verbal > financial — consistent with the trivialization effect.

dependent_variable: Standardized total test score (s_tot)
main_predictor: avg5_girl (fraction of 5 nearest neighbors who are female)
sample_definition: Female students only
model_specification: OLS with class (gc) fixed effects, cluster-robust SE at class level
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns females surrounded by 5 females vs 5 males; avg5_girl captures gender composition of the 5-neighbor microenvironment. Restricted to females and added class FEs to mimic the paper's random within-class seat assignment design.
reasoning: Among female students, the share of the five nearest classmates who are girls (avg5_girl) is positively and significantly associated with standardized test scores (coef≈0.68, cluster-robust z=3.00, p=0.003, N=292). The positive sign matches the paper's claim that being surrounded by females rather than males raises female test scores.

dependent_variable: Attitude stability operationalized as -|att_T2 - att_T1| (negative absolute change of the 3-item attitude mean)
main_predictor: Ambivalence (Griffin: (pos+neg)/2 - |pos-neg|) × Certainty (mean of cert1-cert7) interaction, both mean-centered
sample_definition: All participants from Study 1 and Study 2 with complete T1 attitudes, T2 attitudes, ambivalence, and certainty (N=588 combined)
model_specification: OLS regression: stability ~ ambiv_c*cert_c + study fixed effect
operationalization_notes: Pooled Studies 1 and 2 since claim is 'across studies'; used Griffin ambivalence index and averaged certainty/attitude items; stability operationalized as the negative absolute T1→T2 attitude change so that a negative interaction reflects the hypothesized pattern.
reasoning: The ambivalence × certainty interaction predicting attitude stability (negative absolute attitude change from T1 to T2) is significant, t(583) = -3.89, p < .001. The negative interaction coefficient indicates that certainty predicts greater stability when ambivalence is lower, and ambivalence predicts greater instability when certainty is higher, matching the directional claim.

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters)
main_predictor: Log foreign direct investment stock (foreign ownership of capital)
sample_definition: OECD country-election observations 1970-2007 with non-missing turnout, log FDI stock, and the covariates listed
model_specification: OLS with country and year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by country
controls: log GDP per capita, share aged 30-69, time since last election, no-presidential dummy, closeness, PR dummy, compulsory voting (cvfranklin)
operationalization_notes: Foreign ownership operationalized as logged FDI stock (the paper's principal foreign-ownership measure). TWFE accounts for unobserved country and year heterogeneity; controls follow standard turnout determinants.
reasoning: Regressing electoral turnout on log FDI stock (foreign-ownership measure) with country and year fixed effects and standard turnout covariates, the coefficient on foreign ownership is negative (b = -1.99, cluster-robust SE = 1.15, t = -1.73, p ≈ 0.08, N=275, 23 country clusters). The direction matches the ownership-constraint hypothesis: greater foreign ownership is associated with lower turnout.

dependent_variable: Number of service complaints in 2008 (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: first_A indicator (firm name begins with A or a number)
sample_definition: All 2293 plumbing firms in final_data.dta
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test (unequal variances)
operationalization_notes: The claim is a simple group-mean comparison of complaints by first-letter category; final_data.dta provides the firm-level complaint counts and the first_A indicator used in the paper.
reasoning: Welch's t-test comparing 2008 service complaints between plumbing firms whose name begins with A or a number (first_A=1, mean=1.34, n=295) vs others (mean=0.25, n=1998) yields t(310.1)=3.85, p=0.00014. Firms starting with A/number receive significantly more complaints, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: dv (ordinal bargaining strategy, 0=least to 3=most cooperative/concessionary)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure (degree to which issues are differently valued)
sample_definition: All 588 EU state-bargain observations in the dataset
model_specification: Ordered logistic regression (proportional-odds)

The OLS regression of BoniVote on the FemmeFon dummy yields t(135)=2.06, p=0.041, n=137, supporting the claim that priming the first lady's ethnicity increases support among coethnics.

dependent_variable: effort_t1 (individual first-stage effort)
main_predictor: Treatment indicator (TS vs OS)

dependent_variable: preference_first (binary: prefer first vs. novel group)
main_predictor: condition (positive-shared/negative-unique = 1 vs. negative-shared/positive-unique = 0)
sample_definition: All participants across Experiments 1, 2, and 3

reasoning: Pooling all three experiments, condition (positive-shared/negative-unique vs. negative-shared/positive-unique) was strongly associated with preference for the first group, χ²(1, N=641)=22.62, p<.001. In the negative-unique condition 213/320 (66.6%) preferred the first group, vs. 154/321 (48.0%) in the positive-unique condition, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Total household income (totinc)
main_predictor: domlow (village dominated by low caste = 1, by high caste = 0)

model_specification: Two-sample independent t-test (equal variances) comparing means of totinc across domlow groups
controls: None (simple bivariate t-test, mirroring the paper's Table 2 style)
operationalization_notes: The claim is a direct mean comparison of income for low-caste households across the two village types. I identified low-caste households as those with caste==5 (the group with the lowest mean income, consistent with scheduled/low caste) and tested totinc by the domlow indicator, paralleling the ttest specifications in the paper's program file.
reasoning: Among low-caste (caste==5) households, total income is significantly higher in villages dominated by a low caste (mean=3989.7, n=216) than in villages dominated by a high caste (mean=2092.9, n=263); t(477)=2.83, p=0.005. This reproduces the paper's directional claim.

dependent_variable: Total money raised per session (variable 'money')
main_predictor: Verbal-ask treatment (A1 or A2) vs. silent/mute solicitor treatment (M1 or M2)
sample_definition: All 64 sessions assigned to one of the four solicitor treatments (A1, A2, M1, M2); pure control sessions (C) excluded because no solicitor was present and hence 'money' is not defined.

operationalization_notes: The verbal-ask manipulation contrasts solicitors who explicitly asked (A1/A2) with solicitors who stood silently (M1/M2). Session-level total money raised is the most direct measure of 'giving'.
reasoning: Across the four Salvation Army solicitor treatments (A1, A2, M1, M2), sessions with a verbal ask raised significantly more money per session ($70.74) than sessions with a silent/mute solicitor ($46.40); Welch t(59.24)=4.82, p<0.001 (n=64 sessions). This supports the paper's claim that the verbal ask increased giving.

dependent_variable: zakaibag (Bagrut certification, 0/1)
main_predictor: treated (school-level treatment assignment)
sample_definition: Girls (boy==0) in the base01 sample (2001 cohort)
model_specification: OLS regression of certification on treatment with pair fixed effects; standard errors clustered at the school level
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns girls' certification rates under school-based randomization, so I restricted to girls, used Bagrut certification as the outcome, the treatment dummy as the predictor, included pair fixed effects to reflect the matched-pair school randomization, and clustered SEs by school.
reasoning: OLS with pair fixed effects and school-clustered SEs estimates treated girls' Bagrut certification rate as 7.87 percentage points higher than controls (t=1.62, p=0.11, N=1861 across 34 school clusters). The point estimate is positive and substantial, consistent with the claimed increase in certification rates for girls, though only marginally significant.

dependent_variable: Intrafirm import share (imp_intrafirm) at the country-industry-year level
main_predictor: DownMeasure × High-Sigma interaction (sigma above median)
sample_definition: All country–IO2002 industry–year observations (2000-2010) with non-missing intrafirm share, downstreamness, sigma, and industry controls

operationalization_notes: Claim states positive D–intrafirm relationship emerges only for high-sigma industries. Most direct test: interaction of DownMeasure with an above-median sigma dummy in the full panel. Used Census Related-Party trade panel merged with downstreamness, sigma, factor intensities, R&D.
reasoning: The interaction between the DownMeasure index of downstreamness and a high-sigma (above-median import demand elasticity) indicator has a positive coefficient (0.037) in the predicted direction, but is statistically insignificant (t=0.89, p=0.37). The main effect of downstreamness is significantly negative (t=-2.77), so the claimed conditional reversal for high-sigma industries is not clearly supported in my specification.

dependent_variable: bid_on_d (PAP showed interest in case)
main_predictor: baby_girl_d (child is a girl, vs boy)

operationalization_notes: The claim concerns AP preference favoring non-AA girls; the most direct reduced-form test is whether PAPs are more likely to express interest in non-AA girls than non-AA boys. ChoicePanel2 already includes nonaa_girl/nonaa_boy indicators, so I restrict to non-AA known-gender cases and compare bid rates by gender.
reasoning: Among non-African American children (nonaa_girl or nonaa_boy = 1) in the PAP-case choice panel, the bid rate is 6.92% for girls vs 6.18% for boys; OLS of bid_on_d on baby_girl_d yields coef=+0.0074 (cluster-robust SE by mother_id = 0.0091, z=0.81, p=0.42). The sign favors girls, consistent with the claimed positive preference for non-AA girls, but the difference is not statistically significant in this simple reduced-form test (which lacks the PAP-specific structure of the paper's choice model).

dependent_variable: a-index of ambiguity-induced insensitivity in part 1 (3*(1/3 - (mc - ms)))
main_predictor: Treatment (time pressure vs control)
sample_definition: All 104 subjects (62 TP, 42 control); within-subject mean computed from non-missing matching probabilities in part 1

operationalization_notes: Part 1 is the part administered with time pressure (only part where 'missing' flag can be 1 for TP subjects). The a-index is the standard Baillon et al. measure of ambiguity-generated insensitivity; missing matching probabilities were excluded from the within-subject averages.
reasoning: The a-index of ambiguity-induced insensitivity, computed as 3*(1/3 - (mean composite MP - mean single MP)) using part 1 (the part administered under time pressure), is significantly higher in the TP group (mean = 0.340, n=62) than in the control group (mean = 0.150, n=42); Welch's t(90.08) = 2.13, p = 0.036, consistent with the paper's claim that people become more insensitive under time pressure.

dependent_variable: durationmonths (duration of civil war in months)
main_predictor: technologyrebellion (irregular vs. conventional+SNC)
sample_definition: All 142 civil wars in the TR dataset with non-missing duration and warfare-technology codes
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test comparing irregular wars to all other warfare types
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts irregular conflicts against 'all other types,' so I dichotomized warfare technology (irregular=1 vs. conventional/SNC=0) and used a Welch t-test on conflict duration as the most direct test.
reasoning: Irregular civil wars (n=76) lasted on average 113.3 months versus 42.0 months for conventional and SNC wars combined (n=66); Welch's two-sample t-test yields t=5.14, df≈116, p≈1.1e-6, supporting the claim that irregular conflicts last longer than other types.

dependent_variable: lndrate (log of monthly all-cause, all-age mortality rate per 100,000 population)
main_predictor: Number of days with mean temperature in 80-90F and >90F bins, interacted with a post-1960 indicator
sample_definition: All state-year-month observations 1900-2004 with non-missing log mortality rate
model_specification: OLS regression of lndrate on temperature-bin counts (omitting 50-60F as reference) each fully interacted with pre/post-1960 indicators, with state-by-month and year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by state. Joint Wald F-test of equality of pre/post coefficients for the two hot-day bins (>80F).
controls: State-by-month fixed effects, year fixed effects, full set of temperature bins (interacted with period), cluster-robust SEs by state
operationalization_notes: Claim specifically concerns temperature-mortality relationship decline; paper's key threshold is >80F. Split sample at 1960 (paper notes 'almost the entire decline occurred after 1960'). Joint F-test on equality of the two hot-day bins gives a single statistic directly testing the claim.
reasoning: A joint Wald F-test of equality of the coefficients on days in 80-90F (b10_9) and >90F (b10_10) between pre-1960 and post-1960 periods yields F(2,48)=10.52, p<0.001. The point estimates show the effect of >90F days on log monthly mortality fell from +0.0083 (pre-1960) to -0.014 (post-1960), confirming a substantial and significant decline in the temperature-mortality relationship across decades.

dependent_variable: Binary purchase decision (notBuy: 1 = chose not to buy DVD, 0 = chose to buy)
main_predictor: Opportunity-cost reminder (oppcost: 11 reminder vs 10 no reminder) × future-self connectedness (ZFINAL, z-scored composite of rate1 and length)
sample_definition: All 88 participants in the DVD-purchase study
model_specification: Logistic regression: notbuy ~ opp + ZFINAL + opp*ZFINAL
operationalization_notes: The claim is about a moderation of the opportunity-cost manipulation by connectedness on spending; the dataset's purchase choice (notBuy) is the spending DV, oppcost is the manipulation, and ZFINAL is the provided composite connectedness score. The interaction term is the test most directly tied to the claim.
reasoning: Logistic regression of choosing not-to-buy on opportunity-cost reminder × future-self connectedness (ZFINAL) yields a significant positive interaction (b=1.05, z=2.10, p=.036, N=88). The opportunity-cost cue increases the probability of forgoing purchase more strongly among consumers higher in connectedness to the future self, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: REF_female (referral is female, 0/1)

sample_definition: Conventional Applicant (CA) condition: treat_either==1 (no gender specified) and treat_perf==0 (flat pay), restricted to OPs who made a referral with non-missing REF_female and OP_female (N=133).
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 table of OP gender by referral gender (no continuity correction).
operationalization_notes: CA is operationalized as the baseline 'either gender / flat-pay' condition. Claim is directly tested by comparing share of female referrals between male and female CA OPs.
reasoning: Among CA (gender-unspecified, flat-pay) OPs who made a referral, 23.4% of male OPs referred a woman vs. 42.9% of female OPs (chi2(1)=5.69, p=0.017, N=133). CA men are significantly less likely to refer women than CA women, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: ali_stdscore_gr10 (grade-10 ALI mathematics test score, year 1)
main_predictor: Treatment 3 (ALI: aligned student+teacher+admin incentives) dummy (dum_treat4)
sample_definition: All grade-10 students in the 88 randomized schools with non-missing ALI math score in year 1 (n=11,436)
model_specification: OLS regression of ALI score on three treatment dummies (T1, T2, T3) vs. control, with standard errors clustered at the school (clavecct) level
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns T3 (ALI). I used the grade-10 year-1 ALI standardized math score as the primary outcome and tested the T3 coefficient relative to the control group via a cluster-robust z-test, mirroring the paper's primary regression structure visible in table_2.log.
reasoning: Regressing the grade-10 year-1 ALI standardized math score on treatment dummies (T1, T2, T3) with school-clustered SEs, the T3 (ALI) coefficient is 38.78 with z=2.96 (p=0.003), indicating a significantly positive effect of T3 on math test scores, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Log discount rate (interval-censored from binary-choice elicitations across four small/large × short/long-horizon intertemporal tasks)
main_predictor: treatE — indicator for the ethnicity-salience priming condition
sample_definition: Asian-American subjects from Experiment 1 (raceA==1); 71 subjects, 4 choice tasks each (284 obs)
model_specification: Interval regression (intreg) with subject-clustered robust standard errors
operationalization_notes: This matches the pooled Table 2A specification — the most direct test of the verbal claim that ethnic-identity salience increases patience among Asian-Americans. Numerical estimation done by maximum-likelihood in Python; standard errors via cluster-robust sandwich with Stata's G/(G-1)·(N-1)/(N-k) adjustment.
reasoning: Cluster-robust interval regression of the log discount rate on the ethnicity-salience treatment among Asian-American subjects (controlling for stakes, time horizon, and their interaction; 71 subjects × 4 intertemporal-choice types = 284 observations clustered on subject) yields a treatment coefficient of -1.417 (SE 0.381, z = -3.72, p ≈ 0.0002). The negative coefficient on log discount rate indicates that making ethnic identity salient leads Asian-American subjects to choose more patiently, replicating the paper's finding.

dependent_variable: Mean cooperation frequency (per matching group across matches)
main_predictor: Horizon: deterministic (condition 3) vs stochastic (condition 4)
sample_definition: Short-duration treatments only (conditions 3 and 4); 12 matching groups in each of 2 sessions per condition = 24 groups per condition
model_specification: Mann-Whitney U test (one-sided, deterministic > stochastic) on group-level mean cooperation frequency
operationalization_notes: Matching group used as independent unit (standard in experimental econ); coop_frequency averaged per group across all subjects, periods, and matches. Computed z from U via normal approximation: z ≈ (U - n1*n2/2)/sqrt(n1*n2*(n1+n2+1)/12) = (486-288)/sqrt(4900) ≈ 2.83 (two-sided p≈0.0047); reported test_statistic uses scipy's normal-approx z for the one-sided p-value.
reasoning: Mann-Whitney U test on group-level mean cooperation frequencies in the short-duration treatments: short-deterministic (mean≈63.3) vs short-stochastic (mean≈52.3) yields U=486 (one-sided p≈2.3e-5), confirming significantly higher cooperation under deterministic than stochastic horizon.

dependent_variable: Distance between plurality party and median voter (pldist1)
main_predictor: Election rule (SMD vs PR)
sample_definition: All country-election observations with non-missing smd and pldist1 (deduplicated by country-year)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test comparing pldist1 across SMD vs PR
operationalization_notes: The claim implies plurality winners are closer to the median voter under SMD competition; the most direct test is whether the plurality-median distance variable is smaller in SMD than in PR systems.

There is no evidence that SMD election rules produce a plurality winner closer to the median voter than under PR.

dependent_variable: nwar1 (binary indicator of new/renewed civil war)

controls: wardur, dead, victory, truce, gdpend, prv10yrs
operationalization_notes: The verbal claim links short time-to-election to renewed war; the natural test is a logit of renewed-war on election-timing (months) with standard civil-war controls (war duration, deaths, victory, truce, GDP at end, prior conflict in 10 years). A negative coefficient on T2fpemths1 would support the claim.

The sign is opposite to the claim (longer waits associated with more, not less, renewed war) and the effect is not statistically significant, so the data do not support the claim that earlier elections increase renewed fighting.

dependent_variable: Femininity rating of the target shopper (item _25)

model_specification: 2x2 between-subjects ANOVA; reporting main effect of green condition
controls: Target gender included as second factor (and its interaction)
operationalization_notes: Without the codebook, item _25 was identified as the femininity rating because its means tracked target gender (higher for female than male targets) across both green conditions, consistent with a manipulation-check feminine-trait item.
reasoning: In a 2 (target green vs. non-green) × 2 (target gender) ANOVA on the feminine rating (item 25), green targets were rated more feminine (M=2.23) than non-green targets (M=1.95), F(1,190)=3.57, p=.060. The direction matches the claim though the main effect is only marginally significant.

dependent_variable: Number of LV-format errors per subject (count out of 10 of choices inconsistent with choosing the stochastically dominant lottery for a risk-averse agent)
main_predictor: Degree of risk aversion = mean number of safe choices across the PV and RV MPL formats
sample_definition: All experimental subjects after dropping the 2 confederate stations flagged with age=99 (n=106)
model_specification: Pearson product-moment correlation between risk-aversion score and LV error count
operationalization_notes: Paper's Hypothesis 2 / Figure 4 reports correlations between risk aversion (avg safe choices in PV and RV) and LV decision error; Risk1*, Risk2*, Risk3* in the data correspond to PV, RV, LV formats based on choice-pattern inspection.

This strong negative correlation supports the claim that decision error decreases with risk aversion.

dependent_variable: Desired compensation (midpoint of reported salary range, in $1000s)
main_predictor: Treatment (public vs private — classmates expected to see preferences)
sample_definition: Single female students in the main experiment (3_mainexp_responses.dta), n=60

operationalization_notes: Desired compensation was coded as the numeric midpoint of the reported salary range. Subsample restricted to single (single==1) female (female==1) respondents, consistent with the claim. Treatment B had the lower mean, indicating it is the public/observable condition.
reasoning: Among single female students, mean desired compensation in treatment B (public/classmates-see) was $113.8k vs $130.6k in treatment A (private), Welch t(48.59)=2.17, p=0.035. Single women report significantly lower desired salaries when they expect classmates to see their preferences.

dependent_variable: pay_for_conditionality (indicator: parent willing to pay to keep CCT conditionality)
main_predictor: Treatment assignment: baseline (treatment==1) vs. SMS-monitoring (treatment==2)

model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 table
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts the proportion willing to pay for conditionality in the SMS treatment vs. baseline; treatment proportions (82% vs 20%) match the paper's text, identifying treatment 1 as baseline and treatment 2 as SMS.
