A Pearson chi-square test of independence yields χ²(1, N=111)=42.64, p≈6.6e-11, strongly supporting the claim that the SMS treatment reduces the proportion willing to pay for conditionality.

dependent_variable: deaths_total (monthly DTO-related deaths in a municipality)
main_predictor: lpub_after06 — indicator for the 1–6 months following a leader capture/kill in the municipality
sample_definition: All municipality-month observations with non-missing deaths_total (Dec 2006–Dec 2010 panel)
model_specification: Two-way fixed-effects linear panel model (municipality and year-month FE) with three post-capture window dummies (1–6, 7–12, >12 months); cluster-robust SE by municipality
controls: Municipality fixed effects, year-month fixed effects, plus 7-12 and >12-month post-capture dummies
operationalization_notes: Chose deaths_total (DTO-related homicides) as the DV most directly tied to the claim, and the leader-capture 1–6 month dummy (lpub_after06) as the short-term treatment indicator, in a standard DiD with two-way FE consistent with the paper's stated approach.
reasoning: Two-way fixed-effects DiD (municipality and year-month FE, SEs clustered by municipality) regressing DTO-related deaths on post-capture dummies yields a positive, statistically significant short-term effect of leader captures in the treated municipality 1–6 months after capture: coefficient = 10.52, t = 2.17, p ≈ 0.03 (N = 119,609). This supports the paper's claim that captures/killings of cartel leaders have exacerbating short-term effects on DTO-related violence.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of the largest connected component of the group's semantic-fluency network
main_predictor: Median split on LATENT openness factor score (high vs low openness)
sample_definition: All 516 participants with cleaned animal-fluency responses; n=258 high vs n=258 low openness
model_specification: Bootstrap test of difference in ASPL between two group networks (500 participant-level resamples); z = mean(diff)/SD(diff)
operationalization_notes: Group networks built by linking animals named consecutively by any subject (binary edges). ASPL is the standard 'interconnectedness' index used in semantic-network studies; lower ASPL indicates a more interconnected network. Bootstrap over subjects approximates the SemNeT-style group comparison.
reasoning: Building group-level semantic networks from consecutive responses on the animal-fluency task, the average shortest path length (ASPL; lower = more interconnected) was 2.85 for the high-openness group and 2.76 for the low-openness group. A bootstrap (500 resamples of participants within each group) gave a mean difference of +0.070 (SD=0.063), z=1.11, p=0.27. The high-openness network was therefore not significantly more interconnected than the low-openness network in this independent re-analysis; the point estimate is actually in the opposite direction, but it is not statistically distinguishable from zero.

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Index (ciri_physint)
main_predictor: tax revenue as share (tax_rev_new)
sample_definition: All country-year observations with complete data on DV, predictors, and controls (N=1739)

controls: total revenue, lagged ciri_physint, log population, income, polity democracy, external/internal conflict, UK colony, ethnic fractionalization, Catholic %, Muslim %
operationalization_notes: Used the main CIRI physical integrity index (the paper's principal DV) with continuous tax_rev_new and a lagged DV specification, mirroring typical operationalizations in this literature.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of CIRI physical integrity rights on tax revenue share (controlling for total revenue, lagged DV, population, income, democracy, conflicts, colonial history, ethnic fractionalization, and religion), tax_rev_new has a positive coefficient (0.0065) with cluster-robust z=2.91, p=0.004, supporting the claim that higher reliance on taxes is associated with better human rights protection.

dependent_variable: pt_gcse_5_a_c (share of pupils achieving 5+ GCSEs at grades A-C)
main_predictor: win = indicator for vote share > 50% in first GM ballot
sample_definition: School-year observations from main_data.dta with non-missing vote share and GCSE outcome (schools that held a GM ballot)
model_specification: OLS with linear running variable (vote share centered at 50) interacted with treatment indicator, plus year fixed effects; cluster-robust SEs at school level
controls: Year fixed effects; linear control for centered vote share and its interaction with treatment
operationalization_notes: Local-linear RD around the 50% ballot threshold, using GCSE pass rate as the primary achievement measure described in the abstract; running variable rescaled to percent because vote ranges 0-100 in the data.
reasoning: In a regression discontinuity specification, schools that narrowly won the GM ballot (vote share > 50%) score about 6.1 percentage points higher on the share of pupils achieving 5+ GCSEs at grades A-C than narrow losers (SE=3.03, t=2.00, p=0.045, N=8,665 school-years, 742 school clusters). This positive and statistically significant discontinuity matches the paper's qualitative claim of large achievement gains from GM conversion.

dependent_variable: Participated (lab) (0/1)
main_predictor: Sent_Class (amount sent in classroom trust game, 0-20)

model_specification: Logistic regression: Participated ~ Sent_Class
operationalization_notes: The claim is directly about whether lower amounts sent in the trust game predict higher likelihood of showing up at the lab; a simple bivariate logit on the classroom-measured Sent variable predicting lab participation is the most direct test.

dependent_variable: took_act (indicator for whether the patient took an ACT antimalarial for the illness episode)
main_predictor: High-subsidy treatment assignment (Coartem price = 40 KSh) vs. unsubsidized control (price = 500 KSh)
sample_definition: Illness episodes assigned to either the 40 KSh ACT price arm or the 500 KSh (no-subsidy) control arm, with non-missing took_act
model_specification: Two-sample z-test for difference in proportions
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether the very high subsidy increases access to antimalarials. Access is operationalized as ACT uptake (took_act). The very high subsidy corresponds to the 40 KSh price (~92% subsidy off the 500 KSh control). A two-proportion z-test most directly tests the directional claim; clustering at household level was attempted in a regression specification but failed in statsmodels, so the simpler unclustered proportion test is reported.
reasoning: Among illness episodes in the highest-subsidy arm (Coartem price = 40 KSh, ~92% subsidy), 34.8% (650/1866) of patients took an ACT, versus 20.6% (94/457) in the unsubsidized control arm (price = 500 KSh). A two-sample proportions z-test yields z = 5.86, p ≈ 4.7e-9, indicating that the very high subsidy substantially increased access to antimalarials, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Change in combined standardized PIAT score = (piamatsn + piarersn)/2 (first difference within child, 2-year gap)
main_predictor: Change in real family income (earned + unearned + non-taxable), in thousands of dollars; instrumented by change in real imputed EITC (rtotweadimp2)
sample_definition: Child-year observations from the NLSY mother-child data with non-missing combined PIAT, family income, and EITC; restricted to consecutive PIAT assessments two years apart
model_specification: Two-stage least squares on first differences with cluster-robust SEs (clustered by child)
controls: Year fixed effects (test year), change in mother's marital status, change in number of adults in household, change in child age
operationalization_notes: First-differencing absorbs child fixed effects; using imputed EITC as instrument follows the paper's IV identification strategy. Combined score defined as the mean of standardized PIAT math and reading-recognition components since these have the largest, comparable sample coverage.
reasoning: Using first-differenced IV (2SLS), regressing the change in the average of standardized PIAT math and reading-recognition scores on the change in real family income (in $1000s), instrumented by the change in the imputed real EITC payment, the coefficient is -0.010 (SE 0.010, t = -0.98, p = 0.33, N = 10,028). The estimate is not statistically distinguishable from zero, so on this operationalization the claim that a $1,000 income increase raises short-run combined math+reading scores does not reproduce.

dependent_variable: work absorption (engwkabs)
main_predictor: single childless indicator (singchild1: 1 = single childless, 0 = other family structure)
sample_definition: Study 1 business-school alumni, employed (filter_$ == 1), with non-missing absorption and family structure (n=361)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test comparing absorption means between single-childless and other workers
operationalization_notes: Claim is a direct mean comparison between single-childless workers and all others on absorption; used the dataset's singchild1 indicator and engwkabs measure within the provided analysis filter.
reasoning: Single, childless workers (n=86, M=4.01) reported significantly lower absorption than workers with other family structures (n=275, M=4.40); Welch's t(123.23) = -2.83, p = .005.

dependent_variable: ProperName (greeted by proper name, 1/0)
main_predictor: Hispanic vs white sender (from TreatmentGroup)
sample_definition: Emails sent under Hispanic or white aliases (excluding black) with non-missing ProperName outcome
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2)
operationalization_notes: Claim contrasts Hispanic vs white applicants on being greeted by name; restricted to those two race groups and used the ProperName indicator as DV with a simple chi-square.
reasoning: Among emails sent under Hispanic vs white aliases that received a response coded for ProperName, 41.2% of Hispanic emailers were greeted by name vs 61.1% of white emailers; chi-square(1)=14.42, p<.001.

dependent_variable: shading indicator (delivered quality = 1, i.e., minimum performance) among realized trades
main_predictor: contract type (1=rigid/fixed-price vs 2=flexible/price-range)
sample_definition: all realized contracts (contractrealizedc==1); non-trade observations with qualityc=-1 excluded
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 contingency table
operationalization_notes: contracttypec=1 = fixed-price (rigid); contracttypec=2 = price-range (flexible). Quality codes are -1 (no trade), 1 (low/shaded performance), 2 (high performance). Shading is naturally operationalized as quality=1 conditional on trade.
reasoning: Among realized trades, shading (quality=1, the minimum-effort outcome) occurred in 9.2% of rigid (fixed-price) contracts vs 21.8% of flexible contracts, χ²(1, N=2273)=55.79, p<1e-13 — substantially less shading under rigid contracts, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: log(state CO2 emissions, unadjusted)
main_predictor: log(average weekly working hours)
sample_definition: 50 US states, years 2007-2013 (350 state-years) from compiled.dta
model_specification: OLS with two-way fixed effects (state and year), cluster-robust SE by state
controls: log real GDP per capita, log population, log employment-to-population, log manufacturing share
operationalization_notes: Selected the state-year panel restricted to 2007–2013 per the claim window; used a standard STIRPAT-style log-log FE specification with common controls suggested by available variables.
reasoning: In a two-way (state and year) fixed-effects log-log regression of state CO2 emissions on average working hours with controls for real GDP per capita, population, employment-to-population ratio, and manufacturing share, the coefficient on log working hours is positive (b=0.53) with a cluster-robust t=1.65 (p≈0.10), consistent with the paper's positive working-hours/emissions relationship.

dependent_variable: consider (state seriously considered attacking another's nuclear program in a given dyad-year)
main_predictor: hostileMID (prior violent militarized interstate dispute between dyad)
sample_definition: All directed dyad-years 1941-2000 with non-missing covariates
model_specification: Binary logit with cubic peace-year splines
controls: polity2DUM, s_un_regDUM, pwrratio, postArt56, postCW, prgmyrs, NCAnosafetodate, contig, noconsideryrs and three peace-year splines
operationalization_notes: DV 'consider' captures salience/serious consideration of strikes on nuclear programs; hostileMID operationalizes prior violent conflict. Controls follow the variables included in the dataset suggestive of the paper's full model.
reasoning: In a logit model of whether a state considered attacking another's nuclear program, prior violent militarized conflict (hostileMID) is a strong positive predictor (b=4.35, z=7.51, p<0.001, N=58,951), consistent with the paper's claim that prior conflict increases the salience of the proliferation threat.

dependent_variable: splinter (binary: county secedes to form a new district)
main_predictor: support_loser (county majority supported the loser in LC5 chair election — proxy for political marginalization)
sample_definition: All county-period observations with non-missing values on outcome, predictor, and controls (N=483)
model_specification: Logistic regression (Logit MLE)
controls: log population, log area, ethnic minority indicator, socioeconomic marginalization index (MARG)
operationalization_notes: Political marginalization operationalized as a county whose constituents supported the loser in the district-level LC5 chairperson election; outcome is the splinter indicator. Controls include geographic/demographic baseline and an orthogonal economic marginalization index to isolate the political dimension.
reasoning: In a logit regression of county-level secession (splinter) on political marginalization (support for LC5 election loser) with controls (log population, log area, ethnic minority status, and the socioeconomic marginalization index MARG), the coefficient on support_loser is positive (b=0.52, z=1.87, p=0.061), indicating that counties whose majority supported the local political loser are more likely to splinter—consistent with the paper's claim that politically marginalized areas are more likely to secede.

dependent_variable: recog1dum (binary: whether state A is recognized by state B in given directed-dyad-year)
main_predictor: nukeduma (state A possesses nuclear weapons, 0/1)
sample_definition: All directed dyad-years with non-missing recognition and nuclear-status data (Gartzke-Jo extension of MID dyadic dataset)
model_specification: Binary logistic regression with standard errors clustered by state A
controls: none (bivariate baseline tied directly to the verbal claim)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether nuclear-capable states attract more diplomatic recognition. recog1dum is the dyadic recognition outcome included in the dataset. A bivariate logit clustered on the recognized state is the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: Logit of dyadic recognition indicator (recog1dum: state A recognized by state B in year t) on state A's nuclear status (nukeduma) yields a positive, highly significant coefficient (b=1.57, cluster-robust z=5.48, p<.001), indicating nuclear-armed states are substantially more likely to be diplomatically recognized.

dependent_variable: Count of immigration-related survey items (out of 20) for which the participant's response changed between Wave 1 (pre) and Wave 3 (post-deliberation)
main_predictor: jlev_max — participant's maximum DQI level of justification observed in small-group speech acts (0=no justification ... 4=sophisticated justification linked to common good)
sample_definition: EuroPolis participants with both pre/post survey responses and at least one coded speech act (N=180)
model_specification: OLS linear regression: n_changes ~ const + jlev_max
operationalization_notes: The claim ties speech-level rational justification to participant-level opinion change. I summed the number of changed pre/post responses across the 20 immigration-related items in the survey (treating 997/998/999 as missing) and used the maximum DQI justification level reached by the participant as the index of 'rational justification used'.
reasoning: OLS regression of the number of immigration-related opinion items that a participant changed between Wave 1 (pre) and Wave 3 (post-deliberation) on the participant's maximum justification level (jlev_max, 0-4 DQI scale) yields a small NEGATIVE and non-significant coefficient (b=-0.31, t(178)=-1.40, p=0.16, N=180). Thus in these data, higher-quality rational justification by a participant is not associated with more frequent opinion change; the claim does not reproduce.

dependent_variable: Average effort (binary 'work' decision) per group, aggregated across all periods
main_predictor: Reward scheme: discriminating (345COM) vs. symmetric (444COM)
sample_definition: Only complementarity-technology treatments (345COM and 444COM); all periods included; aggregated to group (mg) means as the independent unit of observation
model_specification: Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) test on group-level mean effort
operationalization_notes: Effort is operationalized as the binary 'work' decision; groups (matching groups, 'mg') are the independent units to avoid within-group dependence. Non-parametric test chosen since group-level distributions are bounded and small-N.
reasoning: Group-level average effort (work) was higher under the discriminating reward scheme 345COM (mean 0.917, n=12 groups) than under the symmetric scheme 444COM (mean 0.722, n=11 groups). Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test yields z=1.78, p=0.074, consistent with the direction claimed by the authors (symmetric < discriminating under complementarity), though only marginally significant.

dependent_variable: Use of anti-immigration framing in the explanation (companti_anti vs. companti_pro), paired within senator
main_predictor: Audience type (anti-immigration vs. pro-immigration constituent letter)
sample_definition: Senators who responded to both the pro- and anti-immigration constituent letters (N=56 senator pairs)
model_specification: McNemar's chi-squared test (paired binary outcome)
operationalization_notes: The 'tailoring' claim implies within-senator differences in explanation content across audience types. A paired McNemar test on whether anti-tone framing was used is the most direct test. The pro-tone counterpart (comppro) trends the same direction (b=7,c=1, p=.07).
reasoning: McNemar's test on the paired indicator of whether each senator used anti-immigration framing in their explanation to the anti-immigration constituent versus the pro-immigration constituent shows a significant within-senator discordance (b=8 used anti-tone only to the anti-audience, c=1 used it only to the pro-audience; chi2=5.44, df=1, p≈0.02). Senators systematically tailor explanation content to the audience.

dependent_variable: Log wage gain at migration: log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted)
main_predictor: Education group: less than high school (edyrs<=8) vs. college degree (edyrs>=16)
sample_definition: All MMP/LAMP migrants in the wage_gain_table with non-missing pre- and post-migration adjusted wages and years of schooling; restricted to the two extreme education groups
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test of the mean log wage gain between the two education groups
operationalization_notes: The NIS restricted folder is empty in the archive, so I used the mmp_lamp wage_gain_table.xlsx, which provides matched pre-/post-migration wages used in the paper's robustness analyses. Education groups operationalized as edyrs<=8 ('never been to high school') vs. edyrs>=16 ('college degree').
reasoning: Using the MMP/LAMP wage-gain microdata (the only pre-/post-migration wage data available in the replication archive; NIS is restricted), I computed log(US adjusted wage) - log(home adjusted wage) for each migrant. Immigrants with no high-school exposure (edyrs<=8, n=1594) have a mean log wage gain of 0.858, significantly larger than that of college graduates (edyrs>=16, n=152) at 0.597 (Welch t=2.16, df≈184, p=0.032). This matches the paper's claim that wage gains at migration decline with education.

dependent_variable: Percent negative meaning in free associations (FAbaseC vs FAsuppC)
main_predictor: Item condition (baseline vs suppress), within-subjects
sample_definition: Nonruminators (Group=1), N=27, from Experiment 2 free-association transfer task
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing FAbaseC vs FAsuppC within nonruminators
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the indirect transfer task in nonruminators, where suppression should reduce expression of the trained (negative) meaning. The relevant comparison is baseline (learned, not suppressed) vs suppress within the nonruminator subsample.
reasoning: Among nonruminators (N=27), the percent of negative-meaning free associations was higher for baseline cues (M=45.68) than for suppressed cues (M=29.63), paired t(26)=3.03, p=.005, indicating that suppression practice reduced the originally learned meaning — a beneficial suppression-induced forgetting effect on the indirect transfer test. Ruminators showed no such effect (t(26)=-0.41, p=.68).

dependent_variable: wellbeing (shortened CES-D composite, higher = better wellbeing)
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction: childless (1=childless vs. 0=parent) × country-level standardized disapproval of childlessness (childless_disapp_std)
sample_definition: ESS3 respondents aged >40 in 24 European countries with non-missing wellbeing, parental status, country-level norms, and individual controls (N=25,096)
model_specification: Linear mixed-effects model with random intercept for country (statsmodels MixedLM, REML)
controls: Age, age squared, marital status (4 cat.), education (4 cat.), parents' education (5 cat.), religious attendance, gender
operationalization_notes: Childless coded as par_stat=='Childless' (parents = empty nest + living-with-children combined). Country-level tolerance operationalized using the precomputed childless_disapp_std variable (higher = more disapproval/less tolerance). Claim corresponds to the cross-level interaction term.
reasoning: In a country-clustered multilevel regression of psychological well-being on a childless dummy, country-level standardized disapproval of childlessness, their cross-level interaction, and individual controls, the interaction childless × childless_disapp_std = -0.032 (z = -3.03, p = .002, N = 25,096 in 24 countries). Because higher wellbeing scores indicate better wellbeing and higher disapp scores indicate less tolerance, the negative interaction means the childless disadvantage grows as countries become less tolerant — equivalently, the disadvantage is smaller in more tolerant countries, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: DSM5_Total (total psychopathology symptom score)
main_predictor: MiniK_Total (life history strategy; higher = slower)
sample_definition: All 138 participants with complete data on both measures
model_specification: Bivariate Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: The Mini-K is the standard summary index of LH strategy (higher = slower, lower = faster) and DSM5_Total is the listed total psychopathology score in the codebook; a simple bivariate correlation is the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between Mini-K total (higher = slower LH strategy) and DSM-5 psychopathology total is r = -.587, t(136) = -8.46, p < .001, n = 138. Lower Mini-K (faster LH) is strongly associated with more psychopathology symptoms, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (political knowledge test score)
main_predictor: Stereotypaktivierung condition (0=not activated vs 2=activated by gender difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender_alle=1) in conditions 0 or 2
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test
operationalization_notes: Claim compares female participants in condition 1 (stereotype not activated) vs condition 3 (gender difference statement) on political knowledge; used the precomputed PolWis_score.
reasoning: Among female participants, the mean political knowledge score in the stereotype-not-activated condition (M=8.38, n=79) was higher than in the stereotype-activated-by-gender-difference-statement condition (M=7.17, n=81); Welch's t(154.18)=1.69, p=.093. The direction matches the claim, though only marginally significant.

dependent_variable: f2gdpidx (two-year-ahead annual GDP growth index of the city)
main_predictor: msec2currentsec (binary: city party secretary has informal/career tie to the incumbent provincial party secretary)
sample_definition: Chinese prefecture-city-year panel, all city-years with non-missing two-year-ahead GDP growth and tie indicator (1999-2011)
model_specification: OLS with city fixed effects and province-by-year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by city (PanelOLS)
controls: None beyond city FE and province-year FE
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether informal ties between a city leader and the incumbent provincial leader translate into faster growth. The most direct test is to regress city growth on the tie indicator while absorbing time-invariant city characteristics (city FE) and province-wide shocks/leader changes each year (province-year FE), using forward-looking growth (f2gdpidx) to allow effects to materialize.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects regression of two-year-ahead city GDP growth (f2gdpidx) on a binary indicator for whether the municipal party secretary has an informal tie to the incumbent provincial party secretary (msec2currentsec), with city and province-year fixed effects and standard errors clustered by city, the coefficient is positive (b=0.198) but not statistically significant (t=1.33, p=0.18, N=4321). The direction matches the paper's claim that connected city leaders deliver faster growth, but the estimate is not significant under this specification.

dependent_variable: Ability classification of foreign players in Denmark (top vs low ability, from stop/slow counts)
main_predictor: Period: pre-reform (1980-1990) vs post-reform (1991-2008) Danish preferential foreigner tax scheme
sample_definition: All foreign players in the Danish top division 1980-2008 (from basesynthetic_control.dta, country=='dnk')
model_specification: 2x2 Pearson chi-square test of independence between reform period and player ability category
operationalization_notes: The synthetic-control dataset provides annual counts of top-ability (stop) and low-ability (slow) foreigners in Denmark. The claim is directly tested by comparing the ability mix of foreigners before vs after the 1991 special tax scheme for foreigners.
reasoning: Pooling foreign-player counts in Denmark before (1980-1990) and after (1991-2008) the preferential tax scheme, the share of top-ability foreigners rose from 7/45 (15.6%) to 195/364 (53.6%). A 2x2 chi-square test of association between period (pre vs post reform) and ability (top vs low) yields chi2(1)=23.16, p≈1.5e-06, confirming a significant shift in the ability composition of foreigners toward higher-ability players.

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay (composite)
main_predictor: intrin_extrin (intrinsic minus extrinsic value score)
sample_definition: Study 1 dataset; all participants with complete data on the two variables
model_specification: Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: Claim is a bivariate association; used the precomputed intrinsic-vs-extrinsic difference score and the willingness-to-pay composite already in the SPSS file.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between the intrinsic-minus-extrinsic value score and willingness to pay to protect the environment is r=.43, p<.001, N=155, confirming that higher relative endorsement of intrinsic values is associated with greater willingness to pay.

dependent_variable: ln(product-level imports from partner)
main_predictor: interaction of post-dispute indicator (counter>0) with complainant dummy
sample_definition: All product-respondent-partner-year observations within the ±5 year dispute window, restricted to disputes resolved by early settlement (earlysettle=1) and to partners that are either complainants or non-participants; year-of-dispute (counter=0) observations dropped.
model_specification: OLS DiD: ln_imports ~ post + complainant + post*complainant + dispute fixed effects; SEs clustered by dispute.
operationalization_notes: The claim is that early/private settlements produce discriminatory gains for complainants relative to the WTO membership. The cleanest test is a DiD comparing pre vs post imports for complainants vs non-participants within early-settled disputes; the coefficient on post*complainant captures the discriminatory premium.
reasoning: In a difference-in-differences OLS of ln(imports) on post × complainant (with dispute fixed effects, SEs clustered by dispute), restricted to early-settled disputes and to complainant/nonparticipant observations, the interaction term is positive (b = 0.327) — i.e., complainants' imports rise more after early settlement than non-participants', consistent with the paper's directional claim — but it is only marginally significant (t ≈ 1.76, p ≈ 0.08, N = 10,564), so on this operationalization the discriminatory-gain claim does not reach conventional significance.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (new business formation rate, country-year)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of working-age population)
sample_definition: All country-year observations in GEM_Country_Year.dta with non-missing dependent variable, predictor, and weight (N=393, 82 countries, 2001-2010)
model_specification: WLS with year fixed effects, weighted by nobs_cy, cluster-robust SEs by countryid
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 2 Col. 3 specification implied by data archive: country-year panel, GEM new-business-formation rate regressed on median age with year FE, weighted by sample size and clustered by country.
reasoning: Weighted regression (by survey N) of country-year new-business-formation rate (entre_wage) on median age (20-64) with year fixed effects and SEs clustered by country yields a coefficient of -0.0073 (t=-5.71, p<0.001, N=393, 82 clusters). Lower median age is significantly associated with higher new business formation, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Perceived arm length (cm)
main_predictor: Arm side (right vs left) — within-subject
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (Handedness=2), n=15
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test (PerceivedRight vs PerceivedLeft)
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns right-handers' perception of own arms; used the raw perceived length values in a within-subject paired t-test, the most direct test of the directional claim.
reasoning: Paired t-test on right-handed participants comparing perceived right vs. left arm length: M_right=69.93 vs M_left=66.31, t(14)=2.38, p=.032. Right arms perceived significantly longer than left arms.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (mean of feeling appreciated, valued, and satisfied; 7-pt scales)
main_predictor: condition (0 = acknowledgment only/verbal; 1 = 5-cent financial acknowledgment)
sample_definition: Participants with exclude=0 (finished the study); N=49
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: Study 1a directly contrasts verbal vs. small financial acknowledgment; used the provided 3-item composite as the outcome and the binary condition as predictor, applying the dataset's own exclusion filter.
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test comparing the verbal acknowledgment (M=5.57) vs. 5-cent financial acknowledgment (M=4.38) conditions on the 3-item appreciation/valued/satisfaction index yielded t(47)=2.92, p=.005, with verbal > financial — consistent with the claimed trivialization effect.

dependent_variable: Standardized total test score (s_tot)
main_predictor: avg5_girl (share of girls among 5 nearest classroom neighbors)
sample_definition: Female students with non-missing s_tot and avg5_girl
model_specification: OLS with classroom (gc) fixed effects; standard errors clustered by classroom
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns surrounding 5 peers' gender composition affecting females' scores; avg5_girl is the natural treatment variable. Restricted to girls. Classroom FEs used given random seat assignment within classrooms.
reasoning: OLS of standardized total score on share of girls among 5 nearest neighbors (avg5_girl) for female students, with classroom fixed effects and SEs clustered by classroom, yields a positive and significant coefficient (b=0.68, z=3.00, p=0.003, N=292). Going from 0 to 1 (5 males to 5 females) raises female test scores, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Time-2 attitude (mean of three attitude items at T2)
main_predictor: Three-way interaction: Time-1 attitude × ambivalence (Griffin formula on pos/neg) × certainty (mean of cert1–cert7)
sample_definition: All participants in Study 1 and Study 2 with complete attitude data at T1 and T2 and complete ambivalence/certainty items (N=588).
model_specification: OLS moderated regression: att_T2 ~ att_T1 * amb * cert, all predictors mean-centered.
controls: none beyond the lower-order terms in the interaction model
operationalization_notes: Attitude stability is operationalized as the T1→T2 slope. The claim implies the slope depends jointly on ambivalence and certainty, which corresponds to the 3-way interaction term. Ambivalence computed with Griffin's index (M-|P-N|); certainty as mean of cert1–7.
reasoning: Pooling Study 1 and Study 2, I regressed Time-2 attitude on Time-1 attitude, ambivalence, certainty, and all interactions (mean-centered). The key 3-way interaction T1×ambivalence×certainty — which tests whether the stability (T1→T2) coefficient depends on the amb×cert combination — was not significant, b=-0.014, t(580)=-1.32, p=.19. Thus the data do not reproduce the claimed ambivalence-by-certainty moderation of attitude stability in this operationalization.

dependent_variable: National electoral turnout (% of registered voters)
main_predictor: logfdistockliab (log of inward FDI stock / foreign ownership of domestic assets)
sample_definition: Country-election observations with non-missing turnout and covariates (24 OECD countries)
model_specification: OLS with country fixed effects and cluster-robust SEs by country
controls: log trade openness, KAOPEN capital openness, log GDP per capita, share of voting-age population 30-69, election closeness, effective number of parties, PR system dummy
operationalization_notes: Foreign ownership operationalized as inward FDI stock (liabilities). Country FE absorb time-invariant heterogeneity; year FE omitted to retain sample (with year FE coefficient is still negative but smaller in magnitude).
reasoning: In a country fixed-effects OLS regression of national electoral turnout on logged FDI stock liabilities (a proxy for foreign ownership) with standard economic and institutional controls, the coefficient on foreign ownership is negative and statistically significant (b=-2.04, t=-2.05, p=0.041, n=262), consistent with the ownership-constraint hypothesis that foreign ownership reduces turnout.

dependent_variable: complaints_2008 (number of service complaints in 2008)
main_predictor: first_A indicator (firm name begins with 'A' or a number)
sample_definition: All 2,293 plumbing firms in final_data.dta with non-missing complaints and first_A
model_specification: Negative binomial regression (count outcome with overdispersion)
operationalization_notes: Claim is a simple group comparison on service complaints; chose NB regression given count outcome with heavy overdispersion. The z-test on the first_A coefficient directly tests the claim.
reasoning: Negative binomial regression of 2008 service complaints on a first_A indicator (name begins with 'A' or a number) yields a positive coefficient of 1.685 (z=6.61, p<0.001). Mean complaints are 1.34 for first_A firms vs 0.25 for others, supporting the claim that A/number-named plumbing firms receive more complaints.

dependent_variable: Cooperativeness of bargaining strategy (dv, 0-3 ordered: 0 veto/blocking, 1 hold position, 2 partial concession, 3 full concession)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure (differential valuation of issues being bargained over)
sample_definition: All 588 state-bargaining-interaction observations in the dataset
model_specification: Ordered logit (proportional odds) model
controls: agreement_importance, voting_power, foreignpolicy, new_ms, qmv, euro, publicity, presidency, lngdp, pillarii, pillariii, parl_scrut, lag_dv
operationalization_notes: The codebook identifies dv as the ordered cooperative-strategy measure and issue_linkage_structure captures the extent to which issues are differently valued. I included all theoretically relevant covariates present in the dataset (power, socialization, and other structural variables) plus the lagged dv that is provided in the file.
reasoning: Ordered logit on cooperative-strategy dv (0-3) with issue_linkage_structure as the main predictor and the paper's listed covariates (power, socialization, structural, and lag_dv) yields a positive, highly significant coefficient (b=1.05, z=13.33, p<0.001, N=588). Greater issue value differentiation is associated with substantially higher probability of offering concessions, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: credittogovtstateenterp (credit directed to government and state-owned enterprises)
main_predictor: icrg_qog (ICRG quality of government; inverse proxy for state weakness)
sample_definition: All country-year observations with non-missing values for DV, predictor, marketpower, country, and year
model_specification: OLS with two-way fixed effects (country and year) and country-clustered standard errors
controls: marketpower (Lerner index proxy for banking profit potential / financial repression), country FE, year FE
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns within-country effects of state weakness on credit allocation to the public sector after controlling for the profit potential implied by financial repression; icrg_qog is the cleanest available state-capacity measure and marketpower is the available profit-potential measure in the country-year file.
reasoning: Regressing credit to government and SOEs (% of total credit) on ICRG quality-of-government (inverse measure of state weakness) while controlling for banking-sector market power and including country and year fixed effects yields a negative coefficient (b=-10.29, t=-1.82, p=0.068, clustered by country, N=1411). Lower state quality (i.e., weaker states) is associated with more credit to government/SOEs, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: dispute (MID with hostility level >=4 begins in year)
main_predictor: llcoupsum (lagged log of cumulative coups, proxy for threat to political survival)
sample_definition: Latin American country-years 1960-1999 in scamerica5.dta with non-missing covariates
model_specification: Binary logistic regression
controls: nborder, CINC, rwar, regconf, llrgdpch, ethfrac, polity2l, lagdisp
operationalization_notes: Abstract emphasizes coup-related threats to leader survival; llcoupsum is the lagged log coup count available in the data. DV chosen as dispute participation to match 'conflict involvement'. The paper uses simultaneous-equations methods; this single-equation logit is a defensible direct test of the bivariate directional claim.
reasoning: In a logit of MID dispute involvement on lagged log of coup history (operationalizing threats to leader survival) plus controls (borders, CINC, regional war, regional conflict, lagged log GDP/cap, ethnic fractionalization, lagged polity2, lagged dispute), the coefficient on llcoupsum is -0.057 with z=-0.29, p=0.77 (N=776). The threat measure is not positively associated with conflict involvement, failing to reproduce the paper's claim in this single-equation specification.

dependent_variable: d12outgroup: amount (0-5) sent to out-group (Albanian) recipient in dictator game
main_predictor: Exposure to out-group, coded 0=primarily Serb region, 1=border region, 2=primarily Albanian region
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb subjects in the replication dataset
model_specification: OLS regression of d12outgroup on ordinal exposure variable
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns bridging (out-group giving) increasing with exposure. The natural exposure gradient in the data is the region variable, which the authors use to capture variation in contact with Albanians. A simple bivariate OLS provides the most direct test.

dependent_variable: Total dollars donated per session (variable 'money', summed across both doors)
main_predictor: Verbal ask (treatments A1+A2) vs silent (M1+M2)
sample_definition: 64 sessions from the 2013 field experiment with bell ringers (treatments A1,A2,M1,M2); 2009 control sessions excluded

operationalization_notes: Claim concerns the verbal-ask manipulation, which was implemented in 2013 across four conditions crossing verbal/silent with one/two-door coverage. Pooling across the door factor isolates the ask effect on per-session donations.
reasoning: Across the 64 sessions of the 2013 verbal-ask experiment, total donations per session were substantially higher under the verbal 'please give' treatment (M=$70.74) than the silent treatment (M=$46.40), Welch t(59.2)=4.82, p≈1.0e-5, confirming that the verbal ask increased giving.

dependent_variable: zakaibag (Bagrut certification indicator)
main_predictor: treated (school-level treatment assignment)

controls: pair FE, lagscore, parental education (educav, educem), ole5 (immigrant), m_ahim (siblings)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the treated 2001 cohort's certification (Bagrut) outcomes for girls; standard specification with matched-pair FE and baseline controls.
reasoning: OLS regression of Bagrut certification (zakaibag) on treatment for girls in the 2001 cohort, with pair fixed effects, lagged score and family background controls, and standard errors clustered by school, yields a treatment effect of 0.086 (t=2.39, p=0.017), indicating a significant rise in certification rates for girls.

dependent_variable: Industry-level US intrafirm import share = sum(imp_rel)/(sum(imp_rel)+sum(imp_non)) over 2000-2011 across all source countries
main_predictor: Downstreamness (downmeasure) interacted with a high-sigma indicator (= 1 - M1sigma, identifying above-median Broda-Weinstein import demand elasticity)
sample_definition: 253 IO2002 industries with non-missing intrafirm trade data, downstreamness measure, sigma classification, and all controls (factor intensities, R&D intensity, dispersion).
model_specification: OLS: share = a + b1·downmeasure + b2·high_sigma + b3·(downmeasure × high_sigma) + controls; test is t-statistic on the interaction term.
controls: log skill/labor (ls_l_0005), log capital/labor (lk_l_0005), log materials/labor (lm_l_0005), log US R&D intensity, and industry dispersion measure (disp1_2000).
operationalization_notes: Aggregated USIOrelatedparty data to the industry level (consistent with the paper's industry-level analysis of intrafirm import shares). M1sigma in the file is a below-median indicator (mean sigma=3.3 when M1sigma=1 vs 15.4 when M1sigma=0), so the high-elasticity dummy is 1-M1sigma. The interaction coefficient captures whether the downstreamness slope is more positive at high sigma, which is precisely the empirical claim.
reasoning: In an industry-level OLS regression of the US intrafirm import share on downstreamness (downmeasure), a high-sigma indicator (above median import demand elasticity), their interaction, and industry controls, the coefficient on downstreamness for low-sigma industries is negative (-0.12), while the interaction term (downstreamness × high-sigma) is positive and significant (b=0.289, t=3.07, p=0.002, N=253). This implies a positive downstreamness-intrafirm share relationship emerges only in high-elasticity (sequential substitutes) industries, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: bid_on_d (PAP bids on a given child case, =1 if bid)
main_predictor: nonaa_girl indicator (vs. baseline non-AA boy)
sample_definition: All PAP-child pairs in ChoicePanel2.dta (full choice panel)
model_specification: Linear probability OLS of bid_on_d on child-type dummies (nonaa_girl, nonaa_unknown, black_girl, black_boy, black_unknown), with constant; SEs clustered by pap_id
controls: Other child race-gender dummies; non-AA boy as omitted baseline
operationalization_notes: Claim is about PAP preferences on the choice-panel; the cleanest direct test is whether the probability of a PAP bidding on a child is higher for non-AA girls than the baseline non-AA boys, and lower for black children, in a single LPM with PAP-clustered SEs.
reasoning: In an OLS linear-probability model of PAP bid on child-type dummies (baseline = non-AA boy) with PAP-clustered SEs, the coefficient on non-AA girl is +0.0141 (z=2.17, p=0.030), indicating PAPs are more likely to bid on non-AA girls than non-AA boys, while all African-American categories have significantly negative coefficients. This supports the claim that AP have a positive preference in favor of non-AA girls.

dependent_variable: a-insensitivity index in part 1: 1 - (m12+m23+m13 - m1-m2-m3)/100
main_predictor: Treatment (tp vs control)
sample_definition: All 104 subjects; subjects with missing matching probabilities (4 in tp group) dropped from index
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test
operationalization_notes: Used Baillon-style a-insensitivity computed from singles and composites in part 1 where the time-pressure manipulation applies; compared between-subjects tp vs control.
reasoning: The a-insensitivity index in part 1 (1 - (sum composite m12+m23+m13 - sum single m1+m2+m3)/100) is significantly higher under time pressure (mean=0.354, n=62) than control (mean=0.150, n=42); Welch t(89.2)=2.30, p=0.024, indicating greater perceived ambiguity under time pressure.

dependent_variable: log(durationmonths) — civil war duration in months
main_predictor: Irregular conflict dummy (technologyrebellion==2 vs. conventional or SNC)
sample_definition: All 147 civil-war episodes in TRdataset_JCR2014_replication_final.dta with non-missing duration and technologyrebellion (N=142)
model_specification: OLS bivariate regression of log-duration on irregular dummy
operationalization_notes: Claim contrasts irregular vs. all other technology-of-rebellion categories. Log-duration used because durationmonths is right-skewed; bivariate spec isolates the directional claim.
reasoning: Regressing log(duration in months) on an irregular-conflict dummy yields a coefficient of 1.17 (t=4.99, df=140, p<0.001, N=142), meaning irregular civil wars last roughly exp(1.17)≈3.2× longer than non-irregular ones, supporting the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: lndrate (log monthly all-cause mortality rate per 100,000)
main_predictor: b10_10 (days with mean temperature >90F) interacted with post-1960 indicator
sample_definition: state-year-month observations 1900-2004 with non-missing lndrate
model_specification: OLS with state, year, and month fixed effects; cluster-robust SEs by state
controls: Other mean-temperature bin counts (b10_1 through b10_9 excluding the omitted reference 50-60F); state, year, month FEs
operationalization_notes: Tested decline in hot-day mortality relationship by an interaction of the >90F-day count with a post-1960 indicator; the t-statistic on the interaction is the most direct single-statistic test of whether the temperature-mortality relationship declined.
reasoning: Regressing log monthly mortality rate on number of days with mean temperature >90F interacted with a post-1960 dummy (with state, year, and month fixed effects, other temperature bins as controls, SE clustered by state), the interaction coefficient is -0.0186 (t=-3.10, p=0.002). The marginal effect of a hot day on mortality fell sharply after 1960 (from +0.0075 to -0.0110 in log-rate units), consistent with the claimed decline.

dependent_variable: notBuy (1=buy DVD, 2=do not buy; coded as 1=not buy for logistic model)
main_predictor: Opportunity-cost cue condition (oppcost: 10 vs 11) × future-self connectedness (ZFINAL composite)
sample_definition: All 88 participants in the DVD study
model_specification: Logistic regression: notBuy ~ oppcost_condition * ZFINAL
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns whether the opportunity-cost cue reduces spending more strongly for those higher in future-self connectedness; tested via the condition × ZFINAL interaction on the binary purchase decision.
reasoning: Logistic regression of not-buying the DVD on opportunity-cost cue (10 vs 11), future-self connectedness (ZFINAL), and their interaction yields a significant positive interaction (b=1.05, z=2.10, p=.036), indicating that the opportunity-cost cue reduces spending (raises probability of declining purchase) more strongly among participants more connected to their future selves.

dependent_variable: REF_female (whether the referred candidate is female)
main_predictor: OP_female (gender of conventional applicant making referral)
sample_definition: Original participants in the 'either gender' (CA / conventional) referral condition with a non-missing referral gender (treat_either==1)
model_specification: Two-sample z-test of proportions (equivalent to Pearson chi-square without continuity correction)
operationalization_notes: Interpreted CA = conventional applicant = the 'either' gender treatment arm with no performance-pay incentive (treat_either==1). Outcome is the probability that the referred person is female.
reasoning: Among CA (treat_either, no gender-specific request, no performance pay constraint) applicants, 22.6% (30/133) of male OPs referred a woman vs 42.5% (37/87) of female OPs. Two-proportion z = -3.15, p = .0016, confirming CA men are significantly less likely than CA women to refer a woman.

dependent_variable: ALI curriculum-based math test standardized score (ali_stdscore)
main_predictor: Treatment 3 (ALI: incentives to students, math teachers, and administrators), with T1 and T2 also included; control group is the omitted category
sample_definition: All students with non-missing ALI test scores in grades 10-12 across years 1-3 of the experiment (115,248 student-test observations across 88 randomized schools)
model_specification: OLS regression of ali_stdscore on treatment dummies (T1, T2, T3) with grade and year fixed effects; cluster-robust standard errors at the school (clavecct) level
controls: Grade fixed effects, year fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Pooled the 9 grade-by-year files released for table 7, harmonizing the ALI standardized score across grades. T3 dummy (dum_treat4) is the focal predictor since the claim concerns the comprehensive ALI package.
reasoning: Pooling all grade-year ALI standardized math scores and regressing on treatment dummies with grade and year fixed effects and cluster-robust SEs at the school level (88 clusters), the T3 (ALI) coefficient is 63.30 (z = 4.05, p < 0.001), indicating a sizeable and statistically significant positive impact of the combined incentive package on test scores, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Log monthly discount rate (interval-censored: lndiscratelo, lndiscratehi) across 4 intertemporal choice types per subject
main_predictor: treatE (ethnic-identity salience prime, 1=primed, 0=control)
sample_definition: Asian-American subjects (raceA==1) in Experiment 1; each contributes up to 4 choice-type observations (stakes x time horizon); observations with both bounds missing dropped
model_specification: Interval (Tobit-style) regression with left-censored and interval-censored observations, controls for largestakes, longterm, and their interaction; standard errors clustered at the subject id level (MLE via scipy)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's baseline pooled specification for Asian subjects (cf. Experiment1_Claims.log footnote 10 regression), which is the most direct single test of whether ethnic-identity priming increases patience among Asian-Americans.
reasoning: Pooled interval regression of log discount rate on the ethnic-identity salience treatment (treatE) for Asian-American subjects yields a treatment coefficient of -1.417 with cluster-robust SE 0.380 (z = -3.73, p ≈ 0.0002). The negative coefficient indicates substantially lower discount rates (more patient choices) when ethnic identity was made salient, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Subject-level mean cooperation frequency (% of seconds cooperating, averaged across all matches within a subject)
main_predictor: Treatment condition: Short-Deterministic (3) vs Short-Stochastic (4)
sample_definition: All subjects in the two short-horizon treatments (conditions 3 and 4) from subjects_data_ready.dta; 48 subjects per condition
model_specification: Two-sided Mann–Whitney U test (normal approximation for z)
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns short-duration treatments only. Used subject as unit of observation to retain independence; aggregated cooperation across the 23 matches per subject. Non-parametric test follows the paper's general style of treatment comparisons.
reasoning: Mann–Whitney U test on subject-level mean cooperation rates comparing Short-Deterministic (n=48, mean=63.3%) vs Short-Stochastic (n=48, mean=52.3%) yields U=1565, z=3.03, p=0.0025. Cooperation is significantly higher under the deterministic horizon, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Plurality party's ideological distance from the median voter (pldist1)
main_predictor: SMD electoral rule (binary: SMD vs. PR)
sample_definition: All 329 elections in the Powell dataset with non-missing smd and pldist1
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test comparing mean plurality distance across SMD vs. non-SMD elections
operationalization_notes: The claim asserts that SMD competition should bring the plurality winner near the median voter. The most direct test is whether the plurality party's distance to the median voter (pldist1) is smaller under SMD than under PR; a simple between-systems t-test on pldist1 isolates this comparison.
reasoning: Comparing the plurality party's distance from the median voter (pldist1) between SMD (n=85, mean=11.40) and non-SMD/PR (n=244, mean=11.07) elections via Welch's t-test yields t(181.04)=0.28, p=0.78. The plurality winner is not closer to the median voter in SMD systems; if anything the distance is marginally (and non-significantly) larger.

dependent_variable: nwar1 (occurrence of a new war after the conflict)
main_predictor: T2fpemths1 (months between civil war end and first postwar election)
sample_definition: All civil-war cases in iDOSERESPONSE_fpebase.dta with complete data on the baseline covariates (N=98)
model_specification: Binary logistic regression (logit) of nwar1 on T2fpemths1 + baseline controls
controls: fpepolity1, postCW, victory, unintrvnALL, UNfpeaid1, cycle2, eventno2 (fintvngwar1 dropped due to no variation in the analysis sample)
operationalization_notes: Used the variables assembled in the authors' baseline dose-response dataset (iDOSERESPONSE_fpebase.dta) because they exactly match the paper's primary specification for the impact of election timing on conflict recurrence. Logit chosen because outcome is binary.
reasoning: In a logistic regression of new war recurrence (nwar1) on the time-to-first-postwar-election (T2fpemths1) with the baseline covariates used in the authors' dose-response specification (post-Cold War, victory, UN intervention, UN election aid, election cycle, event number, FPE polity), the coefficient on election timing is negative (b = -0.0059, z = -1.125, p = 0.26). The direction is consistent with the claim (earlier elections associated with greater renewed-fighting risk), but the effect is not statistically significant, so the claim does not clearly reproduce in this baseline test.

dependent_variable: Perceived femininity (average of items 26 and 33)
main_predictor: Green vs. nongreen consumer behavior condition
sample_definition: All 194 participants in Study 2 (4 between-subjects cells: target gender × green/nongreen)
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test (green vs. nongreen, collapsing across target gender)
operationalization_notes: Each participant rated a single target on 11 trait items; items 26 and 33 clustered together (r≈.70) and showed the pattern expected of feminine-trait ratings (higher for green targets), distinct from masculine-trait items (27/28/32/34) and the apparent eco-friendly manipulation check (item 24). I averaged items 26 and 33 as a femininity index and compared green vs. nongreen targets via a two-sample t-test.
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test comparing perceived femininity (mean of items 26 and 33, which formed a coherent cluster strongly differing by condition) for green (M≈2.84) vs. nongreen (M≈1.76) targets yielded t(192)=8.32, p<.001 — green consumers were perceived as significantly more feminine.

dependent_variable: Number of stochastic-dominance violations in the 10 LV-format decisions per subject
main_predictor: Degree of risk aversion = average number of safe choices in PV and RV formats
sample_definition: All 106 real subjects (subjects with age=99, who were experimenter-controlled stations, excluded)
model_specification: Spearman rank correlation between risk-aversion score and LV error count
operationalization_notes: Operationalization follows the paper's Figure 4: per-subject risk aversion measured as average safe choices in the PV and RV menus; error rate measured as count of LV choices inconsistent with stochastic dominance (dominant choice = RV lottery for decisions 1-4, PV lottery for decisions 5-10). Spearman correlation is the test most directly tied to the directional claim.
reasoning: Across all 106 subjects, the Spearman correlation between degree of risk aversion (average safe choices in PV and RV formats) and number of stochastic-dominance violations in the LV format is r = -0.44 (p ≈ 2e-6). The strongly negative, significant relationship supports the claim that decision error decreases with risk aversion.

dependent_variable: Desired annual compensation (midpoint of reported salary range, in $1000s)
main_predictor: Treatment: public (classmates see responses) vs private (career-services-only)
sample_definition: Main experiment respondents who are female and single, with non-missing desired compensation
model_specification: Two-sample Welch t-test comparing public vs private treatment means
operationalization_notes: Used midpoint of categorical salary range as numeric outcome; identified treatment B as the public condition based on direction implied by the claim (single females reported lower in public). The salary categories were converted to numeric midpoints by averaging the bounds.
reasoning: Among single female MBA students (n=60), those in the public condition (preferences shown to classmates) reported a mean desired compensation of $113.8k vs $130.6k in the private condition, Welch's t(48.6)=-2.17, p=0.035, consistent with the paper's claim that single females lowered desired salaries when classmates would see them.

dependent_variable: pay_for_conditionality / WTP_dummy (parent willing to pay to keep CCT conditionality)
main_predictor: Treatment assignment: baseline (T=1) vs. SMS monitoring (T=2)
sample_definition: Parents in baseline and SMS parent-incentivized treatments (treatment in {1,2}), N=111
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2 contingency table)
operationalization_notes: Claim contrasts SMS treatment vs baseline on the binary willingness-to-pay outcome; used the dataset's WTP_dummy/pay_for_conditionality indicator restricted to those two arms.
reasoning: In the baseline treatment 49/60 (81.7%) parents were willing to pay to keep conditionality, vs. only 10/51 (19.6%) in the SMS treatment. A Pearson chi-square test of independence yields chi2(1)=42.64, p<1e-10, strongly supporting the claim that SMS monitoring reduces willingness to pay for conditionality.

dependent_variable: deaths_total (homicides presumed drug-trafficking-related, CENAPI)
main_predictor: lpub_after06 (1-6 months after leader capture/killing in municipality)
sample_definition: Treated-leader municipalities (aux_treated==1) and control municipalities (aux_control==1); months where deaths_total is non-missing
model_specification: Two-way fixed-effects OLS DiD via iterative within-demeaning by municipality and month, including lpub_after06, lpub_after612, lpub_after12; cluster-robust SE at municipality
controls: Municipality and month fixed effects; longer-horizon post dummies (7-12, >12 months)
operationalization_notes: Short-term effect on DTO-related violence is captured by lpub_after06 in the canonical DiD specification suggested by the dataset's structure (treated/control flags and 6/12/12+ month post dummies). Lieutenant variables omitted to isolate leader-removal short-term effect.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects (municipality + month) difference-in-differences using treated-leader and control municipalities, the dummy for 1-6 months after a leader capture has a positive, significant effect on DTO-related homicides (coef=10.53, cluster-robust SE=4.79, z=2.20, p=0.028, N=104,027 with 2,123 municipality clusters). This supports the paper's claim that leader removals exacerbate DTO-related violence in the short term.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of the group semantic network (lower = more interconnected)
main_predictor: High vs. low openness to experience (median split on composite of NEO-FFI Openness and BFAS Openness/Intellect)
sample_definition: All 516 adults with verbal fluency data; bootstrap subsamples of 200 participants per group, 200 iterations
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test on bootstrap distributions of group-level ASPL; networks were built from co-occurrence of animal responses in participants' fluency lists (edge if co-listed by >=2 participants), restricted to the 224 animals listed in both groups so node sets were equated
controls: None (groups equated on node set and subsample size)
operationalization_notes: Used common-node co-occurrence networks (standard fair comparison when group sizes/vocabulary differ) and ASPL as the canonical 'interconnectedness' measure (shorter paths => more interconnected). Composite openness used ranks of both openness measures to ensure both NEO and BFAS contributed equally.
reasoning: Bootstrapped (n=200 iterations; 200 participants each) semantic networks restricted to nodes shared by both groups yielded a mean ASPL of 1.756 for the high-openness group and 1.770 for the low-openness group; the difference was significant (t(398) = -13.14, p < .001). Shorter average path length indicates the high-openness network is more interconnected, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Rights index (ciri_physint)
main_predictor: tax_rev_new (tax revenue as % of GDP)
sample_definition: All country-years with non-missing values on all included variables
model_specification: OLS regression with lagged dependent variable
controls: tot_rev_new, lagged ciri_physint, log_pop, income, p_democ, extconf, intconf, ukcol, r_elf85, lp_catho80, lp_muslim80
operationalization_notes: Used the headline CIRI physical integrity index as outcome and tax_rev_new as main predictor, including the paper's other listed covariates and lagged DV as a standard dynamic specification.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of CIRI physical integrity rights on tax revenue (% of GDP) controlling for total revenue, lagged DV, population, income, democracy, conflicts, colonial history, ethnic fractionalization, and religion, tax reliance has a positive, statistically significant coefficient (b=0.0065, t=3.12, p=0.002, N=1739). This supports the claim that higher reliance on taxes is associated with better human rights protection.

dependent_variable: pt_gcse_5_a_c (% of pupils with 5+ GCSEs at grades A*-C)
main_predictor: gm_win (indicator for parental ballot in favor of GM status)
sample_definition: School-year observations from schools that held a GM ballot, restricted to post-ballot years and vote share within 20 percentage points of the 50% threshold
model_specification: Sharp RD: WLS local linear regression with triangular kernel weights, including running variable (vote-50), its interaction with gm_win, baseline pre-vote GCSE pass rate, and year fixed effects; cluster-robust SEs at school level
controls: Baseline (pre-vote) pass rate, year fixed effects, linear running variable on each side
operationalization_notes: Used main_data.dta; 'vote' is vote share in %, threshold=50. Restricted to post-ballot school-years to capture treatment effect on achievement after GM conversion.
reasoning: In a sharp RD comparing GCSE pass rates (% 5+ A-C) of schools that narrowly won vs. narrowly lost their grant-maintained ballot (vote within 20 pts of 50%, triangular kernel, post-ballot years), winning the vote is associated with a +2.77 percentage-point gain in the 5+A-C GCSE pass rate (t=1.73, p=0.08, cluster-robust SEs over 286 schools, N=2934). The estimate is positive and economically sizeable, broadly consistent with the paper's claim of large achievement gains from GM conversion, though only marginally significant in this specification.

dependent_variable: Participated (lab) (0/1)
main_predictor: Sent_Class (amount sent in classroom trust game, 0-10)
sample_definition: All subjects with non-missing Sent_Class and Participated (lab) values
model_specification: Logistic regression (Logit) of Participated on Sent_Class with constant
operationalization_notes: Claim links trust-game sending behavior (measured in the classroom) to subsequent lab participation; simplest bivariate logit captures the directional association most directly.
reasoning: Logistic regression of lab participation on amount sent in the classroom trust game yields a negative, statistically significant coefficient (b=-0.045, z=-2.50, p=0.013, n=658). Subjects who sent less in the trust game were more likely to show up to the lab, replicating the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: took_act (indicator: patient took an ACT antimalarial for the illness episode)
main_predictor: act40 indicator (very high subsidy: price 40 Ksh), with act500/no-subsidy as omitted category
sample_definition: All illness episodes in ACT_IllLvlMainWithMalProbs with non-missing treatment-arm and outcome data (N=6919); included act40, act60, act100, and act500 households
model_specification: Linear probability model: took_act ~ act40 + act60 + act100 (act500 omitted) with constant; cluster-robust SEs at household level
controls: None beyond treatment-arm dummies (strata dummies dropped due to collinearity); intent-to-treat
operationalization_notes: act40 corresponds to ~92% subsidy (highest subsidy arm), interpreted as the 'very high subsidy' in the claim; took_act operationalizes 'access to antimalarials.' Reported z is for the act40 coefficient vs act500.
reasoning: Among illness episodes, taking an ACT antimalarial (took_act) was 14.3 percentage points higher in the very-high-subsidy arm (price = 40 Ksh, ~92% subsidy) than in the unsubsidized control arm (price = 500 Ksh), with cluster-robust z = 5.13 (p < 0.001), supporting the claim that a very high subsidy dramatically increases access.

dependent_variable: Two-year change in combined PIAT math + reading standardized scores (piamatsn + piarersn)
main_predictor: Two-year change in real total family income (earnincrsimp + unearnincrsimp + nontaxincrsimp), in thousands of dollars
sample_definition: Child-year observations with non-missing PIAT math and reading scores and a valid 2-year lag of the same child (i.e., consecutive biennial test waves)
model_specification: Within-child first-differences OLS regression with cluster-robust standard errors at the child level
controls: None beyond the within-child differencing (which absorbs child fixed effects and any time-invariant family characteristics)
operationalization_notes: Without access to the paper's methods I could not identify the simulated-EITC instrument among the data's many constructed variables, so I committed to the reduced-form/OLS first-difference analogue of the paper's IV specification. This directly tests whether short-run income changes are positively associated with short-run test-score changes, but does not address the endogeneity the paper's IV is meant to correct.
reasoning: Using first-differences OLS of the child's combined math+reading score change on the change in total family income (in $1000s) over a 2-year interval, the estimated coefficient is 0.00063 SD per $1,000 (cluster-robust SE = 0.00084, t = 0.75, p = 0.45, n = 16,060). The point estimate is far below the paper's claimed 6% of an SD per $1,000 and is statistically indistinguishable from zero, so the short-run income effect on test scores does not reproduce in a simple FD specification.

dependent_variable: engwkabs (work absorption)
main_predictor: singchild1 (single & childless vs. all other family structures)
sample_definition: Study 1 employed alumni respondents (filter_$ = 1) with complete data on absorption, predictor, and controls (N = 353)
model_specification: OLS linear regression; t-test on singchild1 coefficient
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns a directional difference in absorption between single-childless workers and others; used the provided single-childless indicator and absorption scale with standard demographic controls.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of absorption on a single-childless indicator (controlling for gender, age, and job position) on Study 1's employed sample, the single-childless coefficient is -0.311 (t(348) = -2.36, p = .019), indicating single childless workers report significantly lower absorption than others.

dependent_variable: ProperName (greeted by applicant's name, 0/1)
main_predictor: Sender race (Hispanic vs. white) from TreatmentGroup
sample_definition: Emails sent by Hispanic or white aliases with non-missing ProperName outcome (i.e., responses received)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2 contingency table)
operationalization_notes: Claim compares Hispanic vs white on being greeted by name; ProperName is the appropriate outcome. Excluded black senders and non-respondents (where ProperName is undefined).
reasoning: Among responded emails (with non-missing ProperName), 41.2% of Hispanic-sender emails were greeted by name vs. 61.1% of white-sender emails. Chi-square test of independence: χ²(1, N=362)=14.42, p<.001, confirming Hispanic applicants were significantly less likely to be greeted by name than whites.

dependent_variable: qualityc (quality delivered by seller; lower = more shading)
main_predictor: contracttypec (1 = rigid/fixed-price, 2 = flexible)
sample_definition: All transactions where the contract was realized (contractrealizedc==1); pooled across conditions 1, 3, and 4
model_specification: Mann-Whitney U test (one-sided: rigid > flexible quality), normal approximation for z
operationalization_notes: Quality is the natural measure of shading in this dataset (range 1-2 given trade). Restricted to trades because untraded contracts (-1) do not provide a shading observation. Non-parametric test follows the paper's typical comparison style.
reasoning: Conditional on the contract being executed (trade occurred), average quality is higher under rigid contracts (mean 1.91, n=765) than under flexible contracts (mean 1.78, n=1508).
