sample_definition: All PAP-BMO panel observations in ChoicePanel2.dta with non-missing covariates (N=1,444,870)
model_specification: Probit of bid_on_d on race/gender category dummies, already-born indicator, months-to-birth, log finalization cost, PAP-type dummies (single/gay/lesbian; straight is reference), and year fixed effects
controls: already_born_d, month_to_birth, log finalization cost, black_girl, black_boy, black_unknown, nonaa_boy, race_hispanic, full_single, full_gay, full_lesbian, year FE
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 5 column 1 specification on ChoicePanel2.dta. I did not impose the paper's 10-day activity-window filter because it was not unambiguously identifiable in the data; the qualitative test of the claim (sign and significance of nonaa_girl) is unaffected.
reasoning: Probit of bid_on_d on BMO attribute dummies (with reference category = Caucasian unknown gender) yields a positive and highly significant coefficient on Non-African-American girl (coef=0.193, z=31.3, p<0.001), indicating PAPs are more likely to apply to a non-African American girl BMO than to the reference group — same direction as the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: a-insensitivity index a = 3*(1/3 - (mean composite mp - mean single mp)) computed from Part 1 matching probabilities
main_predictor: Treatment (TP vs control)
sample_definition: All 104 subjects, using Part 1 only (the part where TP treatment imposed time pressure)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test comparing Part 1 a-index between TP and control groups
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns greater insensitivity under TP. The cleanest test is the between-subject comparison of the a-insensitivity index in Part 1 (where the TP manipulation occurs). This corresponds to the 'Part 1 * TP treatment' coefficient in Table V of the paper.
reasoning: Mean a-insensitivity index in Part 1 is 0.353 under TP (n=62) vs 0.150 under control (n=42); Welch's t-test gives t=2.30, p=0.024, confirming greater a-insensitivity under time pressure.

dependent_variable: Civil war duration in months (durationmonths)
main_predictor: Conflict technology of rebellion type (Irregular [reference] vs Conventional vs SNC)
sample_definition: All civil wars in the Balcells-Kalyvas TR dataset with non-missing duration and conflict-type codes (N=142; 76 irregular, 50 conventional, 16 SNC)
model_specification: Weibull accelerated-failure-time (AFT) regression with all events observed; joint Wald test that the Conventional and SNC AFT coefficients both equal zero
controls: none (bivariate specification, matching Model 1 in the paper's duration table)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether irregular wars last longer than every other type. Following the paper's duration analysis, I fit a Weibull AFT with conflict-type dummies (irregular as base) and performed a joint Wald test on the two non-irregular dummies, which most directly tests whether irregular is longer than the others.
reasoning: In a Weibull AFT model on civil-war duration (months) with irregular as the reference category, both Conventional (β=-1.08, SE=0.21) and SNC (β=-0.85, SE=0.31) wars have significantly shorter durations than Irregular wars. A joint Wald test that the Conventional and SNC AFT coefficients are zero yields χ²(2)=29.31, p<.001 (N=142), confirming that irregular conflicts last longer than both other types.

dependent_variable: Log monthly death rate (lndrate)
main_predictor: Days above 90°F (b10_10) interacted with post-1959 indicator
sample_definition: U.S. state-month observations, 1930-2004, non-missing log death rate (N=43,464; 49 states)
model_specification: Weighted (by total population) two-way fixed-effects linear regression with state and year-month fixed effects, cluster-robust SE at state level; test on hot × post-1959 interaction coefficient
controls: Population age shares (sh_0000, sh_4564, sh_6599), log real per-capita income (lri), state FE, year-month FE
operationalization_notes: Followed the spirit of Table 4's baseline contrast (1931-59 vs 1960-2004), but pooled the two periods into a single regression and tested the difference directly via an interaction term, providing one t-statistic for the decline.
reasoning: In a state-month panel (1931-2004), the interaction between days above 90°F and a post-1959 indicator is -0.0217 (cluster-robust SE 0.0044, t=-4.92, p<0.001), while the pre-1960 main effect of hot days on the log death rate is +0.0206. This indicates the temperature-mortality relationship declined sharply across the twentieth century, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Choice to buy DVD (1=buy, 0=do not buy)
main_predictor: Opportunity-cost reminder (0/1) × ZFINAL (z-scored future-self connectedness composite)
sample_definition: All study participants with non-missing connectedness, opportunity-cost condition, and choice (N=88)
model_specification: Logistic regression: buy ~ oppcost + ZFINAL + oppcost*ZFINAL
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's described DV (choice) and used the provided composite z-score of the two connectedness measures (ZFINAL); interaction term operationalizes 'primarily when more connected'.
reasoning: Logistic regression of buying decision on opportunity-cost reminder, future-self connectedness, and their interaction yields a significant negative interaction (z=-2.10, p=.036, N=88): the opportunity-cost cue reduces the probability of purchase more strongly among participants with higher future-self connectedness, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: REF_female (referral is female, 0/1)
main_predictor: OP_female (CA is female, 0/1)
sample_definition: Conventional applicants in the either-gender treatment who made a referral (n=220)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 table
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns free choice of referral gender, which is identified in the either-gender treatment. Compare proportion referring a woman between male and female CAs.
reasoning: In the either-gender treatment among CAs who made a referral, male CAs referred a woman 22.6% of the time (30/133) vs. female CAs 42.5% (37/87). Pearson chi-square = 9.91, df=1, p=0.0016, confirming CA men are significantly less likely to refer women than CA women.

dependent_variable: Cheating-adjusted ALI mathematics score in 10th grade, year 1 (ali_stdscore_gr10)
main_predictor: T3 treatment indicator (incentives to students, teachers, and administrators) vs. control; T1 and T2 dummies also included
sample_definition: 10th-grade students in year 1 of the ALI experiment with non-missing adjusted ALI score, baseline 9th-grade ENLACE scores, and gender (n=11,053 across 86 schools)
model_specification: OLS with three treatment dummies (T1, T2, T3), school-clustered standard errors
controls: Baseline 9th-grade ENLACE math and language scores, student gender, region dummies
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 7 design from the paper: the test most directly tied to the claim about ALI (T3) effects on test scores is the T3 coefficient in a regression of adjusted scores on treatment indicators with baseline controls and school-clustered SEs. Chose the 10th-grade year 1 cohort as the primary specification.
reasoning: Regressing the cheating-adjusted ALI math test score on treatment dummies with baseline ENLACE math/language, gender and region controls (school-clustered SEs, 86 schools) yields a T3 effect of +43.4 points (t=4.27, p<.0001) — a large positive, highly significant effect of the ALI T3 (students + teachers + administrators) treatment on test scores, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Fraction of impatient choices (chose smaller-sooner over larger-later) across the four intertemporal choice tasks
main_predictor: Ethnic-identity salience treatment (treatE: 1 = ethnic-identity prime, 0 = control)
sample_definition: Experiment 1 participants of Asian descent (raceA==1)
model_specification: Two-sample t-test with equal variances comparing mean 'impatient' between treatE groups
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether making ethnic identity salient leads Asian-Americans to make more patient choices. The most direct test is a between-subjects comparison of the impatience rate among Asian subjects across the identity-prime vs. control condition (matching the Table 1 comparison).
reasoning: Among Asian-American subjects (n=71), the control group made impatient choices 26.4% of the time vs 12.6% in the ethnic-identity-salience treatment; a two-sample t-test gives t(69)=3.43, p=.001, indicating that priming ethnic identity made Asians significantly more patient.

dependent_variable: Subject-level mean cooperation rate (coop_frequency averaged across matches)
main_predictor: Termination rule (deterministic vs stochastic) within short-horizon treatments (tmnt=3 vs tmnt=4)
sample_definition: All 96 subjects in the short-horizon treatments (tmnt 3 and 4) from subjects_data_ready.dta
model_specification: Mann-Whitney U (Wilcoxon rank-sum) test, two-sided
operationalization_notes: Paper's Table 1 reports median comparisons with nonparametric significance markers between deterministic and stochastic short treatments; rank-sum on subject-level coop rates is the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: Mann-Whitney rank-sum test on subject-level mean cooperation rates: short-deterministic (n=48, mean=63.3) vs short-stochastic (n=48, mean=52.3). U=1565, p=0.0025 (two-sided); approx z≈3.02. Cooperation is significantly higher under the deterministic short horizon, replicating the paper.

dependent_variable: Plurality party's ideological distance from the median voter (pldist1)
main_predictor: Electoral system type (SMD vs PR), variable smd
sample_definition: All elections in the manifesto data set with non-missing plurality-distance and electoral-system codes (85 SMD and 244 PR elections, 1946-2003)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test of mean plurality-median distance, SMD vs PR
operationalization_notes: The claim that SMD competition makes the plurality winner close to the median voter is most directly tested by comparing the plurality party's distance from the median voter under SMD vs the natural comparator, PR. pldist1 is the variable that directly captures this distance in the original manifesto data.
reasoning: The plurality party's distance from the median voter is essentially the same in SMD systems (mean=11.40, n=85) as in PR systems (mean=11.07, n=244); Welch's t=0.28, p=0.78. The Downsian prediction that SMD competition should bring the plurality winner especially close to the median voter is not supported as a distinctive SMD effect in the manifesto data.

dependent_variable: nwar1 (renewed civil war following the first post-conflict election)
main_predictor: T2fpemths1 (months between end of civil war and first post-conflict election; 'Election timing')
sample_definition: Civil-war endings in BS09_DATA_main.dta with a first post-conflict election (fENDinELECTION1==1) and complete data on all covariates (N=98).
model_specification: Binary logistic regression (logit)
controls: FPE level (national), FPE level (concurrent), Polity IV at FPE, post-Cold War era, victory, UN intervention, UN electoral assistance, previous civil wars in last 10 years
operationalization_notes: Replicates the baseline model in Table 1, column 1 (the simplest specification corresponding to the verbal claim). The sample size of 98 matches the paper exactly; coefficient sign matches but, like column 1 in the paper, the baseline estimate of election timing is not statistically significant.
reasoning: In a logit of renewed civil war (nwar1) on time-to-first-post-conflict election (T2fpemths1) with the controls listed in Table 1, column 1 (FPE level national/concurrent, Polity, post-Cold War, victory, UN intervention, UN electoral assistance, previous civil wars), restricted to the 98 civil-war endings that held a first post-conflict election, the coefficient on election timing is -0.0052 (SE 0.0049), z = -1.07, p = 0.28. The direction matches the paper's claim that earlier elections raise the probability of renewed war, but the effect is not statistically significant in this baseline specification.

dependent_variable: Femininity index (mean of three feminine trait ratings of the target, items 25, 26, 33)
main_predictor: Target's environmental behavior (green vs. nongreen)
sample_definition: All Study 2 participants who rated one of the four targets (N=194)
model_specification: 2x2 between-subjects ANOVA (green x target gender) with Type II sums of squares; main effect of green tested
controls: Target gender included as factor; interaction included in model
operationalization_notes: Identified the three feminine items (25, 26, 33) by matching the paper's reported cell means, SDs, and Cronbach's alpha (.80) for the femininity index; ran the 2x2 ANOVA described in Study 2.
reasoning: In a 2 (green vs. nongreen target) x 2 (target gender) ANOVA on the femininity index (mean of the three feminine traits, α≈.80), the green target was rated significantly more feminine (M=2.64, SD=.90, N=94) than the nongreen target (M=1.82, SD=.86, N=100); F(1,190)=43.59, p<.001. This reproduces the paper's reported effect (F(1,190)=44.00).

dependent_variable: Error rate in LV format (fraction of 10 dominance choices where the dominated lottery was selected)
main_predictor: Degree of risk aversion = average number of safe choices across PV and RV MPL formats
sample_definition: All non-experimenter subjects (excluding age==99) classified as risk averse (avg safe choices in PV and RV ≥ 5); N = 79
model_specification: Pearson correlation between LV error rate and average safe choices; reported as t-test of correlation
operationalization_notes: Following the paper's Fig. 4 description: error rate computed from LV choices treating RV lottery as dominant in decisions 1-4 and PV lottery as dominant in decisions 5-10. Risk aversion measured as the across-format mean number of safe choices. Risk-averse restriction (avg ≥ 5) matches the paper's restricted sample of 79.
reasoning: Among the 79 risk-averse subjects (averaging ≥5 safe choices across PV and RV formats), the Pearson correlation between the LV-format error rate (proportion of dominated-lottery choices) and degree of risk aversion (average safe choices in PV/RV) is r = -0.443, t(77) = -4.33, p < 0.0001. Decision error decreases significantly with risk aversion, replicating the paper's main finding.

dependent_variable: Desired annual compensation (midpoint of selected $25k range, in thousands USD)
main_predictor: Public vs. private treatment assignment (whether classmates would see answers)
sample_definition: Single female respondents to the main experiment questionnaire with parseable compensation responses (n=60: 31 private, 29 public)
model_specification: Two-sample independent t-test (equal variances), public vs. private
operationalization_notes: desiredcompensation was given as $25k bins; I used bin midpoints (and 62.5 for '<75', 275 for 'Above 250'/'>250'); ambiguous/very-wide ranges were dropped. Treatment A corresponds to the private condition and B to the public condition, identified by matching the paper's reported private-treatment mean of ~$131k for single women.
reasoning: Among single female MBA students, those in the public treatment (B, classmates would see answers) reported a mean desired compensation of $112.9k vs $131.5k in the private treatment (A), a difference of about $18.5k. A two-sample t-test (equal variances) yields t(58)=-2.17, p=0.034, supporting the paper's claim that single women reported lower desired salaries under public observability.

dependent_variable: pay_for_conditionality (1 = parent willing to pay any positive amount to keep CCT conditionality)
main_predictor: treatment assignment: baseline (1) vs text-message (4)
sample_definition: Parents assigned to baseline or text-message treatment arms; don't-tell and other arms excluded.
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 contingency table (treatment x pay_for_conditionality)
operationalization_notes: Claim compares text-message arm vs baseline on proportion of parents willing to pay to keep conditionality. The binary outcome pay_for_conditionality directly matches; treatment codes identified by sample sizes matching Table 3 (baseline N=60, text message N=47).
reasoning: Among parents in the baseline (N=60) and text-message (N=47) treatments, 81.7% vs 17.0% were willing to pay to keep the conditionality. A Pearson chi-square test of independence yields chi2(1)=44.24, p<1e-10, confirming a large and highly significant drop in willingness to pay to keep the conditionality under the text-message monitoring condition.

dependent_variable: deaths_total (monthly homicides presumably related to DTOs)
main_predictor: lpub_after06 — indicator for 1-6 months after a publicly known capture/killing of a DTO leader in that municipality
sample_definition: Municipalities flagged treat_leader==1 (treated leader municipalities and their matched controls), all monthly observations 1998–2010; year-months with zero total homicides across the subsample were dropped because they are perfectly predicted by the time fixed effects.
model_specification: Poisson regression with municipality and year-month fixed effects; coefficients on lpub_after06, lpub_after612, lieupub_after06, lieupub_after612 estimated jointly; cluster-robust (sandwich) standard errors clustered by municipality.
controls: Municipality fixed effects, year-month fixed effects, and indicators for 6-12 months post-leader capture and for 1-6 and 6-12 months post-lieutenant capture.
operationalization_notes: Operationalization follows Table 1, column 1 of the paper (treatment-leader subsample, DTO-related homicides). Sample size differs slightly from the paper (686 vs 637) because the paper appears to apply an additional event-window restriction not visible after redaction; the test statistic reported here is the one produced by my code on the original data.
reasoning: In a municipality and year-month fixed effects Poisson regression on the leader-treatment subsample (14 treated/control municipalities, dropping months with no homicides for identification), the coefficient on the indicator for 1-6 months after a leader capture/killing is 0.426 (cluster-robust SE = 0.190; z = 2.25, p ≈ 0.025), implying a roughly 53% short-term increase in DTO-related homicides. This positive and significant short-term effect matches the paper's claim that beheadings have exacerbating short-term effects on DTO-related violence.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) across bootstrapped partial semantic networks
main_predictor: Openness to experience group (median split on latent openness factor: high vs. low)
sample_definition: All 516 participants split at the median latent openness score into n=258 high and n=258 low groups; semantic network nodes were animal exemplars produced by ≥2 participants in BOTH groups (N=168 common nodes).
model_specification: For each group, a binary semantic network was built by computing cosine similarities between word-by-participant binary vectors and filtering with a Triangulated Maximally Filtered Graph (TMFG, planar 3N-6 edges). 1000 bootstrap samples each retained a random 90% subset of nodes; ASPL was computed on the largest connected component of each filtered partial network. Two-sample independent t-test compared ASPL distributions of high vs low groups.
operationalization_notes: Methods section was redacted; this operationalization (cosine similarity + TMFG filter + node-drop bootstrap, then independent-samples t-test on ASPL) follows the Kenett-style semantic network pipeline that the paper uses (and that the SemNeT R package implements). Reported statistic is at 90% nodes retained, the largest effect-size cell in the paper's Table 3.
reasoning: Using a partial-network node-drop bootstrap (1000 samples at 90% nodes retained per group), the high-openness group's semantic network had a significantly shorter average shortest path length (mean ASPL ≈ 2.85) than the low-openness group's (mean ASPL ≈ 3.29), Welch t(1998) = -70.06, p < .001, Cohen's d ≈ -3.13. This replicates the paper's claim that the high-openness group's network is more interconnected (shorter ASPL).

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Index (ciri_physint, 0-8 ordinal)
main_predictor: Reliance on Taxes (tax_rev_new, % of govt revenues from taxes)
sample_definition: All country-years with non-missing values on DV, predictors, and controls (N=1739), mirroring Model 6 in the paper
model_specification: Ordered probit regression with lagged dependent variable
controls: Size of govt revenues (tot_rev_new), log population, income per capita, Polity democracy, external conflict, internal armed conflict, UK colony, lagged CIRI Physical Integrity
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table column (6) — the main specification with full controls and lagged DV on the CIRI physical integrity index, which most directly tests the verbal claim.
reasoning: In an ordered probit of CIRI Physical Integrity Index on Reliance on Taxes with the paper's controls and lagged DV, the tax-reliance coefficient is 0.0056 (SE 0.0019, z=2.98, p=0.003), positive and significant, consistent with the claim that greater tax reliance is associated with better protection of human rights.

dependent_variable: GCSE pass rate: percent of students scoring 5+ A-C grades (pt_gcse_5_a_c)
main_predictor: gm_win (1 if school won its GM ballot, 0 if lost)
sample_definition: School-year observations 2-8 years after the GM ballot ('base' year), restricted to schools that held a GM vote
model_specification: OLS regression of pass rate on gm_win + baseline pass rate + year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by school
controls: Year fixed effects and baseline (pre-ballot) pass rate (pt_gcse_5_a_c_base)
operationalization_notes: Replicates the 'ADJ-ITT' specification of Table 1 panel B (pooled base+2 to base+8), the paper's main intent-to-treat estimate of GM conversion's effect on student achievement. Sample sizes (N=4,954, N_schools=726) match the paper exactly.
reasoning: Pooled ADJ-ITT regression of the GCSE pass-rate outcome (% 5+ A-C) on a GM vote-winner indicator, restricted to school-years 2-8 years after the GM ballot (N=4,954 obs from 726 schools), with year fixed effects and baseline pass rate as controls, yields a coefficient of 3.27 percentage points (cluster-robust SE 0.56, t=5.83, p<.001). This confirms the paper's claim of large positive achievement gains following GM conversion (paper's analogous Table 1B estimate is 2.50, same direction and significance).

dependent_variable: Participated (lab) – binary indicator of laboratory experiment participation
main_predictor: Sent_Class – amount sent (out of 20) in the classroom trust game
sample_definition: All subjects with non-missing classroom trust-game sent amount and lab participation status
model_specification: Logistic regression: Participated ~ Sent_Class
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns relationship between trust-game sending and lab participation; simplest direct test is bivariate logit using classroom (pre-recruitment) trust-game send amount predicting lab show-up.
reasoning: Logistic regression of lab participation on amount sent in the classroom trust game yields a negative, statistically significant coefficient (b=-0.045, z=-2.50, p=0.013, n=658). Mean sent was 8.39 among non-participants vs 6.13 among participants, consistent with the claim that those who sent less were more likely to participate.

dependent_variable: took_act (illness was treated with an ACT)
main_predictor: act40 (92% ACT subsidy arm) vs no-subsidy control (act500)
sample_definition: First illness episode per household, excluding RDT and ex-post arms, non-missing took_act (N=631), matching Table 1
model_specification: OLS linear probability model with arm dummies (act40, act60, act100) and stratum fixed effects; standard errors clustered at household
operationalization_notes: Claim refers to the access effect of the very high (92%) subsidy on ACT take-up; this is the coefficient on act40 in the Table 1 specification.
reasoning: Linear-probability regression of Took ACT on subsidy-arm dummies (with stratum fixed effects, household-clustered SE) shows the 92% (very high) subsidy raises the probability of taking an ACT by 0.214 (SE 0.053), t=4.03, p<0.001, relative to the no-subsidy control mean of 0.19 — supporting the claim that a very high subsidy increases access.

dependent_variable: Normalized average of PIAT math, reading recognition, and reading comprehension scores (combined math-reading)
main_predictor: Current total family income (earnings + welfare + unearned + nontaxable) in $1000s of year-2000 dollars
sample_definition: Child-year observations from survey years 1988-1999 with non-missing combined PIAT score
model_specification: OLS levels regression (equation 1) with family-clustered standard errors
controls: Child gender, age, race (black/Hispanic), siblings, mother's AFQT, mother's and father's grade completed, lived with both parents, mother's/father's step status, marriage status last year, year dummies
operationalization_notes: Methods section was redacted; chose the simplest direct test of the short-run effect of income on combined math-reading achievement (Table 2 column 1, panel A OLS levels). The IV specification (Table 3) would be the paper's preferred test but requires constructing the simulated EITC instrument from the tax-schedule code, which is not directly available in the dataset.
reasoning: OLS levels regression of normalized combined math-reading PIAT scores on current total family income (in $1000s, 2000 dollars) with baseline controls and year fixed effects yields a coefficient of 0.0048 (cluster-robust SE = 0.0007; t = 6.84, p < 0.001, N = 20,256). A $1,000 increase in income is associated with a positive and highly significant rise in test scores, matching the paper's Table 2 column 1 baseline OLS estimate (0.0047) and supporting the directional claim that income raises short-run achievement.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs)
main_predictor: Single-childless indicator (singchild1: 1 = single & childless, 0 = otherwise)
sample_definition: Employed respondents (filter=1) with non-missing values on absorption, family structure, gender, age, and job level (N=355)
model_specification: OLS regression: engwkabs ~ singchild1 + gender + age + position
operationalization_notes: Claim is a simple group comparison; used OLS with the single-childless dummy as predictor and the demographic controls present in the dataset, matching the predictors that appear available for this analysis.
reasoning: OLS regression of work absorption on a single-childless indicator, controlling for gender, age, and job level, yields a negative and significant coefficient (b = -0.296, t(350) = -2.24, p = .026, N = 355). Single childless workers report lower absorption than those with other family structures, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: ProperName (whether the response used the applicant's proper name)
main_predictor: Applicant race signaled by name (Hispanic vs. white)
sample_definition: Hispanic- and white-named applicants whose emails received a response (ProperName non-missing); Black-named applicants excluded to isolate the Hispanic-vs-white comparison.
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 race x proper-name table
operationalization_notes: The claim is a direct Hispanic-vs-white comparison on a binary outcome; a chi-square test on the cross-tab is the simplest direct test. ProperName is observed only conditional on response, matching how the variable is defined in the data.
reasoning: Among emails that received a response, 41.2% (77/187) of Hispanic-named applicants were greeted by their proper name vs. 61.1% (107/175) of white-named applicants. A chi-square test of independence yields χ²(1, N=362)=14.42, p<.001, confirming Hispanic applicants were significantly less likely to be greeted by name than white applicants.

dependent_variable: Session-level frequency of normal (non-shaded) quality in the good state
main_predictor: Contract type (rigid vs. flexible)
sample_definition: Baseline treatment (condition==1), trades realized in the good state (cost in {20,25}); aggregated to 5 session-level pairs
model_specification: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired session averages (one-sided: rigid > flexible)
operationalization_notes: Matches the paper's footnote 16 nonparametric test; uses session as independent unit to avoid within-session dependence.
reasoning: Replicating the paper's session-level Wilcoxon signed-rank test (one-sided) on the frequency of normal quality in the good state, baseline condition: rigid contracts have higher normal-quality frequency (~93%) than flexible contracts (~75%) in every one of the 5 sessions, W=15, p=0.03125. Shading is significantly lower under rigid contracts.

dependent_variable: log(state CO2 emissions, adjusted)
main_predictor: log(average weekly working hours)
sample_definition: 50 US states, 2007-2013 (N=350 state-years)
model_specification: OLS two-way fixed effects (state + year dummies) with state-clustered standard errors
controls: log employed-population %, log GDP per hour, log total population, manufacturing % of GDP, log energy production, log working-age population
operationalization_notes: Approximates Model 1 (Scale, FE) from Table 3 using variables available in compiled.dta; household size and state environmentalism not present in the compiled file were omitted.
reasoning: In a two-way (state and year) fixed-effects regression of log(carbon emissions, adjusted) on log(working hours) with controls (log emp/pop, log labor productivity, log population, manufacturing share, log energy production, log working-age population) and state-clustered SEs, the coefficient on log working hours is positive (b=0.49, SE=0.33, t=1.50). The direction matches the paper's positive relationship, though my reduced spec (lacking household size and environmentalism controls available in the paper) is not significant at conventional levels.

dependent_variable: Considered attack on a state's nuclear program (binary)
main_predictor: Prior violent militarized conflict (hostileMID, binary, lagged 1 year)
sample_definition: Politically relevant dyad-years (polrel==1) with non-missing values for the variables used in the paper's Model 1 (consider, hostileMID, polity2, s_un_reg, peace-year spline terms); N=5360, matching Table 5 Model 1
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on the 2x2 contingency table consider × hostileMID
controls: none (bivariate cross-tabulation, sample restricted to observations used in the multivariate Model 1)
operationalization_notes: The paper presents the most direct test of this claim as a bivariate cross-tab (Table 3A) between violent conflict and considered attacks; I reproduced this on the politically-relevant sample used in the paper's main regression. A multivariate logit yields a strong positive coefficient on violent conflict as well, but suffers from quasi-separation; the chi-square test is the cleanest single statistic tied to the claim.
reasoning: In politically-relevant dyad-years (1941-2000), prior hostile militarized interstate disputes are strongly associated with serious consideration of attacks on a state's nuclear program: 25 of 526 (4.8%) conflict-preceded dyad-years involved a considered attack vs. only 12 of 4,834 (0.25%) peaceful dyad-years; χ²(1,N=5360)=140.4, p<1e-31. This replicates the original study's finding that prior violent conflict raises the salience of the proliferation threat.

dependent_variable: splinter (county-year indicator that the county broke off to form its own new district)
main_predictor: DEC_rep — county's ethnic group share of seats in District Executive Committee relative to its population share (political (under)representation)
sample_definition: County-electoral-wave observations from the DistrictFormation.dta with non-missing covariates (waves 1-3); all available counties retained
model_specification: Logistic regression (Model M1 specification from Table 3)

A lower share of political representation (greater political marginalization) raises the probability of secession, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: recog1dum (State B diplomatically recognizes State A, dichotomous)

Sample size differs slightly from the paper (213,454) likely due to small differences in handling missing controls, but the substantive result is the same.
reasoning: In a directed-dyad logit predicting whether State B diplomatically recognizes State A (recog1dum), the coefficient on State A's nuclear-weapons capability is 0.815 (SE=0.029, z=27.68, p<0.001), strongly positive. Nuclear-capable states are substantially more likely to be recognized by other nations, matching the claim.

dependent_variable: Absolute opinion change on immigration (wave3-wave2), change_w3w2_log
main_predictor: Group-level mean justification level (DQ_jlev)

operationalization_notes: Operationalization follows Table 1 column 2 (absolute opinion change on immigration). The pre-computed group-level justification level (DQ_jlev) and the pre-computed absolute change variable (change_w3w2_log) in the SANDERS_Replication file are used; individual-level controls included follow those displayed in Table 1 plus standard demographic controls.

The point estimate is in the predicted positive direction but does not reach conventional significance, so the claim that participants change opinions more often when rational justification is used is not statistically supported in my replication.

dependent_variable: Mean effort (frequency of 'work') per matching group across rounds 1-5
main_predictor: Reward scheme (345COM = discriminating vs 444COM = symmetrical), under complementarity production
sample_definition: All subjects in treatments 345COM and 444COM; aggregated to matching-group means (12 groups in 345COM, 11 in 444COM)

operationalization_notes: Matching groups are treated as independent observations, following the paper's footnotes and Table 2 (‡ Mean effort level of each matching group is one independent observation).
reasoning: Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon rank-sum test on matching-group mean effort levels (rounds 1-5) comparing 345COM (n=12 groups, mean=91.7%) vs 444COM (n=11 groups, mean=72.2%) yields U=95, two-sided p≈0.070, approximate z≈1.81. The symmetric scheme elicits substantially lower effort than the discriminating scheme under complementarity, matching the paper's reported direction and magnitude (the paper reports rank-sum p=.0649).

dependent_variable: Tailoring index: (mentions of anti-immigration actions) - (mentions of pro-immigration actions) in a senator's letter
main_predictor: Letter recipient type (anti-immigration vs pro-immigration constituent), within-subject
sample_definition: 56 senators who responded to both the anti- and pro-immigration constituent letters
model_specification: Paired (within-subjects) t-test of the tailoring index across the two letter conditions
operationalization_notes: The claim about senators tailoring explanations corresponds most directly to the within-subjects field experiment (Table 2). I compute, for each senator, the difference between mentions of anti- vs pro-immigration secondary actions in each letter and compare these paired values across the two letter types.
reasoning: Within-senator paired t-test of the tailoring index (anti-immigration minus pro-immigration action mentions) across the anti vs pro letters yields t(55)=3.45, p=0.001, replicating the paper's <0.01 result in Table 2's 'Anti - Pro' column. Senators emphasize anti-immigration actions more when writing to anti-immigration constituents and pro-immigration actions more when writing to pro-immigration constituents.

dependent_variable: Log wage gain at migration = log(last U.S. hourly wage, PPP-adjusted) − log(last home-country hourly wage, PPP-adjusted)
main_predictor: Education category (No HS, Some HS, HS grad, Some college, College grad [reference])

operationalization_notes: The paper's NIS microdata are restricted and not included in the public replication archive, so I implemented the Table 2-style regression (education dummies with country FE, dependent variable = log wage gain) on the available MP+LAMP sample. Education thresholds use years of schooling: <9 = No HS, 9–11 = Some HS, 12 = HS grad, 13–15 = Some college, 16+ = College.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of the log wage gain at migration on education-category dummies with country fixed effects, using the Migration Projects (MP) sample (the publicly available data; NIS files are restricted), the coefficient on 'No high school' relative to the omitted 'College graduate' category is +0.197 (SE=0.129, t=1.52, p=0.128, N=2,854). The point estimate is positive — immigrants with no high school gain more upon migration than college graduates — matching the directional claim in the paper, though it is not statistically significant in this MP-only subsample.

dependent_variable: Percent negative (learned) meaning of free associations to homograph cues (FAHbaseC vs FAHsuppC)
main_predictor: Item type (baseline vs suppressed) within nonruminator group
sample_definition: Nonruminators (Group=1) in Experiment 2 free-association dataset; n=27
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing FAHbaseC and FAHsuppC
operationalization_notes: Only Experiment 2 data are available. The claim that nonruminators show suppression benefits on the indirect transfer test is most directly tested by the baseline–suppressed contrast within the nonruminator subsample on the homograph free-association measure (the critical indirect index of SIF).
reasoning: Among nonruminators (Group=1, n=27), percent negative-meaning responses to homograph cues was significantly lower for suppressed items (M=34.57) than baseline items (M=54.32), paired t(26)=2.94, p=.007, indicating suppression-induced forgetting on this indirect free-association transfer task — consistent with the paper's claim that nonruminators benefit from suppression practice.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being (CES-D-based wellbeing score, mean of 8 items recoded so higher = better)
main_predictor: Interaction between parental status (childless ref. vs. lives with children, empty nest) and country-level percentage who (strongly) disapprove of childlessness
sample_definition: ESS Round 3 respondents aged >=40 in 24 European countries, with complete data on all model variables (paper's analytic sample)
model_specification: Two-level linear mixed model: wellbeing ~ par_stat * pct_disapp + individual controls, random intercept by country
controls: Age, age squared, marital status, education, parental education, religious attendance, paid employment, born in country, gender
operationalization_notes: Pooled both genders into one model (with gender control) to give a single main test of the cross-level interaction. Country % disapproving constructed as share with childless_disapp>=3 (disapprove/strongly disapprove). Key test = z on 'lives with children × pct_disapp' interaction.
reasoning: In a multilevel model with random intercepts by country, the interaction of 'Lives with children' (vs. childless) with country-level % (strongly) disapproving of childlessness was positive and significant (B=0.0020, SE=0.00044, z=4.61, p<.001). This means childless people fare worse relative to parents in countries with more disapproval — i.e., the childlessness disadvantage is smaller in more tolerant countries, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: DSM5_Total (total psychopathology symptoms)
main_predictor: MiniK_Total (slow life history strategy; higher = slower)
sample_definition: All respondents with non-missing MiniK_Total and DSM5_Total
model_specification: Pearson correlation (bivariate)
operationalization_notes: Mini-K is the standard slow life-history index used in the paper; DSM5_Total is the paper's psychopathology composite. A negative correlation indicates that faster (lower Mini-K) life history is associated with greater psychopathology, the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between Mini-K (slow life history) and DSM-5 total psychopathology score is r=-0.587, t(136)=-8.46, p<.001, N=138. Lower Mini-K (faster strategy) is strongly associated with more psychopathology symptoms, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (total political knowledge score, 20 items)
main_predictor: Stereotypaktivierung experimental condition (0 = stereotype not activated vs. 2 = stereotype activated by gender difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender==1) assigned to either condition 0 or condition 2 of the Study 2 experiment
model_specification: Independent-samples two-tailed Student's t-test (equal variances assumed)
operationalization_notes: Claim is a direct contrast between two experimental cells for women on the political knowledge test; used the paper's primary outcome variable PolWis_score and a simple between-groups t-test, matching the experimental design.
reasoning: Female participants in the 'stereotype not activated' condition scored higher on the political knowledge test (M=8.33, SD=4.84, n=76) than female participants in the 'stereotype activated by gender difference statement' condition (M=7.17, SD=4.20, n=81). The direction matches the claim, though the independent-samples t-test was not statistically significant at conventional thresholds, t(155)=1.60, p=.11.

dependent_variable: GDP growth index two years ahead (f2gdpidx)
main_predictor: msec2currentsec — city party secretary informally connected to incumbent provincial party secretary
sample_definition: All city-years in the merged citypanel/econ_panel for which DV, predictor, and controls are non-missing
model_specification: OLS with city fixed effects and province-by-year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by city
controls: loggdp, logpop, govsize, msec_tenure, mayor_tenure, msec_edu_year, mayor_edu_year, msec age, mayor age
operationalization_notes: Mirrors the paper's two-way FE specification (city + province-year) used for growth analyses; uses two-year-ahead growth index as the dependent variable to capture leader effects with a lag, and the binary informal-tie indicator to provincial secretary as the main predictor.
reasoning: Regressing GDP growth at t+2 on the indicator of city-secretary connection to the incumbent provincial secretary, with city and province-year fixed effects plus city economic and leader controls (clustered SEs by city), yields a coefficient of 0.132 (SE = 0.175, t = 0.75, p = 0.45, N = 2281). There is no statistically detectable growth advantage for connected leaders, contrary to the conventional-wisdom claim.

dependent_variable: Top-quality indicator among foreign players (1 if the player ever appeared for his home country's national team)
main_predictor: Post-reform indicator (year >= 1991, when the Danish preferential tax scheme for foreigners began)
sample_definition: All player-year observations in the Danish first league (Superligaen/predecessor) from 1985 to 2008 whose nationality differs from Denmark (foreign players)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 contingency table (top vs. non-top × pre vs. post 1991)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns a change in the ability composition of foreigners in Denmark after the 1991 tax reform. Following the paper's own definition of top-ability players (national-team selection), I compared the share of top-ability players among foreigners before vs. after 1991 using a chi-square test. This is the most direct simple test of a compositional shift; the data file is the baseplayer.dta used by the paper for the synthetic-control graphs.
reasoning: Among foreign players in the Danish top league, the share classified as top-ability (ever played for their home national team) rose from 27.3% in 1985-1990 (pre-reform) to 63.5% in 1991-2008 (post-reform). The chi-square test of independence yields χ²(1)=27.42, p<0.001, n=1095, confirming that the 1991 tax cut to foreigners shifted the ability composition of foreigners toward higher-ability players.

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay (willingness to pay to protect the environment)

reasoning: Pearson correlation between the intrinsic-minus-extrinsic relative values score and willingness to pay to protect the environment was r=.43, p<.001, n=155, supporting the claim that higher endorsement of intrinsic relative to extrinsic values is associated with higher willingness to pay.

dependent_variable: ln_imports (log of product-level imports)
main_predictor: complainant (indicator: trading pair is the complainant)

operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 1 Model 2 specification (early settlements subsample). Sample size differs from paper (11,309 vs 6,027) because the methods section was redacted and exact sample-restriction rule could not be determined, but the substantive coefficient sign and significance directly test the claim.
reasoning: On the early-settlement subsample, regressing log product-level imports on a complainant indicator with controls (defendant GDP, partner GDP, democratic pair, lagged disputed imports, total imports) and dispute-clustered SEs yields a positive, significant complainant coefficient (b=0.183, SE=0.081, z=2.25, p=0.024), indicating that complainants gain more imports than non-participants under privacy.

dependent_variable: Early-stage entrepreneurship rate that pays wages (entre_wage)
main_predictor: Country median age of population aged 20-64 (medage_20_64)

operationalization_notes: Chose Table 2 column 3 specification because it is the most direct bivariate test of the claim that lower median age increases new business formation; clustered SEs at the country level match the paper's reported SE.

Lower median age is associated with higher new business formation.

dependent_variable: Ratio of perceived to actual arm length (RatioRight, RatioLeft)

reasoning: For right-handed participants (n=15), a paired t-test comparing perceived-to-actual length ratios for the right vs. left arm yielded t(14)=2.12, p=.052, with the right arm ratio (M=0.970) higher than the left (M=0.920), consistent with the claim that the right arm is perceived as relatively longer.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (composite of appreciated, valued, satisfied; 7-point)

dependent_variable: Standardized mean of midterm + final exam scores (s_tot)

Moving from 0% to 100% female neighbors (five males to five females) raises a girl's score by ~0.3 SD, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Absolute attitude change |T1-T2| (mean of three attitude items)
main_predictor: Certainty x objective ambivalence interaction
sample_definition: Study 1 participants who completed attitude measures at both T1 and T2 (n=174)
model_specification: OLS regression: change ~ certainty + ambivalence + extremity + certainty*ambivalence
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's described analytic approach (Petrocelli-style hierarchical regression with extremity covariate); ambivalence computed via Griffin formula (P+N)/2-|P-N|; certainty as mean of 7 certainty items.
reasoning: In Study 1, regressing absolute attitude change (T1-T2) on mean certainty, objective ambivalence (Griffin's formula), and their interaction while covarying attitude extremity, the certainty x ambivalence interaction was significant, B=0.037, t(169)=2.28, p=.024. The interaction direction matches the original: greater certainty predicts more stability as ambivalence decreases.

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters)
main_predictor: Portfolio equity stock (log, % GDP) — most flexible foreign-ownership measure
sample_definition: Election-year observations in 23 OECD countries 1970-2007 with nonmissing covariates (yielding 22 countries, 196 elections)

controls: Lagged turnout, log registered voters, %VAP 30-69, years since last election, US mid-term dummy, compulsory voting, mixed system, PR system, disproportionality, ENPS, closeness (margin)
operationalization_notes: Replicated Table 1 Model 4 (Portfolio Stock), the most direct test of the ownership-constraint hypothesis emphasized as the strongest/most flexible ownership measure in the paper.
reasoning: Regressing turnout on log Portfolio Equity Stock with country fixed effects, country-specific linear time trends, and the paper's listed controls (LDV, log registered voters, %VAP 30-69, years since election, US mid-term, compulsory voting, mixed/PR system, disproportionality, ENPS, margin) yields a coefficient of -2.08 (cluster-robust SE 0.54, t = -3.83, p < 0.001, N = 196, 22 countries). Foreign ownership (portfolio equity) is significantly negatively associated with turnout, supporting the ownership-constraint hypothesis.

dependent_variable: Number of service complaints in 2008 (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: Indicator: firm name begins with letter A or a number (first_A)

controls: Ad spending ($000s), firm age, Metro Chicago indicator
operationalization_notes: Matches the specification of Table 5 column (2) in the paper; employees enters as exposure (coefficient constrained to 1 in log-link).
reasoning: In a negative-binomial regression of 2008 service complaints on a 'name begins with A/number' indicator, controlling for ad spending, firm age, Metro Chicago, and number of employees (as exposure), the coefficient on first_A is 1.382 (SE=0.111, z=12.50, p<0.001), indicating A-named plumbing firms receive substantially more complaints than other firms — same direction as the paper's Table 5.

dependent_variable: Cooperative bargaining strategy (dv, 4 categories)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure

controls: ln GDP, security/foreign-policy issue, Euro state, new member state, agreement importance, parliamentary scrutiny, QMV, publicity, presidency, lagged DV
operationalization_notes: Replicates Model 1 of Table 1 (lngdp specification). Tested the central predictor (issue-linkage structure) with a joint Wald test across multinomial categories since the claim is about a directional effect on offering concessions rather than a single category contrast.
reasoning: In a multinomial logit of bargaining/cooperative strategy on issue-linkage structure plus the paper's covariates, the issue-linkage coefficient is positive and significant in every non-baseline category (b=0.82, 1.82, 2.84). A joint Wald test that the issue-linkage coefficient equals zero across all three equations gives chi2(3)=134.2, p<.001, supporting the claim that more differently valued (linkable) issues lead to more concessionary strategies.

dependent_variable: Directed Credit to Government and SOEs (% GDP) (credittogovtstateenterp)
main_predictor: State Capacity – ICRG Quality of Government index (icrg_qog)
sample_definition: All country-year observations in Country Year Dataset.dta with non-missing directed credit, lagged directed credit, ICRG quality of government, private credit, and year.
model_specification: Pooled OLS with lagged dependent variable: DirectedCredit_t = b0 + b1*DirectedCredit_{t-1} + b2*StateCapacity + b3*PrivateCredit + b4*year + e; cluster-robust SEs by country.
controls: Lagged Directed Credit, Private Credit (profit potential of financial repression), linear time trend; SEs clustered by country.
operationalization_notes: Mirrors the dynamic specification in Table 1 column 1 (lagged DV, IQG, Private Credit, time trend) but uses pooled OLS with clustered SEs instead of the paper's system-GMM, since the methods section is redacted and GMM is not directly implementable without additional packages. Private Credit serves as the profit-potential control. A negative coefficient on State Capacity would support the claim.
reasoning: In a dynamic panel OLS of Directed Credit to Govt./SOEs on State Capacity (icrg_qog), with a lagged dependent variable, Private Credit, and a time trend (cluster-robust SEs by country), the State Capacity coefficient is -0.142 with t=-0.358 (p=0.72, N=2787). The sign matches the paper's negative direction but the effect is far from statistically significant, so the data do not reproduce the paper's system-GMM finding under this simpler operationalization.

dependent_variable: dispute (militarized interstate dispute involvement, binary)

controls: lagged dispute, ethnic fractionalization, CINC (relative power), number of borders, log allies, regional conflict, lagged polity, lagged log real GDP
operationalization_notes: Methods section redacted. Chose dispute involvement as the most direct operationalization of 'conflict involvement,' coup risk as the standard proxy for threats to political survival, and the control set mirroring Table 3 with cluster-robust SEs.
reasoning: In a logit regression of militarized dispute involvement on coup risk (lcoupsum) with controls and cluster-robust SEs by country, the coefficient on coup risk is positive (b=0.158) but not statistically significant (z=1.07, p=0.28, N=798). The sign aligns with the paper's claim that increasing threats to political survival raise the probability of conflict involvement, but the effect is not distinguishable from zero in this specification.

dependent_variable: Amount sent to out-group in dictator game (d12outgroup, 0-5 euros)
main_predictor: Region of residence (Primarily Albanian / Border / Primarily Serb)
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb participants in the Kosovo dictator-game experiment
model_specification: OLS regression of out-group giving on region dummies (Primarily Serb region as reference); overall F-test for joint significance of region
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns out-group bridging; the most direct DV is euros sent to an Albanian (out-group) recipient. Exposure to out-group is operationalized via the three-region indicator, with Primarily Serb (least exposure) as the reference category. Reported statistic is the joint F-test on the region dummies.
reasoning: Regressing amount sent to out-group on region dummies (primarily Albanian, border; primarily Serb omitted) yields F(2,155)=9.26, p<0.001. Mean out-group giving is highest in the Primarily Albanian region (intercept+1.49) and lowest in the Primarily Serb region, consistent with the claim that out-group bridging norms increase with exposure to the out-group.

dependent_variable: enjoyrelativ (relative enjoyment rating)
main_predictor: condition (commercial interruption: 'good' vs. 'no')
sample_definition: All 102 study-2 participants with non-missing enjoyment ratings (53 interrupted, 49 not interrupted)
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test
operationalization_notes: The dataset's single enjoyment measure ('enjoyrelativ') is the most direct test of whether interruption increases enjoyment; compared the two between-subjects conditions.
reasoning: Participants who viewed the program with commercial interruptions reported significantly greater enjoyment (M=5.38) than those without interruptions (M=4.47), t(100)=2.45, p=.016, supporting the claim that commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable.

dependent_variable: resigninvest (4-point belief that the politician resigned because he is under investigation for bribery)
main_predictor: Experimental condition: causal correction vs denial of innuendo (innuendo as omitted baseline)
sample_definition: Respondents assigned to innuendo, denial, or causal-correction conditions with non-missing belief outcome (control excluded because the question was not asked of them); N=764
model_specification: Weighted least squares (inverse probability weights, variable 'aw') of resigninvest on denial and causal dummies; linear contrast testing equality of denial and causal coefficients
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the causal correction being more effective than the innuendo denial at limiting misperceptions; the most direct test is the contrast of denial vs causal coefficients in the Model 5 specification using the question that measured belief in the specific misperception.
reasoning: In a WLS regression (IPW weights) of belief that Swensen resigned due to the bribery investigation on denial and causal-correction dummies (innuendo = baseline), causal correction reduced belief substantially more than denial (denial = -0.246, causal = -0.581). A linear contrast (causal vs denial) yielded a difference of -0.335, t(761)=5.07, p<.001, confirming the causal correction is more effective at limiting acceptance of the misperception.

dependent_variable: Aggregated Intimacy score (mean of r1–r10 items) toward the partner
main_predictor: Attention condition (attention vs. no-attention)
sample_definition: All 30 participants in Study 2a (Sheet3 of the dataset)
model_specification: Independent-samples Student's t-test comparing intimacy across the two attention conditions
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the experimental effect of partner attention on intimacy. Sheet3 contains the aggregated 'Intimacy' variable and a binary condition (cnd) corresponding to the attention manipulation in Study 2a, so a between-subjects t-test on Intimacy by condition is the most direct test.
reasoning: Participants in the attention condition (cnd=1, M=4.58) reported substantially higher intimacy toward the partner than those in the no-attention condition (cnd=2, M=2.78), t(28)=6.20, p<.001, confirming that attention from a partner increased intimacy.

dependent_variable: Willing to monitor the budget (q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2; binary)
main_predictor: Tax treatment assignment (taxgrp: 1=tax, 0=windfall)
sample_definition: All 1,863 campaign participants with non-missing outcome
model_specification: OLS with block (randomization block) fixed effects and information-treatment indicator, HC1 robust standard errors
controls: Block fixed effects; information treatment (infogrp) indicator
operationalization_notes: Primary monitoring outcome in Table 1 Panel A (H1) is willingness to monitor the budget. Used block FE per the experimental block-randomized design and included the orthogonal information treatment as a covariate.
reasoning: OLS with block fixed effects shows the tax treatment increases willingness to monitor the budget by 5.2 percentage points (SE=0.017, t=3.10, p=0.002, N=1863), matching the paper's reported 5pp effect (Table 1, row 1).

dependent_variable: Voter turnout (binary)

dependent_variable: bid_on_d (PAP submitted application for a given BMO child)

dependent_variable: a-insensitivity index a = 3*(1/3 - (mean composite matching prob - mean single matching prob)) computed per subject from Part 1 questions

dependent_variable: Civil war duration (months)

This supports the paper's claim that irregular wars last longer.

dependent_variable: log mortality rate (lndrate) at the state-year-month level
main_predictor: number of days with mean temperature >=90°F (b10_10) interacted with post-1960 indicator

The pre-1960 effect is 0.0257 and is essentially eliminated post-1960 (sum=0.0003), confirming a substantial and statistically significant decline in the temperature-mortality relationship across decades.

dependent_variable: Binary choice: chose not to buy the DVD (notBuy=2 coded 1) vs. chose to buy

dependent_variable: REF_female (referral is female, 0/1)

dependent_variable: Log implied discount rate (interval-censored between adjacent switching-row bounds)

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of giant component of partial bootstrapped semantic networks
main_predictor: Openness-to-experience group (high vs low; median split on composite AVERAGE score)

The high-openness group had a significantly lower ASPL (M=4.47) than the low-openness group (M=4.56), Welch t(1998)=-4.09, p<.001, d=-0.18 — same direction as the published finding that the high-openness network is more interconnected.

dependent_variable: splinter (1 = county broke away to form new district, 0 otherwise)

dependent_variable: recog1dum (dichotomous: State B recognizes State A)

Direction matches the claim that nuclear-capable states are more likely to be recognized.

dependent_variable: Log of absolute opinion change on immigration index between waves 2 and 3 (change_w3w2_log)

operationalization_notes: Operationalized following the paper's Model 2b in Table 2 using the SANDERS_Replication.dta replication file; this is the model the claim directly references (magnitude/absolute opinion change as a function of group-level justification rationality).

Higher justification rationality in a group is associated with greater magnitude of opinion change.

dependent_variable: Mean work decision (1=work, 0=shirk) per matching group across 6 periods
main_predictor: Reward scheme: 345COM (discriminating) vs 444COM (symmetric), both under complementarity

operationalization_notes: Cost-equivalent comparison under complementarity is 345COM vs 444COM (sum of bonuses = 12 in both). Matching group is treated as the independent unit to avoid within-group dependence across periods and members.
reasoning: Aggregating to the matching-group level (the independent unit), mean work effort under complementarity is 0.917 in the discriminating 345COM scheme vs 0.722 in the symmetric 444COM scheme. A two-sided Mann-Whitney U test gives U=95, p=0.070 (n1=12, n2=11), with the discriminating scheme eliciting higher effort, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Within-senator difference between mentioning a compensating anti-immigration action and mentioning a compensating pro-immigration action in the letter response

model_specification: Paired (within-subjects) t-test on the difference-in-differences of action mentions across the two letters per senator
operationalization_notes: The claim that senators 'tailor explanations to audiences' is most directly tested by checking whether the secondary policy actions senators mention shift with the letter writer's stated position. A paired test on the difference between anti- and pro-immigration action mentions across the two letter conditions captures this within-senator tailoring, matching the design reported in Table 1.
reasoning: Among 56 senators who responded to both letters, the within-senator difference in (anti-immigration actions mentioned − pro-immigration actions mentioned) was 42.9% in responses to the anti-immigration constituent letter but only 19.7% in responses to the pro-immigration letter. A paired t-test of this difference-in-differences yields t(55)=3.45, p=0.001, providing strong evidence that senators tailor the policy actions they mention to the views of the constituent audience.

dependent_variable: Wage gain at migration: log(post-migration US hourly wage) − log(pre-migration home hourly wage)
main_predictor: Education category dummies: No HS (≤8 yrs), Some HS (9-11), HS grad (12), Some college (13-15), College+ (≥16, reference)
sample_definition: All MMP/LAMP (MP) individuals with valid pre- and post-migration adjusted hourly wages and education years; 10 sending countries (mostly Mexico). NIS individual microdata are restricted and not included in the replication archive, so the analysis is restricted to the MP subsample.
model_specification: OLS of wage_gain on education category dummies with country fixed effects (no other controls); homoskedastic standard errors. Reported statistic is the t-test on the No-HS dummy (i.e., No-HS minus College).
operationalization_notes: This mirrors the Table II specification (wage gain ~ education category + country FE) most directly tied to the claim that immigrants who never attended high school gain more than college graduates. Because NIS individual data are restricted, only the MP sample (n=2854) was available, versus 3,539 in the paper's pooled NIS+MP analysis.
reasoning: Regressing the individual wage gain at migration (log US wage − log home wage) on education-category dummies with country fixed effects (college graduates as the omitted reference) yields a coefficient of 0.197 for the 'no high school' (≤8 years schooling) category, t(2840)=1.52, p=0.13. The point estimate is in the direction implied by the claim (less-educated immigrants gain more than college-educated ones), but the effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero in the MP sample that was accessible.

dependent_variable: Percent negative-meaning free associations (FAbaseC vs FAsuppC)
main_predictor: Item type (baseline vs suppressed) within nonruminators
sample_definition: Nonruminators only (Group==1) from Experiment 2 dataset
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing baseline vs suppressed within-subject means
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns nonruminators showing transfer benefit of suppression on indirect (free-association) test. Operationalized as within-subject paired t-test of percent negative-meaning responses for baseline vs suppressed items among nonruminators.
reasoning: Among nonruminators (Group=1, n=27), the percentage of negative free-association responses was significantly higher for baseline cues (M=45.68%) than for suppressed cues (M=29.63%), paired t(26)=3.03, p=.0055, demonstrating suppression-induced forgetting on this indirect transfer task — consistent with the paper's claim that suppression practice can be beneficial for nonruminators.

dependent_variable: Psychological wellbeing index (wellbeing)
main_predictor: Parental status (childless ref vs lives with children / empty nest) interacted with country-level tolerance toward childlessness (childless_perc)
sample_definition: ESS Round 3 respondents from 24 countries with non-missing key variables (missing==0); N=23,754
model_specification: Random-intercept multilevel linear model (statsmodels MixedLM) with country as grouping variable
controls: age, age^2, marital status, education, parental education, religious attendance, paid employment, born in country, gender
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's setup using provided derived variables. The cross-level interaction of parental status with the country tolerance indicator operationalizes the claim. Joint Wald test for the two interaction dummies serves as the single omnibus test; the lives-with-children interaction is significantly negative, indicating a smaller childlessness disadvantage in more tolerant countries.
reasoning: In a multilevel (random-intercept) model regressing wellbeing on parental status, country-level tolerance proxy (childless_perc), their interaction, and individual controls, the joint Wald test of the two parental-status × tolerance interaction terms is chi2(2)=30.66, p<.001. The interaction for 'lives with children' vs childless is -0.009 (z=-3.59), meaning the parental advantage in wellbeing shrinks (i.e., the childless disadvantage is smaller) in more tolerant countries — consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: DSM5_Total (total psychopathology symptoms)
main_predictor: MiniK_Total (life history strategy; higher = slower)
sample_definition: All 138 adolescent participants with complete Mini-K and DSM-5 scores
model_specification: Pearson zero-order correlation
operationalization_notes: The paper's headline claim links faster life history strategy with more psychopathology symptoms; the most direct test is the bivariate correlation between the Mini-K life history index and the DSM-5 total psychopathology score.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between Mini-K (slower life history strategy) and DSM5 total psychopathology score is r=-0.587, t(136)=-8.46, p<.001, N=138. Slower LH strategy is strongly associated with fewer psychopathology symptoms, equivalently faster LH = more psychopathology, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Political knowledge test score (PolWis_score, 0-20)
main_predictor: Stereotype activation condition (condition 1: not activated vs condition 3: activated by gender difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender_alle==1) with Filter==1 (study's analytic sample), restricted to the first and third experimental conditions
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test assuming equal variances
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns a direct contrast between female participants in condition 1 and condition 3 on the political knowledge test. PolWis_score is the paper's political knowledge measure; the paper's reported df=141 confirms the filtered female cond1+cond3 subsample (73+70). The simple Welch/equal-variance t-test reproduces the paper's reported direction and significance closely (paper reports t=2.46, ours 2.57); small differences likely reflect ANCOVA-adjusted means in the original.
reasoning: Among female participants in the filtered analytic sample (Filter=1), the political-knowledge test score (PolWis_score) was higher in the stereotype-not-activated condition (M=8.90, SD=4.60, n=73) than in the stereotype-activated-by-gender-difference-statement condition (M=7.03, SD=4.11, n=70). An independent-samples t-test yielded t(141)=2.57, p=0.011, supporting the paper's directional claim.

dependent_variable: City annual real GDP growth rate (gdpidx, last year = 100)
main_predictor: msec2currentsec: indicator that the city party secretary was promoted by the incumbent provincial party secretary (i.e., patronage tie)
sample_definition: Chinese prefecture-city-year panel 2000-2011 from citypanel_base.dta merged with econ_panel.dta; observations with non-missing GDP growth, connection indicator, and all controls
model_specification: Two-way fixed-effects OLS (city FE + province-year FE) with cluster-robust SEs at the city level, estimated via linearmodels.PanelOLS
controls: loggdp, logpop, govsize, growrev, startmsec_loggdp, startmayor_loggdp, msec_tenure, mayor_tenure, msec_edu, mayor_edu, msec_central_exp, mayor_central_exp, msec_prov_exp, mayor_prov_exp
operationalization_notes: The methods section is redacted, but Tables 2-3 in the article use 'Connected to provincial secretary' (the city party secretary—the de facto top city leader) as the focal predictor with city FE, province-year FE, and city economic + leader controls. I therefore used msec2currentsec as the predictor, the contemporaneous city GDP growth (gdpidx) as the outcome, and the same FE/control structure with city-clustered SEs.
reasoning: Regressing city-year GDP growth on the indicator for the city party secretary being connected (via past promotion) to the incumbent provincial party secretary, with city and province-year fixed effects plus city economic and leader controls (mirroring the control structure of Tables 2-3), yields a coefficient of 0.228 percentage points (cluster-robust SE 0.142; t=1.61, p≈0.11, N=4,373). The point estimate is positive—consistent with the directional claim that connected city leaders deliver faster growth—but it does not reach conventional statistical significance in this specification, so the result is inconclusive at the 5% level (though marginally significant at 10%).

dependent_variable: Ability class (top-quality vs lower-quality) of foreign players in the Danish first league
main_predictor: Post-1991 indicator (after introduction of the Researchers' Tax Scheme)
sample_definition: Foreign player-year observations in the Danish first league, 1985-2008 (from basesynthetic_control.dta)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 contingency table (pre/post reform x top/low quality)
operationalization_notes: The claim is about a change in the ability composition of foreigners in Denmark after the 1991 tax reform. Counts of top-quality (stop) and lower-quality (slow) foreigners in Denmark by year are taken directly from the paper's replication file; aggregating pre (1985-1990) and post (1991-2008) periods gives the simplest direct test of whether the composition shifted.
reasoning: Among foreigners in the Danish top league, the share who are top-quality (have appeared for their national team) rose from 4/24 = 16.7% in 1985-1990 to 195/364 = 53.6% in 1991-2008. A chi-square test on the 2x2 table (pre/post-1991 reform x top/low quality among foreigners) yields chi2(1)=10.84, p<0.001, confirming a shift in ability composition toward higher-ability players following the Danish foreigner tax cut.

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay
main_predictor: intrin_extrin (intrinsic minus extrinsic value endorsement)

dependent_variable: imports_post (post-dispute imports from partner, logged)

operationalization_notes: Targeted the paper's Model 2 (Early Settlements). The N matches exactly (6027) when using imports_post as DV on the earlysettle==1 subset with the listed controls; standard OLS without clustering.

Complainant countries see significantly greater post-settlement imports than non-complainant members, replicating the paper's discriminatory-gains result.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (rate of new business formation, GEM)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of working-age population 20-64)
sample_definition: GEM country-year panel, 1999-2010, all countries (n=393, 82 countries)

operationalization_notes: Replicated Table 2 column 3 from the published log: simplest specification directly testing the bivariate (within-year) relationship between median age and new business formation in the full GEM sample.

Lower median age is significantly associated with higher new business formation, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Perceived arm length / actual arm length ratio (RatioRight, RatioLeft)

sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (n=15)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test (RatioRight vs RatioLeft)

operationalization_notes: Used perceived/actual ratio to control for differences in true arm length; restricted to right-handers per the claim.
reasoning: Paired t-test among right-handed participants comparing the perceived-to-actual length ratio for the right arm vs left arm: right (M=0.970) > left (M=0.920), t(14)=2.12, p=.052. Directional effect matches the claim that right-handers perceive their right arm as longer (relative to actual) than their left.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (mean of appreciated, valued, satisfied items, 7-point)

dependent_variable: Standardized total midterm+final exam score (s_tot)

sample_definition: Female students (girl==1), excluding special-needs students (special1==0), with non-missing controls
