controls: Baseline score of self (s0_totx) and of 5 neighbors (avg5_s0_totx); age, mother's/father's education, baseline interest in Chinese/math/English, birth order (childnth)
operationalization_notes: Neighbor-5 corresponds to 'five surrounding students' in the claim. Following standard practice in the paper's tables, used random-assignment block fixed effects with classroom-clustered SEs; dropped special-needs students (whose seats were not randomized) to recover the paper's reported sample size (~245).
reasoning: Restricting to non-special female students and regressing standardized exam score on share-female among the 5 neighbors (with average baseline neighbor score, own baseline score and demographic controls plus class-row-block fixed effects, clustered by classroom), the share-female coefficient is 0.215 (SE 0.082, t=2.62, p=0.009, n=246). Going from 0 to 1 (5 males to 5 females) increases test scores by ~0.22 SD, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Absolute change in mean attitude from T1 to T2 (|att_T2 - att_T1|)
main_predictor: Mean attitude certainty (cert1-cert7) × objective ambivalence (Griffin formula from pos/neg)
sample_definition: Study 1 participants with complete attitude data at both time points and complete certainty/ambivalence ratings (N=174)
model_specification: OLS regression: change ~ certainty_c * ambivalence_c + extremity_c (all predictors mean-centered)
operationalization_notes: Followed the analytic approach the paper describes for the interaction test: hierarchical regression with mean-centered certainty and objective ambivalence, controlling for extremity. Objective ambivalence computed with Thompson/Griffin formula. Focused on Study 1 since the claim summarizes a result that the paper demonstrates within each study via this interaction.
reasoning: In Study 1 (organic foods), the certainty × objective ambivalence interaction significantly predicted absolute attitude change between T1 and T2, t(169)=2.28, p=.024, controlling for attitude extremity. The positive coefficient indicates that the traditional certainty-stability link (negative association with change) emerges as ambivalence decreases, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Voter turnout (% of registered voters) at national legislative elections
main_predictor: Foreign portfolio equity stock (log) — operationalization of foreign ownership
sample_definition: OECD election-year observations (rows with non-missing election indicator t) for the 23 countries, complete cases on covariates
model_specification: OLS panel regression with country fixed effects and lagged turnout (a static-LDV approximation of the paper's dynamic panel), clustered standard errors by country
controls: Lagged turnout, log registered voters, %VAP 30-69, years-since-last-election dummies, no-presidential-election dummy, compulsory voting, mixed system, PR system, disproportionality (disrel), effective number of parties, closeness of election
operationalization_notes: The methods section is redacted; I implemented a country-FE LDV specification close to Model 4 of Table 1, using logportequ as the principal foreign-ownership proxy because portfolio equity stock is the ownership variable highlighted in the paper's ownership-constraint analysis.
reasoning: In a country-fixed-effects election-level regression of voter turnout on the (logged) foreign portfolio equity stock with the lagged dependent variable and the paper's standard institutional and political controls (clustered SEs by country), the foreign-ownership coefficient is -1.43 with t = -3.65 (p<0.001, n=251 elections, 23 countries). Foreign ownership is significantly associated with lower turnout, consistent with the ownership-constraint hypothesis.

dependent_variable: Number of BBB service complaints in 2008 (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: Indicator that firm name begins with A or a number (first_A)
sample_definition: All 2,293 plumbing firms in final_data.dta with non-missing covariates
model_specification: Negative binomial regression with ln(employees) offset
operationalization_notes: Mirrors Table 5 column 3 specification, the headline test of the claim.
reasoning: In a negative binomial regression of 2008 service complaints on a 'name begins with A' indicator with controls for multiple names, ad spending, firm age, metro Chicago, and an ln(employees) offset, the coefficient on first_A is 0.72 (SE 0.25, z=2.91, p≈.004), indicating A-named plumbing firms receive significantly more complaints than other firms, replicating the paper's claim (Table 5, col. 3).

dependent_variable: Cooperative bargaining strategy (dv, ordered 0-3, with higher values indicating greater concessions/cooperation)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure (extent to which states value bargained issues differently)
sample_definition: All 588 state-bargaining observations in the replication dataset
model_specification: Ordered logistic regression (proxy for the paper's generalized ordered/partial proportional-odds logit) with the issue-linkage coefficient constrained equal across outcome categories
controls: ln(GDP), security/defense-policy issue, Euro state, new member state, agreement importance, parliamentary scrutiny, QMV, publicity, presidency, lagged DV
operationalization_notes: Methods section was redacted; based on Table 1, the paper estimates a (generalized) ordered logit of the 4-category cooperative strategy on these covariates. I report the z-statistic on issue_linkage_structure from a standard ordered logit, which most directly tests the claim that more differently valued issues lead to greater concessions.
reasoning: In an ordered logit of cooperative bargaining strategy (0-3) on the issue-linkage structure variable (which captures differential issue valuation) plus the paper's controls, issue_linkage_structure has a strongly positive coefficient (b=1.054, z=13.46, p<0.001, N=588). Higher differential valuation of issues thus predicts more cooperative/concessionary strategies, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Directed credit by domestic money banks to government and SOEs (% GDP) (credittogovtstateenterp)
main_predictor: State capacity, ICRG Quality of Government index (icrg_qog)
sample_definition: All country-years in the Country Year Dataset with non-missing directed credit, its one-year lag, IQG, private credit, and year (1972–2009 panel).
model_specification: Pooled dynamic OLS with one-year lagged dependent variable and a linear time trend, cluster-robust SEs by country (ccodecow).
controls: Lagged directed credit, private credit (% GDP), linear year time trend.
operationalization_notes: The paper's Table 1, column 1 specification (system-GMM) is the closest reported test of this claim; with the methods section redacted I implemented a transparent dynamic OLS analogue (lagged DV + time trend, clustered SEs) controlling for private credit as the profit-potential proxy, with state capacity as the main predictor. I did not attempt to replicate the system-GMM internal instruments.
reasoning: In a dynamic panel OLS regression of directed credit to govt./SOEs on its lag, state capacity (IQG), private credit (proxying the profit potential of financial repression), and a time trend, with country-clustered SEs, the coefficient on state capacity is -0.142 (t = -0.36, p ≈ 0.72) on 2,787 country-year observations. The sign is consistent with the paper's claim (weaker state capacity → more directed credit) but the effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero, so the claim does not robustly reproduce outside the system-GMM specification.

dependent_variable: originit — country-year indicator of MID initiation as originator
main_predictor: lcoupsum — lagged, log-weighted count of coup events (plotted/attempted/successful) as observable proxy for threats to political survival
sample_definition: All Latin American country-years 1960-99 with complete data on model variables (N = 798)
model_specification: Probit regression (single-equation, monadic; replicates the form of the paper's Table 5)
controls: Previous dispute (lagdisp), ethnic fractionalization, relative power (CINC), number of borders, log number of allies, regional conflict, lagged polity score, lagged log real GDP per capita
operationalization_notes: The redacted methods section prevented exact replication of the Maddala two-stage (cdsimeq) procedure used in Table 3 because the first-stage instrument set is not identified in the data. I therefore committed to the simplest probit specification that uses the same dependent variable and controls and an observable measure of coup threat (lcoupsum) — exactly the design described in Table 5 of the paper. Log-likelihood (-264.1) and N (798) match the paper's Table 3 sample, confirming the variables/sample were correctly identified.
reasoning: In a probit model of MID initiation (originator) on lagged log coup events plus the same controls used in the paper's Tables 3-5, the coefficient on coup events is -0.111 (z = -0.80, p = 0.42, N = 798). The data therefore do not support the claim that increased threats to political survival raise the likelihood of conflict involvement when estimated without the paper's endogeneity correction; this matches the negative/non-significant result the authors themselves report in Table 5, even though their preferred simultaneous-equations specification (Table 3) finds a positive effect.

dependent_variable: d12outgroup: euros (0–5) sent by Serb dictator to Albanian recipient
main_predictor: Region of residence (Primarily Albanian, Border, Primarily Serb) — proxy for exposure to out-group
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb participants in the dictator experiment
model_specification: OLS regression with region dummies; joint F-test on the two region dummies
operationalization_notes: Claim is operationalized as the effect of out-group exposure (region) on altruism toward Albanians. Used the paper's baseline (no-controls) specification (Table 2, Model 3) and report the joint F-test on region dummies.
reasoning: OLS regression of amount sent to out-group (0–5 euros) on region dummies (Primarily Albanian, Border; reference = Primarily Serb) yields F(2,155)=9.26, p<0.001. Serbs in the Primarily Albanian region give 1.49 euros more (p<0.001) than Serbs in the segregated Primarily Serb region, consistent with the claim that out-group bridging increases with exposure to the out-group.

dependent_variable: enjoyrelativ (self-reported relative enjoyment of the program)
main_predictor: condition (commercial-interrupted 'good' vs. uninterrupted 'no')
sample_definition: All Study 2 participants with non-missing enjoyrelativ (n=102; 53 interrupted, 49 uninterrupted)
model_specification: Two-sample independent t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: Directly compared the enjoyment rating between the two between-subjects conditions of Study 2 since the claim concerns the effect of commercial interruption on program enjoyment.
reasoning: Participants in the commercial-interrupted condition reported higher relative enjoyment (M=5.38) than those in the uninterrupted condition (M=4.47); independent-samples t-test t(100)=2.45, p=.016, consistent with the claim that commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable.

dependent_variable: resigninvest (4-point belief Swensen resigned because of the bribery investigation; 1=not likely at all to 4=very likely)
main_predictor: Experimental condition: denial vs. causal correction (innuendo = reference category)
sample_definition: Respondents assigned to innuendo, denial, or causal-correction conditions who answered the resigninvest item (control condition excluded because the item was only asked of those exposed to the rumor); N=764
model_specification: IPW-weighted OLS (WLS using inverse-probability-of-treatment weights 'aw'): resigninvest ~ denial + causal; linear contrast test of causal − denial = 0
controls: None (treatment dummies only, IPW weights account for block-randomization probabilities)

dependent_variable: Bagrut certification (zakaibag, 0/1)

The direction and magnitude match the paper's reported ~10 percentage-point gain in girls' certification.

dependent_variable: Intrafirm import share (imp_rel/(imp_rel+imp_non)) at IO2002 sector × year level

dependent_variable: bid_on_d (PAP applies to BMO)

reasoning: Probit of PAP-applies-to-BMO on child attribute dummies (with year FE and PAP-type dummies), clustered by mother_id, yields a positive and significant coefficient on Non-African-American girl (β=0.189, z=2.76, p=0.006), confirming PAPs' positive preference for non-AA girls.

dependent_variable: a-insensitivity index a = 1 - 3*(mean(m_composite) - mean(m_single)) computed per subject per part

reasoning: Regressing the a-insensitivity index on indicators for Part1*TP, Part2*control, Part2*TP (reference: Part1*control) with subject-clustered SEs gives a Part1*TP coefficient of 0.204 (SE 0.089, z=2.29, p=0.022), indicating significantly higher ambiguity insensitivity for the TP-administered questions, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Civil war duration in months (durationmonths)
main_predictor: Conflict technology (Irregular vs. Conventional [base] vs. SNC)

operationalization_notes: The paper's Table reporting duration (M1, TR) uses a Weibull regression with the three technology categories. I replicated the bivariate specification on the conflict-level TR dataset to directly test whether irregular wars last longer than conventional and SNC wars.
reasoning: In a Weibull AFT model of civil-war duration (months) with conflict-technology dummies (conventional = baseline), the irregular coefficient is 1.08 (SE 0.21), z = 5.23, p < 0.001, indicating irregular wars last roughly exp(1.08) ≈ 2.95× longer than conventional, and longer than SNC (whose coefficient is small and insignificant). This reproduces the paper's finding that irregular conflicts last longer than the other types.

dependent_variable: Log monthly mortality rate (lndrate)
main_predictor: Days with mean temperature >90°F (cumulative current + 1-month lag) interacted with a post-1960 indicator
sample_definition: State-year-month observations from 1931-2004 (1930 dropped due to lag and 1929 cutoff for income); non-missing temperature, mortality, income, and precipitation variables
model_specification: Weighted (state population) OLS with three temperature bin variables (days <40°F, 80-89°F, >90°F; reference = 40-79°F) entered for current and lagged month, each interacted with post-1960; state-by-month and year-by-month fixed effects, state-by-month quadratic time trends; SEs clustered on state
controls: Precipitation deviation indicators (devp25, devp75), month-specific log per capita income interactions, state-by-month and year-by-month FEs, state-by-month linear and quadratic time trends
operationalization_notes: Closely mirrors Table 4 row 1 baseline specification: 3 temperature bins, 2-month exposure window (current + lag), baseline covariates. Reports the t-statistic on the post-1960 interaction for the cumulative >90°F effect, which directly tests whether the high-temperature-mortality link declined across decades.
reasoning: The pre-1960 cumulative effect of an extra day >90°F on log monthly mortality is 0.0209 (SE 0.0086), while the post-1960 cumulative effect is essentially zero (-0.0016). The post-pre difference is -0.0225 (SE 0.0101), t = -2.23, p = .026, confirming a statistically significant decline in the temperature-mortality relationship across decades, consistent with the paper's claim (Table 4, row 1).

dependent_variable: Binary purchase intent (would buy DVD set vs. not)
main_predictor: Opportunity-cost cue × connectedness-to-future-self (ZFINAL) interaction
sample_definition: All 88 participants in DVD_data with non-missing cue, connectedness, and purchase intent

operationalization_notes: Claim states opportunity-cost cues reduce spending primarily for those high in future-self connectedness; this is the cue × connectedness interaction on purchase. Followed paper's coding convention (-1/+1 for cue; z-scored connectedness).
reasoning: Logistic regression of purchase intent on opportunity-cost cue (effect coded -1/1), z-scored connectedness to future self (ZFINAL), and their interaction yields a significant negative interaction (b = -0.525, z = -2.10, p = .036, N = 88). The cue depresses purchasing more strongly at higher connectedness, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: REF_female (referral is female, 1/0)
main_predictor: OP_female (CA gender)
sample_definition: CAs assigned to the either-gender referral treatment who made a referral (treat_either==1 & REF_female not missing)
model_specification: Two-sample proportion z-test (statsmodels proportions_ztest)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether male CAs refer women less often than female CAs; this is most directly tested in the either-gender (unrestricted) treatment, comparing the proportion of female referrals by CA gender.
reasoning: Among CAs in the either-gender treatment who made a referral, 22.6% of male CAs' referrals were women vs 42.5% of female CAs' referrals (z=-3.15, p=0.002), confirming CA men are less likely to refer women than CA women.

dependent_variable: ALI mathematics test score (ali_stdscore, with copying adjustment)
main_predictor: Treatment arm T3 (ALI: aligned incentives for students, math teachers, and administrators) vs. control
sample_definition: All students with non-missing ALI math scores across grades 10-12 in years 1-3 from the table_7 files
model_specification: OLS regression: score ~ T1 + T2 + T3 + grade FE + year FE, with cluster-robust SEs at the school (clavecct) level
controls: Grade fixed effects, year fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Pooled the nine grade-by-year datasets used in Table 7 to obtain a single overall test of the T3 effect on the copying-adjusted ALI score. Used the same outcome the paper highlights (ali_stdscore) and clustered SEs at the school level (the unit of randomization).
reasoning: Pooling ALI test scores across all three grades and three years and regressing on treatment dummies with grade and year fixed effects (SEs clustered at the school level), the T3 (ALI) treatment increases scores by 63.3 points relative to controls (z=4.05, p<0.001), versus 39.6 for T1 (students only) and 4.9 (n.s.) for T2 (teachers only). This replicates the paper's finding that providing aligned incentives to students, teachers, and administrators raised test scores.

dependent_variable: Subject-level mean of the upper-bound log discount rate across the four intertemporal choice tasks (small/large stake x short/long horizon); lower = more patient
main_predictor: treatE (ethnic-identity salience treatment indicator)
sample_definition: Experiment 1 Asian-American subjects only (raceA == 1)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test comparing treatE=1 vs treatE=0
operationalization_notes: The paper's tests use interval (Tobit) regressions on per-task log-discount-rate intervals; as a single, directly interpretable subject-level test of the claim I averaged each subject's upper-bound log discount rate across the four tasks (the upper bound is always observed, unlike the lower bound for left-censored choices) and compared treated vs control Asians with a t-test.
reasoning: Among Asian-American subjects (N=71), those primed with ethnic identity (treatE=1) had a substantially lower mean log discount rate (-3.24) than the control group (-2.28), Welch t(69)=3.85, p<0.001, indicating more patient intertemporal choices in line with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Subject-level mean cooperation frequency (% of time cooperating, averaged over supergames)
main_predictor: Horizon termination rule (Short-Deterministic vs Short-Stochastic)
sample_definition: All subjects in conditions 3 (Short-Deterministic) and 4 (Short-Stochastic); 48 subjects per condition, averaged across all supergames
model_specification: Mann-Whitney U test (two-sided) on subject-level mean cooperation frequencies
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns a marginal comparison between two treatments. Using a nonparametric rank-sum test on subject-level averages (subject ID disambiguated by session) avoids distributional assumptions and approximates the paper's typical inference across treatments.
reasoning: Subject-level mean cooperation frequency is higher in Short-Deterministic (63.3%) than Short-Stochastic (52.3%). Mann-Whitney U = 1565 (n1=n2=48), two-sided p ≈ 0.0025, corresponding to z ≈ 3.02, supporting the claim that cooperation is significantly higher under deterministic than stochastic horizon in short-duration treatments.

dependent_variable: Ideological distance between the plurality (largest vote-share) party and the median voter (pldist1, manifesto-based)
main_predictor: Election rule: SMD vs PR (smd)
sample_definition: All election-level observations in Powell's dataset with non-missing plurality-party distance and election-rule code (n=329)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test of group means (SMD vs PR)
operationalization_notes: The claim specifies that under SMD, the plurality winner is close to the median voter. The most direct test is whether the plurality party's distance to the median voter (pldist1) is smaller under SMD than under PR. A two-sample t-test contrasts these means without additional controls.
reasoning: Welch t-test comparing plurality-party ideological distance to the median voter under SMD (M=11.40, n=85) vs PR (M=11.07, n=244) yields t(181.0)=0.28, p=.78. SMD plurality winners are not significantly closer (in fact slightly further) from the median voter, so the data do not support the claim.

dependent_variable: nwar1 — recurrence of civil war following the first postconflict election (binary)

sample_definition: 98 postconflict cases from iDOSERESPONSE_fpebase.dta (cases with a definitive end-of-war and an observed FPE, merged with covariates from BS09_DATA_main.dta)

controls: FPE level (national), FPE level (concurrent), Polity IV at FPE, post-cold war era, victory, UN intervention, UN electoral assistance, previous civil wars
operationalization_notes: Replicates the baseline specification of Brancati & Snyder's Table 1, col. 1 (FPE sample, no power-sharing controls). Tested the directional claim via the sign and significance of the election-timing coefficient in a logit on renewed war.
reasoning: Logit regression of renewed civil war (nwar1) on months until first postconflict election (T2fpemths1) plus the paper's baseline controls yields a coefficient of -0.0052 (SE 0.005, z=-1.07, p=0.28) on N=98. The sign is consistent with the claim (longer wait until election → less renewed fighting, equivalently sooner elections → more fighting), but the effect is not statistically significant in this baseline specification.

dependent_variable: Femininity index (mean of three feminine trait ratings: items 25, 26, 33)
main_predictor: Target's behavior (Green vs. Nongreen)
sample_definition: All 194 study-2 participants; each rated one of four targets (Male/Female x Green/Nongreen)
model_specification: 2x2 between-subjects ANOVA (target gender x green behavior) on the femininity index; F reported for the green main effect

operationalization_notes: Methods section was redacted, so the three feminine items were identified by matching the paper-reported reliability (α=.80) and condition means (M_G=2.64, M_NG=1.82) across all 3-item combinations of the 9 candidate trait items; items 25, 26, 33 exactly reproduced these statistics.
reasoning: In a 2 (target gender) x 2 (green vs nongreen behavior) ANOVA on the 3-item femininity index (items 25, 26, 33; α=.80), the main effect of green vs nongreen behavior was significant: F(1,190)=43.59, p<.001. Green targets were rated more feminine (M=2.64, SD=.90, N=94) than nongreen targets (M=1.82, SD=.86, N=100), matching the paper's reported F(1,190)=44.00.

dependent_variable: Number of stochastic-dominance violations in the 10-decision LV format (errors = 10 - number of dominant lotteries chosen, where the RV lottery dominates for decisions 1-4 and the PV lottery dominates for decisions 5-10)
main_predictor: Degree of risk aversion = average number of safe choices made in the PV and RV multiple-price-list formats
sample_definition: All 106 actual subjects (two experimenter-controlled stations with age=99 excluded, per the README)
model_specification: Spearman rank correlation test (two-sided)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns a monotonic association between error rate and risk aversion, and Figure 4 / footnote 19 of the paper explicitly reports the Spearman (and Pearson) correlation between these two subject-level measures across all subjects. I therefore replicated that subject-level Spearman correlation.

The strong, highly significant negative correlation supports the claim that decision error decreases with risk aversion.

dependent_variable: Desired yearly compensation (in $1,000s; midpoint of selected bracket)

A two-sample t-test (equal variances) yields t(58)=2.13, p=0.037, confirming that single females reported lower desired salaries when classmates would see their answers.

dependent_variable: pay_for_conditionality (dummy: willing to pay a positive amount to keep CCT)

dependent_variable: Monthly count of homicides of males aged 15–39 (proxy for DTO-related violence)

reasoning: Negative binomial regression on the subsample of municipalities where a DTO leader was captured (Dec 2006–Dec 2010) yields a positive and highly significant coefficient on the 1–6 month post-leader-capture indicator (b=0.312, SE=0.083, z=3.75, p<0.001), corresponding to roughly a 37% short-term increase in DTO-related homicides. This replicates the paper's claim of an exacerbating short-term effect of leadership beheadings on DTO violence.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of bootstrapped partial semantic networks
main_predictor: Openness-to-experience group (high vs. low; median split on composite z-score of NEO-FFI-3 openness and BFAS Openness/Intellect)

operationalization_notes: Followed the partial-bootstrapped network procedure described in the paper (Table 3). reasoning: At 90% node retention partial bootstrap (1000 iterations per group), the high-openness group's semantic network had a significantly lower ASPL (M=1.691) than the low-openness group (M=1.757), Welch t(1998)=115.17, p<.001, Cohen's d≈5.15. dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Index (ciri_physint)

operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 2 column (6) of the paper, the central specification cited for this claim.
reasoning: In an ordered probit of CIRI Physical Integrity Index on reliance on taxes with the paper's controls and a lagged DV, the tax reliance coefficient is 0.0056 (SE 0.0019), z=2.98, p=0.003, indicating higher tax reliance is associated with better human rights protection, matching the original study's column (6) finding.

dependent_variable: GCSE pass rate: percent of pupils achieving 5+ grades A*-C (pt_gcse_5_a_c)
main_predictor: gm_win (indicator that the GM ballot passed / school converted to grant-maintained status)
sample_definition: School-year observations from main_data.dta for years strictly after each school's GM ballot (year > base), with non-missing pass rate, base pass rate, and gm_win

controls: Pre-vote (base) pass rate and year fixed effects

Schools whose ballots passed (and thus converted to grant-maintained status) had pass rates about 3.4 percentage points higher than non-converters, consistent with Clark's claim of large achievement gains.

dependent_variable: Participated (lab) [0/1]

dependent_variable: took_act (illness treated with an ACT)

reasoning: In the first-illness-episode sample (excluding RDT-arm and ex-post households), assignment to the 92% ACT subsidy raises the probability of taking an ACT by 25.4 percentage points (SE=0.054, cluster-robust by household; z=4.68, p<0.001) above the 19% control mean — i.e., a very high subsidy more than doubles ACT access, matching the paper's directional claim.

dependent_variable: Standardized average of PIAT math, reading recognition, and reading comprehension scores
main_predictor: Real total family income in $1,000s (earned+unearned+nontaxable, CPI-deflated)
sample_definition: All child-year observations in main.dta with non-missing combined PIAT score, income, and control covariates

controls: Male, black, hispanic, other race, child age and age squared, number of adults, mother married, mother's grandparents' education (hgcbym79, hgcbyf79), mother's AFQT, lived with both parents at age 14
operationalization_notes: The IV instrument (predicted EITC) is not directly available in the data and reproducing the simulator is infeasible; I therefore use the most directly related OLS levels specification (cf. Table 2 col 1), which tests the same directional claim about income raising test scores in the short run.
reasoning: OLS regression of standardized combined math-reading PIAT score on real total family income (in $1,000s) with demographic controls yields a positive, highly significant coefficient of 0.0125 (clustered SE 0.0016, t=7.98, N=25,270). A $1,000 increase in family income is associated with about 1.25% of a SD higher test scores, supporting the directional claim (though smaller than the IV estimate of ~6% in the paper).

dependent_variable: General work absorption (engwkabs)
main_predictor: Single childless dummy (singchild1: 1=single childless, 0=other family structures)

operationalization_notes: Claim is directly comparative between single-childless vs other family structures on absorption; used the general absorption variable (person-level) with a simple between-group t-test as the most direct test.
reasoning: Single childless workers reported significantly lower general absorption (M=4.01, n=86) than those with other family structures (M=4.39, n=277); Welch t(123.6)=-2.76, p=.007.

dependent_variable: ProperName (greeted by proper name, 0/1)
main_predictor: Treatment group: Hispanic vs White (pooled male/female)
sample_definition: Emails in Hispanic or White treatment groups with non-missing ProperName (i.e., responding emails coded for greeting)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2)
operationalization_notes: Claim directly contrasts Hispanic vs white applicants on being greeted by name. Used ProperName indicator and pooled gender within each race condition.
reasoning: Among emails that received a response with name data available, Hispanic applicants were greeted by name 41.2% (77/187) of the time vs 62.0% (49/79) for white applicants; chi-square test of independence yields chi2(1)=9.68, p=0.002, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Session-level frequency of normal quality (qualityc==2) in the good state of nature (1 - shading rate)

sample_definition: Baseline treatment (condition==1), trades only (qualityc != -1), good state (costc in {20,25}); aggregated to 5 session-level paired observations by contract type
model_specification: One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired session averages (rigid > flexible normal quality)
operationalization_notes: Follows the paper's stated nonparametric session-level signed-rank approach (footnote 16). Shading is operationalized as (1 - share of normal quality) among traded contracts in the good state, since rigid contracts do not produce trade in the bad state.
reasoning: Per-session frequency of normal quality (1 - shading) in the good state is ~94% in rigid contracts vs ~75% in flexible contracts across all 5 baseline sessions. A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on these 5 paired session averages yields W=15, p=0.03125, indicating significantly less shading in rigid contracts.

dependent_variable: log(state CO2 emissions, adjusted)
main_predictor: log(average weekly working hours)
sample_definition: 50 U.S. states, years 2007-2013 (N=350)
model_specification: OLS with state fixed effects on logged variables (scale/Model 1 specification)

The negative coefficient on log discount rate means more patient choices when ethnic identity is salient, replicating the paper.

dependent_variable: Mean cooperation frequency (% of time cooperating) per subject across all supergames

dependent_variable: Plurality party ideological distance from median voter (pldist1, manifesto-based)

controls: polity2, s_un_reg (foreign-policy similarity), cap_2 (target power), pwrratio, postArt56, postCW, prgmyrs, NCAnosafetodate (nuclear assistance), cap_1 (attacker power), contig, noconsideryrs and three peace-year splines

reasoning: In a logit regression of 'consider' (state seriously considering attacking another state's nuclear program) on prior violent militarized conflict (hostileMID) with the controls described in the paper (target polity, foreign-policy similarity, target/attacker power, power ratio, Article 56, post-Cold War, program years, nuclear assistance, contiguity, plus peace-years splines), the coefficient on violent conflict is 2.84 (SE=0.26, z=11.09, p<.0001). This positive, highly significant effect mirrors the paper's finding that prior violent conflict increases the salience of the proliferation threat.

dependent_variable: splinter (county broke away to form a new district, 1/0)
main_predictor: DEC share ratio (county's share of seats on the District Executive Committee divided by its population share)
sample_definition: County-electoral-wave observations from Ugandan post-1996 waves with non-missing covariates (excludes baseline wave 0).

controls: Ethnic minority indicator, development summary index (mean of economic and social-services indices), number of counties in the district, breakup lag, region dummies (Eastern/Northern/Western, Central reference), and electoral-wave dummies.
operationalization_notes: Modeled the paper's M1-style specification: probability that a county splinters off as a function of DEC seat-share ratio (political marginalization) plus ethnic and development marginalization and structural controls. The negative, highly significant coefficient on DEC share ratio is the test most directly tied to the political-marginalization claim.
reasoning: In a logistic regression predicting whether a county became a splinter (formed its own new district) on the political-marginalization measure (county DEC seat-share ratio relative to its population share), the coefficient is -0.724 (SE 0.193, z=-3.75, p<0.001), controlling for ethnic minority status, a development index, number of counties in the district, breakup lag, region, and electoral wave. Lower political representation (greater marginalization) is associated with higher probability of secession, replicating the paper's finding.

dependent_variable: recog1dum (State B recognizes State A, dichotomous)
main_predictor: nukeduma (State A has nuclear weapons capability)

operationalization_notes: Replicated the dichotomous diplomatic-recognition logit in Table 2 column 1 of the paper as the analysis most directly tied to the claim.
reasoning: Logit of dichotomous diplomatic recognition (State B recognizes State A) on Nuclear Weapons A yields coefficient 0.815 (SE 0.029, z=27.68, p<0.001), indicating nuclear-capable states are significantly more likely to be recognized — consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Log absolute opinion change in immigration position (wave 3 - wave 2)
main_predictor: Group-level deliberative quality – level of justification (DQ_jlev)
sample_definition: 174 EuroPolis participants in 13 discussion groups with complete data on outcome, predictor, and controls
model_specification: Multilevel linear regression (REML) with individuals nested in small groups
controls: gender, age, education, Catholic, Protestant, working class, religiosity, left-right ideology + squared term, left/right party vote intent, knowledge change, clarify-thinking items (participants/experts/politicians/briefing), social conformity pressure above/below
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 2 Model 2b: directly tests whether group-level justification rationality predicts magnitude of immigration opinion change, the specific test tied to the claim.
reasoning: Multilevel REML model of log absolute opinion change on immigration (waves 2→3) with individuals nested in 13 small groups, including Sanders-style controls, yields a coefficient of 0.130 (SE 0.066, z=1.96, p≈0.049) for group-level deliberative justification (DQ_jlev). Higher group justification predicts greater opinion change, replicating the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Average effort (work, binary per period) per subject across all periods
main_predictor: Reward scheme: discriminating (345) vs. symmetric (444)
sample_definition: All subjects in the two complementarity (COM) treatments: 345COM and 444COM
model_specification: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U test comparing subject-level mean effort between the two reward schemes
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the COM (complementarity) production technology and contrasts the symmetric (444) vs. discriminating (345) bonus schemes. I collapsed binary period-level work decisions to a subject-level mean to obtain independent observations and used a nonparametric rank-sum test, the natural test for this between-subjects comparison.
reasoning: Under complementarity, average effort per subject was higher in the discriminating 345COM scheme (mean work = 0.917, n=36) than in the symmetric 444COM scheme (mean = 0.722, n=33). A Mann-Whitney U test rejects equality (U=795, z=2.41, p=0.007), supporting the claim that the symmetric scheme elicits substantially lower efforts under complementarity.

dependent_variable: Difference in proportion of anti- vs pro-immigration actions cited in the senator's reply letter
main_predictor: Constituent letter type (pro- vs anti-immigration) — within-senator
sample_definition: 56 senators who responded to both pro- and anti-immigration constituent letters
model_specification: Paired (within-senator) t-test on (companti − comppro) across letter type
operationalization_notes: The 'tailoring to audience' claim is most directly tested by Table 1: do senators mention different action profiles when writing back to pro- vs anti-immigration constituents? Using the same audience as their own control via a paired test isolates within-senator tailoring.
reasoning: Among the 56 senators who responded to both the pro- and anti-immigration constituent letters, the (anti-action mentions minus pro-action mentions) score was significantly higher in replies to anti-immigration constituents (0.429) than in replies to pro-immigration constituents (0.196). Paired t(55)=3.45, p=0.001, indicating senators tailor the policy actions they highlight to the constituent's expressed view.

dependent_variable: log(post-migration U.S. wage / pre-migration home wage), both PPP-adjusted
main_predictor: Education category dummies (No HS [<9 yrs], Some HS [9-11], HS grad [12], Some college [13-15], College grad [16+] as base)
sample_definition: All MMP/LAMP immigrants with positive pre- and post-migration adjusted wages in the provided wage_gain_table.xlsx (N=2,854; 10 Latin American/Caribbean source countries, dominated by Mexico).
model_specification: OLS of log wage gain on education-category dummies with country fixed effects; t-test on the 'No HS' coefficient (i.e., No HS vs. College graduate).
operationalization_notes: Paper's Table III is the regression most directly tied to the claim. Only MMP microdata are present in the public archive (NIS micro-data are not). I therefore re-run the same specification on the available MMP subsample. Education cutoffs follow standard U.S. schooling categories used in the paper (no HS = <9 years).
reasoning: Regressing the log wage gain at migration on education-category dummies (college graduate = base) and country fixed effects on the MMP wage-gain microdata yields a coefficient of 0.197 (SE 0.129) on the 'no high school' category, t = 1.52, p = 0.13. The sign matches the paper's claim (those with no high school gain more than college graduates), but in this subsample alone the difference is not statistically significant. The paper's reported 0.599 effect relies on the pooled NIS+MMP sample of N=3,539; the NIS micro-data are not present in this archive, so I cannot reproduce that pooled estimate.

dependent_variable: Proportion of free-association responses matching learned target (FAbaseC vs FAsuppC)
main_predictor: Item type (baseline vs suppressed) within nonruminators
sample_definition: Nonruminators only (Group==1), N=27, from Experiment 2 (free-association transfer task)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing baseline vs suppressed proportions
operationalization_notes: The claim is that nonruminators show a benefit of suppression on transfer tasks. The most direct test in the Ashley dataset (Experiment 2 free-association test) is the within-subject baseline vs suppressed contrast restricted to nonruminators.
reasoning: Among nonruminators, the proportion of free-association responses matching the learned target was significantly lower for suppressed cues (M=29.63) than for baseline cues (M=45.68), paired t(26)=3.03, p=.0055, indicating suppression-induced forgetting — i.e., a benefit of suppression practice on this indirect transfer task, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being (CES-D short, recoded so higher = better) — variable 'wellbeing'
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction of parental status (childless / lives with children / empty nest, childless = ref.) with country-level standardized disapproval of childlessness ('childless_disapp_std')
sample_definition: ESS3 respondents aged 40+ from 24 countries in the prepared replication dataset, with missing==0 and non-missing values on all model variables (N = 23,754; men and women pooled)
model_specification: Multilevel linear regression (random intercept by country) via statsmodels MixedLM, MLE
controls: Age, age², marital status, education, parents' education (incl. missing dummy), religious attendance, paid employment, born in country, gender
operationalization_notes: The paper's table reports gender-separated models with the country-level 'percent (strongly) disapproves' moderator. The replication file does not contain a percent-disapproves variable (childless_perc is the % childless, not % disapprove), but it contains 'childless_disapp_std', a country-level standardized aggregate of disapproval that is invariant within country. I therefore used that as the country-level moderator and pooled genders (adding a gender dummy) to obtain a single test statistic directly tied to the claim. Higher childless_disapp_std = less tolerant; the positive parents-vs-childless × disapproval interaction means the childless disadvantage is smaller in tolerant countries.
reasoning: In a two-level (individuals nested in 24 countries) random-intercept linear model of psychological well-being on parental status × country-level disapproval-of-childlessness (standardized), with the paper's individual controls and gender, the cross-level interaction Lives-with-children × country disapproval is positive and significant (B = 0.055, SE = 0.012, z = 4.52, p < .001). This means parents' well-being advantage over the childless grows as country-level disapproval rises — equivalently, the childless disadvantage shrinks in more tolerant countries, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: DSM5_Total (total psychopathology score)
main_predictor: Mini-K total (life-history strategy; higher = slower)
sample_definition: All participants with complete Mini-K and DSM5 totals (N=138)
model_specification: Pearson correlation between Mini-K and DSM5 totals
operationalization_notes: Mini-K is the primary LHS measure (higher = slower); DSM5 total indexes general psychopathology. A negative correlation indicates faster LHS = more psychopathology.
reasoning: Pearson r = -.587 (t(136) = -8.46, p < .001, N = 138) between Mini-K (slow life history score) and DSM-5 total psychopathology. Lower (faster) life-history scores are associated with greater psychopathology, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (political knowledge test score)
main_predictor: Stereotypaktivierung condition (0=not activated vs. 2=activated by gender difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender==1) in conditions 0 and 2 of Study 2
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: Claim contrasts the first vs. third experimental conditions for female participants in Study 2 on the political knowledge composite score (PolWis_score).
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test comparing female participants in the 'stereotype not activated' condition (n=76, M=8.33, SD=4.84) vs. 'stereotype activated by gender difference statement' (n=81, M=7.17, SD=4.20) yielded t(155)=1.60, p=.11. The direction matches the claim (control > stereotype-activated) but the difference is not statistically significant.

dependent_variable: GDP growth rate at t+2 (f2gdpidx)
main_predictor: City leader (city party secretary OR mayor) connected to incumbent provincial secretary (binary; =1 if either msec2currentsec or mayor2currentsec equals 1)
sample_definition: City-year panel 2000-2011 with non-missing values on all variables; observations dropped where city/province-year FE absorb variation
model_specification: Two-way fixed effects OLS: f2gdpidx_{it} = beta*connected_{it} + X_{it}gamma + alpha_i + delta_{p,t} + e, with city fixed effects and province-year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by city
controls: City economic controls (loggdp, logpop, govsize, growrev, startmsec/mayor_loggdp, startmsec/mayor_gdpidx) and city leader controls (msec/mayor tenure, education, prov/central/county/SOE/league experience)
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's stated design: t+2 GDP growth as DV (matches Table 1 horizon used elsewhere), connection indicator combining city secretary and mayor ties to incumbent provincial secretary, two-way (city and province-year) FE, with city economic and city-leader controls, SE clustered at city.
reasoning: The coefficient on the 'connected to incumbent provincial secretary' indicator is positive (b=0.236 percentage points of GDP growth at t+2; SE=0.139) and in the direction claimed by the paper, but only marginally significant (t=1.70, p=0.090, clustered at city; N=3,727). At conventional thresholds, this does not constitute a statistically significant performance premium.

dependent_variable: Counts of foreign players in Denmark by ability (top-quality vs lower-quality), where top-quality = ever played for home national team
main_predictor: Pre- vs post-1991 Danish 'Researchers' Tax Scheme reform period
sample_definition: Foreign players in the Danish first league, 1985-2008 (pre-period 1985-1990 vs post-period 1991-2008)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 contingency table (period x ability category)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the change in ability composition (not levels) of foreign players in Denmark after the 1991 tax reform. The most direct test is whether the top-quality vs lower-quality share among foreigners differs pre vs post the reform. Counts are taken from the paper's synthetic-control dataset (basesynthetic_control.dta), restricted to Denmark; stop and slow denote counts of top and lower-quality foreign players.
reasoning: Among foreigners in the Danish first league, the share of top-quality players (those who played for their national team) rose from 4/24 = 17% pre-reform (1985-1990) to 195/364 = 54% post-reform (1991-2008). A 2x2 chi-square test of independence rejects the null of identical top/low composition pre vs post (chi2(1)=10.84, p=0.001), consistent with the paper's claim that the Danish tax cut shifted the composition of foreigners toward higher-ability players.

dependent_variable: Willingness to pay (mean of 3 items)
main_predictor: Intrinsic relative to extrinsic values (I/E)
sample_definition: All Study 1 participants with non-missing I/E and WTP (n=155)
model_specification: Pearson product-moment correlation
operationalization_notes: The claim is the bivariate association; Table 1 reports the Pearson r between I/E and WTP, so I computed this same correlation on the Study 1 SPSS file.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between intrinsic relative to extrinsic values (I/E) and willingness to pay in Study 1 was r=.43, t(153)=5.83, p<.001, supporting that higher I/E is associated with higher WTP.

dependent_variable: ln_imports (log of partner imports from defendant)
main_predictor: Complainant indicator (partner is the complainant in the dispute)
sample_definition: Observations from disputes that ended in early settlement (earlysettle==1), with non-missing covariates
model_specification: OLS with cluster-robust SEs at the dispute level
controls: Defendant GDP (ln), Partner GDP (ln), Democratic Pair, Lagged Disputed Imports (imports_tminus1), Total Imports (ln)
operationalization_notes: Replicates the paper's Model 2 (early-settlement subsample) using the variables available in the replication dataset; N differs from paper (paper reports 6,027), likely due to additional sample restrictions in the redacted methods section, but the coefficient sign and significance match.
reasoning: Restricting to product-level observations associated with early-settlement disputes and regressing ln(imports) on the complainant dummy plus the paper's controls (defendant GDP, partner GDP, democratic pair, lagged disputed imports, total imports), with dispute-clustered SEs, the complainant indicator has coefficient 0.183 (SE 0.083), z=2.21, p=0.027. Complainants gain significantly more from early settlements than other WTO members, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (GEM entrepreneurship-to-wage-employment rate)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of working-age population 20-64)
sample_definition: GEM country-year panel, 82 countries, 2001-2010, 393 country-year observations with non-missing key variables
model_specification: Weighted least squares with year fixed effects; cluster-robust SE by countryid
controls: Year fixed effects only (matches Table 2 col. 3 specification)
operationalization_notes: Replicated the baseline median-age specification (Table 2, col. 3) from the deposited Stata log, which directly tests the claim that lower median age raises new business formation.
reasoning: Regressing the entrepreneurship rate (entre_wage) on country median age (20-64) with year fixed effects, population (nobs_cy) weights, and standard errors clustered by country (82 clusters) yields a coefficient of -0.00732 on median age with t = -5.71, indicating that a lower median age is significantly associated with higher new business formation, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Perceived/actual arm-length ratio (RatioRight, RatioLeft)
main_predictor: Arm (right vs. left), within-subject
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (Handedness == 1; n = 15)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing RatioRight to RatioLeft
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's approach of comparing perceived-to-actual length ratios between right and left arms within right-handers; this is the test most directly tied to the claim that right-handers perceive their right arm as longer than their left.
reasoning: Paired t-test on perceived/actual arm-length ratios for the 15 right-handed participants yielded t(14) = -0.82, p = .43. Mean RatioRight = 0.978 vs. RatioLeft = 0.993, i.e., the right arm was, if anything, perceived as slightly more underestimated than the left — opposite to the paper's reported direction and not statistically significant.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (mean of appreciated, valued, satisfied; 7-pt)
main_predictor: condition (verbal acknowledgment vs. 5-cent financial acknowledgment)
sample_definition: Study 1a participants who completed the study (exclude=0); n=49
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test

reasoning: Verbal acknowledgment (M=5.57) yielded significantly higher appreciation/value/satisfaction index than 5-cent financial acknowledgment (M=4.38); t(47)=2.92, p=.005, consistent with the trivialization claim.

dependent_variable: s_tot (mean of standardized midterm and final exam scores)
main_predictor: avg5_girl (share of female neighbor-5 peers, i.e., desk mate plus 4 neighbors)
sample_definition: Female students (girl==1) with random seat assignment (special1==0); complete cases on covariates
model_specification: OLS with block (gcb) fixed effects; SEs clustered by classroom (gc)
controls: baseline test score, desk-mate favored indicator, share favored among neighbor 4, height, age, birth order, mother's & father's education, baseline interest in Chinese/math/English, block FE
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's eq. (2) setup; used avg5_girl directly because the claim concerns being surrounded by 5 females versus 5 males (desk mate + 4 neighbors).
reasoning: For female students (excluding favored students with non-random seat assignments), regressing standardized mean midterm/final test scores on the share of female neighbor-5 peers (desk mate + neighbor 4), with block fixed effects and baseline controls and SEs clustered by classroom, yields a coefficient of 0.215 (SE=0.078), t=2.77, p=0.006. This indicates that being surrounded by all females rather than all males raises a girl's test score by ~0.22 SD, consistent with the paper's 0.2–0.3 SD claim.

dependent_variable: Absolute change in mean attitude from T1 to T2 (|att_T2 - att_T1|)
main_predictor: Certainty × Objective Ambivalence interaction
sample_definition: Study 1 participants who completed all three attitude items at both time points (N=174)
model_specification: OLS: change ~ certainty * objective_ambivalence + extremity
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's approach: certainty = mean of 7 certainty items; objective ambivalence = (pos+neg)/2 - |pos-neg| (Thompson et al. 1995); extremity covaried as in original analysis. Means/SDs match Table 1 (cert M=4.19/SD=1.52; amb M=.89/SD=1.86; change M=.61/SD=.59).
reasoning: Regressing absolute attitude change on certainty, objective ambivalence, their interaction, and extremity in Study 1 yields a significant certainty × ambivalence interaction, B=0.037, t(169)=2.28, p=.024, matching the paper's reported pattern (B=.04, t(169)=2.28).

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters)
main_predictor: Ownership scale (standardized mean of log FDI stock, log FDI flow, log portfolio equity stock)
sample_definition: Election-year observations across 23 OECD democracies, 1970–2007, with non-missing turnout, lagged turnout, and all controls/components of the ownership scale
model_specification: OLS with lagged dependent variable, country fixed effects, country-specific linear and quadratic time trends, cluster-robust SE by country
controls: Lagged turnout, log registered voters, %VAP 30-69, years since last election, US midterm dummy, compulsory voting, mixed system, PR system, disproportionality, ENPS, margin of victory
operationalization_notes: Replicates the Model 5 specification in the turnout table (only ownership-scale measure available in the data). Ownership scale built by z-scoring its three components on the full sample and averaging across non-missing components, requiring all three present.
reasoning: In an LDV turnout regression with country fixed effects and country-specific linear and quadratic time trends, the ownership-scale index (standardized average of log FDI stock, FDI flow, and portfolio equity stock) has a negative, statistically significant coefficient (b = -4.18, cluster-robust SE = 1.28, t(148) = -3.27, p ≈ 0.001, N = 226). This supports the ownership-constraint hypothesis that higher foreign ownership is associated with lower turnout.

dependent_variable: Number of BBB complaints in 2008 (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: first_A indicator (firm name begins with A or number)
sample_definition: All 2293 Illinois plumbing firms in final_data.dta
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test of mean complaints by first_A
operationalization_notes: Claim is about raw mean difference in complaints; used unequal-variance t-test on the BBB complaint count by first_A grouping in the main analysis dataset.
reasoning: A-name/number plumbing firms average 1.34 BBB complaints vs 0.25 for other firms (~5.4x), Welch's t=3.85, p<.001, replicating the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Cooperative strategy (dv)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure
sample_definition: All 588 state-bargaining observations in the replication dataset
model_specification: Ordered logistic regression (proportional odds)
controls: agreement_importance, parl_scrut, qmv, publicity, lngdp, foreignpolicy, euro, new_ms, presidency, lag_dv
operationalization_notes: Methods section redacted; paper's Table 1 uses a generalized ordered/multinomial logit with issue-linkage structure constrained equal across categories. I used an ordered logit on the same outcome with the same covariates as a parsimonious, directly comparable test of the directional claim.
reasoning: In an ordered logit of cooperative bargaining strategy (dv) on issue-linkage structure and the paper's controls, the issue-linkage-structure coefficient is 1.054 (SE=0.078), z=13.46, p<0.001 with N=588. The positive, highly significant effect supports the claim that when issues are more differently valued (greater scope for issue linkage), states are more likely to offer concessions.

dependent_variable: Credit to government and state-owned enterprises (% GDP) [credittogovtstateenterp]
main_predictor: State Capacity = ICRG Quality of Government index (icrg_qog)
sample_definition: All country-years in the Country Year Dataset with non-missing values for directed credit, its 1-year lag, ICRG QoG, private credit, and year (n=2,787).
model_specification: Pooled OLS dynamic panel: DC_t = a + b1*DC_{t-1} + b2*StateCapacity + b3*PrivateCredit + b4*Year + e, with country-clustered robust SEs (mirrors Table 1 column 1 of the paper, which used system GMM).
controls: Lagged dependent variable (Directed Credit t-1), Private Credit (% GDP), linear time trend
operationalization_notes: The claim specifies controlling for 'profit potential implied by financial repression', operationalized in the paper as Private Credit. I retained the same set of right-hand-side variables as Table 1 col.1 but replaced the difficult-to-replicate system-GMM with cluster-robust pooled OLS using the lagged DV; the substantive direction matches the paper but the effect is no longer significant.
reasoning: In a dynamic panel OLS of Directed Credit to Govt/SOEs on its lag, state capacity (ICRG quality of government), private credit, and a time trend (cluster-robust SEs by country), the state-capacity coefficient is -0.142 (z=-0.36, p=0.72). The point estimate is in the direction the claim predicts (weaker states -> more directed credit), but is far from statistical significance under cluster-robust standard errors, so the claim does not clearly reproduce with this simpler specification.

dependent_variable: dispute (Latin American state-year participation in a militarized interstate dispute, 1=yes)
main_predictor: Coup risk (lcoupsum, log of weighted coup-events sum, the paper's measure of threats to political survival)
sample_definition: Latin American state-years 1960–1999 with complete data on all predictors (N=798)
model_specification: Binary logit with country-clustered robust standard errors
controls: Lagged dispute, ethnic fractionalization, CINC (relative power), number of borders, log number of allies, regional conflict, lagged Polity, log real GDP per capita
operationalization_notes: Methods section was redacted; I implemented the analysis that most directly matches Table 3 (logit of dispute on coup risk + listed controls with cluster-robust SEs, N=798). The paper's headline test uses a Maddala simultaneous-equations correction with predicted coup-risk; without access to that first stage, I use observed coup risk, which is the most defensible single-equation test of the claim.
reasoning: In a logit model of dispute involvement on coup risk (lcoupsum) and the paper's controls (previous dispute, ethnic fractionalization, relative power [CINC], number of borders, log allies, regional conflict, lagged polity, log real GDP), with country-clustered robust SEs, the coup-risk coefficient is 0.158 (SE=0.147, z=1.07, p=0.28). Without the paper's simultaneous-equations (Maddala) correction, the observed coup-risk measure does not show a statistically significant effect on conflict involvement, so this direct test is inconclusive about the claim.

dependent_variable: Amount sent to out-group (Albanian) in dictator game (d12outgroup, 0-5 euros)
main_predictor: Region of residence (Primarily Albanian vs. Border vs. Primarily Serb reference)
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb respondents from the March 2011 Kosovo study
model_specification: OLS regression of out-group offer on region dummies; overall F-test of joint significance of exposure regions
operationalization_notes: The claim targets out-group bridging norms; the most direct DV is dictator offers to Albanians. Exposure operationalized via region categories as in the paper's Table 2 Model 3 (no controls). F-test gives a single overall test of the exposure effect.
reasoning: Regressing dictator-game offers to out-group Albanians on region dummies (Primarily Albanian, Border; reference = Primarily Serb) yields F(2,155)=9.26, p<.001. Serbs in the primarily Albanian region give 1.49 euros more (p<.001), and the border region 0.52 more (n.s.), supporting that out-group bridging norms increase with exposure to Albanians.

dependent_variable: enjoyrelativ (program enjoyment rating)
main_predictor: condition (disrupted by 'good' commercial vs. 'no' commercial/continuous)
sample_definition: All 102 study-2 participants with non-missing enjoyment ratings
model_specification: Independent samples two-sided t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: The cited claim on p.164 refers to Study 2's comparison of disrupted vs. continuous program enjoyment; used the provided study 2 data and the enjoyment DV.
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test on enjoyment ratings (study 2) shows participants in the commercial-disrupted condition rated the program more enjoyable (M=5.38) than those in the continuous condition (M=4.47), t(100)=2.45, p=.016. This reproduces the paper's directional claim.

dependent_variable: resigninvest (belief politician resigned due to bribery investigation, 1-4 scale)
main_predictor: Treatment condition: causal correction vs. denial of innuendo (innuendo serves as baseline)
sample_definition: Respondents in the innuendo, denial-of-innuendo, and causal-correction conditions who answered the resigninvest item (N=764). Control (no-rumor) condition excluded because the item was only asked of those exposed to the rumor.
model_specification: Weighted least squares regression of resigninvest on denial and causal dummies (innuendo baseline) with inverse probability weights; linear contrast test of causal = denial.
controls: None beyond the two treatment indicators; block-randomization accounted for via inverse probability weights.
operationalization_notes: Mirrors Model 5 of Table 2 in the paper, which is the test most directly tied to the claim. The substantive test for the claim is the contrast between the causal correction and denial coefficients.
reasoning: In an IPW-weighted OLS of belief that Swensen resigned due to the investigation on denial and causal-correction dummies (innuendo baseline), the causal-correction coefficient (-0.58) is significantly more negative than the denial coefficient (-0.25). A Wald test of equality of the two coefficients yields t(761) = -5.07, p < .001, indicating the causal correction reduces misperception acceptance significantly more than the denial.

dependent_variable: Intimacy (aggregated 4-item scale)
main_predictor: Attention condition (attention vs. no-attention)
