reasoning: Among female participants, the mean political knowledge score was higher in the stereotype-not-activated condition (M=8.90, SD=4.60, n=73) than in the stereotype-activated-by-gender-difference-statement condition (M=7.03, SD=4.11, n=70); independent-samples t(141)=2.57, p=.011, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: GDP growth index at t+2 (last year = 100)
main_predictor: psec_dominant: indicator =1 if city secretary or mayor is connected to incumbent provincial secretary
sample_definition: City-year panel 1999-2015 with non-missing covariates (333 cities, 3915 obs)
model_specification: OLS with city fixed effects and province-by-year fixed effects, robust SEs clustered by city
controls: Starting Log GDP, GDP growth, Log Pop, Log Fixed Asset Investment for both predecessors of city secretary and mayor; Net Transfer (dep); age, gender, and college dummy for both city secretary and mayor
operationalization_notes: Followed Eq. and Table 1 col. 3: combined citypanel_base.dta and econ_panel.dta; used psec_dominant as the connection indicator; included economic and leader controls described in the methods section; clustered SEs at city level.
reasoning: Replicating the paper's main fixed-effects specification (Table 1, col. 3), the coefficient on Connected-to-incumbent-provincial-secretary on city GDP growth at t+2 is positive (b = 1.60, SE = 0.76 with city-clustered SEs) and statistically significant (t = 2.11, p ≈ 0.035), indicating that connected city leaders are associated with faster economic growth than unconnected ones, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: log of the fraction of top-quality foreign players in the top league (stop / total players)
main_predictor: log(1 - top marginal tax rate on foreign players); IV = 1(country=Denmark)*1(year>=1991)
sample_definition: Country-year observations 1985-2008 for Denmark (treatment) and synthetic control country (weighted average of Norway and Sweden); years with zero top-quality foreigners dropped due to log
model_specification: 2SLS Wald-type DD: log P_ct = e*log(1-tau_ct) + beta*1(c=DK) + gamma*1(t>=1991) + eps; first stage uses Denmark x Post as instrument for log(1-tau)
operationalization_notes: Follows the Table 1 Panel B2 design exactly: synthetic-control DD with weights from online Appendix Table A2 (Fig 3A), 2SLS using the reform interaction as instrument. Top quality defined as having played for one's national team (variable 'stop' in basesynthetic_control.dta). Synthetic outcome computed as weighted average of fractions; synthetic log(1-tau) as log of weighted (1-tau).
reasoning: Replicating Table 1, panel B2 of Kleven et al. (2013) for top-quality players, I estimated a 2SLS regression of log(fraction of top-quality foreign players) on log(1-MTR_f), instrumented by Denmark×Post-1991, using Denmark vs. the synthetic control (0.227*Norway + 0.773*Sweden, weights from online Appendix Table A2). The elasticity is large, positive, and significant (e=5.49, SE=1.94, t=2.82, p<0.01), confirming that the 1991 Danish tax cut for foreigners disproportionately attracted top-ability foreign players. This is the same directional conclusion as the original paper (which reports e=3.01, SE=0.78 for top-quality and -0.70 for lower-quality).

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay (composite of environment/income/tax items)
main_predictor: intrin_extrin (intrinsic minus extrinsic value score)

operationalization_notes: The claim directly maps to Study 1's bivariate association between relative intrinsic-vs-extrinsic value endorsement and willingness to pay, using the pre-computed composite variables in the SPSS file.

dependent_variable: ln_imports (post-dispute log product-level import flows into the defendant market)
main_predictor: Complainant indicator (1 if partner j is complainant in dispute d)

controls: Log Defendant GDP, Log Partner GDP, Democratic Pair, Lagged disputed imports (imports_tminus1), Log total imports
operationalization_notes: Mirrors Model 2 in Table 1 (early-settlement subsample). Used the dataset's pre-built variables; counter>=0 restricts to post-dispute years matching the paper's post-dispute trade DV. Cluster-robust SEs by dispute used following paper note that SEs are clustered.
reasoning: Within the early-settlement subsample, complainants show a positive and statistically significant coefficient on post-dispute log imports (b = 0.258, cluster-robust SE = 0.101, z = 2.55, p ≈ 0.011), consistent with the paper's claim that complainants gain disproportionately more than the rest of the membership under private settlement.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (TEA rate among wage-employed population, country-year)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of working-age population 20-64)
sample_definition: All GEM country-year observations with non-missing entre_wage and medage_20_64 (2001-2010, 82 countries, 393 country-years)
model_specification: WLS regression with year fixed effects, weights = nobs_cy, robust SE clustered by country
controls: Year fixed effects only (Table 2 column 3 baseline specification)
operationalization_notes: Follows the paper's most direct cross-country test linking median age to entrepreneurship (Table 2, col. 3). Standard errors clustered by country with df=clusters-1=81.
reasoning: Weighted regression of entre_wage (TEA wage-employed rate) on median age (20-64) with year fixed effects, weighted by country-year obs and clustered SEs by country, yields a coefficient of -0.00732 (SE=0.00128, t=-5.71, p<0.001, N=393, 82 country clusters). A lower median age is significantly associated with higher new business formation, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Ratio of perceived to actual arm length
main_predictor: Arm (right vs left), within-subject
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (n=15)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test (one-tailed, as in paper)
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Experiment 1 analysis: paired t-test on perceived/actual arm-length ratios within right-handed subsample.
reasoning: Paired t-test on right-handed participants comparing perceived/actual arm-length ratio for right vs left arm yielded t(14)=2.12, one-tailed p=.026 (mean RatioRight=0.970 vs RatioLeft=0.920). Right arms were perceived as relatively longer than left arms, replicating the claim.

dependent_variable: dv_index3: average of appreciated/valued/satisfied (3 items, 7-point)
main_predictor: condition (0=acknowledgment only verbal, 1=5-cent financial acknowledgment)
sample_definition: Study 1a participants who finished study (exclude=0), N=49

operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Study 1a design with composite DV index across 3 items; used the provided exclude filter.
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test on the 3-item DV index comparing verbal acknowledgment (M=5.57) vs. 5-cent financial acknowledgment (M=4.38) yields t(47)=2.92, p=.005, supporting that adding a small monetary benefit produced less positive feelings than verbal acknowledgment alone.

dependent_variable: Mean standardized midterm + final exam score (s_tot)
main_predictor: Share female among 5 nearest neighbors (avg5_girl)
sample_definition: Female students (girl==1), excluding favored students with nonrandom seats (special1==0); complete-case on outcome, predictor, controls, and block FE
model_specification: OLS with classroom-block fixed effects (gcb)
controls: baseline test score, height, age, birth order, mother's & father's education, baseline interest in Chinese/math/English, favored desk mate indicator, share favored among neighbor-4, leave-out-block mean of female share, block FE
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 4 Panel B column 1 (female sample, neighbor-5 specification) per the paper's equation (2).
reasoning: In the female subsample, regressing standardized exam scores on the share of female neighbor-5 peers (with block fixed effects and baseline controls) yields a coefficient of 0.215 (SE 0.102, t=2.12, p=0.036). Moving from 0 to 1 in the share (5 males to 5 females) raises female test scores by ~0.22 SD, matching the paper's 0.21 estimate.

dependent_variable: Absolute attitude change |T2 attitude − T1 attitude| (one-year follow-up; alcohol attitude index from 3 semantic differential items)
main_predictor: Certainty × Objective ambivalence interaction (centered)
sample_definition: Study 2 (alcohol) participants who completed both initial survey and one-year follow-up (Date3 / att*_T3 present), N=135
model_specification: OLS: change ~ cert_c * ambiv_c + extremity_c
operationalization_notes: Paper's Study 2 reports B=.07, t(130)=3.42 for the certainty×objective-ambivalence interaction predicting one-year attitude stability with extremity as covariate; I replicated this using the T3 (one-year) wave (T2 in data is shorter interval). Objective ambivalence computed via Griffin formula ((pos+neg)/2 − |pos−neg|); certainty as mean of 7 Petrocelli items.
reasoning: OLS regression of absolute attitude change (T1→T3, one-year follow-up, alcohol attitudes) on mean-centered certainty, objective ambivalence, their interaction, and attitude extremity yielded a significant certainty × ambivalence interaction, B=0.075, t(130)=3.42, p<.001. The positive coefficient indicates that the negative certainty-change association (i.e., greater stability with greater certainty) is strongest at low ambivalence and reverses at high ambivalence, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters) at the country-election level
main_predictor: Log FDI Flows (a 'most-flexible' foreign-ownership measure)
sample_definition: 23 OECD countries, election-years 1970-2007, observations with non-missing covariates
model_specification: OLS with lagged DV, country fixed effects, country-specific quadratic time trends, country-clustered standard errors (a linear analogue of the paper's one-step Arellano-Bond difference GMM specification)
controls: Lagged turnout, log registered voters, %VAP 30-69, years since last election, US-midterm dummy, compulsory voting, mixed/PR system dummies, disproportionality, ENPS, margin/closeness
operationalization_notes: The 'ownership-constraint hypothesis' for turnout is most directly captured by the coefficient on a foreign-ownership measure in the turnout equation. FDI Flows was selected as the headline 'most flexible' ownership variable highlighted in the paper. Because exact replication of one-step Arellano-Bond GMM is non-trivial in Python, a fixed-effects OLS with LDV and country-specific quadratic trends (the paper's stated specification) was used, providing a charitable and directly comparable linear test.
reasoning: In a turnout regression with a lagged DV, country fixed effects, country-specific quadratic time trends, and the paper's turnout-model controls, log FDI Flows enters negatively and significantly (b = -2.23, cluster-robust SE = 0.88, t = -2.55, p = 0.011, N = 218 elections, 23 countries). This supports the ownership-constraint hypothesis: more foreign ownership of capital is associated with lower turnout, in the same direction and similar magnitude as the paper's Arellano-Bond difference-GMM estimate (-2.030).

dependent_variable: Number of BBB service complaints (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: first_A (firm name begins with A or a number)
sample_definition: All Illinois plumbing firms in final_data.dta (n=2293)
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test on mean complaints by name type
operationalization_notes: Most direct test of the difference-in-means claim ('5x more complaints'). Used the BBB complaints variable that the paper identifies as the primary firm-quality measure.
reasoning: Welch's t-test comparing BBB complaints (2008) between plumbing firms with names beginning with A/number (n=295, mean=1.34) vs. others (n=1998, mean=0.25) gives t=3.85, p<.001. The A-name firms receive ~5.4x as many complaints, matching the paper's claim of >5x.

dependent_variable: Ordered cooperative bargaining strategy (dv, 0-3)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure (average zone of agreement across issue pairs)
sample_definition: All 588 state-negotiation observations in the McKibben EU bargaining dataset
model_specification: Ordered logit (proxy for the paper's generalized ordered logit Model 1)
controls: ln GDP, security/defense policy, euro state, new member state, agreement importance, parliamentary scrutiny, majority voting, publicity, presidency, lagged DV
operationalization_notes: Used ordered logit as a parsimonious test of the directional claim; the paper uses a generalized ordered logit but the issue-linkage variable is constrained to a single coefficient across categories, so the standard ordered logit z-statistic directly tests the claim.
reasoning: An ordered logit regression of the bargaining strategy (0-3 cooperative scale) on the issue-linkage structure measure plus the full set of paper controls yields a coefficient of 1.054 (SE=0.078, z=13.46, p<0.001) on N=588 state-negotiation observations. This positive and highly significant effect supports Hypothesis S1: more differently valued issues are associated with more cooperative, concession-offering behavior.

dependent_variable: Directed Credit to Government and SOEs (% GDP) (credittogovtstateenterp)
main_predictor: State Capacity = ICRG Indicator of Quality of Government (icrg_qog), lagged 1 year
sample_definition: Country-year panel, all countries with non-missing observations for the DV, lagged DV, IQG, and Private Credit; 130 countries, 1984-2010 era.
model_specification: Two-step system GMM (Arellano-Bover/Blundell-Bond) dynamic panel with LDV, IQG, Private Credit, and linear time trend; instruments collapsed (Roodman 2009); Windmeijer-corrected standard errors. Implemented via pydynpd.
controls: Lagged dependent variable (directed credit at t-1), Private Credit (% GDP), linear time trend
operationalization_notes: Mirrors Table 2 column 1 of the paper: collapsed-instrument two-step system GMM regression of directed credit on lagged state capacity, controlling for the profit-potential variable (Private Credit). I report the z-test on the IQG coefficient with Windmeijer-corrected SE, which is the standard inferential statistic for this specification.
reasoning: Two-step system GMM with collapsed instruments yields a coefficient on lagged state capacity (IQG) of -3.12 (Windmeijer-corrected SE = 2.44; z = -1.28; p = 0.20) predicting Directed Credit to Government and SOEs, controlling for the lagged DV, Private Credit (the profit-potential proxy for financial repression), and a linear time trend. The sign matches the paper (weaker states -> more directed credit) but the effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero in my replication.

dependent_variable: Dispute (1 = country initiated an MID in year t, else 0)
main_predictor: Predicted coup risk (log of summed coup events), instrumented via first-stage OLS on exogenous regressors
sample_definition: Latin American country-years 1960-1999 (full analytic sample of 798 observations from scamerica5.dta)
model_specification: Two-stage simultaneous-equations approximation: Stage 1 OLS of lcoupsum on rwar, cinc, polity2l, llrgdpch, ethfrac, regconf, confend, lagdisp, nborder, lnumber; Stage 2 probit of dispute on predicted lcoupsum plus controls
controls: lagged dispute, ethnic fractionalization, relative power (CINC), number of borders, log number of allies, regional conflict, lagged polity, log real GDP (lagged)

operationalization_notes: Follows the paper's main Table 2 specification for ACT access (col. 1): first illness episodes among households without RDT subsidy, regression of ACT use on three subsidy dummies with strata FE and household-clustered SEs. The claim about a 'very high subsidy' increasing access is operationalized as the act40 (92% subsidy) coefficient.
reasoning: Linear probability model on first illness episodes (excluding RDT-subsidy households) shows the 92% ACT subsidy (act40) raises the probability of taking an ACT by 21.5 percentage points (z=5.09, p<0.001) relative to the no-subsidy control, more than doubling access from the control mean of ~19%. This corroborates the paper's claim that a very high subsidy dramatically increases access.

dependent_variable: Normalized combined math-reading PIAT score (mean of normalized math and reading recognition, renormalized in the random sample to mean 0, SD 1)
main_predictor: Total family pretax income (sum of parental wages, dividends, other property income, pensions, social security, unemployment insurance) deflated to year 2000 dollars and expressed in $1,000s
sample_definition: Children of NLSY79 with valid math and reading PIAT scores from survey income years 1987 onward (i.e., 1988 survey wave or later), N = 23,043 child-year observations from 7,782 children
model_specification: OLS levels regression with cluster-robust standard errors clustered at the mother (family) level
controls: Male, age, Black, Hispanic, one-sibling indicator, two-or-more siblings indicator
operationalization_notes: The dataset does not include the pre-built simulated-EITC instrument or post-tax/EITC family income series used in the paper's headline IV (Table 3, col 1). As the most charitable replicable analysis tied to the directional claim, I ran the OLS-levels version (analogous to Table 2 Panel A, col 1) of achievement on current real family income with baseline child controls. This tests whether a $1,000 increase in income is associated with higher combined math-reading achievement, which is the substantive claim, while acknowledging that the magnitude is expected to be smaller than the paper's IV estimate.
reasoning: Regressing the normalized combined math-reading PIAT score on real total family income (in $1,000s of year 2000 dollars), with baseline child controls (gender, age, race, siblings) and family-clustered SEs, yields a coefficient of 0.0059 (cluster-robust SE 0.00045), t = 13.05 on 23,043 child-year observations. Income is robustly and positively associated with achievement in the original data, supporting the paper's directional claim that higher income raises combined math-reading test scores. The OLS-levels magnitude (~0.6% of an SD per $1,000) is smaller than the paper's IV estimate (~6% of an SD), but the sign and significance match.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs)
main_predictor: Single, childless (singchild1; 1 = single childless, 0 = others)
sample_definition: Study 1 sample (filter_$ = 1), listwise deletion on all variables, n=353
model_specification: OLS regression: engwkabs ~ singchild1 + gender + age + position
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Study 1 methods (OLS with sex, age, job level controls). Used singchild1 dummy as the family structure indicator.
reasoning: OLS regression of work absorption on single-childless status with controls (sex, age, job position) yields b = -0.31, t(348) = -2.36, p = .019, indicating single, childless employees report significantly lower absorption than those with other family structures, replicating the Study 1 finding.

dependent_variable: ProperName (1 if response greeted applicant by proper name, 0 otherwise)
main_predictor: Applicant race signaled by name (Hispanic vs. white)
sample_definition: Email audit observations assigned to Hispanic or white treatment names with a non-missing ProperName outcome (i.e., received a response that could be coded); Black treatment arm excluded.
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on the 2x2 table of Hispanic-vs-white by greeted-by-name
operationalization_notes: Claim directly contrasts Hispanic vs. white applicants on being greeted by name. Restricted to those two arms; outcome only defined when an email response was received. Used uncorrected Pearson chi-square as the simplest direct test.
reasoning: Among email responses, 41.2% of Hispanic-named applicants were greeted by proper name vs. 61.1% of white-named applicants. A chi-square test of independence yields chi2(1, N=362)=14.42, p=0.00015, confirming Hispanic applicants were significantly less likely to be greeted by name than white counterparts.

dependent_variable: Per-session frequency of low (shaded) quality among realized trades
main_predictor: Contract type (rigid vs. flexible)
sample_definition: Baseline treatment (condition==1), only realized trades (contractrealizedc==1)
model_specification: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on session-level pairs (matched by session, comparing rigid vs flexible)
controls: none (nonparametric paired test on session averages)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's standard practice of using session averages as independent observations for nonparametric inference; restricted to baseline condition and trades that occurred (rigid bad-state cases have no quality choice). One-sided test in direction of claim.
reasoning: Average shading rates (low quality among realized trades) per session were 6.4% in rigid contracts and 26.2% in flexible contracts. A Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the 5 session-level pairs yields W=0 (one-sided p=0.03125), confirming significantly less shading in rigid than flexible contracts.

dependent_variable: ln(state CO2 emissions, unadjusted)
main_predictor: ln(average weekly working hours)
sample_definition: All 50 U.S. states, years 2007–2013 (N = 350 state-years)
model_specification: Two-way fixed effects (state + year dummies) OLS log-log panel regression
controls: ln(employed population %), ln(GDP per hour), ln(total population), ln(energy production), ln(manufacturing % of GDP), ln(working-age population %); household size unavailable in provided data (requires IPUMS extract)
operationalization_notes: Replicates the paper's Model 1 (scale-effect, fixed effects) specification as closely as the provided data allow. Prais–Winsten AR(1) correction not applied; standard OLS standard errors used. Household-size variable omitted because it requires IPUMS access.
reasoning: Two-way (state and year) fixed-effects OLS regression of log carbon emissions on log working hours plus the Model-1 covariates yields a positive coefficient of 0.465 (SE = 0.239, t(287) = 1.95, p ≈ 0.052). The direction matches the paper's reported positive scale-effect relationship, though without the Prais–Winsten AR(1) correction and the household-size control (unavailable without IPUMS) the effect is only marginally significant.

dependent_variable: consider (state seriously considered or carried out attack on another's nuclear program in a dyad-year)
main_predictor: hostileMID (prior violent militarized conflict in the dyad)
sample_definition: Politically relevant dyad-years with a non-nuclear proliferator (polrel==1), 1941-2000; N=5,360
model_specification: Logistic regression with cubic-spline peace-year correction, dyad-clustered standard errors (replicates Table 3, Model 1)
controls: Target's polity, foreign policy similarity (s_un_reg), no-consider-years, three peace-year splines
operationalization_notes: Replicated the paper's baseline Model 1 (DV: Consider) using the variables provided in the .dta file; used cluster-robust SEs by dyadid to match the paper's inference approach.
reasoning: In a logit regression of considered attacks on prior violent militarized conflict (hostileMID), target's polity, foreign policy similarity, and peace-year splines (clustered SE by dyad), hostileMID has coefficient 2.352 (SE 0.549, z = 4.28, p < .001). This confirms the paper's claim that prior violent militarized conflict significantly increases the probability of targeting nuclear programs.

dependent_variable: splinter (county becomes part of a new district in wave t)
main_predictor: DEC_rep — DEC seat share / population share (political marginalization)
sample_definition: County-electoral-wave observations with non-missing covariates (1996–2010 waves)
model_specification: Logistic regression (pooled) with region and wave fixed effects
controls: ethnic_min, margA (development summary index), ncounties, break_lag, region dummies, wave dummies
operationalization_notes: Follows Table 4 M1 in the paper: splinter as DV, DEC share ratio as the political marginalization measure; uses margA as the development summary index. Slight N difference from the paper (475 vs 434) likely reflects different listwise handling but direction, magnitude and significance match.
reasoning: In a logistic regression of county-wave splinter formation on DEC share-to-population ratio (political marginalization), ethnic minority status, development index, number of counties, breakup lag, region and wave dummies, the DEC share ratio coefficient is -0.722 (z=-3.74, p<0.001, N=475). Lower DEC representation relative to population (i.e., greater political marginalization) significantly predicts secession, supporting H1.

dependent_variable: recog1dum (State B's diplomatic recognition of State A, dichotomous)
main_predictor: nukeduma (State A nuclear-capable, 0/1)
sample_definition: Directed dyad-years with non-missing recognition observations (no interpolation), as in the paper
model_specification: Binary logit with constant
controls: Nuclear Weapons B, Nuke A x Nuke B, Rivalry Status A, Rivalry Status B, Dyadic Rivalry, CINC A, CINC B, CINC A x CINC B, Democracy A, Democracy B, Dem A x Dem B, Contiguity, ln(Distance), Alliance
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 1 dichotomous specification. BTSCS splines were not added; results are otherwise the most direct replication of the diplomatic-recognition regression.
reasoning: Logit regression of dichotomous diplomatic recognition (State B recognizes State A) on Nuclear Weapons A with full set of controls from the paper yields a coefficient of 0.815 (SE=0.029, z=27.68, p<0.001), indicating that nuclear-capable states are significantly more likely to be recognized by other nations, matching the original study's claim.

dependent_variable: Log of absolute opinion change in pro-immigration index between wave 2 and wave 3
main_predictor: Group-level justification rationality (DQ_jlev) from external DQI coding
sample_definition: EuroPolis participants with complete data on DV, predictor and controls (174 individuals across 13 small groups)
model_specification: Multilevel linear regression (REML), individuals nested in small groups, random intercept
controls: Knowledge change; clarify-thinking from other participants/experts/politicians/briefing; social conformity pressure (above/below); gender, age, education, Catholic, Protestant, working class, religiosity, left-right ideology + squared, left-party and right-party vote intention
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Model 2b specification (Table 2) replicating Sanders with DQI-based justification rationality as group-level predictor of magnitude of opinion change.
reasoning: Multilevel REML model of log absolute opinion change on immigration with group-level justification rationality (DQ_jlev) and the Sanders control set yields coef=0.130, SE=0.066, z=1.96, p=0.049 (N=174 in 13 groups), matching the paper's Model 2b and supporting the claim that higher group-level rational justification corresponds to greater opinion change.

dependent_variable: Mean effort (proportion of rounds in which the subject worked), averaged within group
main_predictor: Reward scheme (discriminating 345COM vs symmetrical 444COM)
sample_definition: All subjects in complementarity treatments (345COM and 444COM); group-level means used as independent observations
model_specification: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U / rank-sum test on group-mean efforts
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's approach of using groups (mg) as the independent unit of observation and a nonparametric rank-sum test, directly comparing symmetrical vs discriminating reward under complementarity.
reasoning: Mann-Whitney U test comparing mean effort (work) per group between 345COM (mean=0.917, n=12 groups) and 444COM (mean=0.722, n=11 groups) gives U=95, two-sided p=0.070. The symmetrical reward scheme elicits substantially lower effort than the discriminating one under complementarity, matching the paper's claim direction and magnitudes.

dependent_variable: Difference within senator between letters: (anti-immigration actions mentioned − pro-immigration actions mentioned)
main_predictor: Constituent letter type (pro- vs anti-immigration)
sample_definition: 56 senators who responded to both the pro- and anti-immigration constituent letters
model_specification: Paired (within-subjects) t-test on the anti−pro action-mention balance across the two letters
operationalization_notes: Reproduces Table 2's primary tailoring test: per-senator paired comparison of compensating-action mentions across the two letters, the most direct test of the tailoring claim.
reasoning: Within-subjects paired t-test on the (anti-immigration minus pro-immigration) action-mention balance shows a significantly more anti-leaning balance in letters responding to anti-immigration constituents (42.9%) than in letters to pro-immigration constituents (19.7%); paired difference -23.2pp, t(55)=-3.45, p=0.001. Senators tailor explanations to audiences.

dependent_variable: Log wage gain at migration: log(adjusted last U.S. hourly wage) − log(adjusted last home-country hourly wage)
main_predictor: Education category dummies (omitted = bachelor's degree or more; comparison category 'no high school' = <9 years of schooling)
sample_definition: MP/LAMP immigrants (all available countries: MEX, PRI, DOM, NIC, SLV, GTM, HTI, PER, ECU, COL) with non-missing wages, hourly wages between $0.01 and $1,000, and last home-country job in 1983 or later (per paper's validity rules). NIS subsample is not included because the NIS microdata folders in the replication archive are empty.
model_specification: OLS: log_wage_gain ~ education-category dummies + country fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Section IV.A specification for Table III as closely as possible given that only the MP/LAMP component of the pooled sample is included in the data release. Education categorized into the five groups defined in the paper (no HS, some HS, HS grad, some college, college+). Wage-gain variable uses the CPS-adjusted hourly wages already provided in the wage_gain_table.xlsx file.
reasoning: Regressing log wage gain (log US wage minus log adjusted home-country wage) on education-category dummies with country fixed effects in the available MP (Mexican Migration Project / LAMP) sample yields a coefficient on 'no high school' (relative to college graduates) of 0.292 (SE 0.113, t=2.58, p=0.010, N=2752). The estimate is positive and statistically significant, directionally matching the paper's claim that immigrants who never attended high school gain substantially more from migration than those with a college degree, although the magnitude is smaller than the paper's 0.599 from the pooled NIS+MP sample (NIS micro-data are not included in the provided archive).

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses reflecting the learned (negative) meaning of the cue
main_predictor: Cue status (baseline vs. suppressed) within the TNT paradigm
sample_definition: Nonruminators (Group==1) from Experiment 2 (Ashley dataset), n=27
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing FAbaseC vs FAsuppC among nonruminators
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns evidence of SIF in nonruminators on indirect transfer tasks. The available dataset is the Experiment 2 free-association data; I therefore tested the directly implied within-subject baseline-vs-suppressed contrast within the nonruminator subgroup, which is the most direct analytic test of the claim.
reasoning: Among nonruminators (n=27, Experiment 2 free-association data), the percentage of responses connoting the learned negative meaning was significantly higher for baseline cues (M=45.68) than for suppressed cues (M=29.63), paired t(26)=3.03, p=.005. This indicates suppression practice was beneficial for nonruminators, consistent with the original claim.

dependent_variable: CES-D 8-item psychological well-being scale (mean, higher=better)
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction: parental status (lives with children vs. childless reference) × country-level percentage (strongly) disapproving of voluntary childlessness (grand-mean centered)
sample_definition: ESS Round 3 respondents aged over 40 from 24 European countries (Cyprus excluded); valid CES-D data; complete data on parental status, marital status, education, religious attendance, parental education, employment, born-in-country, gender
model_specification: Two-level linear mixed model with random country intercepts; fixed effects: lives_with, empty_nest (childless ref), country-level disapproval, cross-level interactions of both parental dummies with disapproval, plus controls
controls: Gender, age (centered) and age squared, marital status (married/cohab ref), respondent education (4 levels), religious attendance, parental education (4 levels + missing dummy), paid employment, born in country
operationalization_notes: Single pooled model across men and women (with gender control) for one summary test; childless is reference so a positive lives_with × disapproval coefficient means the parent–childless gap widens with disapproval, equivalently the childless disadvantage shrinks under tolerant norms.
reasoning: In a multilevel linear model of CES-D well-being on parental status, country-level disapproval of childlessness (% disapprove/strongly disapprove, grand-mean centered), and their cross-level interaction (with childless as the reference category and individual-level controls plus gender), the lives-with-children × disapproval interaction is positive and significant (b≈0.002, z=3.39, p≈0.001). A positive interaction means the well-being advantage of parents over the childless is larger in more disapproving countries, i.e., the childless disadvantage is smaller in countries with more tolerant norms—directly supporting the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: DSM-5 Self-Rated Level 1 Cross-Cutting Symptom Measure total (DSM5_Total)
main_predictor: High-K Strategy Scale total (HKSS_Total); higher = slower life-history strategy
sample_definition: All 138 participants in the dataset
model_specification: Bivariate Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: The paper's main test of this claim is the zero-order correlation between life history strategy and total psychopathology. HKSS_Total is the indicator of slow life-history strategy, so a negative correlation indicates faster strategy is associated with more symptoms.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between life-history strategy (HKSS total; higher = slower) and DSM-5 psychopathology total was r = -.485, p < .001, n = 138. Faster life-history strategies (lower HKSS) are associated with greater psychopathology symptoms, replicating the claim.

dependent_variable: Political knowledge test score (PolWis_score)
main_predictor: Stereotype activation condition (1 = not activated vs. 3 = activated by gender difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender_factor = weiblich) who passed the Filter (not cheated/interrupted) in Study 2
model_specification: Independent-samples (equal-variance) two-sample t-test
controls: none (matching the pairwise contrast reported in the paper, not the full ANCOVA)
operationalization_notes: The paper's directional claim is a simple pairwise contrast between conditions 1 and 3 among women; the most direct test is a two-sample t-test on PolWis_score within the filtered female subsample.
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test comparing female participants' political knowledge test scores in the stereotype-not-activated condition (n=73, M=8.90, SD=4.60) vs. the stereotype-activated-by-gender-difference-statement condition (n=70, M=7.03, SD=4.11) yields t(141)=2.57, p=0.011. Women in condition 1 scored significantly higher than women in condition 3, replicating the claim.

dependent_variable: GDP growth rate at t+2 (annual growth in percentage points, derived as f2gdpidx - 100)
main_predictor: Connected to provincial secretary (1 if city secretary or mayor was first promoted to a city leadership position under the incumbent provincial secretary)
sample_definition: City-year panel of prefecture-level/subprovincial cities in mainland China, 2000-2011, excluding observations with missing growth or connection data
model_specification: OLS with city fixed effects and province-by-year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by city
controls: None beyond fixed effects (Model 1 specification of Table 1)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's most parsimonious baseline specification (Model 1 of Table 1): connection indicator combining city secretary and mayor, two-way FE, city-clustered SE. Restricted to 2000-2011 as stated in the methods.
reasoning: Two-way fixed-effects regression (city + province-year FE) of GDP growth at t+2 (last-year=100, minus 100) on a connection indicator equal to 1 if either the city secretary or mayor was first promoted under the incumbent provincial secretary yields a positive coefficient of 0.37 percentage points (city-clustered SE = 0.189, t = 1.95, p ≈ 0.051). This essentially reproduces the paper's 0.389 estimate (Table 1, Model 1) and supports the claim that connected city leaders deliver faster growth.

dependent_variable: log share of TOP-quality foreign players among all players (log treattop)
main_predictor: log net-of-foreign-top-tax rate, log(1 - mtrf), instrumented by Denmark × post-1991 interaction
sample_definition: Denmark and Sweden (single-country proxy for the synthetic control, with Sweden being the highest-weighted country in the paper), 1985-2008, observations with treattop>0 (to take log)
model_specification: 2SLS Wald difference-in-differences as in Table 1 panel B2: log P_ct = e*log(1-tau_ct) + b*1(c=DK) + g*1(t>=1991) + e, instrumenting log(1-tau) with DK x post-1991
controls: country dummy (DK) and post-1991 dummy; no further controls
operationalization_notes: The claim about changed ability composition is most directly tested by the panel B2 elasticity for top-quality foreigners (the paper reports 3.01, s.e. 0.78). Without the do-files or synthetic weights, I used Sweden as the natural comparator since the paper text explicitly contrasts Denmark with Sweden and Table A2 indicates Sweden carries the largest weight in the synthetic control. Standard errors are based on the standard 2SLS variance formula.
reasoning: The 2SLS DiD elasticity of the share of TOP-quality foreign players (treattop) on the log net-of-tax rate for foreigners, comparing Denmark with Sweden (the dominant component of the paper's synthetic control) before vs. after the 1991 Danish Researchers' Tax Scheme, is positive and statistically significant (e=8.17, t=2.80, N=42). This indicates that the Danish tax cut to foreigners disproportionately raised the share of high-ability foreign players, consistent with the claim that it changed the ability composition of foreigners in favor of higher-ability players.

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay (Study 1 WTP composite)
main_predictor: intrin_extrin (I/E ratio of intrinsic relative to extrinsic values)
sample_definition: All Study 1 participants with non-missing values on both variables (university student sample)
model_specification: Pearson product-moment correlation
operationalization_notes: The paper's Table reports a bivariate correlation between I/E and WTP in Study 1; I reproduced this most-direct test using the same I/E composite (intrin_extrin) and WTP variable in the .sav file.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between I/E (intrinsic relative to extrinsic values) and willingness to pay was r=.43, t(153)=5.83, p<.001, n=155, supporting the claim that higher endorsement of intrinsic relative to extrinsic values is associated with greater WTP to protect the environment.

dependent_variable: ln_imports (log of annual imports into defendant from trade partner, post-dispute years)
main_predictor: Complainant (dummy = 1 if trade partner is the complainant in the dispute)
sample_definition: Disputes resolved by early settlement (earlysettle==1), restricted to product-lines with complete 5-year post-dispute trade record (imports_post non-missing) and non-missing controls; N=6027.
model_specification: OLS with cluster-robust standard errors clustered by combined dispute identifier (dispute_combined)
controls: Defendant GDP (ln), Partner GDP (ln), Democratic Pair, lagged Disputed Imports (ln), Total Imports (ln)
operationalization_notes: Reproduces Model 2 of Table 1 in the paper, which is the most direct test of the claim that complainants gain disproportionately under private (early) settlements. Sample size matches the paper exactly (6027). Clustering follows the paper's stated procedure (dispute_combined).
reasoning: In the early-settlement subsample (N=6027, matching the paper's Model 2 exactly), OLS of log(imports) on Complainant with the paper's controls (defendant GDP, partner GDP, democratic pair, lagged disputed imports, total imports) yields a positive coefficient on Complainant of 0.262 (cluster-robust SE=0.143 by combined dispute id), t=1.83. The sign is in the direction the paper claims (complainants import more from defendants than non-participants after private settlements). My coefficient is smaller than the paper's 0.430 but directionally consistent and marginally significant.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (rate of entrepreneurs among wage workers, GEM)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of working-age population 20-64)
sample_definition: GEM country-year panel, 82 countries, years 2001-2010 (all available observations)
model_specification: WLS regression with year fixed effects, weighted by number of country-year observations (nobs_cy), standard errors clustered by country
controls: Year fixed effects only (matching Table 2, Col 3 baseline specification)
operationalization_notes: Replicated the simplest specification in Table 2 (Col. 3) using median age as predictor, since the claim is specifically about median age and new business formation.
reasoning: Weighted regression of new business formation (entre_wage) on median age (20-64) with year fixed effects, weighted by country-year obs and clustered by country, yields a coefficient of -0.0073 (t = -5.71, p < 0.001, N=393, 82 country clusters). Lower median age is strongly associated with higher new business formation, matching the paper's Table 2 Column 3.

dependent_variable: Perceived/actual arm-length ratio
main_predictor: Arm (right vs. left), within-subject
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (Handedness==2), N=15
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test (one-tailed, as in original)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's direct test: separate paired-samples t-test for right-handers on the perceived-to-actual arm length ratio (RatioRight vs. RatioLeft).
reasoning: Paired t-test on right-handed participants comparing perceived/actual arm length ratio for right vs. left arm yielded t(14)=2.12, one-tailed p=.026. Right-handers' right-arm ratio (M=0.97) exceeded left-arm ratio (M=0.92), consistent with the claim that right-handers perceive their right arm as longer (less underestimated) than their left arm.

dependent_variable: dv_index3 (3-item appreciation index)
main_predictor: condition (verbal vs. $0.05 financial acknowledgment)
sample_definition: Study 1a hotel guests with exclude=0 (n=49)
model_specification: One-way ANOVA (between-subjects)
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Study 1a method: one-way ANOVA on the pre-built 3-item appreciation index, excluding flagged participants.
reasoning: One-way ANOVA on the appreciation index by acknowledgment condition shows that guests receiving the verbal acknowledgment (M=5.57) felt significantly more appreciated than those receiving the $0.05 financial acknowledgment (M=4.38), F(1,47)=8.50, p=.005, supporting the trivialization effect (H1).

dependent_variable: Standardized exam score (midterm+final sum, s_tot)
main_predictor: Share female among the five nearest neighbors (avg5_girl)
sample_definition: Female students (girl==1) excluding favored students (special1==0), with non-missing outcomes, peer measures, and covariates
model_specification: OLS with classroom-block fixed effects (gcb) and cluster-robust SE at classroom (gc)
controls: Average baseline score of neighbor 5, deskmate favored status, share favored in neighbor 4, own baseline test score, age, birth order, mother's and father's education, baseline interest in Chinese/math/English
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 4 panel B specification for female sample: share female in neighbor 5 with the average baseline of neighbor 5 included; controls match the paper's preferred full specification yielding N=245.
reasoning: Regressing standardized exam score on share female among the 5 nearest neighbors (avg5_girl) in the female subsample, controlling for average baseline score of the 5 neighbors, deskmate-favored-status, neighbor-4 favored share, own baseline test, demographics, interests, and classroom-block fixed effects (clustered SEs at classroom), yields coefficient 0.217 (SE 0.085, t=2.56, p=0.010, N=245). A move from 0 to 5 female neighbors raises a female's score by ~0.22 SD, matching the paper's claim of 0.2–0.3 SD.

dependent_variable: Absolute attitude change |T2-T1| (mean of 3 attitude items)
main_predictor: Objective ambivalence × overall certainty interaction (mean-centered)
sample_definition: Study 1 participants with complete attitude data at both time points (N=174)
model_specification: OLS regression: |change| ~ amb_c + cert_c + extremity + amb_c*cert_c
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Study 1 methods: objective ambivalence via Thompson et al. (P+N)/2 - |P-N|; certainty as mean of 7 items; DV as absolute difference in 3-item attitude index; centered predictors with extremity covariate.
reasoning: The objective ambivalence × certainty interaction predicting absolute attitude change over time was significant, B=0.037, t(169)=2.28, p=.024, controlling for extremity. The interaction sign matches the claim: certainty predicts more stability when ambivalence is low and less stability when ambivalence is high.

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters)
main_predictor: Log portfolio equity stock (foreign ownership)
sample_definition: 23 OECD countries, election-years 1970-2007 with non-missing variables
model_specification: Dynamic panel OLS with LDV, country FE, country-specific quadratic time trends; cluster-robust SE by country
controls: Log registered voters, %VAP 30-69, years since last election, US mid-term dummy, compulsory voting, mixed system, PR system, disproportionality, ENPS, margin
operationalization_notes: Used Model 4 (log portfolio equity stock) as a direct test of the foreign-ownership constraint hypothesis since the dataset does not contain the composite 'Ownership Scale' variable. Estimated via OLS rather than Arellano-Bond, the most charitable defensible approximation of the paper's specification.
reasoning: Regressing turnout on log portfolio equity stock (foreign ownership measure, Model 4 in the paper) with lagged turnout, full controls, country fixed effects, and country-specific quadratic time trends yields a significant negative coefficient (b = -2.49, SE = 0.72, t = -3.49, p < .001), supporting the ownership-constraint hypothesis that foreign ownership reduces turnout.

dependent_variable: Number of BBB complaints (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: first_A indicator (firm name begins with A or a number)
sample_definition: All Illinois plumbing firms in final_data.dta (n=2,293)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test comparing mean complaints across name types
operationalization_notes: Directly matches the paper's headline comparison of mean complaints by name type (Table 2 panel A).
reasoning: A-name/number plumbing firms average 1.34 BBB complaints vs 0.25 for others (~5.4x), Welch t(310.1)=3.85, p<.001, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Cooperative bargaining strategy (ordinal, 0=concession-extracting to 3=most cooperative)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure (average zone of agreement across linked issues; higher = more differently valued)
sample_definition: All 588 state-by-negotiation observations in the DEU-based bargaining-strategies dataset, no exclusions

model_specification: Fuzzy regression-discontinuity 2SLS: pass-rate regressed on GM-status with vote-share centered at 50 as running variable (linear); WIN = I[vote>50] as instrument; cluster-robust SE at school id
operationalization_notes: Implements the paper's headline RD specification (2SLS-TE, Linear in Table 2, panel A) using the available school-year panel from main_data.dta. Most direct test of the claim that GM conversion improved achievement.
reasoning: Fuzzy RD via 2SLS using win-vote dummy as instrument for GM status, with linear control in vote share minus 50, yields a positive and statistically significant effect of GM conversion on the share of pupils passing 5+ GCSEs of about 9.2 points (cluster-robust SE = 3.27; t = 2.80, p ≈ 0.005, 742 school clusters). This supports the paper's claim of large achievement gains for GM converters.

dependent_variable: Participated in lab experiment (0/1)

reasoning: In a probit of lab participation on amount sent in the trust game with controls for female, commerce, international, day, flyer order, chosen for payment, and tutor fixed effects (robust SE clustered by tutor), the coefficient on Sent is -0.0240 with z=-2.54 (p≈0.011), N=658. More sent => less likely to participate, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: took_act (illness episode treated with an ACT)

sample_definition: First illness episodes only; excluded households assigned to RDT subsidy and households selected for surprise/ex-post drug-shop RDT (first_ep==1 & rdt_any==0 & ex_post==0); N=631

operationalization_notes: Operationalization follows Section 5.1/Table 2: outcome = took_act, predictor = the 92% subsidy dummy (the 'very high subsidy' AMFm-like level), sample restricted as described in the paper. t-statistic reported with cluster-robust SE; df approximated as clusters-1 = 574.
reasoning: OLS of the indicator 'took ACT for illness' on three subsidy-level dummies (omitting the no-subsidy control), with strata FE and age-of-head controls, clustered on household. The 92% subsidy (act40) raises ACT access by 22.5 percentage points (SE 0.053; t=4.26, p<0.001), more than doubling the control mean (~19%), exactly matching the paper's Table 2 Panel B.

dependent_variable: Normalized combined math + reading-recognition PIAT score (renormalized on random sample)

reasoning: Levels OLS regression of the normalized combined math-reading PIAT score on total family income (in year-2000 $1,000s) with the paper's baseline child/mother controls and year fixed effects yields a coefficient of 0.0048 (cluster-robust SE 0.00068; t=7.07, p<0.001), closely matching the 0.005 estimate in Table 2 (panel A col. 1) and supporting the directional claim that higher income raises short-run combined math+reading scores.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs, 4-item average)

reasoning: OLS regression of work absorption on single/childless dummy with controls (gender, age, job level) yielded b = -0.311, SE = 0.132, t(348) = -2.36, p = .019. Single, childless workers reported significantly lower absorption than other family structures, matching the published coefficient (b = -.31, SE = .13).

dependent_variable: ProperName (whether response addressed applicant by proper name)
main_predictor: Applicant race (Hispanic vs. white name)
sample_definition: Responses from emails sent by Hispanic- or white-named applicants where ProperName was coded (i.e., applicants who received a response); Black emailers excluded
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2)
operationalization_notes: Direct bivariate test of the comparative claim, restricting to Hispanic vs. white treatment arms; ProperName is naturally defined only for applicants who got a response, matching the paper's outcome.
reasoning: Among email responses, 77/187 (41.2%) Hispanic-name applicants were greeted by their proper name vs. 107/175 (61.1%) white-name applicants, χ²(1,N=362)=14.42, p<.001 — Hispanic applicants were significantly less likely to be greeted by name, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Shading frequency (qualityc==1, low quality)
main_predictor: Contract type (rigid vs. flexible)
sample_definition: Baseline treatment (condition==1), good state of nature only (costc in {20,25}); rigid contracts have no trade in the bad state.
model_specification: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on 5 session-level shading rates (rigid vs. flexible), one-sided (rigid < flexible).
operationalization_notes: Paper's main test for this claim is a nonparametric signed-rank test using session averages; I replicate that directly using 5 baseline sessions and the good state (only state with trade under rigid contracts).
reasoning: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on 5 baseline-session shading rates (good state) shows shading is strictly lower in rigid than flexible contracts in every session (rigid mean ~4-11%, flexible ~20-33%). Signed-rank W=0, one-sided p=0.031, matching the paper's reported result.

dependent_variable: log of state energy-related CO2 emissions (carbon_adj)
main_predictor: log of average weekly working hours (wrkhrs)
sample_definition: 50 US states, years 2007–2013 (N=350)
model_specification: Two-way fixed effects OLS (state + year dummies), log-log specification
controls: log employed pop %, log GDP per hour (labor productivity), log total population, log manufacturing share of GDP, log energy production, log working-age population share
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 3 Model 1 (Scale FE). Household size omitted (IPUMS data not in replication package). Manufacturing converted to % of GDP, employed and working-age population to % of total population to match paper definitions.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects (state + year) log-log regression of state CO2 emissions on average working hours with the paper's Model 1 (Scale FE) controls (excluding household size, which requires unavailable IPUMS data), the coefficient on log working hours is positive (b≈0.49) and statistically significant (t(287)=2.12, p=0.035), supporting the claim of a positive working-hours/emissions relationship over 2007–2013.

dependent_variable: consider (considered attack on nuclear program in dyad-year)
main_predictor: hostileMID (violent MID in t-1, use of force or war)
sample_definition: Politically relevant dyads (polrel=1) with nonmissing consider and hostileMID
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2 contingency table)
operationalization_notes: Directly mirrors the paper's Table 3A bivariate test of Hypothesis 1, the most direct empirical test of whether prior violent conflict elevates the salience of the proliferation threat (operationalized as considered attacks).
reasoning: In politically relevant dyads, considered attacks occurred in 5.2% of dyad-years preceded by a hostile MID vs. 0.25% of those without; chi-square = 155.79 (df=1, n=5686, p<.0001). This strongly supports the claim that prior violent militarized conflict raises the salience of the proliferation threat, matching the direction and significance of the original Table 3A bivariate test.

dependent_variable: splinter (binary indicator that the county became part of a new splinter district in wave t)
main_predictor: DEC share ratio (county share of seats on District Executive Committee divided by population share) — inverse measure of political marginalization
sample_definition: All county-wave observations with non-missing covariates (475 county-waves across post-1996/2001/2006 election waves in Uganda)

controls: Ethnic marginalization indicator, development summary index (MARG), number of counties in district, lagged breakup status, region dummies, electoral-wave dummies
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's main specification (Eq. 3 / Model 1). Political marginalization operationalized as DEC share ratio per paper's pre-registered measure; negative coefficient supports the directional claim.
reasoning: Logit regression of splinter (county forming a new district) on DEC share ratio (political marginalization measure) with ethnic marginalization, development index, number of counties, breakup lag, and region/wave fixed effects yields a negative coefficient on DEC share ratio of -0.72 (z = -3.74, p < 0.001, N=475). Higher representation in the district executive committee (less political marginalization) reduces secession likelihood, supporting the claim that politically marginalized areas are more likely to secede.

dependent_variable: recog1duml (dichotomous: State B recognizes State A in next observation)
main_predictor: nukeduma (State A nuclear weapons status, dummy)

controls: Nuclear Weapons B, Nuke A x Nuke B, Rivalry Status A, Rivalry Status B, Dyadic Rivalry, CINC A, CINC B, CINC A x CINC B, Democracy A, Democracy B, Democracy A x Democracy B, Contiguity, ln(Distance), Alliance
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 1 (dichotomous model) specification. Omitted BKT temporal splines (variable names not identifiable for the recognition DV); slight resulting N reduction (197k vs 213k reported). Main coefficient on State A's nuclear status is the most direct test of the claim that nuclear-capable states are more likely to be recognized.
reasoning: Logit regression of dichotomous diplomatic recognition (B recognizes A) on State A's nuclear status, controlling for B's nuclear status, the interaction, dyadic and monadic rivalry, CINC capabilities and their interaction, democracy scores and interaction, contiguity, ln(distance) and alliance yields a coefficient of 0.794 (SE 0.030, z=26.08, p<0.001) on nukeduma. Nuclear-capable states are significantly more likely to be recognized, matching the paper's claim and Table 1 dichotomous model.

dependent_variable: Log of absolute opinion change on immigration index (wave 3 - wave 2)
main_predictor: Group-level deliberative quality – level of justification (DQ_jlev)
sample_definition: EuroPolis participants with complete data on outcome, group-level DQI justification score, and Sanders-set controls (N=174 individuals in 13 small groups)

controls: Gender, age, education, Catholic, Protestant, working class, religiosity, left-right ideology and its square, knowledge change, social conformity pressure (above and below), left-party and right-party vote intention, and four clarify-thinking items (other participants, experts, politicians, briefing material)
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 2 Model 2b in the paper: log absolute opinion change as DV, group-level justification rationality as key predictor, multilevel model nesting individuals within small groups, with Sanders's predictor set as controls.
reasoning: Multilevel REML model with individuals nested in 13 discussion groups regresses log absolute opinion change on immigration on group-level justification rationality (DQ_jlev) with the Sanders covariates. The coefficient is 0.130 (SE=0.066, z=1.96, p≈0.05), matching the paper's Table 2 Model 2b and supporting the claim that higher justification rationality is associated with greater opinion change.

dependent_variable: Individual effort (work, 0/1), averaged within each 3-person group across all 6 rounds
main_predictor: Reward scheme under complementarity: symmetrical (444COM) vs. discriminating (345COM)
sample_definition: All subjects in the two complementarity treatments (345COM, n=12 groups; 444COM, n=11 groups), all 6 rounds
model_specification: Two-sided Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon rank-sum test on group-level mean effort (independent observations: matching groups of 3)
operationalization_notes: The paper compares effort across reward schemes within complementarity using nonparametric tests on independent group observations; group means across all rounds provide the most direct test of the claim of 'substantially lower efforts' under the symmetrical scheme.
reasoning: Mean effort (work) across all 6 rounds is 91.7% in the discriminating treatment (345COM) vs 72.2% in the symmetrical treatment (444COM) under complementarity. A two-sided Mann-Whitney rank-sum test on the 23 group-level means yields U=95, p=0.0696, with the discriminating scheme producing substantially higher efforts, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Within-senator difference in (anti-immigration policy actions mentioned − pro-immigration policy actions mentioned) across responses
main_predictor: Letter type sent to senator (pro- vs. anti-immigration constituent letter)
sample_definition: U.S. senators who responded to both the pro- and anti-immigration letters (N=56)
model_specification: Paired (within-subjects) t-test on the (anti − pro) action-mention difference across letter conditions
operationalization_notes: Matches the paper's Table 1 'Anti − Pro' within-subjects comparison, which is the most direct test of tailoring; treats each senator as their own control across the two counterbalanced letters.
reasoning: Within-senator paired t-test on the difference between (anti-immigration actions mentioned − pro-immigration actions mentioned) across the two letter conditions yields t(55) = -3.45, p ≈ 0.001. Senators mention more anti-immigration actions and fewer pro-immigration actions when replying to the anti-immigration constituent than when replying to the pro-immigration constituent, confirming that they tailor explanations to the audience.

dependent_variable: log wage gain at migration (log postmigration wage - log premigration wage)
main_predictor: education category (no high school vs. college graduate, omitted)
sample_definition: Pooled NIS immigrants from countries with GDP per worker < 1/4 of U.S. + all MP (MMP/LAMP) immigrants, with valid pre- and postmigration wages (paper N=3,539)
model_specification: OLS regression of log wage gain on education dummies (omitted: college graduate) with country fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Table III specification (Section IV / p. 682). Could not execute because NIS microdata are confidential and not provided in the replication archive, and MMP data are stored as opaque MATLAB class objects that available Python/Octave readers cannot parse into tabular form.
reasoning: The claim refers to the coefficient on the 'no high school' dummy (relative to college graduates) in a pooled NIS + MP regression of log wage gains on education with country fixed effects (Table III, N=3,539; coefficient ~0.599, implying exp(0.599)-1 ~= 82% higher wage gain). I cannot compute this on the provided dataset: (1) the restricted New Immigrant Survey (NIS) microdata required for the pooled sample is not included (the nis 2003_1/ and nis 2003_2/ directories in the replication archive are empty); and (2) the MMP/LAMP-side data files (mmp_lamp/.../data_table.mat etc.) are stored as MATLAB MCOS class objects (custom dataLH.DataTable), which neither scipy.io, mat73, nor Octave can deserialize. Without the underlying individual-level wage-gain and education variables, the directly relevant t-test on the 'no high school' coefficient cannot be produced.

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses reflecting the learned (negative) meaning of the cue (FAbaseC vs FAsuppC)
main_predictor: TNT status: baseline vs suppressed (within-subjects)

operationalization_notes: Claim concerns the benefit of suppression practice for nonruminators on the indirect (transfer) test. The provided dataset corresponds to Experiment 2 (free-association task). The most direct test is the within-subjects baseline-vs-suppression contrast restricted to nonruminators, mirroring the planned comparison reported in the paper.

This indicates suppression practice reduced retrieval of the learned (negative) meaning, supporting the claim that suppression practice was beneficial for nonruminators.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being (wellbeing scale)
main_predictor: Interaction: parental status (childless ref.) × country-level % (strongly) disapproving of childlessness
sample_definition: ESS3 respondents from 24 countries with non-missing data on all model variables (the analytic sample provided in the authors' replication file; men + women pooled)

controls: Age, age², marital status, education, parental education, religious attendance, paid employment, born in country, gender

Childless is reference category, so the 'Lives with children × disapproval' interaction directly indexes how the childlessness disadvantage varies with country tolerance.

This means parents' well-being advantage over the childless grows as country-level disapproval rises, i.e., the childlessness disadvantage is smaller in more tolerant countries — supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: DSM-5 total psychopathology score (DSM5_Total)

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (political knowledge test score)

dependent_variable: GDP growth rate at t+2 (f2gdpidx)
main_predictor: Connected to provincial secretary (msec2currentsec OR mayor2currentsec)
sample_definition: City-year panel of Chinese prefectures, observations with non-missing dependent variable, connection indicator, and all controls

controls: Net transfer (dep), starting-year log GDP/log pop/log invest/GDP growth for both secretary and mayor predecessors; city secretary and mayor age, education, gender; tenure-length dummies (<1y, 1-3y, 3-5y) for both leaders
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 1 Model 3 specification described in the methods section: dependent variable GDP growth at t+2, binary connection indicator (either secretary or mayor connected to provincial secretary), full set of fixed effects and controls described in Table 1 note.
reasoning: Replicating the paper's baseline Model 3 (Table 1), I regress GDP growth at t+2 on a binary indicator that the city secretary or mayor is connected to the incumbent provincial secretary, with city FE, province-year FE, and economic and leader controls, clustering SEs by city. dependent_variable: log(share of foreign players in the league), for top- vs lower-ability foreigners
main_predictor: treat (Denmark=1) × post (year>=1991) × high-ability (triple-difference interaction)
sample_definition: Denmark and Sweden, 1980-2008, top-league players, stacked across ability tiers (top vs lower) using the variables stop, slow, f, dom in basesynthetic_control.dta
model_specification: OLS DDD: logshare ~ treat + post + high + treat:post + treat:high + post:high + treat:post:high
controls: Main effects and two-way interactions of treat, post, high (DDD design)
operationalization_notes: The verbal claim is differential composition: high-ability foreign share rises more than low-ability foreign share after the Danish reform. Sweden is used as the comparison (the dominant synthetic-control donor for Denmark in Figure 3 of the paper, and the only non-Denmark country available with comparable coverage in the synthetic-control dataset).
reasoning: In a triple-difference (country × post × ability) regression of log(foreign player share) using Denmark vs its synthetic-control comparison (Sweden, the dominant donor in the paper's synthetic control), 1980-2008, the triple interaction is positive and significant (b=1.30, SE=0.575, t=2.27, p=0.026). The post-1991 Danish tax cut to foreigners disproportionately raised the share of high-ability foreign players relative to low-ability foreign players, consistent with the paper's claim of a sorting effect in ability composition.

dependent_variable: willingness to pay to protect the environment (willingness_to_pay)

dependent_variable: ln(imports) of product into defendant market, post-dispute years

sample_definition: Early-settled disputes only (earlysettle==1), post-dispute window (counter 1..5), all positions (complainants, third parties, non-participants), observations with non-missing covariates
model_specification: OLS regression of ln_imports on Complainant, ln Defendant GDP, ln Partner GDP, Democratic pair, lagged disputed imports, ln total imports, with standard errors clustered by dispute
controls: ln Defendant GDP, ln Partner GDP, Democratic pair, lagged disputed imports, ln total imports

reasoning: In the early-settlement subsample of post-dispute product-year observations, the OLS coefficient on Complainant (with disputant-clustered SEs) is 0.283 (z=2.27, p=0.023), indicating that complainant countries' post-dispute imports into defendant markets grow significantly more than non-participants', consistent with the paper's claim of discriminatory outcomes under privacy.

dependent_variable: entre_wage (new business formation per working-age population)
main_predictor: medage_20_64 (median age of population aged 20-64)
sample_definition: GEM country-year panel, 82 countries, years 2001-2010 (N=393)

Lower median age is strongly associated with higher new business formation, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Ratio of perceived to actual arm length (RatioRight, RatioLeft)

model_specification: Paired-samples t-test (one-tailed, as in original)

dependent_variable: Standardized exam score (midterm+final combined), s_tot
main_predictor: Share of females among the 5 surrounding (neighbor-5) peers (avg5_girl)

model_specification: OLS with block (gcb) fixed effects; standard errors clustered by classroom
controls: Average baseline test score of neighbor 5 (avg5_s0_totx); own baseline score; desk mate's favored status; share favored among neighbor 4; height; age; birth order; mother's and father's education; baseline interest in Chinese, math, English; leave-out block means of gender and baseline score; block fixed effects

sample_definition: Study 1 participants with complete T1 attitude, T2 attitude, certainty, and ambivalence data (N=174)

operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Study 1 methods: objective ambivalence via Griffin formula (P+N)/2 - |P-N|; certainty as mean of 7 certainty items; attitudes averaged across 3 items at each wave; extremity controlled as covariate.
reasoning: In Study 1, regressing attitude change on centered certainty, objective ambivalence, their interaction, and extremity yielded a significant certainty × ambivalence interaction, B=.037, t(169)=2.28, p=.024, matching the paper's reported pattern that certainty predicts greater stability as ambivalence decreases.

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters)
main_predictor: Portfolio Equity Stock (log) — the most flexible/mobile foreign ownership measure
sample_definition: Election-year observations from 23 OECD countries, 1970-2007, with complete data on the dependent variable, lagged turnout, and all baseline controls
model_specification: OLS dynamic panel with country fixed effects and country-specific quadratic time trends (syear* and syearsq*), cluster-robust SEs by country (approximates the paper's LSDVC specification; paper notes OLS yields very similar results)

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of bootstrapped partial semantic networks (binarized TMFG-filtered cosine-similarity networks built from animal verbal-fluency responses)

Composite openness based on NEO-FFI and BFAS Openness aspect z-scores (excluding Intellect, matching the Mplus latent-openness model on the OSF).

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Index (0–8, ordinal)

dependent_variable: pt_gcse_5_a_c (% pupils with 5+ GCSE A*-C passes)

dependent_variable: took_act (illness episode was treated with an ACT)

dependent_variable: Two-year change in combined PIAT score (average of normalized math, reading-recognition, reading-comprehension)

operationalization_notes: The paper's headline 0.06 SD per $1,000 comes from a simulated-EITC IV that requires reconstructing the EITC schedule by year and number of children; this is not feasible to reconstruct exactly with the released variables, so I implemented the most direct OLS analog (two-year first differences matching the paper's baseline difference specification and sample restrictions from Tables 2 and A1). This tests the same directional claim using the same panel and same outcome.
reasoning: OLS in two-year first differences of the combined (math + reading recognition + reading comprehension) standardized PIAT score on the two-year change in family income ($1,000s) yields a positive coefficient (0.0008 SD per $1,000) with cluster-robust t = 1.81 (p = 0.07). The direction is consistent with the paper's claim that a $1,000 increase in income raises combined math and reading scores in the short run, though the magnitude is much smaller than the paper's IV estimate (~0.06), as expected given attenuation bias and the lack of EITC-based instrumentation in this direct test.

dependent_variable: work absorption (engwkabs, 4-item Rothbard scale average)

Single, childless employees report significantly lower absorption than others, matching the paper's Study 1 finding (b=-.31, p<.05).

dependent_variable: ProperName (response began with a personalized/named greeting, 1/0)

A 2x2 chi-square most directly tests this; the public dataset lacks continuous covariates used in the paper's logit (only tertile versions are provided), so I used the simple unadjusted test that maps directly to the verbal claim.
reasoning: Among email responses, 41.2% of Hispanic-named applicants received a named greeting versus 61.1% of white-named applicants — a ~20 percentage point gap. Pearson chi-square test of independence gives χ²(1)=14.42, p<.001, confirming Hispanics were significantly less likely to be greeted by name than whites, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Session-level frequency of normal (non-shaded) quality among completed trades
main_predictor: Contract type (rigid vs. flexible)

reasoning: Per-session frequency of normal quality (among trades) is higher in rigid contracts (mean ~0.94) than in flexible contracts (mean ~0.74) in all 5 baseline sessions. A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the 5 session pairs yields W=15, p=0.03125, confirming that shading occurs significantly less under rigid contracts.

dependent_variable: log of state-level CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel combustion (carbon_unadj, MMT CO2)
main_predictor: log of average weekly working hours (wrkhrs)

operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Model 1 (scale-effect, two-way FE) as the most direct test of the claim. Used OLS with state and year dummies since statsmodels lacks built-in Prais-Winsten; omitted average household size because it is not included in the provided compiled.dta. Reported the t-statistic on log working hours.
reasoning: In a two-way (state + year) fixed-effects log-log panel regression of state CO2 emissions on working hours and the scale-effect controls (employed pop %, GDP per hour, total pop, manufacturing % of GDP, energy production, working-age pop), the coefficient on log working hours is positive (b=0.49) and significant (t(287)=2.18, p=0.030), supporting the paper's positive relationship.

dependent_variable: consider (whether a state considered attacking a target's nuclear program)

dependent_variable: splinter (county became part of a new district in wave t)

A lower DEC share ratio (more politically marginalized) significantly increases the probability of secession, matching the paper's M1 result.

dependent_variable: recog1dum (State B formally recognizes State A; dichotomous)

dependent_variable: log of absolute immigration opinion change between wave 2 and wave 3 (change_w3w2_log)

This matches the paper's Model 2b and supports the claim: higher group-level justification rationality is associated with greater absolute opinion change.

dependent_variable: Group-level mean effort (share of work=1 averaged over rounds within group)
main_predictor: Reward scheme (444COM symmetrical vs. 345COM discriminating)

A two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test on group-level mean effort yields z=-1.785 (p=.074), directionally consistent with the paper's claim that the symmetrical scheme elicits substantially lower efforts than the cost-equivalent discriminating scheme.

dependent_variable: Within-senator difference in mentions of anti-immigration minus pro-immigration compensating actions (companti - comppro)

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses indicating the learned meaning of the cue (baseline vs. suppressed conditions, homographic and nonhomographic cues combined: FAbaseC, FAsuppC)

controls: Counterbalancing assignment (CB) included as between-subjects factor; no other covariates
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether suppression practice was beneficial for nonruminators on the indirect transfer test. The most direct test is the baseline-vs-suppressed contrast within nonruminators on the free-association DV, mirroring the paper's reported planned comparison.
reasoning: Within nonruminators (n=27), free-association responses indicating the learned cue meaning were significantly lower for suppressed cues (M=29.6%) than for baseline cues (M=45.7%), F(1,24)=10.94, p=.003 (mixed ANOVA with counterbalancing set as a between-subjects factor). dependent_variable: Psychological well-being (8-item CES-D, reverse-coded so higher = better)
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction: parental status (lives-with-children vs. childless ref.) × country-level % who (strongly) disapprove of childlessness
sample_definition: Respondents aged 40+ from 24 ESS Round 3 countries with non-missing data on all model variables (missing==0); N=23,754 in 24 countries
model_specification: Two-level linear mixed model with random intercepts for country, ML estimation; fixed effects for parental status (lives-with-children, empty nest; childless reference), country-level % (strongly) disapproves of childlessness (constructed from anvcld<=2 aggregated by country), and the two parental-status × disapproval interactions, plus individual controls
controls: Age, age-squared, marital status, own education, parental education (with missing category), religious attendance, paid employment, born in country, gender
operationalization_notes: Combined-gender analogue of Model 2a/2b. Country % disapprove constructed from individual anvcld item (1=strongly disapproves to 5=strongly approves), classifying anvcld in {1,2} as (strongly) disapproves, matching the description in the paper's methods. The pre-supplied 'childless_perc' variable in the file is the % childless, not % disapproving, so the disapproval measure was rebuilt from anvcld.
reasoning: In a multilevel (random-intercept) regression of CES-D well-being on parental status, country-level % strongly disapproving of childlessness, and their interaction (with childless as reference and individual controls), the 'lives with children × % disapproves' interaction is positive and highly significant (B=0.0021, SE=0.00045, z=4.55, p<.001). A positive interaction implies that the parent–childless well-being gap is larger in countries with more disapproving (less tolerant) norms, i.e., the childless disadvantage is smaller in tolerant countries — matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: DSM-5 total psychopathology score (DSM5_Total)
main_predictor: Mini-K total score (life history strategy; higher = slower)
sample_definition: All 138 participants with complete data on both measures
