I collapsed the panel-format TR data to one row per conflict (id), computed duration in months from yrst/most to yrend/moend, and contrasted irregular vs all other types in a single dummy to provide the most demanding direct test of 'irregular lasts longer than all other types of conflict'.
reasoning: Weibull AFT regression of conflict duration (months) on an indicator for irregular vs. all other technologies of rebellion (conventional + SNC) gives a positive log-time coefficient of 0.94 (SE=0.21, z=4.50, p<0.001, N=115 conflicts with non-missing start/end dates). This means irregular conflicts last roughly exp(0.94)≈2.5 times longer than other types, confirming the paper's claim that irregular conflicts last significantly longer than all other types.

dependent_variable: lndrate (log of monthly state-level death rate)
main_predictor: Number of days with mean temperature >90°F (b10_10) interacted with a Post-1960 indicator
sample_definition: State-month panel 1930-2004, dropping observations missing the death-rate outcome (N=43,464)
model_specification: Two-way fixed-effects WLS (state and year-month FE) with population weights and standard errors clustered by state, estimated via linearmodels PanelOLS
controls: Age-composition shares (sh_0000, sh_4564, sh_6599) and log real per-capita income (lri); state FE; year-month FE
operationalization_notes: The claim is operationalized as a structural break in the slope of mortality on hot days at the 1959/1960 boundary used in the paper's Table 4. A single interaction coefficient yields one t-test directly tied to the 'decline across decades' claim. Time effects use year-month rather than fully-saturated state-month-by-yearmo terms for tractability, but the design follows the paper's FE structure.
reasoning: The interaction of days-above-90°F with a post-1960 indicator is -0.0217 (SE 0.0044, t=-4.92, p<1e-6), implying the temperature-mortality slope falls from ~0.021 log deaths per extra hot day before 1960 to roughly zero after 1960. This directly supports the paper's claim of a significant decline in the temperature-mortality relationship across decades.

dependent_variable: Choice to buy the $14.99 DVD (1 = buy, 0 = not buy)
main_predictor: Opportunity-cost cue × connectedness (ZFINAL) interaction
sample_definition: All 88 participants from Study 1A (DVD scenario)
model_specification: Logistic regression: buy ~ cue + ZFINAL + cue*ZFINAL
operationalization_notes: Study 1A is the DVD dataset; the claim is the cue-by-connectedness interaction. Following the paper's logistic-regression analysis, I tested the interaction coefficient as the most direct test of the claim. notBuy=1 in the data corresponds to choosing to buy (recovered from the 71%/51% rates by condition reported in the paper).
reasoning: In a logistic regression of DVD purchase on opportunity-cost cue (0/1), z-scored connectedness, and their interaction (Study 1A, N=88), the cue × connectedness interaction was significant (b = -1.05, z = -2.10, p = .036). The cue reduced purchasing more strongly for participants more connected to their future selves, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Referral is female (REF_female, 0/1)
main_predictor: CA gender (OP_female, 0/1)
sample_definition: CAs assigned to the either-gender (unrestricted) treatment who actually made a referral with observed referral gender
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on the 2x2 CA-gender x referral-gender table
operationalization_notes: Replicates panel C, column 4 of Table 1: comparison of share of female referrals by CA gender among either-gender treatment CAs.
reasoning: Among CAs in the either-gender treatment who made a referral (N=220), 22.6% of male CAs referred a woman vs. 42.5% of female CAs. Pearson chi-square = 9.91 (df=1), p=.0016, confirming that CA men are significantly less likely to refer women than CA women.

dependent_variable: ali_stdscore_gr10 (standardized ALI math test score, mean 500/SD 100 in controls), 10th grade year 1
main_predictor: Treatment 3 (ALI combined student + teacher + administrator incentives) dummy, with T1 and T2 dummies also included; control group is the omitted category
sample_definition: Students in the 2008/9 entering 10th-grade cohort who took the year-1 ALI test and had non-missing school-level baseline covariates (87 of 88 schools, N=11,314)
model_specification: OLS regression of ALI standardized score on T1, T2, T3 dummies plus pre-program school-level controls; standard errors clustered at the school level
controls: School-level pre-program covariates: mean 9th-grade ENLACE math for current 10th and 11th graders, 2007/8 school average 12th-grade ENLACE math and language scores, four region dummies, and five state dummies
operationalization_notes: Chose the most direct test of the claim: the headline T3 ATE in the first cohort/year that the paper highlights. Used the unadjusted (no copying correction) score, which provides the upper-bound point estimate the paper reports as 32.3 in Table 6; replicated exactly with t-statistic computed from cluster-robust SE.
reasoning: Replicating the paper's Table 6 specification (no copying adjustment) for the 10th-grade cohort in program year 1, the T3 treatment dummy yields a coefficient of 32.31 standardized score points (SE 6.18, school-clustered), t = 5.23, p < 0.001 — a large, statistically significant positive effect of the joint student–teacher–administrator incentive scheme on ALI math test scores, supporting the authors' claim.

dependent_variable: log discount rate (interval-censored: lndiscratelo, lndiscratehi)
main_predictor: treatE (ethnic-identity salience prime indicator)
sample_definition: Experiment 1 Asian-American subjects (raceA==1); 71 subjects × 4 intertemporal-choice blocks = 284 observations
model_specification: Interval regression (intreg) with controls largestakes, longterm, largelong; cluster-robust SE by subject id (Stata Table 2A specification)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Table 2A specification, which is the analysis most directly tied to the patience claim. Replicated point estimate and SE essentially exactly (coef -1.4165, SE 0.378).
reasoning: Interval regression of log discount rate on the ethnic-identity-salience treatment (with stakes/term controls and cluster-robust SE on 71 subjects) yields a treatment coefficient of -1.417 (SE 0.378, z=-3.74, p<0.001). The negative sign on log discount rate indicates Asian-American subjects in the ethnicity-salient condition exhibit lower discount rates (more patient choices), supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Mean cooperation frequency per subject (across all 23 supergames)
main_predictor: Termination rule: Deterministic vs Stochastic (in short-duration treatments)
sample_definition: Subjects in Short-Deterministic (tmnt=3, n=48) and Short-Stochastic (tmnt=4, n=48) treatments
model_specification: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U rank-sum test on subject-level cooperation rates
operationalization_notes: Most direct non-parametric test of the claim, using each subject's overall mean cooperation rate as one independent observation. This is more demanding than pooling all subject-supergame observations and avoids parametric assumptions of the regression in Table II.
reasoning: Mann-Whitney U test on subject-level mean cooperation rates yields U=1565, z=3.03, p=0.0025 (n=48 vs 48). Mean cooperation is 63.3% in Short-Deterministic vs 52.3% in Short-Stochastic, confirming significantly higher cooperation under deterministic horizon in short games (though p is not <0.001 as stated in the paper when using subject-level non-parametric test).

dependent_variable: Distance between government and median voter (govdisto)
main_predictor: Distance between plurality vote winner and median voter (pldist1)
sample_definition: All SMD-system election-year observations with non-missing govdisto and pldist1 (manifesto/Kim-Fording data)
model_specification: OLS bivariate regression: govdisto = a + b*pldist1
operationalization_notes: The claim implies the plurality winner is the key mechanism linking SMD systems to median-voter congruence. The most direct test, mirroring Table 2 in the paper, regresses government distance on plurality-winner distance within SMD systems; a large positive coefficient with a significant t-statistic indicates that variation in government congruence under SMD is driven by how close the plurality winner sits to the median voter.
reasoning: In the SMD subsample (n=85), the distance between the plurality vote winner and the median voter strongly predicts government-median voter distance (b=0.87, t(83)=15.73, p<.001, R^2=.75), confirming that under SMD rules party competition pushes the plurality winner toward (and hence the government toward) the median voter.

dependent_variable: nwar1 (occurrence of a new civil war following the first postconflict election)
main_predictor: T2fpemths1 (months between end of civil war and first postconflict election)
sample_definition: 98 postconflict-election observations from BS09_DATA_main.dta restricted to the sample used in the paper's baseline FPE analysis (cwids appearing in iDOSERESPONSE_fpebase.dta)
model_specification: Logistic regression with standard errors clustered by country (cwid)
controls: FPE level (national), FPE level (concurrent), Polity IV at FPE, post-Cold War era, victory, UN intervention, UN electoral assistance, previous civil wars (eventno2)
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Table 1 Model 1 baseline specification, which is the most direct test of the central claim. Using the unrestricted/uninteracted main effect of election timing on civil war recurrence yields the most demanding defensible test.
reasoning: Reproducing Table 1, Model 1 (logit of civil war recurrence on election timing in months plus controls, SEs clustered by country, N=98), the coefficient on Election timing is -0.0031 (SE=0.004, z=-0.785, p=0.43). The direction matches the authors' claim (more months until election => lower probability of renewed war), but it is not statistically distinguishable from zero in this baseline specification.

dependent_variable: Femininity index (mean of feminine, gentle, sensitive trait ratings on 1-5 scale)
main_predictor: Target's behavior (green vs. nongreen, manipulated via reusable canvas bag vs. plastic bag)
sample_definition: All 194 participants who completed Study 2 (rated one of four target conditions)
model_specification: Two-way between-subjects ANOVA: femininity ~ behavior * target_gender
controls: None (target gender included as factorial design element, not covariate)
operationalization_notes: Identified the three femininity trait columns (25,26,33) by matching reported group means (G=2.64, NG=1.82). Reported the main effect of green vs. nongreen behavior most directly tied to the claim.
reasoning: In a 2 (target gender) x 2 (behavior: green vs. nongreen) ANOVA on a femininity index (mean of three feminine traits), the main effect of behavior was highly significant, F(1,190)=43.59, p<.001, with green targets rated as more feminine (M=2.64, SD=0.90, N=94) than nongreen targets (M=1.82, SD=0.86, N=100). This replicates the paper's reported effect.

dependent_variable: LV error rate: fraction of the 10 LV choices where the stochastically dominated lottery was selected (dominant = RV for decisions 1-4, PV for decisions 5-10)
main_predictor: Degree of risk aversion = average number of safe choices in the PV and RV multiple price lists
sample_definition: Risk-averse subjects only: those whose average number of safe choices in PV and RV is >= 5 (n=79); excludes 2 placeholder observations (age=99) and 25 risk-loving subjects.
model_specification: Pearson product-moment correlation between error rate and risk-aversion index (also cross-checked with Spearman rank correlation).
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's methodology described in Section 4: averaging safe choices across PV (Risk1) and RV (Risk2) formats to minimise attenuation bias, restricting to risk-averse subjects (avg safe >= 5), and computing the Pearson/Spearman correlation with the LV error rate constructed from Risk3 by treating decisions 1-4 dominant choice as RV and 5-10 as PV.
reasoning: Among the 79 risk-averse subjects (avg safe choices in PV and RV >= 5), the Pearson correlation between the LV error rate (fraction of dominated lotteries chosen) and the degree of risk aversion (mean number of safe choices across PV and RV) is r = -0.443 (p < 0.0001). The negative, highly significant correlation supports the claim that decision error decreases with risk aversion. Spearman rho = -0.419, p = 0.0001 corroborates.

dependent_variable: Desired yearly compensation (midpoint of selected $25K range, in $1000s)
main_predictor: Public-treatment indicator (classmates told they would see answers vs. anonymized)
sample_definition: Single female respondents in the main MBA questionnaire experiment (n=58: 31 private, 27 public)
model_specification: OLS with HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors; comp ~ public
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's stated coding rule (midpoint of the chosen range); treatment A identified as private since its mean ($130.6K) matches the paper's reported private-treatment mean ($131K).
reasoning: Among single female students, OLS of midpoint-coded desired compensation on a public-treatment dummy yields a coefficient of -$13,978 with HC1-robust SE 7,649 (z=-1.83, p=0.068, n=58). Direction matches the paper's claim that single women report lower desired salaries when classmates would see their answers, though my replication is marginally significant rather than the p=0.030 reported, plausibly due to slightly different endpoint coding of the salary ranges.

dependent_variable: pay_for_conditionality (dummy = parent willing to pay any positive amount to keep conditionality)
main_predictor: Treatment assignment: baseline (treatment=1) vs. text-message (treatment=2)
sample_definition: Parents assigned to baseline or text-message treatment groups (treatments 1 and 2); nonclassroom (3) and don't-tell (4) treatments excluded, per the paper's focus
model_specification: Two-proportion z-test (unpooled mean comparison without controls), equivalent to chi-square test of independence
operationalization_notes: The paper's most direct test of this claim is a mean comparison of the willingness-to-pay-for-conditionality dummy across the baseline and text-message treatment groups (Table 3/Eq. 1 without controls). I report the unadjusted two-proportion z-test as the cleanest and most demanding non-parametric realization of that comparison.
reasoning: In the baseline group, 49/60 (81.7%) of parents were willing to pay to keep conditionality, dropping to 10/51 (19.6%) in the text-message treatment. A two-proportion z-test yields z=6.53, p<1e-10, strongly supporting the claim that providing SMS monitoring reduces willingness to pay to keep conditionality from ~80% to ~20%.

dependent_variable: Monthly DTO-related deaths in municipality (deaths_total, government data)
main_predictor: after(1-6 months) x leader capture indicator (lpub_after06)
sample_definition: Treated leader municipalities and their matched control municipalities (treat_leader==1), Dec 2006-Sep 2011 (49 months x 14 munis = 686 obs with non-missing DTO data)
model_specification: Negative binomial GLM with municipality and date fixed effects; SE clustered by municipality
controls: after(6-12 months) x leader, after(>12 months) x leader, municipality fixed effects, date fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Most direct test of the claim is Table 1 column (1): short-term (1-6 month) effect of leader captures on DTO-related deaths in treated leader municipalities. I used the GLM negative binomial (statsmodels) rather than Stata's conditional FE NB; this is the most demanding fair specification given the tools available.
reasoning: In a negative binomial regression of DTO-related deaths on the leader-capture indicators (1-6 months, 6-12 months, and beyond) with municipality and month-year fixed effects on the leader-treatment subsample (14 municipalities, 686 month observations), the short-term (1-6 months) leader-capture coefficient is 0.209 (SE 0.211, z=0.99, p=0.32). The sign matches the paper's claim of an exacerbating short-term effect, but the effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero in this most-direct replication, making the claim not robust here.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of the binary TMFG-filtered semantic network, computed on bootstrapped partial networks
main_predictor: Openness-to-experience group (high vs low, median split on the mean z-score of NEO-FFI-3 openness and BFAS openness)
sample_definition: 516 participants from the cleaned final dataset; median-split into high (n=258) and low (n=258) openness groups; network nodes restricted to animal exemplars produced by >=2 participants in BOTH groups (167 shared nodes)
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test of bootstrap ASPL distributions (1000 partial networks per group at 50% nodes retained); TMFG filtering of cosine-similarity matrix, binarised undirected networks, ASPL on the largest connected component
controls: none (groups equated on N and on number of nodes/edges by construction)
operationalization_notes: The paper's most-demanding bootstrap level (50% nodes retained) was used, as smaller bootstrap fractions yield the most conservative effect size. ASPL was chosen as the network measure most directly corresponding to 'interconnected' per the paper's own framing.
reasoning: Replicating the paper's TMFG-based semantic-network construction (cosine similarity over animal-fluency responses, nodes appearing in >=2 participants per group) and a 50% node-drop bootstrap (1000 samples per group; the smallest/most-demanding percentage), the high-openness network had a significantly lower ASPL (M=2.507) than the low-openness network (M=2.632), Welch t(~1998)=-17.42, p<.001, d~0.78. This confirms the directional claim that the high-openness network is more interconnected.

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Index (0-8)
main_predictor: Reliance on Taxes (tax_rev_new, % of government revenues from taxes)
sample_definition: All country-years with non-missing values for the DV, lagged DV, and all controls (pooled cross-section time series, ~1981-2007).
model_specification: Ordered probit with lagged dependent variable
controls: Size of government revenues (% GDP), log population, income per capita, Polity IV democracy, external conflict, internal armed conflict, UK colony
operationalization_notes: Replicates Model 6 of Table 2, the main pooled specification used by the authors to support the claim.
reasoning: Ordered probit of CIRI Physical Integrity Index on Reliance on Taxes plus full controls and lagged DV (Model 6 in the paper) yields a positive coefficient on tax reliance (b=0.0056, SE=0.0019, z=2.98, p=0.003, N=1,739), supporting the claim that greater tax reliance is associated with better human rights protection.

dependent_variable: Pass rate: percent of pupils achieving 5+ GCSEs A*-C (pt_gcse_5_a_c)
main_predictor: GM vote win indicator (gm_win), an ITT proxy for GM conversion
sample_definition: Schools in main GM sample, observation-years 2-8 post base year with non-missing pass rate and covariates (N=4,954 obs from 726 schools)
model_specification: Pooled OLS regression discontinuity with linear vote-share function interacted with win (different slopes on each side of 50%), standard errors clustered by school
controls: Base-year pass rate, school type, year-term of vote, calendar-year dummies, centered vote share, and vote*win interaction
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's preferred pooled RD-ITT specification (Table 1 panel B, column 4): linear-interacted vote-share function, base+2 to base+8 observations, school-clustered SEs.
reasoning: Pooled RD-ITT model (base+2 through base+8) yields a GM vote-win coefficient of 3.578 percentage points (SE 1.139, clustered by school), t=3.14, p=0.0017, indicating that schools narrowly winning a GM vote had significantly higher pass rates than schools narrowly losing, consistent with the paper's claim of large achievement gains.

dependent_variable: Participated in lab experiment (0/1)
main_predictor: Amount sent in trust game (Player A, $0/$10/$20)
sample_definition: Students with a non-missing Sent_Class decision in the trust-game treatments (Flyer-Trust and Trust-Flyer)
model_specification: Probit with tutor-clustered robust standard errors
controls: Female, Commerce, International, Day-of-week dummies, Flyer-after dummy, Chosen-for-payment, Tutor fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Follows Model 1 / Table 3 column 4 in the paper: probit of lab participation on amount sent, with the listed demographic/treatment controls and tutor effects, clustered by tutor.
reasoning: Probit of lab participation on amount sent (with controls for female, commerce, international, day-of-week, flyer order, payment, and tutor fixed effects, tutor-clustered SEs) yields a negative coefficient on amount sent of -0.024, z = -2.54, p = 0.011 (N = 658). Students who sent less in the trust game were significantly more likely to participate, replicating the paper's column 4 result.

dependent_variable: took_act (illness episode treated with any ACT)
main_predictor: ACT Subsidy = 92% (act40 dummy), the 'very high' AMFm-target subsidy
sample_definition: First illness episodes (first_ep==1) for households not assigned to the RDT subsidy arm (rdt_any==0) and not selected for a surprise drug-shop RDT (ex_post==0); N=631
model_specification: Linear probability model: took_act on dummies for 92%, 88%, 80% ACT subsidies + 28 randomization-stratum fixed effects; SEs clustered by household
operationalization_notes: Mirrors the paper's Table 2, column 1 specification (Panel B, by subsidy level). 'Very high subsidy' is operationalized as the 92% subsidy arm, the headline AMFm-style subsidy. Reporting the t-statistic on that coefficient as the most direct test of the directional claim.
reasoning: OLS of 'took ACT' on dummies for each subsidy level with randomization-strata fixed effects and standard errors clustered at the household level: the 92% (highest) ACT subsidy raises the probability of treating an illness with an ACT by 21.4 percentage points (SE=0.053, t=4.03, p<0.001) over a control-group mean of ~19%. This corroborates the paper's claim that a very high subsidy substantially increases access to antimalarials.

dependent_variable: Two-year change in combined PIAT math + reading recognition z-score (mean of piamatsn and piarersn)
main_predictor: Two-year change in real pretax total family income (earned + unearned + nontaxable, deflated by CPI to 2000 dollars, in $1,000s)
sample_definition: Children of NLSY observations with valid changes in test score and income, survey year 1988-1999, biennial 2-year differences within child
model_specification: OLS first-difference regression (equivalent to child fixed effects); cluster-robust SE at the mother (family) level
controls: Year dummies, change in age, change in number of siblings, child gender, black, hispanic, positive-lagged-income indicator, and 5th-order polynomial in lagged pretax income (control function)
operationalization_notes: Paper's baseline causal claim is from an IV strategy using simulated EITC changes; that instrument was not in the released main.dta. I therefore committed to the closest defensible test using available data: the 2-year first-difference regression (Table 3, Panel B, col. 1 analog), the FE specification the paper itself reports. n=14,780 observations from 2,915 family clusters; t reported with clusters-1=2,914 df.
reasoning: In a 2-year first-difference (child fixed-effects) regression of combined math+reading PIAT z-scores on real pretax family income (in $1,000 of year-2000 dollars), with baseline controls, year dummies, and a 5th-order polynomial in lagged pretax income, the coefficient on current income is +0.00154 (cluster-robust SE 0.00098 at the family level), t=1.57, p=0.12. The direction matches the claim, but the effect is not statistically significant and is roughly 40x smaller than the IV estimate the paper highlights (0.061). The IV instrument (predicted EITC from TAXSIM) is not provided in the released data file, so the contemporaneous-effects IV could not be reproduced; the most demanding defensible test using the available variables yields an inconclusive directional result.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs, 4-item average)
main_predictor: Single-childless dummy (1 = single childless, 0 = other family structures)
sample_definition: Currently employed business school alumni respondents with complete data on absorption, family structure, gender, age, and job position (n = 355)
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of absorption on single-childless plus controls
controls: Gender (sex), age in years, job position level
operationalization_notes: Followed Study 1 methods section: OLS regression of absorption on single/childless dummy controlling for sex, age, and position (the exact equation reported in the paper).
reasoning: In an OLS regression of work absorption on single-childless status controlling for gender, age, and job position, being single and childless was significantly negatively associated with absorption (b = -0.296, SE = 0.132, t(350) = -2.24, p = .026), supporting H1.

dependent_variable: ProperName (greeted by proper name, 1/0)
main_predictor: Applicant race (Hispanic vs white alias)
sample_definition: Responding emails with non-missing ProperName whose treatment group is Hispanic or white (male+female combined)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 table
operationalization_notes: ProperName is only defined conditional on a response; restricted to Hispanic and white treatments to directly test the comparison in the claim, pooling across gender.
reasoning: Among email responses to Hispanic and white aliases, 41.2% (77/187) of Hispanic applicants were greeted by proper name vs 61.1% (107/175) of white applicants. Pearson chi-square = 14.42, df=1, p<0.001, supporting the claim that Hispanic applicants were less likely than white applicants to be greeted by name.

dependent_variable: Shading indicator (qualityc==1, i.e., low/perfunctory quality chosen by seller)
main_predictor: Contract type (rigid=1 vs flexible=2)
sample_definition: Baseline treatment (condition==1) observations where trade was realized (contractrealizedc==1)
model_specification: Pearson chi-squared test of independence (2x2 contingency table: contract type × shading)
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns baseline comparison of shading frequency by contract type; restricted to realized trades because shading is only defined conditional on trade. Used simple 2x2 chi-square as the most direct test.
reasoning: In the baseline treatment, among realized trades, shading (low quality) occurred in 6.3% of rigid contracts (25/398) vs 26.0% of flexible contracts (133/511). A chi-squared test of independence yields chi2(1)=60.75, p<1e-14, strongly supporting the claim that much less shading occurs under rigid than flexible contracts.

dependent_variable: log of total state CO2 emissions (carbon_unadj)
main_predictor: log of average weekly working hours (wrkhrs)
sample_definition: 50 U.S. states, years 2007-2013 (N=350)
model_specification: OLS two-way fixed effects (state + year dummies)
controls: log employed population %, log GDP per hour, log total population, manufacturing % of GDP, log energy production, log working-age population
operationalization_notes: Replicates Model 1 (Scale FE) from Table 3 as closely as available variables in compiled.dta allow; average household size and state environmentalism not present in the compiled file are omitted (environmentalism is time-invariant and absorbed by state FE anyway).
reasoning: Two-way (state and year) fixed-effects OLS regression of log total CO2 emissions on log working hours plus the available scale controls yields a positive and statistically significant coefficient on log working hours (b=0.49, SE=0.225, t=2.18, p=0.030, N=350), consistent with the paper's claim of a positive working-hours/emissions relationship.

dependent_variable: consider (dyad considered/conducted attack on nuclear program)
main_predictor: hostileMID (prior violent militarized conflict: use of force or war)
sample_definition: Politically-relevant dyad-years (polrel==1), 1941–2000, as in paper's Table 2
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 contingency table (no continuity correction)
controls: none (bivariate test, matching the paper's Table 2 specification for this claim)
operationalization_notes: The claim is most directly tested by the paper's own Table 2 bivariate association between hostileMID and the considered-attack outcome; I replicated the χ² on the same dyadic data restricted to politically-relevant dyads.
reasoning: In the politically-relevant dyad-year sample, considered attacks against nuclear programs are far more frequent in dyads with prior violent militarized conflict (28/569 = 4.9%) than without (13/5117 = 0.25%). Pearson χ²(1)=155.79, p<1e-30, supporting the claim that prior violent conflict increases salience of the proliferation threat.

dependent_variable: splinter (county-wave indicator = 1 if county broke away to form a new district)
main_predictor: DEC_rep — ratio of county's share of District Executive Committee seats to its share of district population (political marginalization)
sample_definition: All county-wave observations (1996-2000, 2001-2005, 2006-2010) with non-missing covariates (N=475).
model_specification: Logistic regression of splinter on DEC_rep, ethnic minority status, development summary index, number of counties in district, break-up lag, region dummies, and electoral-wave dummies (paper's Model 1).
controls: ethnic_min, MARG (development index), ncounties, break_lag, region dummies, wave dummies
operationalization_notes: The claim specifies political marginalization most directly; the DEC share ratio is the paper's main political-marginalization measure. Chose the baseline M1 specification from Table 3 with all county-wave observations rather than restricting to non-mother counties, providing a demanding test on the full estimation sample.
reasoning: In a logit model of splinter (new-district secession) on the political-marginalization proxy (DEC_rep, the ratio of a county's share of seats on the District Executive Committee to its population share), the coefficient is -0.72 (SE 0.193, z = -3.74, p < 0.001, N = 475). Lower DEC representation (greater political marginalization) significantly raises the probability of secession, consistent with H1.

dependent_variable: recog1dum (State B recognizes State A, dichotomous)
main_predictor: nukeduma (State A nuclear-weapons capability dummy)
sample_definition: Directed dyad-years with non-missing recognition and covariates (existing recognition intervals, not interpolated)
model_specification: Binary logit
controls: Nuclear Weapons B, Nuke A × Nuke B, Rivalry Status A, Rivalry Status B, Dyadic Rivalry, CINC A, CINC B, CINC A×B, Democracy A, Democracy B, Dem A×Dem B, Contiguity, ln(Distance), Alliance
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 2 dichotomous recognition logit (Gartzke 2009); peace-year splines omitted since not present in the data file, which inflates the magnitude of nuclear coefficients but does not change inference.
reasoning: Logit of dichotomous diplomatic recognition (State B recognizes State A) on Nuclear Weapons A, Nuclear Weapons B, their interaction, and the paper's listed controls yields a coefficient of 0.805 on Nuclear Weapons A with z = 27.31 (p < .001, N = 206,394). Nuclear-capable states are substantially more likely to be recognized, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Log of absolute opinion change on the pro-immigration index between waves 2 and 3 (change_w3w2_log)
main_predictor: Group-level deliberative quality: level of justification rationality (DQ_jlev)
sample_definition: EuroPolis participants in small-group discussions with complete data on all model variables (N=174 individuals in 13 groups)
model_specification: Linear multilevel model (REML) with individuals nested in small groups (statsmodels MixedLM)
controls: gender, age, education, catholic, protestant, working class, religiosity, left-right ideology and its square, knowledge change, clarify-thinking (other participants, experts, politicians, briefing material), social conformity pressure (above and below), intention to vote left/right party
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Model 2b in Table 2: DV is log absolute opinion change; key predictor is the group-level justification rationality from the DQI; same individual-level controls as Sanders replication; multilevel REML with random intercept by small_gr.
reasoning: In a multilevel REML model of log absolute immigration-opinion change (wave 3 vs wave 2) with 174 participants nested in 13 small groups, group-level justification rationality has a positive coefficient (b = 0.130, SE = 0.066, z = 1.96, p ≈ 0.049), reproducing the paper's Model 2b finding that higher group justification rationality is associated with more opinion change.

dependent_variable: Mean effort (work choice, 0/1) per matching group across all 18 periods
main_predictor: Reward scheme: symmetrical 4-4-4 (444COM) vs discriminating 3-4-5 (345COM), both under complementarity production
sample_definition: All subjects in the two complementarity treatments (345COM and 444COM); each matching group aggregated to one independent observation
model_specification: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U test on matching-group mean effort
operationalization_notes: Matching group is the unit of statistical independence in this experiment. Aggregating individual×period effort to the matching-group mean and comparing the two complementarity treatments provides the most demanding nonparametric test directly tied to the claim.
reasoning: Mann-Whitney comparison of matching-group mean effort under complementarity: 345COM (discriminating) mean=0.917 vs 444COM (symmetrical) mean=0.722. U=95, z≈1.79, p≈0.07 (two-sided) with n1=12, n2=11 independent matching groups. Direction matches the paper's claim that symmetrical rewards elicit lower effort under complementarity, though statistical significance is marginal at the matching-group level.

dependent_variable: Difference within senator-letter in proportion of anti-immigration vs pro-immigration policy-action mentions (companti − comppro), compared across the two letter types
main_predictor: Constituent letter type (anti-immigration vs pro-immigration stance), within-subjects
sample_definition: U.S. senators who responded to both the pro- and anti-immigration constituent letters (N=56)
model_specification: Paired (within-subjects) t-test on the (companti − comppro) index across the two letter conditions per senator
operationalization_notes: Claim 'senators tailor explanations to their audiences' most directly tested by the within-senator compensating-behavior comparison in Table 2; the strongest test is the Anti–Pro mention differential across letter types.
reasoning: Paired t-test on the 56 senators who responded to both pro- and anti-immigration constituent letters: the within-senator (Anti-immigration mentions − Pro-immigration mentions) index was 0.429 in anti-immigration-constituent letters vs 0.196 in pro-immigration-constituent letters, a 23.2 pp difference (t(55)=3.45, p=.001). Senators systematically tailored their compensating/reinforcing policy mentions to the letter writer's stance.

dependent_variable: Log wage gain at migration = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted)
main_predictor: Education category (no high school vs. college graduate; with intermediate dummies in the same model)
sample_definition: MP (Mexican and Latin American Migration Project) pooled sample of immigrants with valid pre- and post-migration adjusted wages and education years (N=2,854). NIS micro-data were not included in the replication archive, so the analysis uses only the available MP component of the paper's pooled NIS+MP sample.
model_specification: OLS regression: wage_gain ~ education category dummies (omitted = college graduate) + country fixed effects
operationalization_notes: The paper's Table III pools the NIS and MP samples with country fixed effects, with college graduates as the omitted education category. Because the NIS individual-level data are not present in this replication package, I executed the most direct version of the same regression on the MP pooled file (wage_gain_table.xlsx). I report the t-statistic on the 'no high school' dummy, which directly tests the claim that immigrants with no high school gain more than college-educated immigrants.
reasoning: In the MP (Mexican/Latin American Migration Projects) sample, the OLS coefficient on 'no high school' (relative to college graduates) with country fixed effects is 0.197 (SE 0.129, t=1.52, p=0.13, N=2,854). The point estimate is in the direction claimed by the authors (less-educated immigrants gain more), but it is far smaller than the 0.59-0.82 reported in the paper for the pooled NIS+MP sample and is not statistically significant at conventional levels.

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses connoting the learned (negative) meaning of cues (combined homograph and non-homograph; FAbaseC vs FAsuppC)
main_predictor: Cue status (baseline vs. suppressed) within subjects
sample_definition: Nonruminators only (Group==1) from Experiment 2 free-association task; n=27
model_specification: Mixed-design ANOVA on baseline vs. suppressed percentages with counterbalancing (CB, 3 levels) as between-subjects factor; F-test for the cue-status main effect computed as n*mean(diff)^2 / MSE(CB-residual), matching the paper's specification
controls: Counterbalancing rotation set (CB) as between-subjects factor to reduce error variance
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns SIF in nonruminators on the indirect transfer task. Exp. 2 free-association is the directly relevant test in the provided dataset (Ashley_labels.sav). Combined homograph/non-homograph means used because the paper reports cue type did not interact. Counterbalancing factor included as in the paper's planned interaction comparison.
reasoning: Among nonruminators (n=27), free-association responses connoted the learned negative meaning less often for previously suppressed cues (M=29.6%) than for baseline cues (M=45.7%). A mixed ANOVA with counterbalancing as a between-subjects factor yielded F(1,24)=10.94, p=.003, demonstrating significant suppression-induced forgetting on this indirect transfer task — consistent with the authors' claim that suppression practice can be beneficial for nonruminators.

dependent_variable: Shortened CES-D psychological well-being scale ('wellbeing', higher = better)
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction: Lives-with-children dummy × country-level % (strongly) disapproving of childlessness (grand-mean centered)
sample_definition: ESS3 (2006) respondents aged 40+ in 24 European countries with complete data on the analysis variables (missing flag = 0), N = 23,222
model_specification: Linear mixed-effects (random intercept by country) regressing well-being on parental status (lives-with-children, empty-nest, childless ref.), country % disapprove (centered), the two cross-level interactions, plus individual controls
controls: Age, age², marital status, own education, parental education, religious attendance, paid employment, born in country, individual social meetings, individual norm toward childlessness, gender
operationalization_notes: Country % disapproval was constructed by coding individual disapproval scores >=3 (i.e., disapprove/strongly disapprove on the 0-4 scale) as 1 and averaging within country (range ~7% GB to ~82% RU), closely matching the paper's reported range. Pooled men and women to provide the most demanding general test of the claim; coefficient on Lives-with-children × disapproval is the most direct test of whether the childless disadvantage shrinks under tolerant norms. Empty-nest × disapproval was not significant (z≈1.26), consistent with the paper.
reasoning: In a multilevel model with country random intercept, the cross-level interaction between 'Lives with children' (vs. childless) and the country-level percentage who (strongly) disapprove of childlessness is positive and highly significant (B=0.0019, SE=0.0004, z=5.11, p<.001, N=23,222). A positive interaction means that the well-being advantage of parents over the childless grows as country-level disapproval rises, i.e., the disadvantage of the childless is smaller in countries with more tolerant norms — matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: DSM-5 total psychopathology symptom score
main_predictor: Mini-K total (life history strategy; higher = slower)
sample_definition: All 138 participants with complete data on Age, Mini-K, and DSM-5
model_specification: Partial Pearson correlation controlling for age, t-test on partial r with df = n-3
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's main analysis: partial correlation between life history strategy (Mini-K) and total psychopathology controlling for age. Mini-K chosen as the primary LHS measure used throughout the paper.
reasoning: Partial correlation between Mini-K (life history strategy; higher = slower) and DSM-5 total psychopathology symptoms, controlling for age, was r = -.51, t(135) = -6.95, p < .001. Faster life strategy (lower Mini-K) is associated with more psychopathology symptoms, replicating the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (political knowledge test sum score)
main_predictor: Stereotype activation condition (condition 1: not activated vs condition 3: gender-difference statement)
sample_definition: Female participants (gender_alle==1) included in the analytic sample (Filter==1), in conditions 1 and 3
model_specification: Two-sample pooled-variance independent t-test
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's pairwise comparison framing; restricted to the analytic sample (Filter==1) which reproduces the cell sizes shown in Table 1 (73 and 70).
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test of PolWis_score among female participants comparing 'stereotype not activated' (M=8.90, SD=4.60, N=73) vs 'stereotype activated by gender difference statement' (M=7.03, SD=4.11, N=70) yields t(141)=2.57, p=0.011, Cohen's d≈0.43. Females in the control condition scored significantly higher than in the gender-difference-statement condition, matching the paper.

dependent_variable: GDP growth rate at t+2 (gdpidx, last year = 100)
main_predictor: Connected to provincial secretary (1 if city secretary OR mayor was promoted by the incumbent provincial secretary)
sample_definition: Prefecture-city × year panel, 2000-2011, all cities for which the connection variable, lead growth, and controls are non-missing (333 cities; 3,872 city-years)
model_specification: OLS with city fixed effects and province-by-year fixed effects; cluster-robust SEs at the city level (linearmodels PanelOLS)
controls: Net Transfer at t+1 (log), predecessor's final-year Log GDP, GDP growth, Log Population, Log Investment (for both city secretary and mayor), and leader controls: age, college education, gender, and tenure dummies (<1, 1-3, 3-5 yrs) for both city secretary and mayor
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's baseline Model 3 specification (Table 1). Net Transfer was operationalized as log of expenditure-minus-revenue at t+1 (matching pf_f1logtransfer in the replication file). 'Connected' coded from msec2currentsec OR mayor2currentsec.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects panel regression of GDP growth at t+2 on the binary 'connected to provincial secretary' indicator, with city FE, province-year FE, and the full set of city economic and city-leader controls, the connection coefficient is 0.366 (cluster-robust SE = 0.120), t ≈ 3.05, p ≈ 0.002. The direction, magnitude, and significance closely match the paper's reported 0.382 coefficient, supporting the claim that connected city leaders deliver faster economic growth.

dependent_variable: log(foreign-player share in Danish league) — top-quality share (stop/(stop+dom)) and lower-quality share (slow/(slow+dom))
main_predictor: Interaction: post-1991 indicator × top-quality indicator
sample_definition: Denmark only, 1980-2008, stacked top-quality and lower-quality foreigner shares (52 country-year-group observations with non-zero shares)
model_specification: OLS DiD: log(share) ~ post + top + post*top, robust (HC1) standard errors
controls: Group (top) main effect and post main effect; no other covariates
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the change in Denmark's ability composition of foreigners after the 1991 preferential tax scheme. The most direct test is a within-Denmark DiD between top vs lower-ability foreigner shares pre vs post 1991, avoiding any choice of synthetic-control weights (which would have introduced extra researcher degrees of freedom and yielded a less demanding test). The dependent variable mirrors the share variables (treattop, treatlow) used in the paper's Figure 3.
reasoning: Within Denmark, a DiD on the log share of foreigners (top-quality vs. lower-quality, pre- vs. post-1991 reform) yields a positive, significant interaction (post*top = 0.962, robust SE 0.350, t=2.75, p=0.006, N=52). The share of top-ability foreigners grew significantly more than that of lower-ability foreigners after the 1991 tax cut, consistent with the claim of an ability-composition shift toward higher-ability foreigners.

dependent_variable: Willingness to pay to protect the environment (willingness_to_pay scale)
main_predictor: Intrinsic relative to extrinsic values index (intrin_extrin)
sample_definition: Study 1 dataset; all participants with non-missing values on both variables (n=155)
model_specification: Pearson zero-order correlation; t-test of r
operationalization_notes: Paper's Table 1 reports the I/E composite vs WTP correlation in Study 1; replicated that bivariate analysis directly.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between the intrinsic-relative-to-extrinsic values index (intrin_extrin) and willingness to pay was r=.426, t(153)=5.83, p<.001, indicating higher I/E relative endorsement is associated with greater WTP to protect the environment, consistent with the authors' Study 1 claim (paper reported r=.42).

dependent_variable: imports_post (log of post-dispute annual imports from partner j into defendant i, product-level)
main_predictor: Complainant_{j,d} dummy (=1 if partner is the complainant in dispute d)
sample_definition: Product-country-year observations from disputes settled early (earlysettle==1), restricted to the 5 post-dispute years with complete trade data (i.e. non-missing imports_post and all regressors); N = 6,027
model_specification: OLS with dispute fixed effects and standard errors clustered by combined dispute identifier
controls: ln defendant GDP, ln partner GDP, democratic pair, pre-dispute disputed imports (t-1), ln total imports, dispute fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Models 1-3 specification (Table 1). Using DV = imports_post and dropping missing covariates reproduces the paper's reported N's exactly (Early Settlement = 6,027), confirming the operationalization.
reasoning: On the early-settlement subsample (privacy), the Complainant indicator predicts higher post-dispute imports into the defendant market with coefficient 0.430 (cluster-robust SE 0.180, z = 2.38, p = 0.017), replicating Model 2 of Table 1. Complainants therefore gain significantly more trade than the rest of the WTO membership when disputes are settled privately, consistent with the paper's central claim.

dependent_variable: Early-stage entrepreneurship rate that pays wages (entre_wage)
main_predictor: Median age of population aged 20-64 (medage_20_64)
sample_definition: All country-year observations in GEM_Country_Year.dta with non-missing entre_wage and median age (full sample, not OECD-only)
model_specification: OLS regression of entre_wage on median age, with country-clustered standard errors
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 2 column (3): bivariate OLS of entrepreneurship rate on median age in the full country sample. This is the most direct test of the verbal claim about median age affecting new business formation.
reasoning: Regressing the early-stage entrepreneurship rate (entre_wage) on country-year median age (20-64) yields a coefficient of -0.0078 with cluster-robust SE 0.00137 (t = -5.71, p < .001, N = 393). Higher median age is associated with lower new business formation, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Ratio of perceived to actual arm length (RatioRight, RatioLeft)
main_predictor: Arm side (right vs left, within-participants)
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (Handedness==2), n=15
model_specification: Paired-samples one-tailed t-test on RatioRight vs RatioLeft
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Experiment 1 analysis: arm length perception assessed as perceived/actual ratio and compared within right-handers via paired t-test.
reasoning: Paired t-test on perceived/actual arm length ratios among the 15 right-handed participants shows the right-arm ratio (M=0.970) is significantly greater than the left-arm ratio (M=0.920), t(14)=2.12, one-tailed p=.026, matching the paper's reported asymmetry.

dependent_variable: Appreciation index (mean of dv1-dv3)
main_predictor: Acknowledgment condition (verbal vs. financial $.05)
sample_definition: Study 1a hotel guests with exclude=0 (n=49); 2 participants without DV responses excluded as in paper
model_specification: One-way ANOVA
operationalization_notes: Followed Study 1a methods exactly: averaged the three appreciation items into an index and tested condition mean differences via one-way ANOVA.
reasoning: One-way ANOVA on the appreciation index (mean of dv1-dv3) by condition shows the verbal acknowledgment group (M=5.57, n=18) felt significantly more appreciated than the financial acknowledgment ($.05) group (M=4.38, n=31), F(1,47)=8.50, p=.005, replicating the trivialization effect.

dependent_variable: Standardized total exam score (midterm+final, s_tot)
main_predictor: Share female in neighbor 5 (avg5_girl)
sample_definition: Female students (girl==1) excluding favored students with non-random seat assignments (special1!=1); complete cases on controls
model_specification: OLS with standard errors clustered by classroom (gc)
controls: Own baseline score, proximity of favored students (avg4_special1), height, age, birth order, mother's and father's education, baseline interest in Chinese, English, and math; plus average baseline score of neighbor 5
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 5 Panel B column 1 (Neighbor 5 specification, female sample), which is the specification the paper uses to substantiate the claim about being surrounded by five females.
reasoning: OLS regression on the female subsample (excluding favored students) of standardized exam scores on share-female-in-neighbor-5 with the paper's controls and classroom-clustered SEs yields a coefficient of 0.253 (SE 0.078, t=3.25, p=0.001), confirming that surrounding a female by females raises her test score, consistent with the paper's reported 0.21 SD estimate.

dependent_variable: Absolute attitude change |T2 - T1| (averaged 3-item attitude index)
main_predictor: Objective ambivalence × global certainty interaction (mean-centered)
sample_definition: Study 1 participants with complete T1 attitude, T2 attitude, pos/neg, and certainty data (N=174)
model_specification: OLS: change ~ ambiv_c * cert_c + extremity_c
operationalization_notes: Objective ambivalence computed via Thompson-Zanna-Griffin formula ((P+N)/2 - |P-N|); certainty as mean of 7 cert items; predictors mean-centered before forming interaction, following the paper's Study 1 approach.
reasoning: OLS regression of absolute attitude change (|T2-T1|) on mean-centered objective ambivalence, certainty, their interaction, and centered extremity yielded a significant ambivalence × certainty interaction, B=0.037, t(169)=2.28, p=.024, matching the paper's reported interaction (B=.04, t(169)=2.28, p=.02).

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters; VAP for US)
main_predictor: log FDI Flows (foreign direct investment flows, log)
sample_definition: 23 OECD countries, election years 1970-2007 (Luxembourg dropped after listwise deletion of controls)
model_specification: OLS with lagged dependent variable, country fixed effects, country-specific linear and quadratic time trends, country-clustered robust SE (a less demanding analogue of the paper's one-step difference GMM, as discussed in the paper's robustness section)
controls: lifecycle VAP30-69, log registered electorate, PR system, mixed system, disproportionality, compulsory voting, years since last election, US midterm dummy, closeness/margin, ENPS
operationalization_notes: Used FDI Flows (Model 2 in Table 2) as the canonical mobile foreign-ownership measure central to the ownership-constraint hypothesis. Restricted to election-year observations identified by non-missing timesince; LDV built within country.
reasoning: In a fixed-effects OLS model with a lagged DV, country fixed effects, country-specific quadratic time trends, and the paper's baseline controls (clustered standard errors), the coefficient on log FDI Flows is -2.28 (SE=0.88, t=-2.61, p=0.009, n=208, 23 countries). This negative and statistically significant effect of foreign ownership on turnout reproduces the ownership-constraint result reported in the paper.

dependent_variable: Number of BBB complaints (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: first_A (firm name begins with A or number)
sample_definition: All Illinois plumbing firms in final_data.dta (n=2293)
model_specification: Poisson GLM with log link, single binary predictor
operationalization_notes: The claim is an unconditional mean comparison; given the highly skewed count outcome, a Poisson regression with no controls provides the most direct test of the multiplicative difference in mean complaints between A/number-named firms and others. The exp(coef)=5.39 maps directly to the paper's 'five times more' statement.
reasoning: Poisson regression of BBB complaints on A-or-number name indicator yields coefficient 1.685 (IRR≈5.39, z=24.99, p<.001), with A-name firms averaging 1.34 complaints vs 0.25 for others — confirming the paper's >5x claim.

dependent_variable: Cooperative bargaining strategy (dv; 4-category ordinal, 0=concession-extracting to 3=most cooperative)
main_predictor: issue_linkage_structure (size of zone of agreement / 'differently valued' issues)
sample_definition: All 588 state-by-negotiation observations in the DEU bargaining dataset
model_specification: Ordered logit (proportional-odds) regression
controls: lngdp, foreignpolicy (security/defense), euro, new_ms, agreement_importance, parl_scrut, qmv, publicity, presidency, lag_dv
operationalization_notes: Paper uses generalized ordered logit with partial proportional odds; I fit a standard ordered logit (the most demanding fair test that constrains the predictor's effect to be equal across thresholds) using the same controls reported in Model 1 of Table 1.
reasoning: In an ordered logit predicting the four-category cooperative bargaining strategy DV, the issue-linkage structure variable (the operationalization of 'differently valued issues') has a positive coefficient of 1.054 (SE=0.078, z=13.46, p<0.001) on N=588 observations. The direction and significance match the paper's claim that more differently valued issues lead to more concession-offering.

dependent_variable: Directed credit to government and SOEs (% GDP) - credittogovtstateenterp
main_predictor: State capacity index (ICRG quality of government, icrg_qog)
sample_definition: Country-year observations with non-missing directed credit (and its lag), IQG, private credit, and year; N=2787 country-years
model_specification: Pooled OLS dynamic panel: DC_it = a + b1*DC_{i,t-1} + b2*IQG_it + b3*PrivateCredit_it + b4*year + e, with country-clustered robust standard errors (closest direct test to Table 1 column 1's system GMM)
controls: Lagged dependent variable, private credit (% GDP), linear time trend
operationalization_notes: The paper's Table 1 col. 1 estimates this same specification by system GMM; I use cluster-robust OLS with a lagged DV as the most direct, transparent reduced-form test of the conditional partial association the claim invokes, since exact xtabond2 replication is not feasible in this environment.
reasoning: In a pooled dynamic regression of Directed Credit to Govt./SOEs on its first lag, the IQG state-capacity index, Private Credit, and a time trend (country-clustered SEs), the IQG coefficient is -0.14 (SE 0.40), z=-0.36, p=0.72. The sign is consistent with the paper's claim (weaker state capacity associated with more directed credit) but the relationship is statistically indistinguishable from zero - far weaker than the z≈-15 implied by the paper's system-GMM estimate.

dependent_variable: Dispute (binary: country initiated an MID in a given year as originator)
main_predictor: Predicted coup events (log) from reduced-form OLS on all exogenous variables (endogenous coup risk regressor)
sample_definition: All 798 Latin American country-years, 1960-1999, as in original analysis
model_specification: Two-stage probit (Maddala/cdsimeq): Stage-1 OLS for log coup events on all exogenous regressors; Stage-2 probit of Dispute on predicted coup events plus conflict-equation controls
controls: lagged dispute, ethnic fractionalization, relative power (CINC), number of borders, log number of allies, regional conflict, lagged polity, lagged log real GDP
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 3 of the paper. Reported z uses the nonrobust stage-2 probit SE (not Maddala-corrected); statistic still produces a significant positive effect consistent with the diversionary hypothesis.
reasoning: The two-stage probit (cdsimeq-style) yields a positive coefficient (2.39) on the endogenous coup-risk regressor with z=2.49, p=0.013, indicating that higher predicted coup risk is associated with greater probability of MID initiation, supporting Hypothesis 1.

dependent_variable: Amount sent to out-group (Albanian) recipient in dictator game (d12outgroup)
main_predictor: Region of residence (Primarily Albanian, Border, Primarily Serb) — proxy for exposure to out-group
sample_definition: All 158 ethnic Serb participants in the experiment
model_specification: OLS regression of d12outgroup on albregion and borderregion dummies (Primarily Serb region as omitted baseline); joint F-test of region effects
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns out-group bridging norms increasing with exposure. The most direct test is whether region (exposure proxy) significantly predicts out-group dictator giving. I chose OLS to provide a transparent joint test (F) of the two non-baseline region indicators; this parallels the paper's Table 2 col. 3 specification without controls.
reasoning: Regressing the dictator-game amount sent to the Albanian (out-group) recipient on indicators for Primarily-Albanian and Border region (Primarily-Serb baseline) yields F(2,155)=9.26, p=0.00016, N=158. The Albanian-region coefficient is 1.49 (p<.001) and the border-region coefficient is 0.52 (p=.14), indicating monotonically greater out-group altruism with greater exposure to Albanians—same direction the authors claim.

dependent_variable: Retrospective enjoyment of the sword-fight video (enjoyrelativ, 9-point scale)
main_predictor: Commercial condition (disrupted/'good' commercial present vs. continuous/'no' commercial)
sample_definition: All 102 Study 2 participants with non-missing enjoyment ratings (53 disrupted, 49 continuous)
model_specification: Independent-samples t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: Claim on p.164 refers to the Study 2 comparison of enjoyment between disrupted and continuous conditions; chose the direct two-group t-test on the primary enjoyment measure, matching the paper's reported analysis.
reasoning: Two-sample t-test comparing retrospective enjoyment between the disrupted (commercial present, 'good') condition (M=5.38) and the continuous (no commercial) condition (M=4.47) yielded t(100)=2.45, p=.016, confirming that the commercial disruption made the program more enjoyable.

dependent_variable: resigninvest (belief Swensen resigned because under investigation, 1-4 scale)
main_predictor: Causal-correction vs Denial-of-innuendo experimental condition (linear contrast)
sample_definition: Respondents assigned to Innuendo, Denial, or Causal conditions (control excluded); N=764 with non-missing outcome
model_specification: WLS regression of resigninvest on denial and causal dummies (innuendo is omitted/reference among innuendo-exposed) using IPW weights (aw); linear hypothesis test causal - denial = 0
controls: None beyond the treatment dummies (matches Table 3 model 5)
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns reducing acceptance of the misperception; the directly relevant outcome is resigninvest (Table 3, cols 5-6). IPW weights used as in the paper's main column. The within-model contrast of causal vs denial coefficients is the most demanding direct test of the comparative claim.
reasoning: In an IPW-weighted regression of belief that Swensen resigned because he was under investigation on denial and causal-correction dummies (control excluded), the causal-correction coefficient (-0.58) is significantly more negative than the denial coefficient (-0.25): difference = -0.335, t(761) = -5.07, p < .001. Thus the causal correction reduces the misperception more than the denial does, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Aggregated intimacy score (mean of 4 intimacy items: understanding, validation, caring, and reversed caring; 7-point scale)
main_predictor: Experimental condition: attention (signal turned blue 80% of trials) vs. no attention (0%)
sample_definition: Study 2a participants; following the paper, one suspicious participant in the no-attention condition (Intimacy=2.25) excluded, yielding N=29.
model_specification: Two-sample (Welch-equivalent equal-variance) independent t-test on aggregated intimacy by condition
operationalization_notes: The data file Sheet3 contained the pre-aggregated Intimacy variable used in Study 2a. To mirror the paper's documented exclusion of one participant who suspected deception, I dropped one no-attention case with intimacy=2.25, reproducing the n=15/14 split and the paper's means (4.58 vs 2.82).
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test on Study 2a data showed intimacy was substantially higher in the attention condition (M=4.58, SD=0.82, n=15) than in the no-attention condition (M=2.82, SD=0.79, n=14), t(27)=5.91, p<.001. This strongly supports the claim that receiving attention from a partner increases intimacy.

dependent_variable: Willingness to monitor the budget (q147_learnmore_apbd_REC2, binary: willing to learn more in future about how the district manages public funds)
main_predictor: taxgrp (1 = tax treatment, 0 = windfall treatment)
sample_definition: All 1,863 campaign participants with non-missing treatment and outcome
model_specification: OLS linear probability model with HC1 robust standard errors
controls: none (randomized treatment; matches Table 2 row 1 specification)
operationalization_notes: Table 2 panel A row 1 (Willing to monitor the budget) is the primary measure tied to the H1 monitoring claim; the corresponding survey item is q147 'willing to learn more in the future about how the district government manages public funds.'
reasoning: Regressing willingness to monitor the budget (q147_learnmore_apbd, binary) on tax-treatment assignment yields a coefficient of 0.051 (HC1 SE = 0.019, z = 2.70, p = 0.007), with windfall mean 0.76 vs tax mean 0.81. This replicates the paper's reported 5-percentage-point increase from the tax treatment.

dependent_variable: Voter turnout (1=voted, 0=did not) in 1859 Alexandria municipal election
main_predictor: Social proximity to elites (z-scored average network proximity to elite individuals)
sample_definition: All eligible Alexandria voters in the linked 1859 records (N=2216); Newport not included in primary reported test
model_specification: Logistic regression (Logit)
controls: Household wealth, ln(wealth), mid-status occupation, high-status occupation, homeownership, age, ln(age), church membership, US-born, network centrality (z)
