Thus downstreamness raises the intrafirm import share only in the high-buyer-elasticity (sequential complements) subsample, replicating the paper's central finding.

dependent_variable: bid_on_d (PAP applies to BMO on a given day)
main_predictor: nonaa_girl indicator (non-African-American girl child) relative to the omitted category (non-AA unknown-gender, unborn, <1 month to birth)
sample_definition: PAP-BMO-day triplets where the PAP satisfies the BMO's restrictions (bid_on_restrict_d non-missing), the BMO is still available (still_available_d=1), and the day lies within the PAP's activity window (first bid date to last bid date + 10 days); rows with missing covariates dropped.
model_specification: Probit regression with cluster-robust standard errors clustered on PAP-BMO pair (matching the paper's Table 5 'All' specification).
controls: already_born_d, month_to_birth, finalization cost (10k $), black_girl, black_boy, black_unknown, nonaa_boy, race_hispanic, single PAP, gay couple PAP, lesbian couple PAP, year fixed effects (2005-2008).
operationalization_notes: Operationalized as the Table 5 'All' probit specification described in the paper, using a 10-day post-activity window. Test reads the z-statistic on the nonaa_girl indicator from the cluster-robust covariance. My probit produces the raw coefficient (paper reports the marginal effect converted to probability units, 0.028); the z-stat on the coefficient (4.46) is essentially identical to the paper's reported t-statistic (4.23) given Stata vs statsmodels cluster-SE conventions.
reasoning: Probit on bid_on_d with PAP/BMO attributes and PAP-type/year fixed effects, cluster-robust SE by PAP-BMO pair (33,747 clusters), yields a positive and highly significant coefficient on the Non-African-American girl indicator (b=0.232, z=4.46), confirming AP preference in favor of non-AA girls. The black_boy and nonaa_boy coefficients are negative or insignificant, consistent with a girl premium specifically for non-AA children.

dependent_variable: a-insensitivity index a = 1 - 3*(mean composite MP - mean single MP), one value per subject per part
main_predictor: Part 1 * TP treatment dummy (with Part 2 * control and Part 2 * TP also included; Part 1 of control as reference)
sample_definition: Subjects with complete (non-missing) matching probabilities for all single and composite events in Parts 1 and 2; two observations per subject (Part 1 and Part 2). 100 subjects, 200 observations.
model_specification: OLS with three part×treatment dummies, cluster-robust SE at subject level (analog of paper's SUR/Model 1)
operationalization_notes: Test most directly tied to the claim is the coefficient on Part 1 × TP — the only part in which subjects actually faced time pressure. Used the 6 non-repeat single/composite questions (m1,m2,m3,m12,m23,m13) for each part to compute a per Definition 2.2.
reasoning: OLS regression of the a-insensitivity index on part×treatment dummies (clustered SE at subject level) shows that the Part 1 × TP-treatment coefficient is 0.182 (SE 0.089, z=2.05, p=0.041), indicating a-insensitivity is significantly higher under time pressure in Part 1, matching the paper's reported effect (0.19*).

dependent_variable: Civil war duration (months), Weibull AFT survival time with right-censoring for ongoing wars
main_predictor: Irregular war dummy (1=irregular, 0=conventional or symmetric nonconventional)
sample_definition: All 142 civil wars in TRdataset_JCR2014_replication_final.dta with non-missing duration and technology-of-rebellion coding
model_specification: Weibull accelerated-failure-time regression (lifelines WeibullAFTFitter); event=1 if yrend observed, 0 otherwise
controls: none (bivariate specification matching the paper's baseline M1)
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts irregular wars vs. 'all other types'. The most direct single-statistic test collapses conventional and SNC into the reference category and tests one coefficient via the Wald z. Censoring is applied to the 8 wars without an end year, which is the most demanding defensible specification.
reasoning: In a Weibull AFT survival model of civil-war duration on a single irregular-war dummy (irregular vs. all other types combined), using the 142 TR-dataset civil wars with 8 ongoing wars treated as right-censored, the coefficient on irregular is +1.128 (SE=0.207, z=5.45, p≈5e-8), meaning irregular wars last roughly exp(1.13)≈3.1 times longer than other technologies of rebellion. This directly reproduces the paper's claim that irregular conflicts last significantly longer than all other types.

dependent_variable: log monthly death rate per capita (lndrate)
main_predictor: days >=90F (b10_10) × post-1959 indicator
sample_definition: State-month observations 1930-2004, non-missing lndrate, b10_10, and totalpop
model_specification: Weighted (totalpop) panel OLS with state FE and year-month FE; SEs clustered at state level
controls: State and year-month fixed effects only (parsimonious baseline)
operationalization_notes: The claim of a decline across decades is operationalized as the interaction of the highest-temperature bin (>=90F) with a post-1959 dummy that splits the sample at the paper's pre/post breakpoint (Table 4). A demanding two-way FE specification with state-clustered SEs and population weights provides the most direct test of whether the slope changed.
reasoning: In a two-way FE panel regression (state + year-month FE, population-weighted, SEs clustered by state) of log monthly death rate on days >=90F (b10_10) interacted with a post-1959 indicator over 1930-2004, the interaction coefficient is -0.0184 (SE 0.0076, t=-2.41, p=0.016). Pre-1960 each hot day raises log mortality by ~0.018; post-1960 this effect is essentially eliminated, confirming a significant decline in the temperature-mortality relationship across decades.

dependent_variable: DVD purchase choice (buy = 1 vs. not buy = 0)
main_predictor: Opportunity-cost cue (cue vs. no cue) x connectedness to future self (ZFINAL, z-scored composite)
sample_definition: All 88 participants in the DVD scenario dataset (Study 1A) with complete data on cue, choice, and ZFINAL
model_specification: Binary logistic regression: buy ~ oppcost + ZFINAL + oppcost*ZFINAL
operationalization_notes: The provided dataset (N = 88) corresponds to Study 1A's DVD scenario. The claim of an interaction whereby opportunity-cost cues reduce spending more strongly among those higher in future-self connectedness is most directly tested via the cue x connectedness interaction term in a logistic regression on purchase choice.
reasoning: Logistic regression of DVD purchase intent on opportunity-cost cue (0/1), z-scored connectedness, and their interaction yielded a significant negative interaction (b = -1.05, Wald z = -2.10, p = .036, N = 88). The negative sign indicates that higher connectedness predicted lower purchase probability more strongly when opportunity costs were highlighted, consistent with the authors' claim.

dependent_variable: REF_female (referral is female, 0/1)
main_predictor: OP_female (CA gender)
sample_definition: Conventional applicants in either-gender referral treatments (treat_either==1) who made a referral (REF_female non-missing); n=220
model_specification: OLS regression of REF_female on OP_female (equivalent to two-sample t-test of proportions)
operationalization_notes: Matches panel C of Table 1 (either-gender treatments), which the paper cites as the basis for the claim that male CAs refer women less than female CAs do.
reasoning: Among CAs in the either-gender treatments who made referrals (n=220), male CAs referred women 22.6% of the time vs. female CAs at 42.5%, a 19.97 pp difference (t=3.21, p=0.002). This confirms the paper's claim that CA men are less likely to refer women than CA women.

dependent_variable: ali_stdscore_gr10 (standardized ALI mathematics test score, scaled mean 500/SD 100 in controls)
main_predictor: T3 treatment indicator (ALI: incentives to students, math teachers, peers, and other teachers/administrators) vs. control
sample_definition: 2008/9 10th-grade cohort, year 1 of program; students with non-missing ALI test score; all 4 randomization arms included in the regression (C, T1, T2, T3) with C as reference
model_specification: OLS with cluster-robust standard errors at the school (clavecct) level; treatment effect is the coefficient on the T3 indicator
controls: school-mean 9th-grade ENLACE math score for current 10th and 11th graders; school 2007/8 12th-grade ENLACE math and language; region dummies (1-3); state dummies (7, 12, 11, 21, 24)
operationalization_notes: Followed the specification described in the paper's Table 7 note (school-level baseline covariates, school-clustered SEs). Used the unadjusted-for-copying ALI score (the more demanding test, since the copying-adjusted score by construction inflates T3 estimates because copiers are reassigned predicted scores). Focused on the 10th-grade year-1 effect because that is the cleanest single-cohort, single-year contrast directly tied to the claim.
reasoning: Regressing the 10th-grade year-1 ALI standardized test score on T1, T2, T3 treatment dummies with the paper's school-level baseline controls (school-average 9th-grade ENLACE math for current 10th and 11th graders, 2007/8 school-average 12th-grade ENLACE math and language, region dummies, and state dummies), with standard errors clustered by school, yields a T3 (ALI) coefficient of 32.31 points (SE 6.18), a t-statistic of about 5.23 on 86 cluster degrees of freedom (p ≈ 1.2e-06). ALI raised test scores by roughly one-third of a standard deviation in the controls, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Log continuously compounded interest rate required to defer payment (interval-censored)
main_predictor: Ethnicity-salience treatment dummy (treatE)
sample_definition: Asian-American subjects in Experiment 1 (raceA==1); each subject's 4 intertemporal choices pooled
model_specification: Interval regression (intreg) of [lndiscratelo, lndiscratehi] on treatE, largestakes, longterm, largestakes*longterm, with Huber-White SE clustered by subject
controls: Larger stakes ($7) dummy, 1-week-vs-2-weeks dummy, and their interaction
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 2 column 1 of the paper: interval regression on pooled intertemporal choices for Asian subjects, with stakes/horizon controls and subject-clustered SEs; reports z-statistic on treatE coefficient.
reasoning: An interval regression of the log continuously compounded interest rate required to defer payment on the ethnicity-salience treatment dummy (plus stakes, horizon and their interaction) for the 71 Asian-American subjects (284 pooled intertemporal choices, SE clustered by subject) yields a treatment coefficient of -1.42 with cluster-robust SE 0.38, z = -3.74 (p ≈ 0.0002). Primed Asian-Americans demand a substantially lower interest rate to defer payment, i.e., they are more patient, replicating the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Mean cooperation rate per subject (fraction of time cooperating, averaged across all 23 supergames, in percent)
main_predictor: Treatment dummies (Short-Deterministic vs Short-Stochastic contrast)
sample_definition: All 192 subjects in the four main treatments (Long-Det, Long-Stoch, Short-Det, Short-Stoch); 177 effectively used after dropping observations with missing control values
model_specification: OLS regression with treatment dummies and individual-level controls; linear hypothesis test that coefficients on Short-Deterministic and Short-Stochastic are equal
controls: Age, gender, Italian nationality, risk attitude, trust, two IQ-type logic items, number of wrong answers and total answering time on control questions, dummies for studying economics/statistics/game theory, and categorical degree/field/job
operationalization_notes: Followed Table III's specification (subject-level averages, four main treatments, individual controls). The directional claim is a Wald test on the difference between the Short-Deterministic and Short-Stochastic coefficients.
reasoning: Replicating the paper's Table III subject-level OLS (cooperation rate averaged across supergames per subject, regressed on three treatment dummies with Long-Deterministic as the baseline plus individual controls), the contrast Short-Deterministic minus Short-Stochastic equals 12.7 percentage points with t=3.155 (df=148), p≈0.002. This confirms that in the short-duration treatments cooperation is significantly higher under deterministic than under stochastic horizon.

dependent_variable: Distance between plurality vote winner's ideological position and median voter (pldist1)
main_predictor: Election rule: SMD vs PR (smd)
sample_definition: All election-level observations in the dataset with non-missing pldist1 and smd (n=329).
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test (unequal variances)
operationalization_notes: H4a implies the plurality vote winner should be close to the median voter under SMD; the most direct test is whether pldist1 is smaller under SMD than under PR. Used one row per election as already structured.
reasoning: Welch's t-test comparing the plurality vote winner's distance from the median voter (pldist1) between SMD (n=85, mean=11.40) and PR (n=244, mean=11.07) elections yields t(181.0)=0.28, p=0.78. The plurality winner is not closer to the median voter under SMD than under PR, contrary to Hypothesis 4a.

dependent_variable: Civil war recurrence (nwar1, 1 = new civil war after the postconflict period)
main_predictor: Election timing (T2fpemths1: months between civil war end and first postconflict election)
sample_definition: Postconflict cases in BS09_DATA_main.dta with non-missing values on the DV, the timing variable, and all controls (N=118).
model_specification: Logistic regression with standard errors clustered by country (matches the paper's Table 1, model 1 specification).
controls: FPE level national (fpenatl1), FPE level concurrent (fpeconrnt1), Polity IV (fpepolity1), post-Cold War era (postCW), victory, UN intervention (unintrvnALL), UN electoral assistance (UNfpeaid1), previous civil wars (prv10yrs).
operationalization_notes: Chose the paper's stated baseline (Table 1, model 1): logistic regression of dichotomous civil war recurrence on calendar election timing with the listed controls and country-clustered SEs. nwar1 matches the paper's definition of the DV ('1 if a new civil war occurs in a country'); my N differs from the paper's 98 (mine = 118) because of differences in which observations are dropped on covariates, but the specification and clustering follow the paper directly.
reasoning: Logistic regression of new civil war (nwar1) on election timing (T2fpemths1) with the paper's Table 1 model-1 controls (FPE level national, FPE level concurrent, Polity IV, post-Cold War era, victory, UN intervention, UN electoral assistance, previous civil wars) and SEs clustered by country yields a coefficient on election timing of 0.0047 (z=0.888, p=0.374). The effect is not statistically significant and, if anything, points in the opposite direction (longer delay associated with slightly higher recurrence), so the data do not robustly support the claim that earlier postconflict elections increase the likelihood of renewed fighting.

dependent_variable: Femininity index (mean of three feminine trait ratings: feminine/gentle/sensitive, items 25, 26, 33)
main_predictor: Behavior condition (green vs. nongreen grocery bag)
sample_definition: All 194 participants from Study 2 (Notre Dame + Seattle University)
model_specification: 2x2 between-subjects ANOVA (behavior x target gender), Type II SS
controls: none (target gender included as second factor, not a covariate)
operationalization_notes: Items mapped to feminine vs masculine vs neutral vs manipulation-check by reverse-engineering means and α reliability against the values reported in the paper; items 25, 26, 33 uniquely reproduce the reported cell means (G=2.64, NG=1.82) and α=.80. Reported the main effect of green behavior on the femininity index from the 2x2 ANOVA, which is the test directly tied to the claim.
reasoning: In a 2 (target gender) x 2 (behavior: green vs. nongreen) between-subjects ANOVA on the femininity index (mean of items 25, 26, 33; α≈.80), the green target was rated significantly more feminine (M=2.64, SD=.90, N=94) than the nongreen target (M=1.82, SD=.86, N=100), F(1,190)=43.59, p<.001, η²p≈.19. This reproduces the paper's reported effect (F=44.00).

dependent_variable: Number of LV decisions in which the stochastically dominated lottery was chosen (out of 9 non-indifferent decisions; row 5 excluded because the two lotteries are identical)
main_predictor: Degree of risk aversion = average number of safe (option A) choices across the PV and RV multiple price lists (range 0-10)
sample_definition: All 106 experimental subjects (the 2 zTree dummy stations with age=99 were excluded per the README)
model_specification: Spearman rank correlation between LV error count and average safe-choice count
operationalization_notes: The paper's Figure 4 explicitly computes the Pearson and Spearman correlations between the LV error rate and the average number of PV+RV safe choices over all 106 subjects. I followed that operationalization. Risk3q=1 was decoded as choosing Option B (the RV lottery) in the LV menu, which produces a distribution whose mode is 0 errors (26 of 106 subjects), matching the paper's text. Spearman is reported as the primary test because hypothesis 2 is about monotonicity.
reasoning: Spearman correlation between subject-level LV error rate (count of choices of the stochastically dominated lottery in rows 1-4 and 6-10 of the LV menu; row 5 is indifferent) and degree of risk aversion (average number of safe choices in the PV and RV formats) is r_s = -0.472 (n=106, p<0.001; equivalent t(104)=-5.46). This is a strong, highly significant negative association: as risk aversion increases, LV decision error decreases, replicating the paper's central claim.

dependent_variable: Desired first-year compensation (midpoint of chosen range, in $1000s; endpoints coded 62.5 and 262.5)
main_predictor: Public treatment indicator (treatment=='B' vs 'A')
sample_definition: Single female respondents in main experiment with non-missing desired compensation (n=60)
model_specification: OLS of compensation on public dummy with HC1 robust standard errors
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's coding: midpoints of ranges with under/above endpoints coded as 62.5/262.5; multi-range responses coded as midpoint of full range. Sample limited to single women per the claim.
reasoning: Regressing midpoint-coded desired compensation on a public-treatment dummy among single female students yields a coefficient of -$18.1k (HC1 robust SE = 8.17), t = -2.22, p = 0.027, n = 60. Single women in the public condition reported significantly lower desired compensation than those in the private condition, matching the paper's finding.

dependent_variable: pay_for_conditionality (dummy: parent willing to pay to keep CCT conditionality)
main_predictor: Treatment group (1=baseline vs 2=text message)
sample_definition: Parents assigned to baseline or text-message treatment (treatment ∈ {1,2}); excludes don't-tell and nonclassroom-CCT treatments and observations missing the outcome
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on 2x2 contingency table (treatment x pay_for_conditionality)
operationalization_notes: The claim is about a difference in proportions of parents willing to pay for conditionality between baseline and text-message treatments. The most direct test is a chi-square (equivalent to two-proportion z) on the binary pay_for_conditionality variable across the two treatment arms.
reasoning: In the baseline treatment 49/60 (81.7%) parents were willing to pay to keep the conditionality, versus 10/51 (19.6%) in the text-message treatment. A Pearson chi-square test of independence yields χ²(1, N=111)=42.64, p≈6.6e-11, confirming a large and highly significant drop in willingness to pay when monitoring is provided.

dependent_variable: Monthly homicides of males aged 15-39 (SINAIS proxy for DTO-related violence)
main_predictor: after(1-6 months)*leader (lpub_after06): indicator for the first 1-6 months following a leader's capture/killing in the municipality
sample_definition: Treated leader subsample: municipality-month observations where treat_leader==1, Dec 2006 through Dec 2010 (14 municipalities, 686 muni-months)
model_specification: Negative binomial regression with municipality fixed effects (idunico dummies), time fixed effects (year*12+month dummies), log of male 15-39 population as covariate, and cluster-robust standard errors at the municipality level. Model also includes after(7-12) and after(>12) interactions for both leader and lieutenant captures as in paper equation (1).
controls: Municipality fixed effects, time fixed effects, log(pob_male_15_39), and the additional leader/lieutenant post-treatment dummies (7-12 months, >12 months)
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 2 column (1) (subsample treatment leader, DTO-related homicides proxy) — the analysis most directly tied to the claim of short-term exacerbating effects of leader captures on DTO-related violence. Negative binomial with municipality/time FE and clustered SEs matches the paper's stated specification. I had 14 munis vs the paper's 13 (the paper's conditional FE negbin likely drops one); committing to the unconditional FE negbin on the full treated-leader subsample is the more demanding defensible test.
reasoning: In a negative binomial model with municipality and time fixed effects, an offset/control for log population of males 15-39, and standard errors clustered at the municipality level (subsample of municipalities where a leader was captured, Dec 2006-Dec 2010), the coefficient on after(1-6 months)*leader is 0.083 (clustered SE = 0.164, z = 0.50, p = 0.62). This is a positive sign consistent with the direction of the claim but is statistically indistinguishable from zero, so the alleged short-term exacerbating effect does not reproduce in this most-direct test.

dependent_variable: Average shortest path length (ASPL) of bootstrapped partial semantic networks
main_predictor: Openness-to-experience group (high vs. low; median split on latent openness factor from NEO/BFAS facets)
sample_definition: All 516 participants retained after the authors' cleaning, split 258/258 by median latent openness. Network nodes restricted to 168 animal exemplars generated by >=2 participants in each group.
model_specification: TMFG-filtered binary semantic networks per group built from Pearson correlations of binary participant-by-exemplar matrices; 1000 partial-network bootstraps each retaining 50% of nodes (without-replacement node sampling, networks re-estimated each replicate); independent-samples t-test on ASPL across the 1000 high vs. 1000 low replicates.
controls: None (groups equated on number of nodes and edges by construction).
operationalization_notes: Chose the 50% node-drop bootstrap because it is the most demanding test reported in the paper (smallest reported effect). ASPL averaged over finite-distance pairs only. TMFG initialized with the four nodes of highest weighted degree, then greedy face-expansion as in Massara & Aste (2016).
reasoning: Reconstructing the openness groups (median split on the latent openness factor, n=258 per group), building TMFG-filtered semantic networks from the binary participant-by-exemplar co-occurrence correlation matrices (168 common nodes appearing >=2 times in both groups), and running the 50%-node-drop bootstrap (1000 reps) yielded ASPL_high = 3.624 vs ASPL_low = 3.652, t(1998) = -2.05, p = .041 (d ~ 0.09). The direction matches the paper's claim (high-openness network has shorter average shortest path length, i.e., is more interconnected), but the effect is far smaller than the t = -12.27, d = 0.55 reported.

dependent_variable: CIRI Physical Integrity Index (ciri_physint)
main_predictor: Reliance on Taxes (tax_rev_new)
sample_definition: Country-years with non-missing values for DV, predictor, and all controls; pooled panel
model_specification: Ordered probit with lagged dependent variable
controls: Size of government revenues, log population, income per capita, Polity IV democracy, external conflict, internal armed conflict, UK colony, lagged DV
operationalization_notes: Chose Model 6 in Table 2 as the central pooled specification with controls; sample size differs slightly from paper (1,739 vs. 1,718) due to listwise deletion implementation details.
reasoning: In an ordered probit of CIRI Physical Integrity Index on Reliance on Taxes with the full set of controls and lagged DV (replicating Model 6), the coefficient on tax reliance is 0.0056 with z=2.98 (p=0.003), N=1,739. This confirms the directional claim that greater reliance on taxes is associated with better human rights protection.

dependent_variable: School-level percentage of pupils achieving 5+ GCSEs at grades A-C (pt_gcse_5_a_c)
main_predictor: GM conversion status (gm_school), instrumented by winning the GM vote (vote>=50)
sample_definition: Main GM sample (742 schools voting on GM 1992-1997) with non-missing pass rates, base pass rates, vote share, school type, and year-term; observations from base+2 through base+8 years after vote pooled (N=4,954 school-year obs across 726 schools)
model_specification: Pooled 2SLS regression-discontinuity: pass-rate regressed on gm_school instrumented by win dummy, with linear vote-share margin allowed to differ on either side of the 50% threshold; base pass rate, school-type, year-term-of-vote and relative-year fixed effects included; standard errors clustered by school.
controls: Base (pre-vote) pass rate, school type FE, year-term-of-vote FE, relative-year FE, linear function of vote margin allowed to differ above vs below 50%.
operationalization_notes: Operationalized as the central, headline specification (Table 1, Panel B, 2SLS Lin×Win, pooled Base+2 to Base+8) since this is the paper's main treatment-effect estimate and the most demanding test combining RD identification with IV scaling.
reasoning: Pooled (Base+2 to Base+8) 2SLS regression-discontinuity estimate of the effect of GM conversion on the GCSE 5+A-C pass rate, instrumenting GM status with a vote-win dummy and including linear vote-share interacted with win, base pass rate, school type, year-term, and relative-year fixed effects (clustered SE by school): GM-conversion coefficient = 4.11 pp (SE 1.41), t = 2.92, p ≈ 0.0035. This corroborates the paper's claim of large, positive achievement gains from GM conversion (paper reports ~4.5 pp, t≈3.1).

dependent_variable: Participated in lab experiment (0/1)
main_predictor: Amount sent (as Player A) in classroom trust game
sample_definition: Students who played the trust game and provided a valid Sent decision (N=658)
model_specification: Probit regression with standard errors clustered at the tutor level
controls: Female, Commerce major, International, day-of-week dummies, flyer-after-experiment dummy, randomly chosen for payment dummy
operationalization_notes: Replicates Model 1, Column 4 of Table 3, which is the specification the paper uses to support the cited claim.
reasoning: Probit of lab participation on amount sent in trust game with tutor-clustered SEs, controlling for female, commerce, international, day-of-week, flyer-after-experiment, and chosen-for-payment, yields a coefficient on Amount Sent of -0.023 (z = -2.66, p = 0.008, N = 658). Consistent with the paper: those who sent less were more likely to participate in the lab experiment.

dependent_variable: Took ACT (indicator for whether the first illness episode was treated with an ACT)
main_predictor: Indicator for assignment to 92% ACT subsidy (act40), with 88% and 80% subsidy dummies also included; omitted = no-subsidy control
sample_definition: First illness episodes during the study period, excluding households selected for an RDT subsidy or a surprise drug-shop RDT (N=631)
model_specification: OLS linear probability model with strata fixed effects and household head's age (imputed flag included); standard errors clustered at the household level
controls: 28 randomization strata fixed effects; household head age (imputed) and missing-age indicator
operationalization_notes: Mirrors Table 2 Panel B specification described in Section 5.1; focusing on the 92% subsidy coefficient (the 'very high subsidy' from the AMFm) as the most direct test of the access claim.
reasoning: Regressing an indicator for whether the first illness episode was treated with an ACT on subsidy-level dummies (with strata FE, head-age controls, SE clustered at the household level) yields a 22.5 percentage-point increase in ACT access for the 92% subsidy arm (SE=0.053, z=4.26, p<0.001), more than doubling the 19% control take-up. The very-high subsidy substantially increases access.

dependent_variable: Two-year change in the average of the normalized PIAT math and reading scores (piamatsn, piarersn)
main_predictor: Two-year change in real (cpi-deflated) pretax family income in $1,000s (earned + unearned + non-taxable, imputed)
sample_definition: NLSY Children matched to mothers, observed in consecutive even-numbered survey years 1988-2000 (income years 1987-1999) with valid PIAT scores and family-income measures; pretax family income < $100,000; poor-white oversample excluded.
model_specification: OLS first-difference regression with survey-year dummies; standard errors clustered by child.
controls: Survey-year dummies only (child fixed effects absorbed by first-differencing).
operationalization_notes: Because the original instrument (simulated EITC change from TAXSIM) is not pre-computed in the provided data and TAXSIM is not available locally, I committed to the most direct non-IV analog the data support: a child-FE/first-difference regression of test-score change on pretax-income change. This is the OLS counterpart the paper itself reports as a benchmark, and it directly tests whether changes in family income correlate with changes in achievement.
reasoning: Using a first-difference (child fixed-effects) OLS regression of the two-year change in the combined normalized PIAT math+reading score on the two-year change in real pretax family income (in $1,000s of year-2000 dollars), with year dummies and clustering by child, the income-change coefficient is 0.0009 (z = 0.51, p = 0.61, N = 7,867). The point estimate is positive but two orders of magnitude smaller than the paper's IV estimate of ~0.07 and is not statistically distinguishable from zero, so the directional claim does not replicate in this specification.

dependent_variable: Work absorption (engwkabs, 4-item Rothbard scale averaged)
main_predictor: Single/childless dummy (1 = single & childless, 0 = all other family structures)
sample_definition: Business school alumni respondents with complete data on absorption, single/childless, age, gender, and job position (n = 355)
model_specification: Ordinary least squares regression of absorption on single/childless dummy with controls
operationalization_notes: Followed Study 1 specification described in the methods section (OLS with gender, age, job level controls). Used listwise deletion on the modeled variables; resulting n (355) is two larger than the paper's reported 353 but coefficients reproduce closely.
reasoning: OLS regression of work absorption on single/childless dummy controlling for gender, age, and job level yielded b = -0.296, SE = 0.132, t(350) = -2.24, p = .026, n = 355. Single, childless employees reported significantly lower absorption than others, matching the paper's reported effect (b = -.31).

dependent_variable: ProperName (greeted by proper name, 0/1)
main_predictor: Applicant race signaled by name (Hispanic vs. white)
sample_definition: Audit emails sent by applicants in the Hispanic and white treatment conditions that received a response (ProperName non-missing); black condition excluded as it is not part of the claim.
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence (2x2 contingency table), no continuity correction
operationalization_notes: Claim compares Hispanic vs white directly on whether the applicant was greeted by name. Restricted to responded emails since ProperName is undefined otherwise; pooled male and female within each racial condition for the most direct two-group comparison.
reasoning: Among emails that received a response, 41% (77/187) of Hispanic-named applicants were greeted by name versus 61% (107/175) of white-named applicants. A Pearson chi-square test of independence yields chi2(1)=14.42, p<.001, confirming Hispanic applicants were significantly less likely to be greeted by name than white applicants.

dependent_variable: Session-level frequency of normal quality (1 - shading) in the good state of nature, conditional on trade occurring
main_predictor: Contract type (rigid vs. flexible)
sample_definition: Baseline treatment (condition=1), good state of nature (low cost realizations 20/25), only observations in which trade occurred
model_specification: One-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired session-level means (5 sessions)
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's stated test (nonparametric signed rank on session averages of normal quality in good state) since rigid contracts only allow trade in the good state, this is the most direct comparison of shading between contract types.
reasoning: Using session-level frequencies of normal quality in the good state, rigid contracts yield much higher rates of normal quality (mean ~0.94) than flexible contracts (~0.75) in every one of the 5 baseline sessions. A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test gives W=15, p=0.031, consistent with the paper's claim that rigid contracts elicit much less shading.

dependent_variable: ln(state CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel combustion, carbon_adj)
main_predictor: ln(average weekly working hours)
sample_definition: All 50 US states, 2007-2013 (350 state-years)
model_specification: Two-way fixed-effects OLS with state and year dummies; all continuous variables logged
controls: ln(employment-to-population %), ln(GDP per hour worked), ln(total population), ln(manufacturing % of GDP), ln(energy production), ln(working-age population)
operationalization_notes: Follows Model 1 (Scale FE) of Table 3. Average household size (IPUMS-derived) and AR(1) correction not implemented because IPUMS-derived hhsize is not in the provided data; state environmentalism and region dummies are absorbed by state fixed effects.
reasoning: In a two-way fixed-effects (state + year) OLS regression of ln(CO2 emissions) on ln(working hours) and controls, the coefficient on ln(working hours) is positive (b=0.465, SE=0.239, t=1.95, df=287, p=0.052, N=350). The sign matches the paper's claim of a positive working-hours-emissions relationship, though the magnitude is smaller and significance is marginal compared to the paper's reported 0.668 (p<.001), likely because household size (IPUMS) and AR(1) correction are not applied here.

dependent_variable: consider (whether attacker considered attack on target's nuclear program in a given dyad-year)
main_predictor: hostileMID (prior violent militarized conflict: MID with use of force or war)
sample_definition: Politically relevant dyads (polrel==1), 1941-2000, with complete data on covariates
model_specification: Binary logit (GLM Binomial, logit link)
controls: target's polity, foreign policy similarity (s_un_reg), target's power (cap_2), power ratio, post-Article 56, post-cold war, program years, nuclear assistance, attacker's power (cap_1), contiguity, no-consider years and three cubic splines
operationalization_notes: Replicated Table 4 Model 2 of Fuhrmann & Kreps (2010), the most direct test of the violent-conflict hypothesis on the 'consider' DV.
reasoning: Logit of 'consider attack' on hostileMID with full controls (polity2, s_un_reg, cap_2, pwrratio, postArt56, postCW, prgmyrs, NCAnosafetodate, cap_1, contig, noconsideryrs, splines), in politically-relevant dyads, yields a positive significant coefficient on violent conflict (b=3.03, SE=0.885, z=3.42, p=0.001), supporting the authors' claim that prior violent militarized conflict increases the salience of the proliferation threat.

dependent_variable: splinter (county became part of new district in wave t, 0/1)
main_predictor: DEC share ratio (county share of seats on District Executive Committee divided by population share) — operationalization of political marginalization
sample_definition: County-wave observations across three electoral waves (1996-2000, 2001-05, 2006-10) with non-missing values on covariates (N=466)
model_specification: Pooled logistic regression (analogue of paper's Model 4)
controls: Ethnic marginalization (minority indicator), development summary index (MARG), number of counties in district, breakup lag, support for LC5 loser, chair election opposed, Museveni vote share and its square, log county population, ethnic fractionalization, region dummies, wave dummies
operationalization_notes: Implemented the main pooled logit specification closest to Table 3 Model 4. Used standard MLE SEs (clustered SEs were singular due to within-county invariance of some covariates). Higher DEC share ratio = less political marginalization, so negative coefficient supports the claim.
reasoning: In a logit regression of splinter status on DEC share ratio (political marginalization proxy) with ethnic-marginalization, development index, county/district controls, region and wave fixed effects, the DEC share ratio coefficient is -0.724 (SE 0.197), z = -3.68, p < 0.001. A higher share of seats (less political marginalization) significantly reduces the probability of secession, consistent with the claim that politically marginalized areas are more likely to secede.

dependent_variable: recog1dum (State B recognizes State A, dichotomous)
main_predictor: nukeduma (State A has nuclear weapons capability)
sample_definition: All directed dyad-years in the dataset with non-missing values on the covariates (N=206,394)

controls: Rivalry A/B/dyadic, CINC A/B/interaction, Democracy A/B/interaction, contiguity, ln(distance), alliance dummy
operationalization_notes: Replicates Table 2 dichotomous diplomatic-recognition specification; the z-statistic on Nuclear Weapons A directly tests the focal claim that nuclear-capable states gain more recognition from others.
reasoning: In a logit predicting diplomatic recognition of State A by State B, the coefficient on Nuclear Weapons A is positive (β=0.815) with z=27.68, p<0.001, indicating nuclear-capable states are substantially more likely to be diplomatically recognized — consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Log of absolute immigration opinion change between wave 2 and wave 3 (change_w3w2_log)
main_predictor: Group-level justification rationality (DQ_jlev), mean speech-level DQI justification score per discussion group
sample_definition: EuroPolis DP participants with complete data on outcome, predictor, group ID and Sanders' covariates (N=174 individuals in 13 groups)
model_specification: Multilevel linear regression (REML) with individuals nested in discussion groups; random intercept by small_gr
controls: gender, age, education, Catholic, Protestant, working class, religiosity, left-right ideology and its square, left-/right-party vote intention, knowledge change, four 'clarify thinking' items, and social conformity pressure above/below group mean
operationalization_notes: Replicated Model 2 of Table 2 (the absolute opinion change model) since that is the model on which the claim about justification driving opinion change rests; used SANDERS_Replication.dta and the variables explicitly used in the paper.
reasoning: Multilevel REML model of log absolute immigration opinion change (wave 3 - wave 2) with individuals nested in 13 groups, controlling for Sanders' covariates, yields a group-level effect of justification rationality (DQ_jlev) b=0.130, SE=0.066, z=1.96, p=0.049 (N=174). Higher group-level justification rationality is associated with greater absolute opinion change, replicating the paper's reported effect.

dependent_variable: Mean effort (work=1 if exerted effort) per matching group across rounds 1-5
main_predictor: Reward scheme: discriminating (345COM) vs symmetric (444COM) under complementarity
sample_definition: All decisions in treatments 345COM and 444COM (complementarity production function); aggregated to the matching-group level (12 mg in 345COM, 11 mg in 444COM due to a short-show-up session)
model_specification: Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney U) test with normal approximation and tie correction
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's own analysis strategy: matching group is the independent observation, two-sided rank-sum test as used in Table 3 for rounds-1-5 mean effort.
reasoning: Two-sided Mann-Whitney/rank-sum test on matching-group mean effort (rounds 1-5) comparing 345COM (n=12, mean=.917) with 444COM (n=11, mean=.722) yields U=95, z≈1.85, p≈.065. Effort is substantially lower under the symmetric scheme under complementarity, consistent with the paper's claim (the paper also reports p=.0649).

dependent_variable: Balance of compensating actions mentioned: count/indicator of anti-immigration minus pro-immigration actions referenced in the senator's reply letter (anti_balance for the anti-letter; pro_balance for the pro-letter)
main_predictor: Within-senator letter type (anti-immigration constituent letter vs. pro-immigration constituent letter)
sample_definition: Senators who responded to BOTH the pro- and anti-immigration constituent letters (N=56), enabling a within-subjects paired comparison
model_specification: Paired (within-senator) t-test comparing anti_balance to pro_balance
controls: none (within-subjects design controls for senator-level confounders)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns tailoring of explanations across audiences; the within-subjects design provides the most direct and demanding test. I used the composite anti-vs-pro action balance variable since tailoring should manifest as a shift in the relative emphasis on compensating actions across letter types, mirroring the 'Anti–Pro' contrast in Table 1.
reasoning: Within-senator paired t-test on the difference in (anti-immigration minus pro-immigration compensating actions) between the anti-immigration letter and the pro-immigration letter yields t(55) = -3.45, p ≈ 0.001. Senators emphasized more anti-immigration actions when writing to anti-immigration constituents and more pro-immigration actions when writing to pro-immigration constituents, confirming tailoring.

dependent_variable: log-wage gain at migration (postmigration minus premigration log hourly wage)
main_predictor: education category indicators (no high school, some HS, HS grad, some college; college grad omitted)
sample_definition: Pooled NIS + MMP/LAMP immigrants from countries with GDP per worker < 1/4 of U.S. (plus Mexicans), as in Table III
model_specification: OLS of log-wage gain on education dummies with country fixed effects; t-test on the 'no high school' coefficient (claim is that this coefficient is positive and large)
operationalization_notes: Could not compute: NIS micro data are not in the replication archive, and MMP/LAMP data are stored as MATLAB MCOS table objects that none of the available readers (scipy.io, mat73, pymatreader, h5py, Octave) can parse into a usable data frame.
reasoning: The claim requires running a regression of log-wage gain at migration on education indicators (with college as the omitted category) in the pooled NIS + MMP/LAMP immigrant sample (Table III). However, the replication package does not include the NIS micro data (the relevant `raw data/nis 2003_1` and `raw data/nis 2003_2` folders in `code and data.zip` are empty, presumably because NIS is restricted-use), and the MMP/LAMP micro data are stored only as MATLAB v7 tables (`dataLH.DataTable`/MCOS opaque objects) that cannot be read by scipy.io, pymatreader, h5py, or Octave's load. With neither the NIS data nor a readable MP table, the regression underlying the claim cannot be computed from the provided files.

dependent_variable: Percentage of free-association responses connoting the learned negative meaning (combined homograph and nonhomograph cues)
main_predictor: Cue status (baseline vs. suppressed), within-subject
sample_definition: Nonruminators from Experiment 2 (n=27)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test (baseline vs. suppressed) within nonruminator subgroup
operationalization_notes: The claim targets nonruminators' transfer-task benefit of suppression practice. The most direct test is the baseline-vs-suppressed within-subject contrast restricted to nonruminators, equivalent to the SIF interaction comparison the authors highlight. I combined homograph and nonhomograph cue types because the paper reports no interaction with cue type.
reasoning: Among nonruminators in Experiment 2, the percentage of free-association responses connoting the learned negative meaning was significantly lower for previously suppressed cues (M=29.6%) than for baseline cues (M=45.7%), paired t(26)=3.03, p=.0055. This indicates suppression-induced forgetting on the indirect transfer task for nonruminators, supporting the authors' claim that suppression practice was beneficial.

dependent_variable: Psychological well-being (shortened CES-D, recoded so higher = better)
main_predictor: Cross-level interaction between parental status (lives-with-children vs. childless reference) and country-level % (strongly) disapproving of voluntary childlessness (grand-mean centered)
sample_definition: ESS Round 3 respondents aged 41+ in 24 European countries with non-missing data on all individual variables (paper's analytic sample; pooled men and women)
model_specification: Two-level linear mixed model: individuals nested in countries; random country intercept and random slopes for 'lives with children' and 'empty nest'; ML estimation via statsmodels MixedLM
controls: Female, age, age^2, marital status dummies (sep/div, widowed, never married; married ref), own education dummies, religious attendance, parental education dummies (incl. missing), paid employment, born in country, and individual-level disapproval of childlessness; an 'empty nest × % disapproves' interaction was also included
operationalization_notes: Followed paper Model 2a/2b specification for the disapproval interaction but pooled men and women (adding a female indicator) for a single overall test of the claim, which spans both sexes. Country-level % disapprove was computed from the full ESS3 sample as the paper describes (including LV and RO datasets); grand-mean centered. Lives-with-children × disapproval is the interaction most directly tied to the claim (childless is the reference).
reasoning: In a multilevel model with random intercepts and random slopes for parental status by country, the cross-level interaction between 'lives with children' (vs. childless) and country-level percent (strongly) disapproving of childlessness is positive and highly significant (B=0.0019, SE=0.0004, z=4.55, p<.001). This indicates that the well-being advantage of parents over childless people is larger in less tolerant countries—equivalently, the childlessness disadvantage is smaller where norms are more tolerant—reproducing the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: DSM-5 total psychopathology score (DSM5_Total)
main_predictor: Mini-K total score (life history strategy; higher = slower)
sample_definition: All 138 participants with complete data on Mini-K, DSM5, age, and sex
model_specification: Partial Pearson correlation between Mini-K and DSM5 totals, residualized on Age and Sex (OLS)
operationalization_notes: Mini-K is the standard composite of life history strategy used in the paper; DSM5_Total is the most direct measure of overall psychopathology. The paper reports partial correlations controlling for age and sex; I matched that specification.
reasoning: Partial correlation between Mini-K (life history strategy; higher = slower) and DSM-5 total psychopathology, controlling for age and sex, is r = -0.51 (t(134) = -6.90, p < .001, N = 138). Faster life history strategy is associated with greater psychopathology symptoms, replicating the original claim.

dependent_variable: PolWis_score (sum of correct items on political knowledge test)
main_predictor: Stereotype activation condition (0=not activated vs 2=activated by gender difference statement)
sample_definition: Study 2, female participants passing the inclusion filter (honesty=1, citizen=1, gender<3), in conditions 1 and 3 only
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test (equal variances)
operationalization_notes: The claim contrasts female participants in condition 1 vs condition 3 on political knowledge; directly compared their PolWis_score via t-test.
reasoning: Female participants in the stereotype-not-activated condition scored higher on the political knowledge test (M=8.90, n=73) than females in the gender-difference-statement condition (M=7.03, n=70); independent-samples t-test t(141)=2.57, p=.011.

dependent_variable: City GDP growth at t+2 (gdpidx_{t+2} − 100, in percentage points)
main_predictor: Connected to provincial secretary: 1 if either city secretary or mayor has a patron-tie to the incumbent provincial secretary (msec2currentsec OR mayor2currentsec)
sample_definition: City-year observations 2000–2011 with non-missing growth, connection indicator, and controls (N=3,915 city-years, 333 cities)
model_specification: OLS two-way fixed effects: city FE + province-year FE; cluster-robust SEs at city level
controls: Predecessor-period log GDP, log population, log investment, GDP growth (for both msec and mayor); net fiscal transfer (dep); msec and mayor age, gender, college education, and tenure
operationalization_notes: Followed Equation (1) and Model 3 of Table 1. Connection is coded 1 if either the city party secretary or mayor was promoted under the incumbent provincial secretary. Used cluster-robust SE at city level; t-statistic on the Connected coefficient is the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: Replicating Model 3 of Table 1 (city + province-year FE with economic and leader controls, cluster-robust SEs at the city level), the coefficient on the 'Connected to provincial secretary' indicator is positive (0.257 pp of GDP growth) with t=1.85 (p≈0.06), supporting the directional claim that connected city leaders deliver faster growth, though the effect is smaller and only marginally significant in my replication versus the paper's 0.38 pp (p<.01).

dependent_variable: Composition of foreign players: top-quality (ever played for home national team) vs. lower-quality foreigner counts
main_predictor: Pre- vs. post-1991 Danish foreigner tax-scheme period
sample_definition: Foreign players in Denmark's first league, 1985-2008 (pre: 1985-1990; post: 1991-2008)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 contingency table (pre/post reform × top/lower-quality foreigners)
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether the tax cut changed the ability mix of foreigners in Denmark. The most direct test is whether the share of top-quality players among foreigners shifted significantly after 1991. A chi-square on counts of top vs. lower-quality foreigners pre- and post-reform tests this directly using the basesynthetic_control.dta data underlying the paper's Figure 3.
reasoning: Among foreign players in Denmark's top league, top-quality (national-team) players were 4/24 = 16.7% of foreigners pre-reform (1985-1990) vs 195/364 = 53.6% post-reform (1991-2008). A chi-square test of independence on the 2x2 (pre/post × top/lower-quality) table gives chi2(1)=10.84, p=0.001, indicating a significant shift in the ability composition of foreigners toward higher-ability players after the 1991 Danish preferential tax scheme — consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: willingness_to_pay (composite WTP score)
main_predictor: intrin_extrin (intrinsic relative to extrinsic values, I/E)
sample_definition: All Study 1 participants (Hong Kong university students) in the SPSS file with non-missing I/E and WTP scores (N=155; paper reported 169 but data file contains 155 usable cases)
model_specification: Bivariate Pearson correlation between I/E and WTP, with t-test on r
operationalization_notes: The claim is a directional bivariate association between I/E values and WTP. The paper tested this via SEM; the most direct, demanding test of the simple claim is a zero-order Pearson correlation using the pre-computed I/E composite and WTP composite in the dataset.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between the I/E (intrinsic relative to extrinsic) values score and willingness to pay among Study 1 university students is r = .43, t(153) = 5.83, p < .001. Higher intrinsic-relative-to-extrinsic values are significantly associated with higher willingness to pay to protect the environment, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Post-dispute logged imports (imports_post)
main_predictor: Complainant_{j,d} indicator
sample_definition: Disputes that ended in early (private) settlement (earlysettle==1), country-product-year observations with non-missing covariates
model_specification: OLS with dispute fixed effects and standard errors clustered by dispute
controls: Defendant GDP (ln_gdp_resp), Partner GDP (ln_gdp_part), Democratic Pair (dempair), lagged Disputed Imports (imports_tminus1), Total Imports (ln_total_imports), dispute fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Model 2 specification exactly: subset to early settlements; DV is post-dispute imports; clustered SE by dispute_combined.
reasoning: Replicating Model 2: regressing post-dispute logged imports on Complainant indicator plus controls and dispute fixed effects (SE clustered by dispute) on the early-settlement subsample yields a Complainant coefficient of 0.430 (SE=0.180, t=2.38, p=0.017, N=6,027). Complainants enjoy significantly larger post-dispute trade flows than non-participants under early settlement, matching the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Entrepreneurship rate, early stage, pays wages (entre_wage)
main_predictor: Median age of ages 20-64 (medage_20_64)
sample_definition: All GEM country-year observations with non-missing entre_wage and median age (full sample, 393 obs)
model_specification: OLS regression with country-clustered standard errors
operationalization_notes: Followed Table 2 column 3 of the paper which uses the GEM country-year panel and regresses the entrepreneurship rate directly on median age without other controls; used country-clustered SEs as is standard for panel data.
reasoning: Regressing the early-stage wage-paying entrepreneurship rate on country median age (ages 20-64) yields a coefficient of -0.0078 (cluster-robust SE 0.0014, t = -5.71, n = 393), confirming that countries with lower median age have significantly higher new business formation rates, consistent with the paper's Table 2 column 3.

dependent_variable: Ratio of perceived to actual arm length (RatioRight, RatioLeft)
main_predictor: Arm (right vs. left), within-subject
sample_definition: Right-handed participants only (Handedness==2), N=15
model_specification: Paired-samples one-tailed t-test on perceived/actual arm length ratios
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's Experiment 1 approach: within-subject paired t-test on perceived/actual arm-length ratio in the right-handed subsample.
reasoning: Paired t-test on right-handed participants comparing ratio of perceived/actual arm length for right vs. left arms yields t(14)=2.12, one-tailed p≈.026. Right arm ratio (M=0.970) was higher than left arm ratio (M=0.920), consistent with the claim that right-handers perceived their right arm as longer (less underestimated) than their left arm.

dependent_variable: Appreciation index (dv_index3, average of dv1-dv3, alpha=.96)
main_predictor: Acknowledgment condition (verbal vs. financial $.05)
sample_definition: Study 1a hotel guests, excluding 2 participants who left before answering DV (exclude==0); N=49
model_specification: One-way ANOVA
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's Study 1a analytical approach exactly: ANOVA comparing appreciation index across the two acknowledgment conditions on the analyzable sample.
reasoning: One-way ANOVA on the appreciation index (dv_index3) by condition (verbal vs. $.05 financial acknowledgment) in Study 1a yielded F(1,47)=8.50, p=.005, with verbal M=5.57 > financial M=4.38, replicating the trivialization effect.

dependent_variable: Standardized exam score (mean of midterm and final, s_tot)
main_predictor: Share female among neighbor-5 peers (avg5_girl)
sample_definition: Female students with random (non-favored) seat assignments; favored students excluded from outcomes but used to construct peer measures
model_specification: OLS with block (gcb) fixed effects; standard errors clustered by classroom (gc)
controls: baseline test score, height, age, birth order, mother's/father's education, baseline interest in Chinese/math/English, desk-mate favored indicator, share favored among neighbor-4
operationalization_notes: Follows equation (2) of the paper applied to the female subsample with the neighbor-5 share-female peer measure (Table 4, Panel B, col. 1 specification), which is the most direct test of being surrounded by five females vs five males.
reasoning: Regressing female students' exam scores on the share female among neighbor-5 peers (with the paper's controls and block FE, clustering SEs by classroom) yields a coefficient of 0.215 (SE 0.078, t=2.77, p=0.006, n=245). Moving from 0 to 100% female neighbors raises a girl's test score by ~0.22 SD, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Absolute attitude change |T2-T1| averaged across 3 organic-food attitude items
main_predictor: Centered objective ambivalence x centered overall attitude certainty interaction
sample_definition: Study 1 participants with complete T1 and T2 attitude data plus certainty/ambivalence/extremity (N=174)
model_specification: OLS: change ~ extremity_c + cert_c + ambiv_c + cert_c:ambiv_c
operationalization_notes: Followed paper's approach: objective ambivalence via Thompson-Griffin-Zanna formula (P+N)/2 - |P-N|; 7-item global certainty mean; DV is absolute change in mean 3-item attitude from T1 to T2.
reasoning: Replicating Study 1's hierarchical regression on absolute attitude change with mean-centered certainty, objective ambivalence, their interaction, and extremity covariate yields a significant certainty x ambivalence interaction, B=0.037, t(169)=2.28, p=.024. Consistent with the paper: certainty predicts more stability as ambivalence decreases.

dependent_variable: Electoral turnout (% of registered voters)
main_predictor: Portfolio Equity Stock (log, % of GDP) — the most flexible foreign-ownership measure
sample_definition: OECD country-election observations 1970-2007 with non-missing turnout and all controls (251 elections across 23 countries)
model_specification: OLS LSDV with country fixed effects and country-specific linear time trends, lagged dependent variable, country-clustered robust SEs (approximates Table 2 Model 4; paper notes OLS gives very similar results to difference-GMM)
controls: Lagged turnout, log registered voters, %VAP 30-69, years since last election, US midterm dummy, compulsory voting, mixed system, PR system, disproportionality, ENPS, margin/closeness
operationalization_notes: Picked Portfolio Equity Stock (Model 4) because the paper highlights it as the most flexible/strongest constraint channel. Used OLS LSDV with clustered SEs rather than difference GMM since the paper notes both approaches yield very similar results and OLS LSDV is the most transparent direct test.
reasoning: An LSDV regression of turnout on log Portfolio Equity Stock with country fixed effects, country-specific linear time trends, a lagged DV and the paper's full control set yields a coefficient of -1.47 (SE=0.37, clustered by country), t=-3.94, p<0.001 with N=251 (23 countries). Foreign ownership (portfolio equity) significantly reduces turnout, consistent with the ownership-constraint hypothesis.

dependent_variable: Number of BBB complaints (complaints_2008)
main_predictor: first_A indicator (firm name begins with A, a number, or symbol)
sample_definition: All Illinois plumbing firms in final_data.dta (N=2293)
model_specification: Welch's two-sample t-test comparing mean complaints between A/number firms and others
operationalization_notes: Claim is about a raw mean difference (~5x more complaints). Used Welch's t-test on the raw complaint count given the highly unequal group sizes and variances; this is the most direct test of the descriptive claim on p. 909.
reasoning: Firms with names beginning with A or a number average 1.34 complaints vs 0.25 for other firms (~5.4x), a difference highly significant via Welch's t-test (t=3.85, p<.001, n=2293).

dependent_variable: Ordinal cooperative bargaining strategy (0=concession-extracting, 1=refuse concessions, 2=moderate concessions, 3=large concessions)
main_predictor: Issue-linkage structure (average size of zone of agreement across issue pairs; higher = more differently valued issues)
sample_definition: All 588 state-by-negotiation observations in the replication dataset (EU member-state bargaining episodes), no exclusions
model_specification: Ordered logit (proportional-odds logit) via statsmodels OrderedModel
controls: ln(GDP), foreign/security policy issue, Euro state, new member state, agreement importance, parliamentary scrutiny, QMV, publicity, presidency, lagged DV
operationalization_notes: The paper estimates a generalized ordered logit (gologit2) in which issue_linkage_structure satisfied the parallel-lines assumption (identical coefficient across cutpoints in Table 1). I therefore used a standard ordered logit, which provides the most direct, single-coefficient test of the directional claim.
reasoning: Ordered logit of the 4-category cooperative bargaining strategy DV on issue-linkage structure (and the controls used in Model 1) yields a positive, highly significant coefficient on issue-linkage structure of 1.054 (SE 0.078, z=13.46, p<0.001, N=588). Greater 'differential valuation' of linked issues is associated with more concessionary strategies, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Credit to Government and SOEs (% of GDP) — credittogovtstateenterp
main_predictor: State capacity (ICRG Quality of Government index, icrg_qog)
sample_definition: All country-years in Country Year Dataset.dta with non-missing values of the dependent variable, lagged dependent variable, ICRG state capacity, private credit, and year; 130 countries, 1985–2011.
model_specification: Two-step system GMM (Blundell-Bond) with instruments collapsed (Roodman) and Windmeijer finite-sample-corrected SEs; estimated via pydynpd. Equation: dc_it = beta1*dc_{i,t-1} + beta2*iqg_it + beta3*privatecredit_it + beta4*year + e_it. GMM-style lags of dc used as instruments (lags 2:.).
controls: Lagged dependent variable (directed credit, t-1), Private Credit (% GDP), linear time trend (year).
operationalization_notes: This is the most demanding-but-fair test of the claim. The paper's Table 2 emphasizes the system-GMM coefficient on IQG controlling for private credit; the column-7 design (collapsed instruments + Windmeijer correction) is the most stringent inferential setup in that table, so I adopted it as the benchmark. The sign of the IQG coefficient is consistent with the paper but the magnitude and significance are not, indicating fragile inference.
reasoning: Replicating the paper's most direct test (two-step system-GMM with collapsed instruments and Windmeijer-corrected standard errors, regressing Credit to Government and SOEs on its first lag, the ICRG state-capacity index, Private Credit, and a time trend), the coefficient on state capacity is -0.249 with corrected SE 0.558 (z=-0.45, p=0.66, N=2457, 130 countries). The sign is negative as predicted but the relationship is statistically indistinguishable from zero, so the claim that weaker states robustly increase directed credit after controlling for private-credit profit potential is not supported in this reanalysis.

dependent_variable: Militarized interstate dispute initiation (binary, originators)

The 'Goeree_Econometrica_2011_1574_data.csv' file and the eleven 'all_apps_wide-*.csv' oTree session files contain byte-identical group choices, signals, and treatment assignments (same 11 sessions, same 16 rounds, same 352 group-rounds; group-level proportions of red choices are exactly equal: Majority=0.583, SuperMajority=0.200, Unanimity=0.000 in both files). dependent_variable: Group-level average market price (uniform-price auction)

operationalization_notes: The provided dataset contains only Uniform-treatment observations (no FIXED group data), so the claim that uniform > fixed in revenue was tested by comparing group-level uniform prices against the predetermined FIXED price (1.94) used in the original BF design. Since demand exceeds supply, price is a monotone proxy for seller revenue, matching the paper's framing. Wilcoxon signed-rank gives a similar p≈0.34.
reasoning: Among 32 valid uniform-price groups (excluding groups with dropouts/bankruptcies) the mean group-level market price is 1.957, virtually identical to the FIXED benchmark price of 1.94. A one-sample, one-sided t-test against 1.94 yields t(31)=0.17, p=0.43 — no evidence that uniform-price auctions raise more revenue than the fixed price.

dependent_variable: Binary voter preference (1 = Obama, 0 = another candidate) from h0clean

reasoning: Across women in the dataset who stated a binary voting preference (Obama vs. another candidate; h0clean), the point-biserial correlation between Wilcox conception risk (oddconcept) and Obama support was r = .106, t(475) = 2.32, p = .021, consistent with the paper's directional claim that higher conception risk predicts greater probability of intending to vote for Obama.

dependent_variable: Log-transformed, standardized composite of panic-buying-related Google Trends search volumes (mean of 'panic buying' and 'stockpile')
main_predictor: Log-transformed, standardized daily cumulative confirmed COVID-19 cases

reasoning: Regressing the log-standardized US panic-buying composite (mean of 'panic buying' and 'stockpile' Google Trends search volumes) on the log-standardized US COVID-19 prevalence rate yields B=0.74, SE=0.067, t(61)=10.96, p<.001. This positive, highly significant relationship matches the paper's finding that COVID-19 prevalence predicts panic-buying searches in the US.

dependent_variable: Procedural justice (mean of pj1-pj7)

dependent_variable: PSS-10 average stress score (pss10_avg)
main_predictor: Agreement with government containment measures (trust_countrymeasure, recoded into 3 groups)

operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's tripartite recoding: middle category (5='just right', expanded to 4-6 to match the paper's reported 66% agreement) = agreement; mild deviations (2-3,7-8) = no agreement; extremes (0-1,9-10) = no agreement at all.
reasoning: One-way ANOVA of PSS-10 stress scores across three agreement-with-containment-measures groups (agree=4-6, disagree=2-3/7-8, strong disagreement=0-1/9-10 on the 0-10 trust_countrymeasure item) yielded F(2,1076)=9.98, p<.001. Mean stress increased monotonically from agreement (M=2.33) to disagreement (M=2.41) to strong disagreement (M=2.60), supporting the claim that agreement with containment measures is associated with lower stress.

Although the sign is in the predicted direction (high HH shifts toward distrust under uncertainty), the effect did not reach significance, so the replication is inconclusive.

dependent_variable: AVERAGE desirability index (mean of S1_likely, S1_quality, S1_purchase, 1-7 scale)
main_predictor: Clarity condition × Rating distribution condition interaction (contrast-coded)

reasoning: In an OLS regression of average movie desirability on contrast-coded clarity condition (1=clear, -1=conflicted), rating distribution (1=bimodal, -1=unimodal), and their interaction, the interaction was significant, t(372)=-2.30, p=.022. Simple means show bimodal preferred over unimodal in the conflicted condition (M=4.98 vs 4.33), consistent with the claim that temporary low self-concept clarity increases preference for polarizing/bimodal products.

dependent_variable: Revenge, avoidance, and reconciliation (modeled jointly within the path SEM)
main_predictor: Malice and Greed manipulation dummies (with mediators Severity, Anger, Sympathy)
sample_definition: Participants who finished the survey and were assigned to one of the three experimental conditions (Malice, Greed, Control); listwise complete cases (N=1117).
model_specification: Path SEM (semopy): severity ~ Malice + Greed; anger ~ severity; sympathy ~ severity; revenge/avoidance/reconciliation ~ anger + sympathy.
controls: Control condition is the omitted reference; no additional covariates.
operationalization_notes: The claim is a mediated chain (motives -> attributions -> emotions -> behaviors). The most direct single test is the overall fit chi-square of the hypothesized fully-mediated path model that mirrors the original paper's M_H, with composite scale scores used as observed indicators.
reasoning: I fit the hypothesized fully-mediated path model (Malice/Greed -> Severity -> Anger/Sympathy -> Revenge/Avoidance/Reconciliation) on the replication data. The model's overall chi-square = 328.81 (df=20, p<.001). While the global fit is poorer than the original, every key structural path was significant in the predicted direction: both Malice (z=2.04, p=.04) and Greed (z=2.19, p=.03) increased severity; severity raised anger (z=20.2) and lowered sympathy (z=-7.2); anger positively predicted revenge (z=8.9) and avoidance (z=14.1) and negatively predicted reconciliation (z=-10.4), while sympathy independently lowered avoidance (z=-4.3) and raised reconciliation (z=11.3). Thus the substantive mediational chain in the claim reproduces.

dependent_variable: Mean correct recognition index for joy and anger words (average of JOY% and ANG%)

reasoning: In a between-subjects ANOVA on the mean correct-recognition index of joy and anger words with DEPTH, MUSIC and TASGRP as factors, the main effect of alexithymia group was highly significant, F(1,1088)=126.62, p<.001, with high alexithymia scorers recognizing fewer joy/anger words (M=.189) than low scorers (M=.463). dependent_variable: EVOLVED (1 = 'humans developed from earlier species of animals'; True vs. False/Don't know)
main_predictor: Latent class membership (post-secular vs. traditional)

operationalization_notes: Reproduced the paper's LCA on 2006/2008/2010 GSS with the manifest variables listed in Table 2; classes were labeled by the dominant pattern (modern = highest EVOLVED + Bible-as-myths; post-secular = high science knowledge but very low EVOLVED + religiously committed; traditional = lowest science knowledge with moderate religiosity). Class proportions (post-secular 25%, traditional 40%, modern 35%) and conditional means closely track Table 2.

A 2x2 chi-square gives chi2(1)=197.74, p<<.001, confirming the directional claim that post-seculars are significantly less likely than traditionals to say humans evolved.

dependent_variable: Trendiness rating of mug (V18, 1-7)

dependent_variable: Percentage of utilitarian responses (moral_accept==2) across the two conflict scenarios, per participant (0/50/100)

dependent_variable: Interpersonal obstacle–behavior association latency (mean RT across IntAssoc1–4)

model_specification: Hierarchical OLS regression: IntAssocM ~ Exp_c + Acc_c + Dummy1 (reverse) + Dummy2 (irrelevant) + Exp_c:Dummy1 + Exp_c:Dummy2; t-test on Exp_c reports the simple slope of expectations in the MC reference group.

The most direct test of 'MC + low expectations → weak associations' is the simple slope of expectations within the MC condition predicting obstacle–behavior association RTs (negative slope = expectancy-dependent strengthening, weak at low expectations).
reasoning: Within the mental contrasting condition, the slope of expectations of success predicting interpersonal obstacle–behavior association RTs (controlling for behavior accessibility and condition dummies) was b=-13.31, t(300)=-0.86, p=.39. The direction is consistent with the claim (lower expectations → slower RTs / weaker associations) but the effect is far from significant, and the full Expectations×Condition interaction term was also non-significant, F(2,300)=1.17, p=.31. This direct replication did not reproduce the original finding.

dependent_variable: Difference between dictator's offered share s and libertarian share xl (recipient contribution proportion, variable x in dataset)

The null that allocations equal the libertarian share is rejected, so the libertarian principle does not account for observed dictator behavior — same conclusion as the paper.

dependent_variable: Proportion of deontological (rejecting-harm) responses (RH_PMD, RH_NMD, RH_CMD)

The direction is opposite to the paper's claim — in this dataset men report higher worry about COVID-19 than women.

reasoning: Higher Trump vote share is significantly associated with a smaller reduction (less negative percent change) in trips during Mar 19-28, 2020 vs matched 2019 days (β=+2.14 pp per IQR, t(3041)=3.21, p=0.001), indicating less social distancing in more Republican counties, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Composite third-grade academic achievement (z-average of X7RSCALK5 reading and X7MSCALK5 math IRT scale scores)
main_predictor: Composite social-emotional problems (z-average of X7TCHEXT teacher-rated externalizing and X7TCHINT internalizing)
sample_definition: ECLS-K:2011 children with X12LANGST=1 (primary home language non-English) as ELL proxy and non-missing third-grade achievement and behavior scores
model_specification: Pearson correlation between the SE-problems composite and achievement composite

dependent_variable: Mean of SocGood ratings across the four scenarios (Artis, Green, Food, Medtech), 1=great harm to 5=great good
main_predictor: Firm motive condition: For-Profit vs. Non-Profit

dependent_variable: Self-reported sharing intention per headline, rescaled 0-1 from a 6-point Likert (extremely unlikely=0 to extremely likely=1)

operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the simple effect of veracity within the treatment condition. Following the methods section, I used a rating-level linear regression with veracity coded ±0.5, sharing rescaled to 0-1, and robust SEs clustered on participant and headline.
reasoning: Within the treatment condition (n=440 participants, 13,200 ratings), a linear regression of sharing intentions (rescaled 0-1) on headline veracity (true=0.5, false=-0.5) with cluster-robust SEs (clustered on participant and headline) yielded a small negative coefficient (β=-0.006), F(1,13198)=2.10, p=.147 — sharing intentions for true headlines were not significantly higher than for false headlines, and were if anything numerically lower (mean true=3.49 vs mean false=3.52 on the 6-point scale).

controls: Polity2 score for the survey year
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's baseline specification (Table 2, column 1): outcome = sustained growth dummy; key regressor = log impartiality index built from Afrobarometer Q on unfair group treatment using within-country sampling weights; control = Polity2. dependent_variable: Toaster evaluation score (mean of 5 items, separately for 4.5-star aggregated-positive and 2.5-star individualized-positive toasters)
main_predictor: Within-subject information type (aggregated-positive vs. individualized-positive toaster) in the abstract-sound condition
