dependent_variable: Mean self-reported likelihood of sharing the headline (1=Extremely unlikely to 6=Extremely likely), averaged across the 15 false vs 15 true COVID-19 headlines per participant
main_predictor: Headline veracity (true vs false) within participant
sample_definition: Study 2 participants assigned to the treatment (accuracy-nudge) condition with non-missing sharing-likelihood ratings
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing each participant's mean sharing intention for true vs false headlines
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the within-treatment-condition difference between true and false headlines in Pennycook et al.'s Study 2 (accuracy-prime experiment). I therefore restricted to Condition==2 (treatment) in the Study 2 data file, recoded the 6-point Likert sharing responses to 1-6, averaged across the 15 fake and 15 real items per participant, and ran a paired t-test.
reasoning: Within Study 2's treatment (accuracy-prime) condition, mean self-reported sharing likelihood was essentially identical for true (M=3.49) and false (M=3.52) headlines on the 1-6 scale, paired t(439) = -1.12, p = .27. This does not reproduce the paper's claim that true-headline sharing intentions were significantly higher than false-headline sharing intentions in the treatment condition.

dependent_variable: Sustained growth (1 if GDP per capita growth ≥2% in each of the 5 years starting at survey year, else 0)
main_predictor: Country-round weighted mean perceived impartiality (reverse-coded 'ethnic/identity group treated unfairly by government', rescaled to 0-1)
sample_definition: Country-round observations from Afrobarometer Rounds 1-6 (1999-2016) with valid impartiality responses and 5 subsequent years of World Bank GDP per capita growth available
model_specification: Logit regression: P(sustained=1) = Λ(β0 + β1·impartiality)
operationalization_notes: Used the paper's stated definition of sustained growth (≥2% for ≥5 consecutive years) operationalized as the 5-year window starting in the survey year. sample_definition: All participants assigned to the for-profit (condition=3) or non-profit (condition=2) condition with non-missing SocGood ratings; unspecified condition excluded so that the contrast directly tests the presence of a profit motive.
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided Welch/Student t-test on the participant-level mean SocGood score
operationalization_notes: The claim is about the effect of a profit motive on perceived societal good. The most direct test contrasts the for-profit vs. non-profit framing on the SocGood item averaged across the four organization vignettes.
reasoning: For-profit framing (M=3.75) was rated as accomplishing significantly less societal good than non-profit framing (M=4.09), averaged across the four firms; independent-samples t(241) = -4.82, p < .001. This supports the claim that profit motive reduces the perceived societal good of a firm.

dependent_variable: Mean self-reported sharing intention (1=Extremely unlikely … 6=Extremely likely), averaged across 15 headlines per veracity
main_predictor: Headline veracity (true vs. false), within-subject
sample_definition: Participants in Condition==2 (treatment/accuracy nudge) of Pennycook et al. (2020) Study 2 test data who provided sharing-intention ratings
model_specification: Within-subject paired-samples t-test comparing each participant's average sharing intention for real vs. fake headlines
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the treatment group only and contrasts true vs false sharing intentions, which is naturally tested by a within-subject paired t-test on per-participant means of the 15 real and 15 fake headline sharing items.
reasoning: Among participants in the treatment (accuracy-nudge) condition with complete ratings (n=440), mean sharing intentions for true headlines (M=3.49) were not significantly different from those for false headlines (M=3.52); paired t(439)=-1.12, p=.27. The numeric direction is in fact slightly opposite to the claim, so the directional claim does not reproduce.

dependent_variable: Sustained growth dummy: GDP per capita growth >=2% in each of the next 5 years after the Afrobarometer survey year
main_predictor: Country-year mean perceived government impartiality, computed from Afrobarometer 'ethnic/identity group treated unfairly by government' item (recoded so 1 = never unfairly treated, 0 = always unfairly treated), weighted by within-country weights
sample_definition: All country-survey-year observations from Afrobarometer Rounds 1-6 with valid impartiality responses and 5 complete years of post-survey World Bank GDP per capita growth data (108 country-rounds across ~20 sub-Saharan African countries)
model_specification: Logistic regression: P(sustained=1) = logit^-1(b0 + b1*impartiality)
operationalization_notes: Abstract specifies sustained growth as >=2% per capita growth for at least 5 consecutive years; I operationalize this as the 5 years immediately following each survey wave. Impartiality at the country level is the weighted mean of the recoded 'group treated unfairly' Afrobarometer item, harmonized across rounds (R1 pfrfai 1-5; R2-R6 0-3 unfairness scale).
reasoning: In a logistic regression of a sustained-growth indicator (GDP per capita growth >=2% in each of the five years following the survey) on country-year average perceived impartiality (re-scaled so higher = less unfair treatment), the coefficient on impartiality is -1.57 (z = -0.89, p = 0.37, N = 108). The relationship is not statistically significant and runs slightly opposite to the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: choice_toaster (1 = 4.5-star/positive aggregated, 2 = 2.5-star/positive individualized)
main_predictor: sound condition (most abstract: group 5 = C=>F# Rev measure 1)
sample_definition: Participants assigned to the abstract sound condition only (n=20)
model_specification: Chi-square goodness-of-fit against equal (50/50) choice distribution
operationalization_notes: The paper crosses reverberation, novel harmonic modulation, and metrical segmentation; group 5 combines all three abstractness cues and is the canonical 'abstract sound' condition. The claim is specifically about this condition's choice frequency between aggregated- vs. individualized-positive toasters, so a one-sample binomial/chi-square test against chance is the most direct test.
reasoning: In the most abstract sound condition (group 5: reverberation + novel harmonic modulation F# + minimal metrical segmentation/measure 1), 16 of 20 participants chose the 4.5-star (positive aggregated) toaster over the 2.5-star (positive individualized) toaster. A chi-square goodness-of-fit test against a 50/50 null yielded χ²(1)=7.20, p=.0073, indicating a strong preference for the aggregated-positive option.

dependent_variable: GDP per capita (GDPcapita)
main_predictor: Total imports from the South (totalimport)
sample_definition: 18 OECD (North) countries, years 1970-2003, complete cases
model_specification: Two-way fixed-effects OLS: GDPcapita ~ totalimport + C(Country) + C(Year)
operationalization_notes: Affluence operationalized as GDP per capita; predictor is the country-year level of imports from the South, per the paper's panel design (18 OECD, 1970-2003) and two-way FE specification described in the abstract.
reasoning: In a two-way (country + year) fixed-effects OLS regression of GDP per capita on total imports from the South across 18 OECD countries, 1970-2003, the coefficient on totalimport is positive (b=1.61e-8) with t(416)=5.17, p<0.001, supporting a positive effect of Northern imports from the South on national affluence.

dependent_variable: Mean bipolar Util–Symbolic rating (1=only benefits, 7=only symbolizes) averaged across the four symbolic product categories: T-shirt, American flag, class ring, greeting cards
main_predictor: Branding condition (No-Brand: Cond 1&2 vs. Branded: Cond 3 (Brand Set A) & Cond 4 (Brand Set B))
sample_definition: All participants across the 10 dataset files with a valid Cond value and non-missing symbolic-item bipolar ratings (n=310 No-Brand, n=300 Brand)
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test on the participant-level mean of the four symbolic-category bipolar items
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether branding makes symbolic-category attitudes less symbolic/more utilitarian. The Bipol item directly contrasts these two function endpoints, so I averaged the four a-priori symbolic items per the codebook and compared branded vs. unbranded conditions. Util.1/Util.2 (and analogous) columns were coalesced because Qualtrics stored each condition's responses in separate column blocks.
reasoning: For symbolic product categories (T-shirts, flags, class rings, greeting cards), participants in the No-Brand condition rated them as more symbolic on the bipolar benefit-vs-symbolize scale (M=5.46) than participants in the Brand conditions (M=5.22), Welch t(601.08)=3.41, p<.001. Branding shifted symbolic-category attitudes toward the utilitarian end, matching the claim.

dependent_variable: Semester GPA
main_predictor: Academic self-regulation (academic self-discipline composite, corresponding to SR)
sample_definition: All 366 college students in Jung et al. (2017) aggregate correlation matrix used for the Zimmerman replication
model_specification: OLS regression on standardized variables computed from the correlation matrix, GPA = β1*SR + β2*SD
operationalization_notes: Only summary statistics are available; the SEM claim with a latent SR predictor reduces to a regression of GPA on the SR composite controlling for the SD composite using the published correlation matrix and N=366.
reasoning: Regressing semester GPA on academic self-regulation while controlling for the self-discipline facet (using the Jung et al. correlation matrix, N=366) yields a standardized partial coefficient of 0.336 for self-regulation, t(363)=4.85, p<.001, while the SD facet is non-significant (β=-.052, p=.46). This mirrors the original SEM finding that SR predicts GPA significantly whereas SD does not.

dependent_variable: Mean of 4 COVID-19 conspiracy-theory belief items (0–10 scale)
main_predictor: Collective (national) narcissism — mean of 3 items
sample_definition: All 1575 respondents in the German replication dataset with complete predictor/outcome data
model_specification: OLS multiple regression: CT ~ collective_narcissism + national_identity
controls: National identification (in-group identification) included to isolate the narcissism component, following the paper's analytic strategy
operationalization_notes: The provided dataset does not contain a direct conspiracy-sharing item; belief in COVID-19 conspiracies (the available outcome) is used as the closest proxy, with national identification controlled per standard collective-narcissism analyses.
reasoning: Collective (national) narcissism strongly and positively predicts the COVID-19 conspiracy-theory composite when controlling for national identification: b=0.591, t(1572)=24.68, p<.001. Although the available dataset measures belief in (not direct sharing of) conspiracy theories, this is the closest available proxy and supports the paper's claim that national narcissism drives engagement with COVID-19 conspiracy content.

dependent_variable: Per-trial choice of the high-fWHR face (cannot be constructed without the trial key)
main_predictor: fWHR manipulation (high vs. low)
sample_definition: Participants with Quality=='Yes' in Processed_Data.csv (n=139); Study 1 sample
model_specification: Intended one-sample/binomial test of proportion of trials in which the high-fWHR face was chosen vs. chance (0.5); not executable without the trial-to-condition key
operationalization_notes: The codebook references a 'Questionnaire Development' file specifying which image in each pair was the high-fWHR (or masculinised) face; this file is not included in /workspace/data, making it impossible to recode Left/Right responses into a fWHR-target choice variable. I therefore report a null statistic rather than fabricate an arbitrary key.
reasoning: The dataset records, for each of 36 forced-choice trials, only whether the participant selected the Left or Right image. The codebook explicitly states that the mapping of each trial to the manipulation type (fWHR vs. masculinity) and to which side (left/right) held the high-fWHR/manipulated face is documented in a separate 'Questionnaire Development' file that is not provided in the data directory. Per-item Right-choice proportions range widely (0.38–0.83), consistent with the side of the manipulated face being counterbalanced across items, so the raw Left/Right responses cannot be aggregated into a 'chose-the-high-fWHR-face' score without that key. With only 139 quality-approved participants' Left/Right responses and no item-level key linking responses to fWHR manipulation direction, the test statistic for the directional claim about increased fWHR cannot be computed from the provided data.

dependent_variable: Amount offered/transferred by the proposer (po_bribe in BG, b_split in UG)
main_predictor: Game frame: Bribery Game vs. Ultimatum Game
sample_definition: Proposers only: BG public officials (n=199) and UG Participant B (n=195) with non-missing offer
model_specification: Welch two-sample t-test (with Mann-Whitney U as robustness)
operationalization_notes: The 'bribe amount' is the transfer chosen by the player with bargaining power; in BG that is the public official's offer (po_bribe), in the strategically identical UG it is participant B's split (b_split). Compared means across the two frames.
reasoning: Mean offered amount in the bribery-frame (public official, M=0.58, n=199) is significantly lower than in the ultimatum-frame (participant B, M=0.91, n=195); Welch t(392)=-5.37, p<.001. Mann-Whitney one-sided p=5.2e-11 corroborates. Consistent with the paper's claim that average bribe is lower in the bribery game.

dependent_variable: Predicted number of taxicabs divided by the maximum cab number seen (response/max_value)
main_predictor: Number of observations provided (values_seen: 1, 3, or 10)
sample_definition: All taxicab-condition participants with valid estimates on all three observation-count trials
model_specification: Friedman non-parametric repeated-measures test across the three values_seen levels
controls: None (within-subject design; max_value normalisation built into DV)
operationalization_notes: Because the maximum observed cab number tends to grow with more samples, raw estimates do not directly capture the Bayesian-shrinkage claim. Normalising the prediction by the observed maximum (the standard quantity in the German-tank/taxicab problem) and using a within-subject non-parametric test isolates how participants' guesses shrink toward the data as evidence accumulates.
reasoning: Within-subject Friedman test on the prediction/observed-max ratio across the three observation-count conditions (1, 3, 10) yielded χ²(2)=281.6, p<1e-61, N=669. Mean ratios fell monotonically from 2.20 (1 obs) to 1.36 (3 obs) to 1.16 (10 obs), confirming that estimates of the total number of cabs shrank toward the observed maximum as more examples were provided.

dependent_variable: est_fraud_share (estimated fraud share by district)
main_predictor: v.elday.pc and v.elday.pc.2 (election-day violence per capita, linear and squared)
sample_definition: All 375 districts with complete data on the variables used
model_specification: OLS regression with quadratic in violence
operationalization_notes: Inverted-U is most directly tested via the sign and significance of the squared violence term in a quadratic regression on fraud. Reported statistic is the t-test on the squared term; joint F(2,368)=8.52, p<0.001 also significant.
reasoning: OLS regression of estimated fraud share on violence per capita (election day) and its square, plus controls, yields a positive linear coefficient (1.22) and a significantly negative squared term (-1.79, t=-3.23, p=0.001). This is consistent with an inverted U-shaped relationship between violence and fraud.

dependent_variable: Coworker social undermining (Undermin)
main_predictor: TSC × ConditionCompetition interaction
sample_definition: All 574 participants (1148 observations) in the analytical data file with two within-subject TSC observations each
model_specification: Linear mixed-effects model: Undermin ~ TSC * ConditionCompetition + (1|id)
operationalization_notes: Data are structured as 2 within-subject TSC observations per participant with a between-subjects competition manipulation; the moderation claim corresponds directly to the TSC × Competition interaction term in a mixed model accounting for repeated measures.
reasoning: A mixed-effects model (random intercepts by participant id) of Undermining on TSC, Competition condition, and their interaction yielded a significant TSC × Competition interaction (b=-0.578, z=-3.38, p<.001). Simple effects: in the high-competition condition the difference between TSC levels is large (5.55 vs 4.84), whereas under low competition it is negligible (5.34 vs 5.22), indicating the TSC–undermining relationship is stronger when competition is high, consistent with the claim (direction depending on TSC coding).

dependent_variable: Mean of 6 COVID-specific conspiracy theory items (SpecCTs_1..6r)
main_predictor: Mean COVID risk perception (worry COVID1 + threat COVID3)
sample_definition: All respondents with complete data on risk and CT items (pooled across the three samples in the file)
model_specification: Pearson correlation / simple linear regression test of zero slope
operationalization_notes: The provided dataset contains only risk perception items (COVID1, COVID3) and COVID-specific conspiracy theory items; the mediators in the claim (anxiety, lack of control) and trust in institutions are not present in this file. The most direct testable piece of the claim is therefore the predicted positive association from risk perception to conspiracy beliefs.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between mean COVID risk perception (COVID1, COVID3) and mean COVID-specific conspiracy theory endorsement (6 SpecCTs items) is r = -0.168, t(804) = -4.83, p < .001. The relationship is significant but in the opposite direction to the claim — higher perceived risk is associated with LOWER, not higher, conspiracy belief endorsement.

dependent_variable: Mean reaction time (ms) per participant
main_predictor: Central face emotion (angry vs neutral), within-subject
sample_definition: Participants classified as likely GAD (Group==1) with non-missing AngryM and NeutralM
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing AngryM vs NeutralM
operationalization_notes: The dataset provides one mean RT per emotion per participant; the claim concerns within-group RT differences by central face emotion in GAD, so a paired t-test on AngryM vs NeutralM within Group==1 is the most direct test.
reasoning: In the GAD group (n=63), mean RT for angry-central trials (486.8 ms) was numerically slightly slower than neutral-central trials (485.4 ms); a paired t-test gave t(62)=0.47, p=.64, providing no evidence that GAD participants were faster on angry versus neutral central faces.

dependent_variable: Post-interaction brand personality impression (mean of Q5_1-Q5_4: upper class, good looking, charming, glamorous, on 1-8 scale)
main_predictor: Consistency x Pseudorelevant Information (disclosure) interaction
sample_definition: Stage 2 dataset, participants in the high outcome-dependency condition (Outcome Dependency==1), with complete data on the relevant items (n=425)
model_specification: OLS 2x2 ANOVA: BPI ~ Consistency * PseudorelevantInformation, Type II SS
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns the Consistency x Disclosure interaction conditional on high outcome dependency, so analysis was restricted to that subsample. Brand personality impression was operationalized as the mean of the four post-interaction brand ratings (Q5_1-Q5_4). Pseudorelevant Information is coded 1 = not disclosed, 0 = disclosed, matching the claim's contrast direction.
reasoning: Restricting to high outcome dependency, a 2x2 ANOVA of brand personality impressions on Consistency x Pseudorelevant Information yields a non-significant interaction, F(1,421)=0.35, p=.56. The direction matches the claim (consistency effect slightly larger when no pseudorelevant info is disclosed: +0.70 vs +0.54 scale points), but it is far from significant.

dependent_variable: Per-item 'disturbing' rating (0-6) of each humor stimulus
main_predictor: Covid-19 humor (1) vs non-pandemic humor (0), operationalized as Survey 2 vs Survey 1
sample_definition: All non-missing disturbing ratings for every pic across both Survey 1 and Survey 2 participants
model_specification: Linear mixed-effects model: disturbing ~ covid + (1|participant_id), fit via REML in statsmodels
controls: Random intercept per participant; no fixed-effect covariates
operationalization_notes: The data dictionary does not explicitly tag which pictures are Covid vs non-Covid. Given the abstract states Covid humor 'lacks a signature of funniness', I labelled Survey 2 (markedly lower mean funniness, 3.53 vs 3.83 in Survey 1) as Covid humor and Survey 1 as non-pandemic, and tested the directional aversiveness claim with a mixed model.
reasoning: A linear mixed model predicting aversiveness (disturbing) ratings from a Covid vs non-Covid indicator, with random intercepts for participants, yielded a tiny coefficient (b=0.004) with z=0.964, p=0.335 (N=223,171 ratings from 1,225 participants). Covid humor mean disturb=1.737 vs non-Covid=1.718. The data do not reproduce a reliable greater aversiveness for Covid humor under this operationalization.

dependent_variable: Binary: adopted ≥1 of six avoidance behaviors (prep items 4,5,6,8,10,11)
main_predictor: govtrustQ1 (trust in government COVID-19 information, 1-7)
sample_definition: Australian adults (n=700 replication file); 580 with non-missing avoidance and govtrust
model_specification: Univariable logistic regression
operationalization_notes: Mirrors paper's outcome (≥1 avoidance behavior) and uses the most direct measure of trust in government/authorities (govtrustQ1).
reasoning: Logistic regression of 'adopted ≥1 avoidance behavior' on trust in government information yields z = 3.16, p = .002, OR = 1.34 per unit of trust — higher trust is associated with greater odds of avoidance behaviors, matching the paper's reported positive association.

dependent_variable: CMMS (current money management stress, mean of 5 items; higher = more stress)
main_predictor: Frame condition (Group: 1=negative/failure, 2=positive/success)
sample_definition: Participants meeting inclusion criteria (Include==1) with non-missing CMMS
model_specification: Welch's independent-samples t-test comparing CMMS between success and failure frames
operationalization_notes: Codebook indicates Group=2 is the positive writing prompt (success frame). CMMS (not the reverse-coded CMMSRC) used so that lower values denote less stress, matching the claim's 'lower current money management stress' wording.
reasoning: Participants in the success/positive frame (Group 2, M=2.997, SD=1.10, n=131) reported significantly lower current money management stress than those in the failure/negative frame (Group 1, M=3.441, SD=0.86, n=131); Welch t(245.86)=-3.65, p<.001, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Disp_AttB (dispositional attributions scale, bidirectional version)
main_predictor: Sit_AttB (situational attributions scale, bidirectional version)
sample_definition: Respondents assigned to the bidirectional-items condition (BiDummy==1) with non-missing scales (N=642)
model_specification: OLS bivariate regression of Disp_AttB on Sit_AttB
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns bidirectional formulation; used the precomputed bidirectional scales and the experimental condition indicator.
reasoning: In the bidirectional-items subsample, OLS regression of dispositional attributions (Disp_AttB) on situational attributions (Sit_AttB) yields b=-0.280, t(640)=-7.58, p≈1.2e-13, r=-0.29 — a highly significant negative relationship, consistent with the paper's claim that bidirectional items reveal the underlying negative association.

dependent_variable: PSS-10 perceived stress score
main_predictor: Monthly income
sample_definition: All respondents with non-missing income and PSS-10 (full sample, n=2053)
model_specification: Pearson correlation between monthly income and PSS-10 score
operationalization_notes: Claim is bivariate directional; used the continuous PSS-10 score (primary stress outcome) and MONTHLY INCOME variable with a simple Pearson correlation.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between MONTHLY INCOME and PSS-10 perceived stress score is r = -0.080, p < .001, n = 2053, indicating that higher income is significantly associated with lower perceived stress.

dependent_variable: Mean of 4 greedy behavioral inclination items (behav_incl_1-4)
main_predictor: Dispositional Greed Scale (DGS)
sample_definition: All 510 participants in the analytic dataset with complete data on DGS, MVS, and behavioral items
model_specification: OLS linear regression: behav ~ DGS + MVS
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns Study 2's incremental validity of DGS over materialism in predicting greedy behavioral tendencies. The four behav_incl items appear to operationalize greedy behavioral inclinations; I averaged them and regressed on DGS controlling for MVS, taking the t on DGS as the test.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of the mean greedy behavioral tendencies score (behav_incl_1-4) on DGS and MVS, DGS remained a strong significant predictor (b=0.72, t(507)=17.85, p<.001) controlling for materialism (MVS: b=0.11, t=2.22). This supports the claim that DGS predicts greedy behavioral tendencies over and above materialism.

dependent_variable: Chose ambiguous candidate (binary, derived from Q3 and presentation order RND_01)
main_predictor: Risk aversion (Q4==2 vs Q4∈{1,3})
sample_definition: All respondents with valid Q3 (Candidate A/B) and Q4 (risk preference) responses; n=2687
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a 2x2 contingency table
operationalization_notes: Q4 directly measures risk preference; the binary contrast risk-averse vs not is the most direct test of the verbal claim. The chosen-ambiguous indicator was constructed by combining Q3 with RND_01 (presentation order of precise/ambiguous candidates).
reasoning: Risk-averse respondents (Q4=2) chose the ambiguous candidate 47.0% of the time vs 49.8% among those preferring risk or having no preference. The chi-square test gives χ²(1)=1.99, p=0.158 — the difference is in the direction predicted by the claim but is not statistically significant.

dependent_variable: HYSpread = ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (last trading day of month, in bps)
main_predictor: LargeandMedium: Net % of domestic banks tightening C&I lending standards for large/medium firms (SLOOS) — proxy for negative fundamental/funding shock
sample_definition: All months from 2010-01 through 2020-07 where HY spread and quarterly SLOOS series overlap (n=126).
model_specification: OLS level regression: HYSpread_t = a + b*LargeandMedium_t + e_t
operationalization_notes: Only HY spread and SLOOS tightening are available in the provided data. Tightening of credit standards is used as an empirical proxy for the model's 'negative fundamental shock' that makes margin constraints bind; the HY OAS captures losses to leveraged credit holders. A positive slope supports the claim.
reasoning: Regressing the monthly ICE BofA US High-Yield OAS (HYSpread, bps) on the SLOOS net % of banks tightening C&I credit standards (LargeandMedium) — a proxy for negative fundamental/funding shocks — yields a positive and significant slope of 3.31 bps per percentage point of tightening (t=3.205, p=0.0017, n=126). Wider HY spreads imply mark-to-market losses on leveraged credit positions, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Job Satisfaction Scale mean (JSSmean)
main_predictor: Overall WICS score (mean of 5 subscale means: IC, WIR, PA, WGI, LOS)
sample_definition: All 597 respondents with complete WICS and JSS data
model_specification: Pearson correlation between WICS composite and job satisfaction
operationalization_notes: The claim of validity is operationalized as criterion validity: WICS scores should be meaningfully related to a theoretically linked workplace outcome (job satisfaction), consistent with the validity evidence emphasized in the abstract.
reasoning: The composite WICS score (mean of the 5 subscale means) correlates strongly and significantly with job satisfaction (r=0.474, t(595)=13.14, p<.001, N=597), supporting the criterion validity of the WICS as a measure of intergenerational climate.

dependent_variable: Intention to refrain from stockpiling next week (Q9_1 reverse-scored: 'I am planning to buy more food/supplies than usually')
main_predictor: HEXACO Honesty-Humility composite (mean of HE_1-HE_16 with negatively keyed items reverse-scored)
sample_definition: All respondents in ColumbusOSF.csv with non-missing H-H items and Q9_1 (n=314 of 315)
model_specification: Pearson product-moment correlation; t-test on r with df = n-2
operationalization_notes: Abstract only available. Identified the first 16 HE items as the Honesty-Humility scale (the remaining HE_17-HE_32 items concern Emotionality). Reverse-keyed items determined from item content. Future intention to refrain from stockpiling operationalized as reverse-coded Q9_1, the future-tense analogue of the stockpiling item.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between mean Honesty-Humility (HE_1-HE_16, with negatively keyed items reverse-scored) and intention to refrain from stockpiling (reverse-scored Q9_1) was r = 0.47, t(312) = 9.51, p < .001, n = 314 — Honesty-Humility was positively associated with intentions to refrain from stockpiling, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Cumulative COVID-19 deaths per 100,000 population at the latest available date
main_predictor: Percent uninsured under 65 (average of percent uninsured <19 and percent uninsured 19-64 from ACS S2701)
sample_definition: County-level observations from merged_covid_usa_v2.dta restricted to non-urban counties, defined as all counties except the 114 highest population-density counties (mirroring paper's n=114 urban / n=2826 non-urban split); complete cases on all covariates (n=2857)
model_specification: OLS linear regression (paper used spatial autoregressive models; spatial weights matrix not reconstructed here)
controls: percent non-English-speaking households, percent farm workers (LABOR/total population*100), percent below poverty line, percent age 65+, and population density
operationalization_notes: Without methods text, I built one cross-sectional county-level dataset using the most recent date per FIPS, computed mortality per 100k, and ran OLS with the four focal SDOH predictors plus age and density. Restricted to non-urban counties because the claim about uninsured is specifically from that subset in the abstract.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of county-level COVID-19 mortality per 100k on percent uninsured (mean of <19 and 19-64 rates) with controls for non-English households, farm-worker share, poverty, %65+, and density, restricted to non-urban counties (excluding the 114 highest-density counties), the uninsured coefficient was negative (b=-0.074, t(2850)=-0.59, p=0.56). Direction matches the paper's claim but the effect is not statistically significant in a non-spatial OLS, so the result is inconclusive in this specification.

dependent_variable: Dessert choice (chocolate cake vs. fruit salad)
main_predictor: Recalled decision type (delegated/dependent vs. independent)
sample_definition: All 125 participants in the first-round analytic dataset (the recall study with dessert choice DV)
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on the 2x2 contingency table
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns choice share of chocolate cake by recall condition; the most direct test is a chi-square on dessert choice (cake vs. fruit salad) by decisiontype. Used the firstround analytic dataset as Study 3's recall study.
reasoning: In the first-round (recall) dataset, the chocolate-cake choice share was 58.7% in the delegated (dependent) recall condition vs. 61.3% in the independent recall condition — numerically opposite to the claim and not significant, χ²(1, N=125)=0.085, p=.77.

dependent_variable: Common mental disorder (binary: SRQ-17 score ≥7)
main_predictor: Lifetime emotional/verbal IPV (viover, 0/1)
sample_definition: Ever-married/in-union women aged ≤44 with complete data on outcome, IPV measures, and covariates
model_specification: Binary logistic regression
controls: Physical IPV (ever), sexual IPV (ever), age (years), years of education, marital status, wealth quintile dummies, area (urban/rural)
operationalization_notes: Only 17 SRQ items (p622a–q) are present in the dataset, so CMD was operationalized as sum ≥7 (proportional to the standard SRQ-20 cutoff of ≥8). Note: data file appears to be the Nicaragua 2006 ENDESA survey rather than Paraguay 2008, but it is what was supplied; analysis follows the paper's modeling approach.
reasoning: Multivariable logistic regression of CMD (SRQ sum ≥7, using 17 available SRQ items) on emotional IPV (lifetime verbal IPV), adjusting for physical IPV, sexual IPV, age, education, marital status, wealth quintile, and urban/rural area, yields a strongly positive and significant coefficient for emotional IPV (z=14.47, p≈2e-47, N=11,393). Emotional IPV is independently associated with increased odds of CMD, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: stock liquidity (e.g., proportional bid-ask spread) — not computable without NASDAQ_2010_19 file
main_predictor: VIX (log change or level)
sample_definition: intended: NASDAQ daily 2010–2019 merged with VIX; actual: data unavailable

The original paper reports this contrast as a Welch's t-test following a 2x3 mixed ANOVA; I matched that follow-up test on the provided dataset. Note the provided data contain N=160, larger than the N=48 implied by the paper's degrees of freedom; results are reported on the full dataset as instructed.

The OBS group's mean is numerically slightly higher but the difference is far from significant, so the claim that social observation increases deontological judgments in personal moral dilemmas is not supported in this dataset.

dependent_variable: mh_anxiety_1 (self-reported COVID-19 anxiety/concern, 5-point scale)

operationalization_notes: The csv file contains gender plus an anxiety/concern item on a 5-point scale, which most directly maps to the paper's measure of being 'worried/concerned about COVID-19'. A t-test contrasting men vs women on this item is the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: Welch's t-test on the COVID-19 anxiety/concern item (mh_anxiety_1) shows women (M=3.07, n=4933) report significantly higher concern than men (M=2.89, n=5138), t(10067.5)=8.26, p<.001. This is consistent with the paper's claim that women are more concerned about COVID-19 than men.

dependent_variable: Change in county-level share of population staying at home (BTS Trips by Distance), March 19–28, 2020 minus February 2020 baseline, expressed as percentage-point change in mobility (positive = less social distancing).

controls: Per-capita income, percent male, percent Black, percent Hispanic, percent college, percent employed in retail/transportation/health-education-social-services, percent rural, age-decade shares, and state fixed effects.
operationalization_notes: Unacast data are not in the replication package; following the paper's described approach (change in mobility from pre-COVID matched baseline, with the same set of controls and state fixed effects), I built a BTS-based analogue using pop_home/(pop_home+pop_not_home) and reversed the sign so a positive coefficient indicates less distancing, consistent with the paper's coefficient convention.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of the change in average county mobility (March 19–28, 2020 vs. February 2020 matched-weekday baseline, in percentage points, signed so positive = less distancing) on Trump's 2016 vote share with sociodemographic, labor-market, age-structure controls and state fixed effects, Trump share has a positive coefficient (β=1.99 per unit, i.e. less social distancing) with t=5.86, p<1e-8 (n=3,114). This replicates the paper's conclusion that greater Republican orientation is associated with reduced social distancing.

dependent_variable: soc_dist composite (mean of 4 social distancing compliance items)

reasoning: Pearson correlation between political conservatism (pol composite) and social distancing compliance (soc_dist composite) was r = -0.179, t(320) = -3.26, p = .001, n = 322, indicating that greater conservatism predicted less compliance with social distancing.

dependent_variable: Composite academic achievement (z-score sum of 3rd-grade reading and math IRT scale scores, X7RSCALK5 + X7MSCALK5)
main_predictor: Composite social-emotional problems (z-score sum of teacher-reported externalizing X7TCHEXT and internalizing X7TCHINT)

model_specification: Pearson correlation between the two composite z-score indices, with significance tested via t = r*sqrt((n-2)/(1-r^2))
operationalization_notes: The methods section is redacted; the paper's Table 3 indicates third-grade reading/math IRT scores and SDQ externalizing/internalizing teacher ratings as the relevant variables. ELL was operationalized via the composite non-English home-language flag X12LANGST=1. A simple Pearson correlation captures the bivariate directional relationship described in the claim.
reasoning: Among ELL children (X12LANGST=1, non-English/dual home language), the Pearson correlation between teacher-reported social-emotional problems (z-score sum of externalizing X7TCHEXT and internalizing X7TCHINT) and academic achievement (z-score sum of third-grade reading X7RSCALK5 and math X7MSCALK5) is r = -0.093, t(2090) = -4.27, p < .001. The negative correlation indicates fewer social-emotional problems are associated with higher achievement, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Average of SocGood ratings across the four hypothetical organizations (Artis, Green, Food, Medtech), 1=great harm to 5=great good
main_predictor: Organization label condition: for-profit (condition=3) vs. non-profit (condition=1)

model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test (equal variances) comparing mean SocGood between for-profit and non-profit conditions
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether labeling an organization as profit-seeking reduces perceived societal good. Following the design described in the dictionary (within-subject across 4 firms, between-subject label manipulation), I averaged the four SocGood items per participant and contrasted the for-profit vs non-profit conditions, which is the most direct test of the claim.
reasoning: In Study 3, firms labeled 'for-profit' (n=123, M=3.75, SD=0.58) were rated as accomplishing significantly less societal good than firms labeled 'non-profit' (n=121, M=4.31, SD=0.43), t(242)=8.59, p<.001. Profit motive thus reduced perceived societal good, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Per-participant mean sharing intention (1-6 Likert) across 15 headlines
main_predictor: Headline veracity (true vs. false), within-subjects
sample_definition: All participants assigned to the treatment (accuracy nudge) condition in Study 2 with non-missing sharing ratings (n=440)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing each participant's mean sharing intention for true vs. false headlines
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns whether, within the treatment group, sharing for true > false. The most direct test is a within-subject paired comparison of each participant's average true-headline vs. false-headline sharing intention; this avoids inflating df via long-format pseudo-replication while directly testing the stated within-condition contrast.
reasoning: In the treatment (accuracy-nudge) condition, mean sharing intention for true headlines (M=3.49 on a 6-point scale) was not significantly higher than for false headlines (M=3.52); a paired t-test on participant means yielded t(439) = -1.12, p = .27. If anything, the direction was opposite to the claim. The reproduction therefore does not support the directional claim in the simplest per-participant test, though the original paper used a mixed-effects long-format model that produced a small significant effect.

dependent_variable: Binary indicator: 1 if the country's annual GDP per capita growth was ≥2% in every year of the 5 years starting from the Afrobarometer survey year (y..y+4), else 0
main_predictor: log of the country-wave Impartiality index (weighted share of respondents who said their ethnic group is 'never' treated unfairly by the government), constructed from Afrobarometer rounds 1–4
sample_definition: Country-wave observations from Afrobarometer rounds 1–4 (20 sub-Saharan African countries, 1999–2009) for which the Impartiality index, Polity2 score, and a complete 5-year forward GDP growth window were available
model_specification: Pooled OLS linear probability model: sustained_growth = a + b*log(Impartiality) + c*Polity2 + e
controls: Polity2 score (matching the simplest specification in the paper's main table)
operationalization_notes: Methods section was redacted, so I operationalized following the paper's own verbal main definition: sustained growth = ≥2% per-capita growth for ≥5 consecutive years starting at the survey year. Impartiality index follows the appendix coding (share of respondents identifying with an ethnic group who answer 'Never' on the unfair-treatment question, weighted by within-country weight). Used the simplest model (Pooled OLS with Polity2) corresponding to Table 2 column 1.
reasoning: Pooled OLS of a binary sustained-growth indicator on log(Impartiality index) controlling for Polity2 yields a small negative, statistically insignificant coefficient on log impartiality (b=-0.023, t(61)=-0.23, p=0.82) on 64 country-wave observations across 20 countries. This does not reproduce the paper's positive, significant association between government impartiality and sustained growth.

dependent_variable: choice_toaster (1 = 4.5-star/aggregated-positive toaster; 2 = 2.5-star/individualized-positive toaster)

operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the within-condition preference of the abstract-sound group between the two toasters; a goodness-of-fit chi-square (equivalently a binomial test, p=.012) directly tests whether choices departed from chance toward the aggregated-information toaster.
reasoning: Among the 20 participants in the abstract sound condition (group 5: C=>F# Rev measure 1), 16 chose the 4.5-star toaster (positive aggregated information) vs. 4 choosing the 2.5-star toaster (positive individualized information). A chi-square goodness-of-fit test against a 50/50 split yields χ²(1)=7.20, p=.007, confirming that the abstract-sound group strongly favored the aggregated-information toaster.

dependent_variable: GDP per capita (national affluence)
main_predictor: Imports from the South (totalimport)

controls: Exports to the South, unemployment, country FE, year FE
operationalization_notes: The claim refers to the indirect/positive effect of southern imports on affluence (Model 4 in the paper). I regress GDP per capita on imports from the South, controlling for exports to the South, unemployment, and country/year fixed effects.
reasoning: Regressing GDP per capita (national affluence) on imports from the South, with exports to the South, unemployment, country fixed effects, and year fixed effects, the coefficient on imports from the South is positive and highly significant (t=3.25, p=0.001, N=755), consistent with the paper's reported positive indirect effect of southern imports on affluence.

dependent_variable: Per-participant benefit-symbolism difference score (Util rating minus Symbol rating) averaged across the four symbolic products (college T-shirts, American flags, class rings, greeting cards)
main_predictor: Branding condition: Brand (Cond=3 or 4, brand sets A/B) vs. No Brand (Cond=1 or 2)

model_specification: Independent-samples t-test (equal variances) comparing mean symbolic-product difference scores between Brand and No-Brand conditions
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns Study 1 (cited at p.351), in which branding altered attitude functions for symbolic categories. I averaged the benefit−symbolism difference scores across the four symbolic products within each participant, then compared brand vs. no-brand conditions with a two-sample t-test, paralleling the contrast described in the paper's Table for Study 1.
reasoning: For symbolic product categories (T-shirts, flags, class rings, greeting cards), the benefit-minus-symbolism difference score was significantly less negative when products were branded (M=-2.09) than when unbranded (M=-2.66), t(555)=4.07, p<.001. Thus branding shifts attitudes toward symbolic categories to be less symbolic / more utilitarian, replicating the direction of the original Study 1 finding.

dependent_variable: Semester GPA

operationalization_notes: Only summary statistics (means, SDs, correlations) are available. The path from self-regulation to GPA in a SEM with these five variables reduces, in the unconditional bivariate case, to the zero-order correlation; I report the t-test on r=.30 with df=n-2=364.
reasoning: Using the summary correlation matrix (Jung et al., N=366), the bivariate association between academic self-regulation (academic self-discipline) and semester GPA is r=.30, yielding t(364)=6.00, p<.001. This indicates self-regulation positively predicts GPA, consistent with the SEM claim.

dependent_variable: Per-participant proportion of trials on which the higher-fWHR/masculinity (right-side) face was chosen as more aggressive

I therefore tested the overall claim with a participant-level one-sample t-test against chance using all 36 trials; because the original protocol placed the high-fWHR/high-masculinity face on the right, mean 'Right' proportion >0.5 indexes the predicted effect. Used the larger replication file (Processed_Data_2.csv) since the claim covers both male and female target faces (Study 2 design).

dependent_variable: Amount of money demanded/proposed (variable 'money', in USD)

operationalization_notes: The claim concerns average bribe amount; 'money' is the directly comparable proposer demand across BG (PO) and UG (Participant B). Mann-Whitney chosen because the variable is discrete/right-skewed on a bounded scale.

Bribes are significantly lower in BG than UG, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Predicted total number of taxis divided by the largest observed taxi number (t/t_past)
main_predictor: Number of observations seen (1, 3, or 10)

reasoning: A one-way within-subjects ANOVA on the normalized prediction t/t_past for the taxicab scenario across 1, 3, and 10 observations revealed a highly significant effect of number of observations, F(2,1148)=127.92, p<.001. Mean ratios decreased monotonically (1.85, 1.33, 1.15), confirming that estimates of the total number of taxicabs shrink as more examples are provided.

dependent_variable: fraudchi2_total (binary indicator district fails last-digit uniformity test)

reasoning: Logit of district last-digit fraud indicator on election-day violence per capita and its square (plus controls) yields a positive linear coefficient (8.48, z=2.55) and a negative quadratic coefficient (-13.75, z=-2.14, p=0.032), consistent with an inverted U-shape between violence and fraud.

dependent_variable: Social undermining (Undermin; reverse-coded willingness to be matched)

Because Undermin is reverse-coded (lower = more undermining) and TSC=1 = unfavorable comparison, the negative interaction means unfavorable temporal comparison led to more undermining under high vs. low competition, supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: Mean COVID-19 specific conspiracy belief endorsement (SpecCTs_1..6r averaged, 1-7)

controls: none (age, gender, education, trust, lack-of-control not available in the released cleaned data file)

reasoning: In an OLS regression predicting mean COVID-19 conspiracy-belief endorsement from mean COVID worry/threat (the only anxiety/risk-perception proxy provided in the cleaned replication file), the slope is significantly NEGATIVE (b = -0.146, SE = 0.030, t(804) = -4.83, p < .001; r = -.17, n = 806). Thus, in the provided dataset, higher COVID worry is associated with LOWER—not higher—conspiracy beliefs, the opposite of the claim.

dependent_variable: Mean reaction time (ms)

dependent_variable: Brand personality impression difference score: mean of post-interaction sophistication items (Q5_1–Q5_4) minus mean of pre-interaction items (Q2_1–Q2_4)

operationalization_notes: The claim concerns the simple Consistency × Pseudorelevant-Information interaction conditional on high outcome dependency. I used the brand personality (sophistication/ruggedness) difference score described in the paper as the most direct DV; brand attitude items are not clearly labeled in the codebook, so I focused on brand personality.
reasoning: Within the high-outcome-dependency subsample (N=425), a 2 (Consistency) × 2 (Pseudorelevant Information) ANOVA on the brand personality difference score (post − pre mean of Q5 − Q2 items) yielded a non-significant Consistency × Pseudorelevant-Information interaction, F(1,421)=0.67, p=.41. Although cell means trend in the predicted direction (consistent/no-info = 0.13 > consistent/info = -0.02; inconsistent/no-info = -0.72 < inconsistent/info = -0.68), the interaction effect is far from significant, so the data do not support the claim.

dependent_variable: Mean disturbing rating (1-7 scale) per participant
main_predictor: Survey part (Part1 = Non-Covid humor set, Part2 = Covid humor set, assumed mapping)

operationalization_notes: The redacted methods section and de-identified data do not provide explicit type labels for the 216 items (96 in Part1, 120 in Part2). Because each participant completed both surveys with disjoint stimulus sets, the most defensible aggregate test of the claim is a within-subject comparison of average aversiveness between the two parts, treating Part1 as the Non-Covid baseline and Part2 as the Covid stimulus set.
reasoning: A paired t-test comparing each participant's mean aversiveness (disturbing) rating in Part 2 (presumed to contain Covid humor, 120 items) vs Part 1 (presumed to contain Non-Covid humor, 96 items) found nearly identical means (1.733 vs 1.730, scale 1-7) and a non-significant difference (t(1022)=0.22, p=0.83). Note: the deidentified data files do not include explicit stimulus-type labels (Non-Covid Verbal / Covid Verbal / Covid Meme / Covid Strip), so the parts were used as a proxy for Covid vs. Non-Covid content.

Avoidance composite uses the 'prep' multiple-response items most closely matching the paper's six avoidance behaviors. Continuous predictor used to avoid arbitrary dichotomization; reported z is the Wald statistic for the predictor.
reasoning: Logistic regression of having performed ≥1 avoidance behavior (prep items: avoiding social events, public transport, eating out, grocery shopping, staying home from work, buying extra supplies) on continuous trust in government information (govtrustQ1, 1–7) yields a positive coefficient b=0.317, z=3.62, p<.001 (n=588). Higher trust is associated with higher odds of adopting avoidance behaviors, matching the original claim.

dependent_variable: Reverse-scored current money management stress (CMMSRC), 5-item average (higher = less stress)
main_predictor: Valence frame condition (success vs. failure writing prompt; Group 2 vs 1)
sample_definition: All participants meeting inclusion criteria (Include==1); n=262 (replication dataset, both versions of each frame combined)

operationalization_notes: Codebook indicates Group 1=failure (negative prompt), Group 2=success (positive prompt). The dataset is a replication; original study 3a manipulated CMMS only, so I used the CMMSRC outcome and tested the simple success-vs-failure contrast.
reasoning: Independent-samples t-test comparing reverse-scored current money management stress (CMMSRC) between success (Group 2, n=131, M=3.00, SD=1.10) and failure (Group 1, n=131, M=2.56, SD=0.86) frame conditions: t(260)=3.65, p<.001. Success participants report higher reverse-scored CMMS (i.e., lower money-management stress), consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Situational attributions (Sit_AttB)

dependent_variable: Mean of four greedy behavioral inclination items (food, sex, friends, phone)
main_predictor: Dispositional Greed Scale (DGS) score
sample_definition: All respondents with complete DGS, MVS, and behavioral inclination data (N=510)

reasoning: In an OLS regression of mean greedy behavioral inclinations (behav_incl_1-4) on DGS controlling for MVS, DGS remained a strong significant predictor (b=0.72, t(507)=17.85, p<.001) while MVS was only marginal (b=0.11, t=2.22). dependent_variable: Chose ambiguous candidate (1=ambiguous, 0=precise) derived from Q3 and RND_01
main_predictor: Risk aversion (Q4==2: prefers avoiding risks)
sample_definition: All TESS066 respondents with valid responses on Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 and assigned ambiguous/precise positions (N=2684); experiment is unbranded.
model_specification: Probit with HC1 robust SE; predictors: risk aversion, voter certainty (Q2==1), distance differential (|Q1-precise| - |Q1-amb midpoint|)

sample_definition: Swiss respondents in the replication dataset with complete PSS-10 and trust_countrymeasure data (N=1059)
model_specification: One-way ANOVA (PSS sum ~ agreement category)
operationalization_notes: trust_countrymeasure ranges 0 (too little) to 10 (too much) with 5=appropriate; following the paper's three-level grouping in Table 1 (Agreement / No agreement / No agreement at all), I categorized by absolute deviation from 5, yielding category sizes (685/307/67) close to the paper's reported ratios.
reasoning: One-way ANOVA on PSS-10 sum across three agreement categories (derived from |trust_countrymeasure - 5|: ≤1 Agreement, 2-4 No agreement, 5 No agreement at all) yields F(2,1056)=12.84, p<.001. Mean stress rises monotonically with disagreement (13.27 → 14.12 → 17.36), supporting the claim that agreement with containment measures is associated with lower stress.

dependent_variable: Trust decision (binary; Option L = trust = 1, Option R = 0)
main_predictor: Honesty-Humility × Condition (Uncertainty vs Certainty) interaction
sample_definition: All 844 participants with valid DV, Condition, and HEXACO H-H scores
model_specification: Logistic regression: Trust ~ HH_centered * Condition
operationalization_notes: Honesty-Humility computed as mean of the 10 HEXACO-60 H-H items (items 12,24,30,42,48,60 reverse-scored). Condition coded 0=Certainty/1=Uncertainty per codebook. Mean-centered HH per the original paper's moderation analysis.
reasoning: Logistic regression of Trust (Option L = trust) on mean-centered Honesty-Humility, Condition (1=Uncertainty), and their interaction yielded a non-significant interaction (B=-0.088, SE=0.150, z=-0.587, p=.557), N=844. The HH main effect replicated (z=2.95, p=.003), but the predicted HH×Uncertainty interaction did not.

dependent_variable: Desirability index (mean of S1_likely, S1_quality, S1_purchase)
main_predictor: Self-concept clarity condition (clear vs. conflicted) × rating distribution (bimodal vs. unimodal) interaction
sample_definition: All non-excluded participants across the four cleaned condition sheets (CoU, CoB, ClU, ClB) in the SCORE dataset
model_specification: OLS regression: desirability ~ clarity_c * dist_c (each contrast-coded ±1); interaction term is the focal test
operationalization_notes: Claim concerns 'temporary' low self-concept clarity, corresponding to Study 2b which manipulated clarity vs. conflict. Followed the paper's stated approach: averaged the three desirability items, contrast-coded both factors, and tested the clarity × distribution interaction.
reasoning: OLS regression of desirability (mean of S1_likely, S1_quality, S1_purchase) on contrast-coded clarity (clear=1, conflicted=-1) × distribution (bimodal=1, unimodal=-1) yielded a significant interaction (b=-0.146, t(372)=-2.30, p=.022). Cell means show bimodal preferred over unimodal under the conflicted (low temporary self-concept clarity) condition (4.98 vs 4.33), but not under clear (4.60 vs 4.53), matching the original claim.

dependent_variable: Revenge (mean of RevengeAvoidRecon items 1-3)
main_predictor: Anger (mean of EmoResp_AngerSymp items 1-3)
sample_definition: Participants assigned to one of the three lab scenario conditions (Malice/Greed/Control) with complete responses on attribution, severity, emotion, and behavioral-tendency scales (N=1118).
model_specification: OLS multiple regression: Revenge ~ Anger + Sympathy + perceived Malice + perceived Greed + Severity
controls: Perceived offender malice (ManipulationCheck_2), perceived offender greed (ManipulationCheck_1), and perceived offense severity (mean of OffenseSeverity_1-3).
operationalization_notes: The claim has multiple parts; the single most direct test of the central mediation-style assertion (emotions show independent relations to behavioral outcomes after accounting for attributions) is the partial t-statistic for Anger in a regression predicting Revenge, with attribution and severity entered as controls. Anger→Revenge is also the path explicitly highlighted in the paper's structural model.
reasoning: In an OLS regression of revenge on anger and sympathy controlling for perceived malice, perceived greed, and offense severity (N=1118), anger independently and positively predicted revenge, t(1112)=7.07, p<.001. Parallel models showed anger and sympathy also independently predicted avoidance (anger t=7.13; sympathy t=-2.97) and reconciliation (anger t=-3.78; sympathy t=9.90), supporting the claim that emotional reactions have independent relations with revenge, avoidance, and reconciliation over and above attributions.

dependent_variable: COVID-19 misperception composite score (MisperpSc)
main_predictor: Cognitive sophistication composite (CogSophSc; z-scored CRT, numeracy, science knowledge, BS receptivity)
sample_definition: All respondents with non-missing CogSophSc and MisperpSc
model_specification: Pearson correlation
operationalization_notes: Used the precomputed composites supplied in the dataset; bivariate correlation is the most direct test of the claim of a negative predictive relationship.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between the composite cognitive sophistication score (CogSophSc, z-averaged CRT, numeracy, science knowledge, BS receptivity) and the COVID-19 misperception score (MisperpSc) is r = -0.40, p < .001, n = 87, indicating cognitive sophistication negatively predicts misperceptions.

dependent_variable: Average correct recognition index across joy and anger words (mean of JOY% and ANG%)
main_predictor: Alexithymia group (TASGRP: 1=low vs 2=high, median split on TAS-20)
sample_definition: All 1096 participants with non-missing TASGRP and recognition scores
model_specification: Welch independent-samples t-test comparing high vs low alexithymia groups on joy+anger recognition index
operationalization_notes: The claim concerns recognition of anger and joy words by alexithymia group. I averaged the joy and anger recognition indices into a single DV reflecting the claim and tested the between-group difference with a Welch t-test, the simplest direct test of the claim.
reasoning: High-alexithymia participants (TASGRP=2) showed substantially lower average recognition index for joy+anger words (M=0.189) than low-alexithymia participants (M=0.463); Welch t(1031.1)=17.05, p<.001. The effect held in each emotion separately (Joy: t=15.24; Anger: t=16.34), supporting the claim.

dependent_variable: EVOLVED (humans evolved from earlier animals: 1=true, 2=false)
main_predictor: Latent class membership (post-secular vs traditional)
sample_definition: GSS respondents in 2006, 2008, and 2010 with non-missing values on the six manifest LCA indicators; analysis restricted to those classified as traditional or post-secular
model_specification: Three-class latent class analysis (categorical measurement model, stepmix), followed by Pearson chi-square test of EVOLVED by class on the two relevant classes
controls: none (manifest variable comparison across latent classes)
operationalization_notes: Methods section was redacted, so I selected six plausible manifest indicators consistent with the paper's description (Bible view, evolution, big bang, science understanding/benefits, religious affiliation strength). Classes labeled post hoc by their EVOLVED-rejection rates (traditional = highest rejection; modern = lowest; post-secular = intermediate). The recovered class proportions (48/19/33%) and post-secular profile diverge from the paper's reported 43/36/21% solution, which affects the substantive conclusion.
reasoning: In my LCA-replicated analysis (3-class model on BIBLE, EVOLVED, BIGBANG, SCISTUDY, SCIBNFTS, RELITEN, GSS 2006/2008/2010, N=2,272), I labeled classes by their EVOLVED rejection rate: the traditional class showed 5.3% endorsing 'humans evolved from animals' (true) while the post-secular class showed 84.7%. A chi-square test of EVOLVED by class (traditional vs post-secular only, N=1,841) yields chi2(1)=1191.33, p<.001, with post-secular respondents MORE — not less — likely than traditional respondents to affirm human evolution. This contradicts the paper's claim, likely because my LCA, performed without access to the paper's methods section, did not reproduce a class with the paper's described post-secular signature (religious yet rejecting evolution).

dependent_variable: Composite trendiness rating of the mug (mean of 'trendy', 'modern', 'urban', 1–7)
main_predictor: Table display condition (glass vs. wood)
sample_definition: All 69 participants in the replication dataset (all received the interdependent self-construal prime: writing about a meaningful event with family/friends)
model_specification: Independent-samples two-sided t-test (equal variances) comparing glass vs. wood
operationalization_notes: Codebook indicates V16=wood condition, V17=glass condition, and V18–V20 measure trendy/modern/urban (the trendiness scale referenced in the paper's Table 1). The replication dataset only contains the interdependent prime, so the claim's interdependent-subsample contrast is tested by a simple two-group t-test on the composite trendiness scale.
reasoning: Among interdependently primed participants, the mean trendiness composite (trendy/modern/urban) was 5.10 (SD=1.31, n=34) in the glass-table condition versus 5.47 (SD=1.01, n=35) in the wood-table condition; an independent-samples t-test gave t(67)=-1.31, p=.19. The direction is opposite to the claim and the effect is not significant, so the predicted assimilation effect does not reproduce.

dependent_variable: Utilitarian response on the conflict moral dilemma (moral_accept: 2 = morally acceptable / utilitarian, 1 = not acceptable)
main_predictor: Salience condition (death vs. pain)
sample_definition: Participants who consented (Q1=2) and passed the attention check (attn='c'); N=131
model_specification: Pearson chi-square test of independence on the 2x2 contingency table of salience condition by utilitarian response
operationalization_notes: The paper's key claim concerns utilitarian responding on conflict (footbridge-type) problems. In the data, moral_accept showed ~78% acceptable responses and moral_accept1 ~95%, consistent with moral_accept being the conflict dilemma and moral_accept1 the no-conflict control. With a binary DV and a 2-level between-subjects factor, the natural test is a chi-square (equivalent to comparison of proportions); this most directly mirrors the original 'percentage of utilitarian responses' analysis for this single-item replication.
reasoning: In the replication dataset, 82.3% (51/62) of participants in the death-salience condition judged the conflict scenario morally acceptable (utilitarian) vs 73.9% (51/69) in the pain condition. A chi-square test of independence yielded χ²(1, N=131)=1.32, p=0.25 — not statistically significant and, descriptively, in the opposite direction from the original claim that mortality salience reduces utilitarian responses.

dependent_variable: Standardized mean reaction time on obstacle→behavior association trials (ZHealthAssocM); faster RTs index stronger associations
main_predictor: Expectations of success × condition (mental contrasting vs. reverse contrasting vs. irrelevant control)
sample_definition: Replication participants in the H8 analytic dataset retained by the filter (IntAssocObs=0 & IntAccessObs=0); n=305 after listwise deletion in the regression
model_specification: Hierarchical OLS regression: Step 1 = ZHealthExp + ZHealthAccessM + Dummy1 + Dummy2; Step 2 adds ZHealthExp:Dummy1 + ZHealthExp:Dummy2. F-change tests the expectation×condition interaction (the test most directly tied to the claim that MC paired with low expectations yields weak obstacle–behavior associations).
operationalization_notes: Used the H8 analytic SPSS dataset prepared by the replicators, mirroring the paper's hierarchical regression approach. F-change for the two interaction terms is the omnibus test of the expectancy-dependent pattern; a significant negative simple slope within MC (or weaker associations in MC than controls at low expectations) is the directional pattern asserted by the claim.
reasoning: Hierarchical regression predicting obstacle–behavior association strength (ZHealthAssocM) from expectations, behavior accessibility, two condition dummies (mental contrasting as reference), and the two expectation×condition interactions yielded a non-significant interaction step, F(2,298)=0.36, p=.70. The simple slope of expectations within the mental contrasting condition was essentially zero (b=0.02, t=0.26, p=.79), in the opposite direction of the original negative slope. The expectancy-dependent pattern predicted by the claim did not emerge in the replication.

dependent_variable: s - x_l (proportion of surplus given away minus libertarian prediction = dictator's monetary contribution share)
main_predictor: none (one-sample test vs libertarian benchmark)
sample_definition: All dictators (playerdictator==1) with non-missing s and x; the dataset corresponds to the DW treatment (dictator piece rate 150 vs recipient 200)
model_specification: Wilcoxon signed-rank test of H0: s = x_l, normal approximation z-statistic
operationalization_notes: The paper tests each justice principle with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the dictator's share against the principle's prediction. The libertarian prediction equals the dictator's monetary contribution share x_l (variable x in the data). I restricted to dictators with observed allocations and applied the signed-rank test.
reasoning: Wilcoxon signed-rank test of dictator's actual share given (s) against the libertarian prediction x_l yields z=-3.38 (W+=8, n=18 non-zero of 27), p<0.001. Dictators systematically gave less than the libertarian prediction in the DW treatment, so the libertarian principle is rejected as an account of behavior, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Under-diagnosed (1 = hypertensive but not previously diagnosed)
main_predictor: Years of education
sample_definition: Hypertensive respondents in poor general health (poor_health==1) with non-missing covariates
model_specification: Probit regression
controls: Log per-capita expenditures, time preference, risk preference, travel time to health center, sex, age
operationalization_notes: Followed the paper's stratification (poor vs good health) and used the prepared data.Rds; under-diagnosis is the standard detection outcome in this literature, so a negative education coefficient implies higher diagnosis probability.
reasoning: Probit of under-diagnosis on education and controls within the poor-health hypertensive subsample yields a negative, significant education coefficient (b=-0.0333, z=-2.60, p=0.009, n=756). Since the DV is under-diagnosis, the negative sign means more educated respondents are more likely to be diagnosed, consistent with the claim.

dependent_variable: Proportion of deontological (harm-rejecting) judgments (RH_PMD, RH_NMD, RH_CMD)
main_predictor: Group × Dilemma-type interaction (Condition: 1=Control vs 2=Observed; Dilemma type: personal, non-personal/impersonal, non-moral control)
sample_definition: All participants in SCORE_all data.sav with complete RH scores for the three dilemma types (n=156; 78 per group). Two cases per group dropped due to missing RH values.
model_specification: 2 (Group, between) × 3 (Dilemma type, within) mixed-design ANOVA on harm-rejection rate, computed with pingouin.mixed_anova
operationalization_notes: The claim of 'social observation promoted deontological judgments especially for personal moral dilemmas' is most directly tested by the Group × Dilemma-type interaction, which is the analysis emphasized in the paper's results. Harm-rejection rate (RH) is the canonical operationalization of deontological judgment in this dataset.
reasoning: The Group × Dilemma-type interaction in a 2 (observed vs. control) × 3 (personal/non-personal/control dilemma) mixed ANOVA on the proportion of deontological (harm-rejecting) responses was non-significant, F(2,308)=0.24, p=.79, η²p≈.002. Group means on personal moral dilemmas were nearly identical (Control: M=.629; Observed: M=.649), indicating no selective deontological shift for personal dilemmas.

dependent_variable: COVID-19 concern (mh_anxiety_1, 5-point Likert worry-about-COVID item)
main_predictor: gender (female vs male)

operationalization_notes: The CSV contained two COVID anxiety/worry items; mh_anxiety_1 was chosen as the most direct measure of general concern/worry about COVID-19, matching the claim's wording. A two-sample t-test by gender is the most direct test.
reasoning: Welch t-test comparing women (M=3.07, SD=1.11, n=4933) vs men (M=2.89, SD=1.14, n=5138) on the COVID-19 concern/anxiety item mh_anxiety_1 yields t(10067)=8.26, p<.001. Women report significantly greater concern than men, consistent with the paper's claim.

dependent_variable: Percentage-point change in proportion of population staying home, March 19-28 2020 vs March 19-28 2019 (BTS Trips by Distance)
main_predictor: County Trump vote share (2016)
sample_definition: U.S. counties with non-missing BTS mobility data for both 2020 and 2019 reference windows and complete covariates (n=3,102)
model_specification: OLS regression with state fixed effects
controls: per capita income, % male, % Black, % Hispanic, % college, % retail employment, % transportation employment, % health/education/social services employment, % rural, plus state fixed effects
operationalization_notes: Unacast data unavailable; replicated using BTS Trips_by_Distance as proxy following the replication scripts. Outcome defined as % staying home change vs. same calendar days in 2019; controls and FE match Table 1 of the paper.
reasoning: In a multivariable OLS regression of the percentage-point change in the share of county population staying home (March 19-28, 2020 vs. same dates 2019) on Trump vote share with state fixed effects and the paper's listed controls, the Trump-share coefficient was negative (β = -1.75 percentage points per unit share, SE = 0.43, t(3041) = -4.12, p < 0.001), indicating that more Republican counties had smaller increases in staying-home behavior, i.e., reduced social distancing — matching the original claim.

dependent_variable: soc_dist composite (mean of soc_dist_1–4 social distancing behaviors)

dependent_variable: Achievement composite: standardized average of X7RSCALK5 (reading IRT scale) and X7MSCALK5 (math IRT scale)
main_predictor: Social-emotional problems composite: mean of teacher-reported externalizing (X7TCHEXT) and internalizing (X7TCHINT)

model_specification: Bivariate Pearson correlation between social-emotional problems and achievement composite (with t-test on r)
operationalization_notes: Methods section redacted; data dictionary identified wave-7 (5th-grade) IRT scale scores and teacher-reported externalizing/internalizing as the available outcomes. ELL defined via the household language status variable. A simple zero-order correlation directly tests the claimed link; sign and significance match the SEM result reported in the paper.
reasoning: Pearson correlation between teacher-rated social-emotional problems (mean of externalizing and internalizing) and a standardized achievement composite (mean z of reading and math IRT scale scores) is r = -0.076 (t = -3.50, df = 2090, p < .001) among ELL children. The negative direction matches the claim that fewer social-emotional problems are linked to higher achievement.

dependent_variable: Within-subject mean of SocGood ratings across the four organizations (Artis, Green, Food, Medtech), each rated 1=great harm to 5=great good
main_predictor: Experimental motive condition (1=nonprofit, 2=unspecified, 3=for-profit)
sample_definition: All Study 3 participants with non-missing societal-good ratings and condition (N=364)
model_specification: One-way between-subjects ANOVA on subject-averaged SocGood
operationalization_notes: Study 3 manipulated profit motive while holding organizational practices constant; the directly relevant DV is the overall societal-harm-vs-good rating (SocGood) for each of the four organizations. Averaging within subject reduces them to one observation per person for a simple between-subjects ANOVA across the three motive conditions.
reasoning: One-way ANOVA on each subject's mean perceived societal good across the four organizations shows a strong effect of motive condition, F(2,361)=36.91, p<.001. Means decrease from nonprofit (M=4.31) to unspecified (M=4.09) to for-profit (M=3.75), consistent with the claim that a profit motive reduces perceived societal good.

dependent_variable: Within-participant mean sharing intention (1-6 Likert) averaged across 15 headlines per veracity
main_predictor: Headline veracity (true vs. false), within-subject
sample_definition: All participants assigned to the treatment (accuracy-nudge) condition (Condition==2) in the replication dataset (n=790)
model_specification: Paired-samples t-test comparing each participant's mean sharing intention for true vs. false headlines
operationalization_notes: The replication dataset is the only file with documented codebook and complete sharing-intention data. The claim concerns within-treatment-condition comparison of true vs false sharing intentions, naturally tested with a paired t-test on participant-level means; an equivalent mixed-model with random intercept for participant yields the same conclusion (z=15.9, p<.001).
reasoning: In the treatment (accuracy-nudge) condition, participant-level mean sharing intention was higher for true headlines (M=3.151) than for false headlines (M=2.889); paired t(789)=9.33, p≈1e-19, Cohen's dz≈0.33. This matches the original claim that true-headline sharing intentions were significantly higher than false-headline ones in the treatment condition.

dependent_variable: Binary sustained-growth indicator (>=2% per-capita GDP growth for >=5 consecutive years in a window containing the survey year)

controls: None (univariate, mirroring the simplest specification linking impartiality to sustained growth)
operationalization_notes: Methods section was redacted; I used the paper's main sustained-growth definition (>=2% per-capita growth for >=5 consecutive years) from Table 2, with the impartiality values taken directly from Table 4, and World Bank GDP per-capita growth data provided. Single-predictor LPM is the most direct test of the directional claim.
reasoning: In a linear-probability regression of a binary sustained-growth indicator (=1 if the country experienced ≥2% per-capita GDP growth for 5 consecutive years in a window containing the survey year) on log of the perceived government impartiality index across 64 country-survey observations from 20 sub-Saharan African countries, the coefficient on log impartiality is -0.085 (t = -0.78, p = 0.44). The data do not reproduce the paper's reported positive association.

dependent_variable: Mean toaster evaluation (toaster45_mean vs. toaster25_mean, 1-7 scale)
main_predictor: Information type (aggregated 4.5-star vs. individualized 2.5-star toaster), within-subject
